name: Borgo Medievale
desc: The post-Roman settlement at Alba Fucens became an administrative center ca. A.D. 870 and remained significant as a center in Marsica until ca. 1143. The area was later subsumed by the Duchy of Spoleto.

name: Tempio Grande at Vulci
desc: A major urban sanctuary at Vulci with a long period of use, stretching from the archaic period into the Roman period.

name: Error? (island)
desc: An island mentioned in an Roman itinerary. It is possibly to be identified with the modern Île Plane, which is located a few kilometers off Cape Farina, Tunisia.

name: *Astora?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 F3 *Astora?

name: Asuccuris?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 H3 Asuccuris?

name: amnis Petronia
desc: A brook in the Campus Martius of ancient Rome that flowed from the Cati fons to the Tiber River.

name: Porta Flumentana
desc: The "Porta Flumentana" or "river gate" was a gate in the Republican-period fortifications along the Tiber River. It is now unlocated. While it may have been in the vicinity of the Pons Aemilius, much debate surrounds its topography.

name: Ghar El Kebir Quarries
desc: Punic and Roman sandstone quarries at Ghar EI Kebir.

name: Hochdorf Chieftain's Grave
desc: Tumulus covering a rich Celtic burial of ca. 530 BC.

name: Giuggianello
desc: A fourth to third century B.C. circular tower in masonry built atop a Middle Bronze Age mound.

name: Church of San Primitivo
desc: The so-called Church of San Primitivo in Monte Compatri. The church's bell tower was converted to a defensive tower around 1200.

name: Fonte dell'Acqua Paola
desc: The Fontana dell'Acqua Paola or Il Fontanone stands on the Ianiculum near the church of San Pietro in Montorio. It was built in 1612 to mark the end of the Acqua Paola aqueduct after it had been restored by Pope Paul V.

name: Roman villa at Anagnina Metro station
desc: The archaeological remains of a villa in the suburbium of the city of Rome located adjacent to what is now a station of the Rome Metro system at Anagnina.

name: Colle Oliva
desc: A Roman villa rustica in use from the middle Republican period until the 4th century A.D.

name: Ursins Gallo-Roman temple
desc: Site of a Gallo-Roman temple.

name: Boville Ernica
desc: A hilltop settlement with megalithic fortifications.

name: Piana di Monte Verna
desc: An ancient Oscan center delimited by a megalithic fortification wall.

name: Tomb of Marcus Tullius
desc: The schola-type tomb of one Marcus Tullius is located outside the Porta Stabia of Pompeii. The decedent is thought to have been the patron of the Aedes For­tunae Augustae and was three times duovir and tribunus militum a populo.

name: Tuscan Archipelago
desc: A chain of islands between the Ligurian Sea and Tyrrhenian Sea.

name: Monte Nuxi
desc: A proto-nuragic settlement on Monte Nuxi that covered approximately one hectare. The remains of various built springs are evident.

name: Pecile at Hadrian's Villa
desc: An artificial terrace surrounding a large pond, 30 m wide x 116 m long, located at the western end of Villa Adriana.

name: Villa of Caius Olius Ampliatus
desc: A 'Villa rustica' associated with one Caius Olius Ampliatus, located in the Ponticelli of Naples, Italy. The site was excavated in 1986-1987, with additional work in 2007. The site covers some 2,000 sq. meters.

name: La Spezia
desc: The modern city of La Spezia, Italy, is located what was in antiquity the territory of the city of Luni. The area of La Spezia has been surveyed by archaeologists.

name: Isole della Marmorata
desc: The Isole della Marmorata off the coast of Sardinia provided the grey granite (also known as granito della Sardegna) that was exported to Rome during the Imperial period.

name: Monte Abatone necropolis, Caere
desc: A necropolis of ancient Caere with particularly important evidence of funerary assemblages showing the influence of the Orientalizing period.

name: Regio VII (Via Lata)
desc: Regio VII (Via Lata) was one of the administrative regions of the city of Rome instituted by Augustus in 7 BCE. In addition to the named monuments and buildings, the Regionary Catalogues indicate that this district also included 15 shrines (aediculae), 120 townhouses (domūs), 25 warehouses (horrea),

name: Basilica Ulpia
desc: The Basilica Ulpia is located in the Forum of Trajan at Rome and derives its name from the emperor Trajan's gentilician nomenclature. The basilica was considered a marvel of ancient Roman architecture by observers, including the historian Ammianus Marcellinus.

name: Horti Maiani
desc: An urban garden of imperial Rome located on the summit of the Esquiline Hill. Based on an inscription dating to the reign of Claudius, it is believed that these gardens were administered by the same magistrate in charge of the Horti Lamiani, an official with the title "procurator hortorum Maianorum

name: Grotte di Pertosa
desc: The Pertosa Caves, a system of karst caves located in the comune of Pertosa, province of Salerno, Campania, Italy.

name: Regio XIII (Aventinus)
desc: The thirteenth administrative region of ancient Rome was created by Augustus in 7 BCE. This district contained 17 shrines (aediculae), 130 townhouses (domūs), 35 warehouses (horrea), 60 bath houses, and 88 fountains in addition to a list of monuments enumerated in the Regionary Catalogues.

name: Basilica Aemilia
desc: A basilica located at the juncture of the Sacra Via and the Argiletum flanking the Forum Romanum that was initially built in 179 B.C.E.

name: City wall of Cosa
desc: Cosa's polygonal masonry fortification wall, reinforced with interval towers, has a length of ca. 1500 meters. Traditionally the wall has been dated between ca. 273 and 264 B.C.

name: Poggio Civitella
desc: The hill of Poggio Civitella near Montalcino, Italy, rises to a height of 661 meters above sea level. Beginning in 1993, excavation campaigns revealed a series of settlement horizons dating to the first millennium BCE, ranging from the archaic to the Hellenistic periods. The hilltop was fortified du

name: Cannatello
desc: An archaeological site located in the territory of the eponymous frazione of the Italian municipality of Agrigento, Sicily. A middle and late Bronze Age fortified settlement dating to the fourteenth to thirteenth / twelfth centuries BCE has been discovered. Archaeologists deem it to be an important

name: Necropoli Romana
desc: A Roman necropolis at Brixia.

name: Temple of Veiovis
desc: The Temple of Veiovis, also attested as Aedes Vediovis, was a temple of ancient Rome located on the Capitoline Hill in a location known as "inter duos lucos", which is interpreted to mean a saddle between the two summits of the hill. The remains of a temple podium were discovered beneath the northwe

name: Vatican Obelisk
desc: An obelisk from Heliopolis in Egypt that the emperor Caius erected in the Circus Gaii et Neronis. It now stands in St. Peter's Square in Vatican City, having been re-erected there by Domenico Fontana in 1586.

name: Lupercal
desc: A cave located at the foot of the Palatine Hill in Rome in which the she-wolf was said to have been found suckling the twins, Romulus and Remus.

name: Künzing Roman amphitheater
desc: A Roman timber amphitheater dating from the first to fifth centuries, the Künzing Roman amphitheater measured 46 by 40 meters. The site was discovered during excavations carried out in 2003 and 2004. The archaeological site is no longer visible but a reconstructed evocation of the ancient structure

name: House of N. Popidius Priscus
desc: A Pompeian domus that, upon excavation, was found to have a large supply of colored marble.

name: Latin League
desc: The Latin League is the name given by scholars to a confederation of about 30 tribes and villages located in ancient Latium that was created for mutual defense purposes and existed from the seventh century BCE until 338 BCE. Its ancient name is unknown.

name: Ponte di Pratolungo
desc: Remains of a Roman Republican bridge crossing the Fosso di Pratolungo along the line of the via Tiburtina.

name: Bergantino nymphaeum
desc: A nymphaeum on the shores of the Alban Lake that is located in a natural grotto that is assigned to the Flavian period and associated with the complex of the Villa of Domitian.

name: Sepulcrum Hirtii
desc: The tomb of Aulus Hirtius, consul in 43 B.C., was discovered beneath the northwest corner of the Palazzo della Cancelleria in Rome in 1938.

name: San Pietro a Badia Pozzeveri
desc: An abbey with tenth century origins connected to the pilgrimage route known as the Via Francigena.

name: Geridu
desc: Geridu, located near the comune of Sorso in Sardinia, was the site of a Medieval village active from the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

name: Potter's workshop
desc: Shop no. 29 located in the commercial area along the via dei Sepolcri outside the Porta Ercolano at the northwest corner of Pompeii. Archaeological excavation in 2012 and 2013 undertaken by the École française de Rome in coordination with Ministero per i Beni e le attività cultural demonstrated that

name: Castellammare della Bruca
desc: A fortified medieval settlement that succeeds the acropolis of ancient Velia.

name: Casale Ciuffa
desc: The Casale Ciuffa occupied the site of a Roman villa; this site now lies within the footprint of the Parco degli Ulivi in the modern comune of Colonna, Lazio.

name: Tumulo Etrusco del Molinello (Asciano)
desc: An Etruscan tumulus-type tomb at Asciano with artifactual evidence dating to the Orientalizing period.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge
desc: An Unnamed Roman bridge that spans the Rio di Fontechiari.

name: San Giuliano Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge crossing the Melfa river in Lazio, Italy.

name: Necropoli di Celle
desc: Extensive areas of rock-cut tombs near Falerii Veteres (modern Civita Castellana, Italy).

name: Esterzili
desc: The Domu de Orgia at Esterzili is the largest nuragic "megaron" structure thus far discovered in Sardinia.

name: So-called Oratory of Phalaris
desc: A small, rectangular Greek temple-type building dated to the first century B.C. and located in the upper agora of Agrigento, on the Poggetto di San Nicola. The name "Oratory" comes from its later use as a Christian chapel.

name: Theatrum Marcelli
desc: Theatrum Marcelli (Theater of Marcellus) is an ancient Roman theater in the Circus Flaminius. Augustus completed its construction and dedicated it in 12 BC.

name: Mausoleum of M. Coelius Vinicianus
desc: A mid-first century B.C. tomb at Tusculum.

name: Santi Giovanni e Paolo
desc: An ancient Christian basilica on the Caelian Hill in Rome that was built in AD 398 by will of a senator known as Pammachius. The basilica was located over the home of two Roman soldiers, John and Paul, who had been martyred under Julian in AD 362. The church was thus called the Titulus Pammachii.

name: Clivus Scauri
desc: A street that ascended from the depression between the Palatine and the Caelian hills.

name: Case Romane del Celio
desc: An archaeological area beneath the basilica of the martyrs John and Paul that has been explored by means of excavation, revealing a series of Imperial period domestic remains dating between the second and fourth centuries A.D.

name: Basilica of San Clemente al Laterano
desc: The eleventh-century Basilica of San Clemente al Laterano is a Roman Catholic basilica dedicated to Clement I. It sits atop a three-tiered series of architectural remains stretching back to the Republican period. The earliest phase is represented by the foundations of a building destroyed by the fir

name: Grotte di Seiano a Pietramelara
desc: A ruined, terraced megalithic complex covering about 900 square meters. The complex likely dates to the second century B.C. and was destroyed in the time of Sulla. Scholars interpret the complex as a Samnite sanctuary.

name: Roman theater of Privernum
desc: The Roman theater of Privernum is attested mainly by means of epigraphic evidence.

name: House of Augustus
desc: An elite domus located at the southwest corner of the Palatine Hill that is identified as the house lived in by the Roman emperor Augustus.

name: Withdrawn: House of Augustus
desc: Withdrawn because unintentional duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/250568480

name: Mont'e Prama
desc: A locality near Cabras, Sardinia, where, in 1974, the cache of monumental prehistoric stone sculptures known as the "Giants of Mont'e Prama" was discovered.

name: Via Amerina
desc: A Roman road begun ca. 241 B.C. that connected Veii and Ameria.

name: Janiculum
desc: This hill is located outside the ancient city of Rome, to the west of the Tiber River, and is not considered one of the Seven Hills of Rome. From an early stage, the Janiculum was connected to the city by fortifications and a bridge over the Tiber. It was also the site of important water-powered mil

name: Piazza d'Oro at Hadrian's Villa
desc: One of the largest and most luxurious complexes of Villa Hadriani. It is situated at the northern end of the Villa, and consists of a vast building, with a vaulted, octagonal vestibule to the north, a cenatio to the south, and a central quadriporticus, down the middle of which runs a canal.

name: Mausoleum of Clesippus Geganius
desc: The ruins of a first century B.C. Roman tomb along the Via Appia at Mesa di Pontinia.

name: Sasso di Furbara
desc: A locality in southern Etruria near the Via Aurelia some 50 km north of Rome that has yielded evidence for human activity across multiple periods. Notable is evidence of Protovillanovan and Villanovan necropoleis as well as ritual activity of the Etruscans.

name: Subura
desc: Subura (or Suburra) refers to an area of ancient Rome, although the precise spatial definition of this area is unclear. In the earliest instances, this toponym may refer to the valley lying between the Oppian and the Caelian. As such it corresponds to one of the four urban regions known as the "Serv

name: Pons Agrippae
desc: A debated bridge upriver from the modern Ponte Sisto.

name: Santuario di Maria Santissima del Lattani
desc: A Marian sanctuary founded in 1430.

name: Colle S. Lucia-Maceralonga (Castelnuovo Parano)
desc: A Pre-Roman fortified center in the territory of Frosinone.

name: Via Olevano Romano columbarium
desc: A late republican to early imperial columbarium along the Via Praenestina. The columbarium is of rectangular plan and was last used during the early Flavian period.

name: Mandra Castellone
desc: A fortified Oscan center at high altitude (647 meters) located near Capriati al Volturno. The site is difficult to access, and the fortifications measure 80 meters in diameter.

name: Mausoleo della Conocchia
desc: A Roman mausoleum dating most likely to the second century.

name: Münster-Sarmsheim Roman Villa
desc: Remains of a Roman villa, including mosaic pavements, were discovered.

name: Villa Romana di Boscorotto
desc: A Roman villa with an area of more than 1,000 square meters was first identified at In Boscorotto, between the Maddaloni and Acerra districts, in 1987. Excavations were carried out between 1992 and 1993 during the construction of the Marcianise-Maddaloni freight yard.

name: Basilica Portuense
desc: A paleochristian basilica at Portus was built in the middle of the fourth century CE, amidst and atop earlier structures.

name: Theater of Nuceria Alfaterna
desc: The ancient Theater of Nuceria Alfaterna was first built during the second century BCE and occupies a zone that abutted the city's fortification wall. The theater was identified and excavated between the late 1970s and early 1980s in the area between Pareti and Pucciano.

name: Roman Bridge (Auletta)
desc: A Roman stone bridge that once crossed the river Tanager.

name: Mausoleum of Tor di Quinto
desc: A circular mausoleum dating to the time of the Roman Empire is visible today at Tor di Quinto. Elements of this marble funereal monument were uncovered in excavations conducted by a landowner in 1876 along the Via Flaminia, not far from the Porta del Popolo. The marble elements were expropriated by

name: Allerona
desc: Allerona is an Italian town in the province of Terni (Umbria). It is the findspot of a Trajanic milestone.

name: Stari Grad Plain
desc: The Stari Grad Plain is located on the island of Hvar in the Adriatic Sea. This cultural landscape is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site due, in part, to its pristine state of preservation, which dates back to the time of Greek colonization by Paros in the fourth century BCE.

name: Temple of Castor and Pollux, Cora
desc: The Temple of Castor and Pollux at Cora was originally built between the fourth and the second centuries B.C. The partially extant architrave carries an inscription of the first century B.C.

name: Theatrum Pompei
desc: Rome's first permanent theater, located in the Campus Martius. The complex was completed under the second consulship of Pompeius Magnus in 55 B.C.

name: Lucone di Polpenazze
desc: The archaeological site of Polpenazze del Garda (BS) Lucone is situated in a morainic basin in northern Italy. It is the site of several prehistoric settlements, which have been documented since archaeological excavations began in 2007. The Early Bronze Age settlement was active from ca. 2034 BCE un

name: Basilica of Constantine (Ostia)
desc: The presence of a basilica created with funds donated by Constantine I in region 5 of ancient Ostia was known from textual sources and then confirmed via geophysical prospection and, ultimately, excavation.

name: Roman Theater of Cluviae
desc: Remains of a Roman theater were identified in the 20th century in the vicinity of modern Piano La Roma in the municipal territory of Casoli, Italy. Its construction is estimated to date to the end of the first century BCE.

name: Pass of the Alpes Graiae
desc: A pass west of Segusio

name: Ad Horrea
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C2 Ad Horrea

name: Alb(i)um Intimilium/Albintimilium
desc: Alb(i)um Intimilium/Albintimilium (modern Ventimiglia) was the main settlement of the Ligurian tribe of the Intemelii. In the 2nd century BC, it came under the control of the Roman Republic. Albintimilium became a municipium in 89 BC in the tribus Falerna. In the same period, the city walls were bui

name: Album Ingaunum/Albingaunum
desc: The fourth century B.C. capital of the Ingauni Ligures sided with Carthage during the Punic War but was reduced by Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus in 181 B.C. A treaty was struck with Rome; the city received Roman citizenship in 45 B.C.

name: *Anao
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 *Anao

name: Antipolis
desc: Antipolis (modern Antibes) was founded as a colony from Massilia in the fifth century BC and emerged as a key trading center. In the late first century BC the city was incorporated into the Roman province of Gallia Narbonensis.

name: Apron (river)
desc: An ancient river on the Mediterranean littoral of what is now France, the Apron is possibly to be associated with the modern Siagne.

name: Athenopolis
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C3 Athenopolis

name: *Avisio
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 *Avisio

name: Baou-des-Noirs
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Baou-des-Noirs

name: Bordighera
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 E2 Bordighera

name: Boulouris
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C3 Boulouris

name: Bouteillière
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C2 Bouteillière

name: *Brigomagus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C2 *Brigomagus

name: Bussana
desc: An early imperial villa along the coast of Liguria. Its ancient name is unknown.

name: Le Candéou
desc: Salvage excavations during the 1970s in modern Le Candéou, a neighborhood of Peymeinade (France), identified multiple Roman-era structures that have been interpreted as agricultural in nature, including facilities for processing olive oil.

name: Cemenelum
desc: An oppidum that was the capital of the Vediantian Ligures; later became a municipium of the tribus Claudia.

name: Col. Forum Iulii
desc: Col. Forum Iulii (modern Fréjus) was a Roman military colony, most likely founded by Iulius Caesar, that served as a major naval base.

name: Costa Bellene/Ballene (Capo Don?)
desc: A Roman mansio on the via Iulia Augusta. An Early Christian complex (basilica, baptistery, cemetery) developed nearby and lasted until the Middle Ages.

name: *Cuntinus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 *Cuntinus

name: Deciates
desc: An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group.

name: Ecdinii
desc: The Ecdinii were an Alpine tribe. They are mentioned both on the inscription of the Tropaeum Augusti and on the Arch of Augustus at Susa.

name: Gallinaria (island)
desc: An island in the Ligurian Sea.

name: Glanate
desc: Glanate was originally a Ligurian settlement that became a Roman town after the annexation of Provence.

name: Herakles Monoikos/Portus Monoeci
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Herakles Monoikos/Portus Monoeci

name: Ingauni
desc: An ancient people, localized in Liguria (BAtlas 16 F1 Ingauni)

name: Intemelii
desc: The Intemelii were a tribe of Liguria.

name: Lero (island)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Lero Ins.

name: Ligauni
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 B2 Ligauni

name: Ligusticum Mare
desc: Ligusticum Mare (Ligurian Sea).

name: Lucus Bormani
desc: A Roman settlement on the coast of Liguria.

name: Lumo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Lumo

name: Mandelieu
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C2 Mandelieu

name: Monte Bignone
desc: Monte Bignone in Liguria is the site of a 'castellaro', a fortified hilltop settlement of Iron Age Ligurian peoples. The fortification is generally dated to the sixth century BCE.

name: Monte Colma
desc: An ancient settlement at Monte Colma in Italy, ancient name unknown (BAtlas 16 E2 Monte Colma).

name: Navelis
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Navelis

name: Nerusii
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C2 Nerusii

name: Nicaea
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Nicaea

name: Olivula
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Olivula

name: Oxubii
desc: The Oxubii or Oxybii were a Ligurian tribe inhabiting the coast of France near Massalia.

name: Planasia/Lerina (island)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Planasia/Lerina Ins.

name: Portus Maurici
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 F2 Portus Maurici

name: Pullopice
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 F1 Pullopice

name: Rotuba (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 E1 Rotuba fl.

name: Roussivau
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C3 Roussivau

name: Roman villa of Aia Nova
desc: A Roman villa of the mid-first century B.C. connected with a Publius Anilius, identified by means of brick and tile stamps. Located in the modern commune of Scansano.

name: Casteddu di Ceccia
desc: A stone-built monument of the Torrean civilization located south of Porto-Vecchio, Corsica.

name: Masseria Petrolio
desc: The substruction (basis) of a Roman villa rustica dating to the late republican period located near the course of the Garigliano river.

name: Villa Prato, Sperlonga
desc: A villa rustica excavated by the École française de Rome between 1979 and 1984.

name: Villa di Pipiano
desc: A Roman nymphaeum dating ca. A.D. 50-55.

name: Orto della Regina
desc: An archaeological site located on Monte La Frascara at Roccamonfina that is enclosed by a megalithic fortification executed in polygonal masonry.

name: Vicus Drusianus
desc: A street located in Regio I of ancient Rome that is known from the so-called Capitoline Base (CIL 6, 975). Part of its course may correspond to the Via della Ferratella in Laterano.

name: San Pietro in Vincoli
desc: San Pietro in Vincoli is a Roman Catholic titular church and minor basilica in Rome, Italy. It is located on the Oppian Hill and it houses relics connected with the Catholic Saint Peter. The basilica was founded as the Basilica Eudoxiana ca. 432-440. Pope Sixtus III consecrated the site in 439. The

name: Nuraghe su Figu
desc: Nuraghe su Figu is a single-tower nuraghe located approximately 300 meters from the nuraghe Sas Casas and Columbos, respectively to the West and southeast.

name: Porticus Boni Eventus
desc: A portico built in 374 CE by an urban prefect named Claudius near the temple of the god Bonus Eventus.

name: Via Statilia tombs
desc: Late Republican chamber tombs (ca. 100 B.C.) located at the intersection of the modern Via Statilia and Via di Santa Croce in Rome.

name: Montelabate
desc: The Montelabate estate of the Gaslini foundation has been investigated by means of both field survey and excavation. This upland area sits astride a frontier zone, one that separates Perugia (Etruria) from Gubbio (Umbria). Simon Stoddart, Maurizio Matteini Chiari, Gabriele Cifani, and other scholars

name: Temple of Venus Genetrix
desc: The Temple of Venus Genetrix located in the Forum Iulium was dedicated ca. 46 BCE.

name: Regio IV (Templum Pacis)
desc: The fourth Augustan region of Rome includes the Subura as well as the valley between the Esquiline and the Viminal hills, along with the no-longer-extant Velian Hill. This region reportedly contained eight shrines (aediculae), 88 domūs, 18 warehouses (horrea), 75 bath houses, and 78 loci. Its perime

name: Temple of Talamonaccio
desc: An Etruscan temple of the fourth century BCE, associated with the ancient settlement of Telamon. It lies on Mount Talamonaccio, across the bay from the modern village of Talamone, north of Orbetello, Italy.

name: Camp celtique de la Bure
desc: A Gallo-Roman settlement of a commercial nature located on the Meurthe river. Archaeological evidence for earthworks, as well as ritual activity, has been discovered. The Gallo-Roman ramparts, in a later phase, make use of marble sculpture as spolia.

name: Nadlesk
desc: Nadlesk, Slovenia, was the site of a Roman fortification and associated settlement.

name: Roman walls, Novaria
desc: A segment of the Roman defensive wall.

name: Tomba della Medusa (Roma)
desc: A Roman chamber tomb now located on the grounds of the Policlinico Umberto I hospital in Rome.

name: St. Pierre Cathedral
desc: Church in Geneva, Switzerland that was originally a Roman Catholic cathedral but was converted into a Protestant church during the Reformation. The original church was built in the 4th century but the present building began construction around 1150.

name: Cercina (Etruria)
desc: A now-unlocated place near Florentia in Etruria (Regio VII) known from epigraphic sources. Caius Caesar, the father of Iulius Caesar, helmed a veterans' colony there.

name: Regio VI (Alta Semita)
desc: The sixth administrative regio of Augustan Rome, Regio VI (Alta Semita) derives its name from the street that crossed over the Quirinal Hill. This is a large district that includes the Viminal Hill, the lower slopes of the Pincian Hill, in addition to the valleys between these hills. The region also

name: Thermae Traiani
desc: A monumental public bath of ancient Rome that was built between 104 and 109. The architect Apollodorus of Damascus built the baths for Trajan.

name: Forcello
desc: An Etruscan settlement north of the Po river.

name: Nuraghe S'Urachi
desc: A nuragic site near San Vero Milis in west central Sardinia, occupied from the Late Bronze Age into the Roman period.

name: Fossa Traiana
desc: The Fossa Traiana (Channel of Trajan) describes a canal of ca. 45 m width connected with the artificial harbors at Portus. Despite the name, its origins may lie in the Claudian harbor works. The cutting of the channel created an artificial island between Ostia and Portus, the so-called Isola Sacra.

name: Forum Iulium
desc: The Forum Iulium (or Forum of Caesar, Forum Caesaris) is a forum built by Iulius Caesar and dedicated ca. 46 B.C. The main cult of the forum is that of Venus Genetrix.

name: House of Sallust
desc: The House of Sallust (VI 2,4) is a domus in Pompeii that assumes its final form around the second century B.C.

name: House of the Small Fountain
desc: A Samnite-type house located on the Via di Mercurio (VI, 8, 23). The house derives its conventional name from a mosaic fountain located at the rear of the peristyle.

name: Roman villa at Verige Bay
desc: A Roman villa rustica located in the bay of Verige, dating from the first century B.C. through the sixth century A.D. The villa's ruins lie within Croatia's Brijuni National Park.

name: Temple of Minerva Medica
desc: The so-called Temple of Minerva Medica is, in fact, a nymphaeum located along the line of the Anio Vetus aqueduct; it most likely dates to the fourth century AD.

name: Acropolis of Selinus
desc: The fortified Acropolis of Selinus occupies a limestone plateau. It was planned following the Hippodamian fashion and it is most noted for the numerous Doric temples that occupied its sacred precincts.

name: Via Claudia Nova
desc: A Roman road built ca. AD 47 to connect the Via Caecilia with the Via Claudia Valeria.

name: Via Claudia Valeria
desc: A portion of the Via Valeria connecting Aternum and Corfinium. A Claudian milestone (CIL 9.5973) records the construction taking place in AD 48/9 and that the road ran from Cerfennia to the mouth of the Aternus river (modern Pescara).

name: Roman macellum at Aeclanum
desc: Once hypothetically identified by some scholars as an amphitheater, this structure at Aeclanum is now understood to be a Roman macellum.

name: Crypt and church of San Lussorio
desc: The Romanesque church of San Lussorio dates to the early twelfth century.

name: ager Volaterranus
desc: The ager Volaterranus was the territory of the city of Volaterrae in northern Etruria.

name: Porticus Philippi
desc: A portico that surrounded the Temple of Hercules Musarum in the Campus Martius of ancient Rome. The construction of the portico was the result of the patronage of L. Marcius Philippus, the stepfather of Augustus.

name: Basilica di Santa Francesca Romana
desc: The Basilica of Santa Francesca Romana, also known as Santa Maria Nova, dates originally from the ninth century when the basilica was erected on the site of a preexisting oratory during the papacy of Paul I.

name: Ara della Regina
desc: A fourth to third century B.C. sanctuary at Tarquinia.

name: Great City Baths at Salona
desc: The so-called Great City Baths at Salona or Great Thermae were built in the second or beginning of third century A.D.

name: Necropoli Orti della Maddalena
desc: A Hellenistic and Roman period necropolis located in Messina, Sicily, in the area now referred to as "Orti della Maddalena".

name: Nuraghe Su Valsu
desc: A Middle Bronze Age nuraghe located southwest of Florinas in Sardinia.

name: Tremona
desc: A multi-phase settlement - Neolithic to Medieval periods - that is now preserved as an archaeological site.

name: Pons Neronianus
desc: A bridge across the Tiber river built either by Caius or Nero in order to connect the western part of the Campus Martius with the Campus Vaticanus.

name: Meta Sudans
desc: A large fountain located southwest of the Flavian Amphitheater and completed under Domitian (ca. A.D. 96). Four of Rome's Augustan regions converged at this point (I, III, IV, X); it is possible that Regio II also intersected the other four regiones at this place.

name: Torre Caetani
desc: A Medieval tower located on Tiber Island.

name: Porta Rauduscula
desc: The Porta Rauduscula was a gate of Rome's so-called Servian Wall. It is known only from textual sources. Varro's listing places it between the Porta Naevia and the Porta Lavernalis.

name: Serapeum
desc: The Serapeum in Ostia's Regio III was built between 123 and 126 CE thanks to private patronage.

name: Terme della Trinacria
desc: The so-called Terme della Trinacria in Regio III of Ostia Antica were built in the Hadrianic period at the same time as the Temple of Serapis (III,XVII,4). The modern toponym is derived from a triskelion included in a mosaic decoration.

name: Absasallensis
desc: A late antique "episcopus Absasallensis" is attested, but the bishopric seems to have been nowhere else mentioned. It probably lay in Africa proconsularis.

name: Poggio Gaiella
desc: An Etruscan tumulus of the fifth century BCE, the tumulus of Poggio Gaiella has been considered by some scholars to be the tomb of Porsenna.

name: Roman castrum at Pyrgi
desc: The Roman castrum at Pyrgi seems to re-use, in a direct fashion, elements of the preceding Etruscan city plan, although covering a smaller area.

name: Dolciano
desc: Dolciano is located in the environs of Chiusi and abundant evidence of Etruscan necropoleis has been documented there.

name: Ganglegg
desc: A multi-period hilltop settlement occupied from the Chalcolithic period to Late Antiquity.

name: Nuraghe Su Casteddu
desc: Nuraghe Su Casteddu is a trilobate nuraghe in Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Bruncu Maduli o Bruncu Madugui
desc: A Middle Bronze Age nuraghe and a proto-nuragic village located on the plain known as Giara di Gestur.

name: Melone del Sodo
desc: Etruscan tumulus-type tombs of the seventh through fourth centuries B.C. located near Cortona, Italy, in località Il Mulino.

name: Selva del Lamone
desc: The Selva del Lamone is a modern forest reserve that preserves undeveloped natural and cultural landscapes of Lazio.

name: Regio III (Isis et Serapis)
desc: The third Augustan administrative region of the city of Rome was centered on the Oppian Hill and derived its name from the Isis et Serapis on the Via Praenestina. name: Foro Romano
desc: The Roman forum of Aquileia.

name: Siebenlinden
desc: Site located in modern Rottenburg am Necker with remains from the Middle Mesolithic, Late Mesolithic, Neolithic, and La Tène Iron Age culture.

name: Castello di Poira
desc: A now-ruined castle with Medieval origins occupying the same range of hilltops as ancient Poira.

name: Templum Veneris et Romae
desc: A double temple sacred to Venus Felix and Roma Aeterna built by Hadrian on the slope of the Velian hill to the north of the Sacra Via beginning in 121 CE.

name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
desc: A church in Trastevere with origins in the fifth century CE. Pope Urban I likely founded the first church on the same site in the third century CE. Its venerated saint is a Christian martyr of the third century CE. Pope Paschal I rebuilt the church in 822 CE, and moved the relics of St Cecilia to th

name: Italia, Regio III
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Lucania and Bruttium. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Italia, Regio VIII
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Aemilia. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Poggio Gramignano Roman Villa
desc: A Roman villa in the modern Lugnano commune of Italy's Terni province. Substantial architectural remains dating to the Roman imperial period have been excavated there, as well as a later (5th century CE?) collection of child and infant burials that gained significant media attention.

name: Villa Redenta
desc: An ancient suburban villa outside of Spoletium, occupied from the Augustan period to the third century A.D. The remains are on the grounds of the modern Villa Redenta complex.

name: Linguella Roman villa
desc: A multi-phase villa on the island of Elba.

name: Ripatransone
desc: In antiquity, Ripatransone was a significant Picene center. It now lies in the Province of Ascoli Piceno, in the Italian region Marche.

name: Villa of L. Crassius Tertius
desc: The Villa of L. Crassius Tertius at Oplontis (modern Torre Annunziata in Italy) was discovered in 1974, approximately 250m east of the Villa of Poppaea.

name: Tor Tignosa
desc: Tor Tignosa, mapped and listed in the 17th century Catasto Alessandrino as a landed estate, is a ruined stone structure located some 8 km northeast of Lavinium. Multiple votive inscriptions were found in the vicinity, providing evidence for an ancient sanctuary dating to between the fifth and second

name: Cala Minnola, Levanzo, Province de Trapani
desc: A productive site connected with fish processing the production of fish sauce.

name: Temple of Hercules at Montorio al Vomano
desc: A sanctuary of Hercules located in the territory of Teramo near the Vomano river.

name: So-called Temple of Hercules
desc: A site on the Via Appia that is likely commercial in nature but that has long been associated with a shrine mentioned by Martial.

name: So-called Grotta Fragapane
desc: A large and rich Early Christian necropolis on the Via Sacra in Agrigento, dated to the fourth century A.D.

name: Temple of Athena at Paestum
desc: A Late Archaic Doric Temple of Athena (ca. 500 B.C.) at Paestum.

name: Forum of Paestum
desc: The forum of Roman Paestum stands north of the Hera sanctuary and measures ca. 57 x 150 meters. name: San Giacomo di Rialto
desc: A church in Venice, Italy. San Giacomo di Rialto is claimed to be the oldest church in the city, with AD 421 as the traditional date of its consecration. The first documented attestations of the church belong to AD 1152.

name: Augusta Praetoria
desc: Augusta Praetoria (modern Aosta) was a settlement of the Salassi conquered by Rome in 25 B.C. From 24 B.C., a colony of 3,000 Roman military veterans occupied the city of Augusta Praetoria Salassorum, and it became the capital of the province of Alpes Graiae in 11 B.C.

name: Augusta Taurinorum
desc: Augusta Taurinorum (modern Turin), the settlement of indigenous Celto-Ligurian peoples, was re-settled as a Roman veteran colony in 28 BC.

name: Ausuciates
desc: An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group whose territory was located around Ossucio.

name: Bedriacum

name: Belounoi

name: Benacenses

name: Bergomum
desc: Originally a center of the archaic Golasecca culture, Bergomum became a municipium of the tribus Voturia. In 452, Attila captured and razed the city.

name: Lys (river)
desc: The modern Lys river is possibly to be identified with the ancient Betuctelum river. The Lys flows from the Lys Glacier of the Monte Rosa massif to converge with the river Dora Baltea as a righthand tributary at Pont-Saint-Martin.

name: Binbelli?

name: Castelletto Ticino
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 39 D2 Castelletto Ticino

name: Cremona
desc: Cremona is a city of Cisalpine Gaul located on the Po River. The Romans established a colony of 6,000 settlers there after 225 B.C. Cremona was the first Latin colony placed north of the Po River.

name: Dertona

name: Desenzano
desc: At Desenzano, in the province of Lombardia, the remains of a Roman villa dating to the mid-fourth century A.D. were here. The structure is axial and palatial in its nature. Its decorative program includes polychrome mosaic pavements. It is noted for mosaic scenes featuring the Good Shepherd.

name: Duria (Bautica) (river)
desc: Duria (Bautica) fl. (Dora Baltea) is a river of northern Italy that is a tributary of the Padus fl. (Po river).

name: Insubres
desc: A Gallic tribe of Northern Italy, giving their name to the region of Insubria.

name: Iria/Forum Iulii Iriensium
