name: Septem Maria (Station)
desc: A station on the Via Popillia in the Po River delta (also known as Septem Maria).

name: Septem Maria (Po River Delta)
desc: The Po (Padus) river delta.

name: Silarus (river)
desc: The Sillaro river.

name: Silis (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C1 Silis fl.

name: Sinnius (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B4 Sinnius fl.

name: Spina
desc: An Etruscan port city at the mouth of the Po River on the Adriatic Sea, most likely founded at the end of the sixth century B.C.

name: Tartarus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A2 Tartarus fl.

name: Tarvisium
desc: Tarvisium (Treviso) is a settlement located in the plain of the Silis river, not far from the Via Claudia Augusta.

name: Togisonus? (river)
desc: A river of the Venetia, possibly in the territory of Patavium.

name: [Torcellum]
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C2 [Torcellum]

name: Utens (river)
desc: Attested in ancient sources, the Utens river is possibly to be associated with the modern Uso.

name: Vatrenus (river)
desc: This ancient river, identified with the modern Santerno, is one of many draining the northern slopes of the Appenines into the Po valley. Today, the Santerno eventually empties into the modern Reno, but in antiquity it flowed, possibly in multiple branches, further into the complex and now much-chan

name: Venetia (region)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A1 Venetia

name: Vicetia
desc: Vicetia (modern Vicenza) as a settlement of the Veneti in northern Italy.

name: [Vicus Aventia]
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B3 [Vicus Aventia]

name: Vicus Serninus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A3 Vicus Serninus

name: Vicus Varianus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B3 Vicus Varianus

name: Montone (river)
desc: The modern Montone river (southwest of Ravenna) was probably known by the ancient name Vitis.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A4 unnamed aqueduct (Bononia)

name: Unnamed aqueduct at Vicetia
desc: An aqueduct supplying Vicetia (modern Vicenza in Italy)

name: Unnamed aqueduct (Ateste)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B2 unnamed aqueduct (Ateste)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C4 unnamed aqueduct (Compitum ad Confluentes)

name: Ravenna Aqueduct
desc: Supplied Ravenna with water from the Bedesis fl.

name: Nuraghe Unia
desc: A well-preserved monopteral nuraghe located in northwestern Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Armungia
desc: A single-tower nuragic site; the diameter of the tower measures ca. 12 meters.

name: Ponte Brabaciera
desc: A second-century Roman bridge on the Riu Brabaciera.

name: Matzanni
desc: A sanctuary that includes a Punic temple built in white limestone, a nuraghe, and a sacred well.

name: Civitas Leonina
desc: The Civitas Leonina or Leonine City is a portion of the city of Rome on the left bank of the river Tiber around which Pope Leo IV commissioned the construction of the Leonine Wall in the ninth century AD. This followed the Saracen sack of Rome in AD 846.

name: House of the surgeon
desc: The so-called "House of the Surgeon" is considered to be one of the oldest domus in Pompeii. (VI, 1, 10, 23)

name: Olginate Roman Bridge
desc: Ruins of a late Roman bridge identified in the mid 20th century at a location now roughly coincident with a modern bridge at Olginate over the Fiume Adda (ancient Addua) immediately below the modern dam that retains the Lago di Garlate.

name: Monte Mario
desc: Monte Mario is a hill located on the right bank of the Tiber River.

name: Hypogeum at Torre del Giudizio
desc: A Roman hypogeum-type tomb in the via Teodora was reused in the construction of the tower known as Torre del Giudizio.

name: Aphrodite sanctuary at Lokroi Epizephyrioi
desc: The worship of Aphrodite is significant in the colonial city of Lokroi Epizephyrioi.

name: Centocamere at Lokroi Epizephyrioi
desc: The so-called "Centocamere" is an urban complex within the city walls dating to the fourth and third centuries B.C. This complex is laid out a organized city blocks separated by planned streets.

name: Cistern
desc: A Roman period cistern of Olbia on Sardinia.

name: Tomb of Caius Cartilius Poplicola
desc: The Tomb of Caius Cartilius Poplicola, dating to ca. 30-20 B.C., is a monumental tomb outside the Porta Marina of Ostia. Poplicola was a prominent citizen of Ostia.

name: Vicus Censorius
desc: A street located on the Tiber Island that connected the Pons Cestius and Pons Fabricius. It is cited on the so-called "Capitoline Base".

name: Auginus mons
desc: A sacred mountain of Italy mentioned by Livy; possibly corresponding to Monte Cimone of the northern Apenines.

name: Sarno Baths
desc: The so-called "Sarno Baths" (Regio VIII, Insula 2, nos. 17–21) at Pompeii resulted from the merger and remodeling of two atrium houses, no. 18 and no. 21. There is considerable debate in the scholarly literature as to the architectural phasing.

name: House VIII.2.13
desc: House VIII.2.13 is linked to VIII.2.12. Excavations took place in 1826, 1888, and 1928.

name: Casa di Championnet
desc: A well-appointed domus with its own bath complex dating to the Late Republican period.

name: San Paolo alla Regola
desc: The Catholic church of San Paolo alla Regola located in the modern Rione of Rome named "Regola", to which it gives its name. The current edifice of the church dates to the seventeenth century. Excavations carried out from 1978 to 1982 documented multiple layers of architecture dating from the imperi

name: Via Lata
desc: Via Lata is a later Latin name for the portion of the ancient Via Flaminia within the walls of Rome. According to Platner and Ashby, the name first appears in the Regionary Catalogue but it is commonly attested in sources, including the liber Pontificalis.

name: Complesso dei Riti Magici
desc: The so-called "complex of the magic rites" is a building located in Regio II of the archaeological site of Pompeii. Excavations were conducted in 1954, 1957, 1963, and 1985. The modern toponym is derived from various ritual items discovered in the complex, which may have been dedicated to the cult o

name: Building with Three Exedrae
desc: The Building with Three Exedrae at Hadrian's Villa, Tivoli, is an architectural complex with a squared central court onto which three exedra with fountains open.

name: Temple E at Selinus
desc: A fifth-century B.C.E. Doric temple, sacred to perhaps Hera or Dionysus, located on the eastern hill at Selinus.

name: Temple of Demeter at the Sanctuary of Demeter Malophoros, Selinus
desc: The Temple of Demeter was used for the worship of Demeter (Malophoros), goddess of fertility, grain, and agriculture. Built in the seventh century BC, the temple was used continuously until its abandonment ca. 250 BC.

name: Roman amphitheater at Paestum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Paestum was built ca. 50 B.C., making it one of the earliest extant amphitheaters.

name: Roiate
desc: A fortified pre-Roman center connected with the Aequi. The ancient name of the site is unknown.

name: Pyramid of Cestius
desc: An ancient pyramid-shaped tomb built for Caius Cestius (ca. 18-12 BC), a magistrate and member of the Septemviri Epulonum. The tomb stands at the fork of the ancient Via Ostiensis and was later incorporated into the city's fortifications.

name: Sep. Eurysacis
desc: The tomb of a baker, M. Vergilius Eurysaces, built at the point where the via Labicana and the via Praenestina exit from Rome's walls to the east. The tomb dates to the later Republican period (ca. 50-20 B.C.).

name: Villa di Capitone
desc: A platform villa located near Tivoli.

name: Torre della Scimmia
desc: A Medieval tower in Rome, perhaps first built by the Frangipani.

name: Ponte Sant'Antonio
desc: The Ponte Sant'Antonio is a Roman aqueduct bridge that was part of the Aqua Anio Novus.

name: Monteriggioni
desc: A Medieval settlement where numerous important Etruscan tombs have been excavated.

name: Nazzano Romano
desc: Nazzano Romano was the site of an Etruscan settlement covering some 7 hectares and dating between the eighth and fifth centuries B.C.

name: Basilica and convent of S. Ippolito
desc: An important paleochristian complex located in the area of Portus.

name: Temenos of Athena
desc: The area on the northeast side of the Piana di Himera is delimited by walls and contains four religious buildings (temples A, B, C, and D), probably dedicated to Athena. The foundations are still visible in the archaeological site of Himera.

name: Stancija Blek
desc: The archaeological site of Stancija Blek (Tar-Vabrega, Istria-Croatia) is located on the west coast of Istria. In antiquity, the site would have been located in the territory of Parentium. Archaeological investigation has documented more than 1,500 years of occupation, beginning perhaps with a Roman

name: Mausoleum of Galba
desc: The so-called mausoleum of Galba is a Roman period tomb located in Monte San Biagio Latium, Italy.

name: Villa Romana di Collesecco
desc: A villa rustica located in the Sabina, ca. 1 km from Cottanello (Rieti). The imperial villa was superimposed over a villa of the republican period.

name: Complesso episcopale
desc: The Late Antique to early Medieval "Episcopal" complex of the Santissima Trinità located at Venosa.

name: Catacomb of San Zotico
desc: A Christian catacomb located at the tenth mile of the ancient Via Labicana.

name: Civita d'Arlena
desc: Civita d'Arlena (also known as Civita del Fosso di Arlena) is an archaeological site that occupies a hilltop near Lake Bolsena. It was the site of Etruscan occupation until the third century BCE. Excavations carried out by the École française de Rome (1952 to 1958) revealed parts of a fortification

name: Santuari Sanniti del Monte Cila
desc: The ruins of a sanctuary associated with the Samnites located on Monte Cila, where a megalithic fortification is also attested.

name: Pincian Hill
desc: The Pincian Hill in Rome likely takes its name from the Pincii, an ancient family. It is not considered a member of the canonical grouping of Rome's hills, but it did lie within the line of the walls built by Aurelian. In the early Imperial period, it is known as a zone of elaborate gardens, hence t

name: Castello normanno-svevo (Sannicandro di Bari)
desc: The Norman-Hohenstaufen Castle (Sannicandro di Bari, Italy) is a Medieval castle that dates from the tenth century.

name: Murgecchia
desc: A place located in the territory of Matera that produced an ancient coin struck at Poseidonia and rediscovered in 1917.

name: Theater of Balbus
desc: Cornelius Balbus dedicated a theater in the Campus Martius at Rome ca. 13 BCE.

name: Withdrawn: Necropoli delle Pianacce
desc: duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/289697636

name: Aqua Augusta (Naples)
desc: The Aqua Augusta (Naples), also known as the Acquedotto romano del Serino, is a complex aqueduct system supplying Roman-period sites in the Bay of Naples. The aqueduct system was built between ca. 33 and 12 B.C. It supplied a number of Campanian centers, including Pompeii, Herculaneum, and Puteoli.

name: Hellenistic-Roman theater at Sarno
desc: An ancient theater.

name: Poggio del Molino
desc: A Roman villa overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea located within the former territory of Populonia.

name: Lago di Biéntina
desc: The Lago di Biéntina was once the largest lake in Italy's Tuscany region. While it was finally drained in 1859 and converted to arable land, the extent to which it was a standing body of water in antiquity remains debated.

name: Hedemünden
desc: An early Roman fort located on the river Werra.

name: Ponte Valentino
desc: A Roman bridge located east of Benevento, Italy, and built by Flavius Iulius Valens.

name: Villamassargia, Nuraghe di Santu Pauli
desc: A nuragic complex situated atop a low hill near Villamassargia, Sardinia.

name: Su Carroppu
desc: A Neolithic rock-shelter settlement.

name: Villa Commedia
desc: A villa on Lake Como described by Pliny the Younger. Scholars have long thought it must be located in the vicinity of modern Lierna, and 19th and 20th century finds of floor mosaics and other elements have led to conjectures that the villa must have been located either in the peninsular "Castello" n

name: Rieti survey area
desc: An archaeological field survey carried out in the territory of Rieti from 1988 to 1991.

name: Necropolis of Ponte Messato
desc: A pre-Roman and Roman period necropolis on the outskirts of Teramo.

name: Via Ciminia
desc: The Via Ciminia was a Roman road that left the Via Cassia and continued toward the Ciminian hills. Its course likely ran from Sutrium to near Viterbo.

name: Wesseling Roman Villa
desc: A villa rustica at modern Wesseling.

name: Ulrichsberg
desc: The ruins of a Late Gothic Church of St. Ulrich which gave its name to the mountain on which it stands.

name: Tomb of Publius Vesonius Phileros
desc: An aedicula tomb built near the Porta Nocera ca. A.D. 25-50 by Publius Vesonius Phileros for himself, his patroness Vesonia, and his friend Marcus Orfellius Faustus. A later added inscription shows a falling out between the two friends.

name: Frascole, S. Martino a Poggio
desc: A stips votiva was discovered at the site of the Christian church of San Martino a Poggio - Frascole in 1887. The main ancient activity at the site likely took place during the middle of the third century B.C.

name: Monte Santa Vittoria Megalithic Enclosure
desc: A megalithic enclosure that includes a circular Nuragic building.

name: Capitolium of Terracina
desc: A Tuscanic podium temple that is often referred to as being of the Capitolium type was built at Terracina in the middle of the first century BCE.

name: Santi Quaranta
desc: The remains of a long, early Imperial-period Roman cryptoporticus at Beneventum that was re-used in the Middle Ages. It is situated between the modern San Lorenzo district and the rural area of Cellarulo, near the Basilica of the Madonna delle Grazie in Benevento, Italy.

name: Betitius Perpetuus Arzygius, Domus
desc: A domus included in Regio III, the house of Betitius Perpetuus Arzygius was located on the Quirinal Hill close to the ara incendii Neroniani. Some of its remains have been documented beneath the present Palazzo delle Esposizioni.

name: Porticus Absidata
desc: The Porticus Absidata was an exedra porticata that served as the northern apsidal entryway to the Forum of Nerva, also known as the Forum Transitorium.

name: Bagnacavallo
desc: Bagnacavallo is the site of a Roman pagus located east of the centuriated area of Faventia.

name: Tawern Roman temple complex
desc: This reconstructed (in-situ) temple complex stands on a hill called Metzenberg, just to the southwest of modern Tawern in Germany. A partially excavated Gallo-Roman vicus lies at the foot of the hill, closer to town.

name: Castellaccio di Capo Ripa
desc: A Hellenistic fortified site (?oppidum) near Capranica (Viterbo).

name: Villa of Agrippa
desc: The so-called Villa (or baths) of Agrippa on Planasia Ins. (modern Pianosa) is the putative location of exile for Agrippa Postumus, grandson of Augustus.

name: Torre Spaccata
desc: The ruined Medieval tower (ninth and tenth centuries) is built atop the remains of a quadrangular Roman tomb of the Antonine period that was executed in opus latericium.

name: Villa di Casale Ghella
desc: A villa complex at the eighth mile of the Via Cassia, to which it was linked by means of a paved diverticulum. The first phase dates to the first century BCE and the villa remained in use until the Late Antique period.

name: Terme Aquae Passeris
desc: A Roman bath located at Aquae Passeris.

name: Unnamed Roman tomb
desc: An unnamed Roman tomb that is located near Casale Ghella.

name: House of the Ara Maxima
desc: The House of the Ara Maxima, located on the Via del Vesuvio, is also known as the House of Pinarius and the House of Narcissus (VI, 16, 15-17).

name: House of Trebius Valens
desc: The House of Aulus Trebius Valens (III,2,1) is an atrium-style house in Pompeii that lies on the north side of Via dell'Abbondanza. It was first excavated in 1913.

name: Tuledo (mountain)
desc: A mountain in the Ligurian Apennines cited in the Sententia Minuciorum; the modern Monte Leco.

name: Valle dei Templi
desc: The "Valle dei Templi" of Agrigento is an archaeological site in Sicily located on a ridge, as opposed to the false suggestion of the conventional name, outside modern Agrigento.

name: Gioiosa Guardia
desc: An ancient city in Sicily that was founded during the reign of Frederick III of Aragon and is located on Mount Meliuso in Sicily.

name: Scheggia Pass
desc: The Scheggia Pass marks the division between the Central and Northern Apennines in northern Umbria. Its elevation is 632 meters above sea level.

name: Guattari Cave
desc: A cave located on the slopes of Monte Circeo with evidence of prehistoric activity. A Homo neanderthalensis cranium was discovered here in 1939.

name: Flaminio Obelisk (Rome)
desc: The so-called "Flaminio Obelisk" at Rome was created in Egypt during the Nineteenth Dynasty under Pharaoh Seti I. The obelisk was erected at Heliopolis under Ramesses II. In 1 BCE, the obelisk was transported to Rome on the orders of Augustus. It was transported with the Obelisk of Montecitorio. The

name: Lucus Stimulae
desc: A grove sacred to Stimula, located at the southwestern foot of the Aventine Hill.

name: Iunonis Curritis Lucus
desc: The sacred 'Grove of Iuno Curritis' located in Falerii Veteres.

name: Tomba del Timpano
desc: A tomb of the Hellenistic period located close to a Graeco-Siceliote center.

name: Capo Graziano
desc: The prehistoric village of Capo Graziano dates to the Middle Bronze Age and is located on the island of Filicudi. The site was excavated between 1952 and 1969. It is situated on a terrace some 100 m above sea level. At least 27 agglomerative huts were identified at the site.

name: Ponte Scotonico
desc: An ancient Roman bridge located along the Via Valeria near Roviano, Italy.

name: Venice
desc: The city of Venice in northern Italy.

name: Via Laurentina
desc: An ancient road, leading southwards from Rome toward Laurentum. Its course, endpoint, and coincidence with the Via Ostiensis and the Via Ardeatina are matters of scholarly contention.

name: Casteddu di Tappa
desc: Casteddu di Tappa is a Bronze Age archaeological site in Corsica connected with the Torréen culture.

name: Large Palaestra
desc: The so-called "Large Palaestra" is an open square (ca. 140 x 140 m) surrounded by porticoes built in the early first century A.D.

name: Ager Lunensis Survey area
desc: An archaeological survey in the territory of Luni that tracked settlement patterns between ca. A.D. 300 and A.D. 1200.

name: Ponte d'Augusto
desc: A Iulio-Claudian bridge located in Ariminum.

name: Arx of Cosa
desc: The citadel of the ancient city and location of its Capitolium.

name: Comitium of Poseidonia/Paestum
desc: The comitium is a component of a monumental forum complex constructed at Paestum after the city became a Latin colony in 273 B.C.

name: Arch of Trajan at Benevento
desc: A triumphal arch built in honor of Trajan at Beneventum; it marks the Trajanic extension of the Via Appia.

name: Archbishop's Chapel, Ravenna
desc: A private, early Christian oratory in Ravenna, Italy, erected by Peter II as archbishop in A.D. 495.

name: Monte Poggiolo
desc: Monte Poggiolo overlooks the Montone River valley. Settlement evidence begins in the Paleolithic period, making the site one of the earliest loci of human habitation in Italy.

name: tribus Tities
desc: An early Roman tribal division said to date from the time of Romulus.

name: Public administration buildings
desc: The administration buildings on Pompeii's forum were built before 80 B.C. and renovated following the earthquake of A.D. 62. The central building is generally regarded as the tabularium.

name: Temple of Vespasian
desc: The "Temple of Vespasian" (VII, 9, 2), also referred to as Aedes Genii Augusti, is situated between the Temple of the Lares Publici and the Building of Eumachia on the eastern side of the forum of Pompeii. Its precise attribution is still a matter of debate.

name: Temple of Fortuna Augusta
desc: A Corinthian order temple in Pompeii dedicated to Fortuna Redux and likely dating to the late first century BC (VII, 4, 1).

name: House of the Dioscuri
desc: A large and well-appointed house that takes its name from frescoes of Castor and Pollux (VI, 9, 6).

name: House of Apollo
desc: Located on the Via di Mercurio, the so-called House of Apollo draws its name from a cycle of frescoes of the myth of Apollo found at the rear of the garden. One M. Herenullius Communis, whose name appears on a ring found in 1830, may have been the owner (VI, 7, 23).

name: House of the Baker
desc: House in Pompeii (VI,3,3) that most likely dates from the second century BC and experienced extensive remodeling after the earthquake of AD 62.

name: So-called Tempio di Venere e Cupido
desc: The so-called Temple of Venus and Cupid at Rome is part of the complex of buildings associated with the Sessorian palace. The structure's modern assignation is owed to the discovery of a fragmentary statue of Sallustia Orbiana in the guise of Venus Felix. Sallustia Orbiana was the wife of Alexander

name: Canopus at Hadrian's Villa
desc: The Canopus garden is set at the principal entrance to Hadrian's Villa. An imposing waterway occupies all its length.

name: Area archeologica di Colle della Noce
desc: The ancient temple in the sacred area of Colle della Noce dates to the fifth and fourth century BCE.

name: Roman baths, Malvindi
desc: The remains of Roman baths located in the ager of Mesagne.

name: Ponte Caldaro
desc: A Roman bridge of the Via Flaminia.

name: Le Spugne di Nocera Umbra
desc: A preserved stretch of masonry substruction for the Roman Via Flaminia.

name: Terme di Caronte
desc: Mineral springs located at modern Lamezia Terme in Italy's Cantanzaro province. There is some archaeological evidence for exploitation of the springs in antiquity, but the current spa complex is completely modern in date. Some scholars have suggested that the Terme di Caronte may correspond to the "

name: Formello villa and mausoleum
desc: A Roman villa in the territory of Blera of which a cistern and a mausoleum remain.

name: Fosso della Fiora
desc: One of the sources of the Aqua Traiana.

name: Via Collatina
desc: A Roman road connecting Rome with Collatia.

name: Via Tiburtina
desc: An ancient road heading east-northeast from Rome to Tibur.

name: Ponte Rotto necropolis
desc: The Ponte Rotto necropolis is associated with the Etruscan city of Vulci.

name: Cantiano
desc: An ancient place at modern Cantiano may have stood along the line of a branch of the Via Flaminia. The so-called "Sassoferrato milestone" was located about one mile from Cantiano (CIL 6629).

name: Bibbiena
desc: Bibbiena likely originated as an Etruscan hilltop settlement. A Medieval castle is eventually built atop the hill, which stands 425 metres (1,394 ft) above sea level.

name: Civita Giuliana
desc: The Civita Giuliana is located in the northern suburbium of Pompeii, about 700 meters from the city walls. Thus far the site has produced archaeological evidence of suburban villas in Pompeii's hinterland. Early twentieth-century excavations were carried out here, only to be published in 1994. Cland

name: Arian Baptistry
desc: Baptistry built by Theodoric the Great in the late fifth or early sixth century AD

name: New Basilica of Saint Apollinaris
desc: A basilica in Ravenna, Italy, erected by Theodoric the Great in the first quarter of the sixth century AD.

name: Amphitheatrum Flavium
desc: The Flavian amphitheater at Rome (the so-called "Colosseum").

name: Arch of Constantine
desc: The Arch of Constantine at Rome, a triumphal arch dedicated in A.D. 315.

name: Campochiaro
desc: An Italic sanctuary sacred to Hercules located in località Civitella in the comune of Campochiaro. The site is to be connected with the Pentrian Samnites.

name: Roman theater at Terracina
desc: The ancient Roman theater of Terracina dates from the first century BCE.

name: Vigna Bevilacqua
desc: In 1834, Edward Dodwell documented a substantial tract of polygonal masonry walling at Bevilacqua near Frascati that was thought to be associated with a Roman villa platform.

name: Monte Semprevisa
desc: The highest peak of the Monti Lepini.

name: Naparis? (river)
desc: The Naparis was a river of Scythia and a left-bank tributary of the Danube. It can no longer be identified.

name: Arienzo
desc: A villa of the second century AD that was destroyed by a flood in the fourth century.

name: Bir Ftouha basilica
desc: An Early Christian pilgrimage complex and baptistry at Carthage.

name: Porta Romanelli
desc: A section of ashlar masonry fortification walls, including a gate, at Tarquinii.

name: Banditaccia necropolis, Caere
desc: The Etruscan necropolis of Caere, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Monterozzi necropolis
desc: The Monterozzi necropolis is an Etruscan necropolis located to the east of Tarquinia. The necropolis contains about 6,000 graves.

name: Roman amphitheater at Florentia
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Florentia was built between 124 and 130.

name: Roman theater at Mogontiacum
desc: The site of the Roman theater in Mainz.

name: Torre di Mercurio
desc: A tower associated with Pompeii's fortification wall that is also sometimes designated as "Tower XI".

name: Via Campana?
desc: A road located on the right bank of the Tiber River leading to the Campus Salinarum romanarum and sharing the first part of its course with the Via Portuensis.

name: San Pietro ad Oratorium
desc: A Romanesque-style Roman Catholic church and Benedictine monastery consecrated in 1117 but with possible origins in the eighth century.

name: Selvicciola necropolis
desc: A prehistoric (Eneolithic) necropolis in mid-Tyrrhenian Italy with activity beginning in the early fourth millennium BCE. The Selvicciola necropolis is located in the valley of the Fiora River.

name: Via Flavia
desc: An ancient Roman road that connected Tergeste to Dalmatia and followed the course of the Istrian coast. The road was built during the reign of emperor Vespasian.

name: Ponte di Annibale - Sant'Angelo
desc: A Roman bridge known by a variety of local toponyms that crosses the Savuto river. It is located in the modern Italian municipality of Altilia, Calabria.

name: Su Mulinu
desc: A nuragic complex with three phases of occupation and construction, beginning as early as the sixteenth century B.C.

name: Nuraghe Perdu Cossu
desc: A monopteral nuraghe located near Norbello, Sardinia.

name: Tomb of Trebius Iustus
desc: A Late Antique hypogeum tomb discovered in 1911 and dedicated to Trebius Iustus and Honoratia Severina.

name: Patronus tomb
desc: A painted tomb located near the Porta Latina in Rome. The tomb's owner, Patronus, is identified as a Greek physician of the first century CE.

name: Pons Fabricius
desc: The Pons Fabricius (sometimes referred to as the Ponte dei Quattro Capi) is a first-century BC bridge in Rome that spans part of the Tiber River from the area of the Circus Flaminius to the Tiber Island.

name: Basilica of Santa Maria in Trastevere
desc: The Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere is a titular minor basilica located in the Trastevere district of Rome, Italy.

name: Vaticanus Mons
desc: A hill located across the Tiber from Rome's traditional seven hills, the Vaticanus Mons now lies within the territory of Vatican City.

name: Pompey
desc: Pompey (Meurthe-et-Moselle, France) produced archaeological evidence of a Roman productive site located near the junction of the Meurthe and Moselle rivers. This site was discovered in 1962 and has been described as a "villa rustica". There is evidence of baths and painted wall plaster. There is evi

name: Roman Aqueduct from Gorze to Metz
desc: A Roman aqueduct with a course of about 22 km, originating from the Bouillons spring near Gorze (208 m) and flowing to the city of Divodurum (Metz) (184 m). Some 12.7 km of the aqueduct is subterranean. Arched aqueduct bridges are extant at Ars-sur-Moselle and Jouy-aux-Arches.

name: Verzino
desc: The compilers of the Barrington Atlas indicate that evidence for ancient silver working was identified at Verzino in the present-day Italian region of Calabria. This site is located in the valley of the River Neto (the ancient Neaethus).

name: La Dogana
desc: A Roman tomb at Centuripe known as "La Dogana".

name: Velia
desc: The Velia, no longer extant, was a spur stretching from the north side of the Palatine Hill toward the Oppian Hill.

name: Archaeological area of Macchia Grande
desc: The archaeological area of Macchia Grande provides archaeological evidence for multiple phases of human occupation from the Villanovan period to the Roman Imperial period.

name: Avezzano Roman villa
desc: A large Roman villa near Alba Fucens that originates in the second century B.C.

name: heroon of Aeneas
desc: A tumulus at Lavinium located near the Latin federal sanctuary that has been associated with the tomb of Aeneas and/or a heroön dedicated to him.

name: Colonne della Sabatina
desc: The so-called "Colonne della Sabatina" are located at the southeastern end of the territory of Campagnatico territory, between Arcille and Baccinello. These fortifications date originally to the thirteenth century and were initially a possession of the Abbey of San Galgano.

name: Santo Stefano al Monte Celio
desc: The Basilica of Saint Stephen in the Round on the Caelian Hill is an ancient titular church located on the Caelian Hill in Rome. Its earliest phase belongs to the reign of Pope Simplicius (468-483). The early martyr Saint Stephen was honored in the church's consecration. Its circular plan is highly

name: Thermae Constantinianae
desc: The last of the great imperial baths of the ancient city of Rome, the Thermae Constantinianae were constructed in Regio VI, perhaps replacing the pre-existing Balineum Claudianum. They were located at the southern end of the Quirinal Hill, between the Vicus Longus and the Alta Semita. Substantial re

name: Thermae Novati
desc: Thermae Novati, ancient baths of the Vicus Patricius that were located in the vicinity of S. Pudenziana.

name: Italia, Regio I
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Latium and Campania. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Italia, Regio II
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Apulia and Calabria. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Tomb of the Volumnii and Palazzone necropolis
desc: A hypogeum-type tomb located in Ponte San Giovanni, a suburb of Perugia. The tomb is generally dated to the third century B.C.

name: Ponte Apollosa
desc: Ponte Apollosa, a bridge of the Via Appia that may have been restored by Septimius Severus in 198 CE.

name: Ponte delle Serretelle
desc: The so-called Ponte delle Serretelle is an ancient arched bridge located southwest of Benevento, Italy. It lies between the Gran Potenza hill and the Serretelle stream. It may have once been located either at or near the point where the Serretelle and the Calor converged.

name: Villa of Caesar and Maxentius at San Cesareo
desc: The so-called Villa of Caesar and Maxentius at San Cesareo is located at the 18th mile of the Via Labicana.

name: Aquae Rusellanae
desc: A thermal site located near Roman Rusellae in regular use and reuse since at least Roman times. Its ancient name is not known. The first modern excavations and mapping efforts date to the 18th century of the modern era.

name: Regio VIII (Forum Romanum)
desc: The eighth administrative region of ancient Rome was created by the Augustan reforms of 7 BCE. Regio VIII contained 34 shrines (aediculae), 130 townhouses (domūs), 18 warehouses (horrea), 85 baths (balneae), and 120 fountains.

name: Regio XI (Circus Maximus)
desc: The eleventh region of Rome was created under the Augustan administrative division of 7 BCE. According to the Regionary catalogues, this region contained 19 shrines (aediculae), 89 townhouses (domūs), 16 warehouses (horrea), 15 bath houses, and 20 fountains.

name: Templum Sol
desc: A sanctuary in the Campus Agrippae that was dedicated by Aurelian on December 25, 274, and funded by means of spoils taken from Palmyra.

name: Horti Liciniani
desc: A complex of elite gardens on the Esquiline Hill connected to the gens Licinia. The gardens were located between the via Labicana and via Praenestina.

name: Column of Trajan
desc: The Column of Trajan (or Trajan's Column) is a victory column that was erected in the Forum of Trajan at Rome ca. 113 in order to commemorate Trajan's victories in the Dacian Wars. The column is particularly noted for its helical historiated bas relief frieze decoration.

name: Thermae Helenianae
desc: The Thermae Helenianae or Thermae Helenae was a thermal complex located in the Horti Spei Veteris, also referred to as the Horti Variani. The baths were situated near the arcus Neroniani adjacent to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. As Helena, mother of Constantine I, restored them following a fire in 32

name: Regio XII (Piscina Publica)
desc: The twelfth administrative region of ancient Rome was created in 7 BCE by Augustan reforms.

name: Porticus Aemilia
desc: A utilitarian porticus and storage building located outside the Porta Trigemina, the Porticus Aemilia was erected in 193 BCE by Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and and Lucius Aemilius Paullus.

name: Horrea Galbana
desc: Horrea (warehouses) located between the southern part of the Aventine Hill and Monte Testaccio.

name: Sant'Egidio del Monte Albino aqueduct
desc: A subterranean Roman aqueduct in the modern Italian province of Salerno.

name: Via Ostiensis necropolis
desc: A necropolis at Ostia that began during the second century B.C. on the south side of the Via Ostiensis.

name: Casa della Biblioteca
desc: The House of the Library (VI, 17, 41) at Pompeii is located along the Vicolo del Farmacista, south of its junction with the Via Consolare. The site was first excavated in 1759 and again during the 1970s.

name: Necropoli Giambertoni
desc: A Hellenistic and Roman necropolis at Agrigento (second century BC to the third century AD) that includes the Tomb of Theron.

name: Temple of Iuno Moneta
desc: A major ancient sanctuary of the Capitoline Hill, the remains of which are likely to be found beneath Santa Maria in Ara Coeli.

name: Amphitheater at Castrum Rauracense
desc: Discovered in late 2021 on the site of the Basler Ruderclub in Augst, this amphitheater lies just west of the Roman fort of Castrum Rauracense. It seems to have been built in an abandoned quarry sometime in the 4th century CE.

name: House of M. Spurius Saturninus and D. Volcius Modestus
desc: A domus in Pompeii that was built using Sarno limestone. The house was excavated in 1760, 1841, and 1910 and re-examined in 2007 and 2010. The site was bombed World War Two (13 September 1943).

name: Doric nymphaeum
desc: The so-called "Doric nymphaeum" is located on the shores of the Alban lake and was a component of the Villa of Domitian.

name: Apollo-Grannus-Tempel
desc: A Roman temple in Faimingen near Lauingen in Bavaria.

name: Strebersdorf
desc: Roman military encampment located approximately halfway between Savaria and Scarabantia, containing remains dated to the 1st-2nd centuries CE.

name: Pietra Dell’Oglio (bridge)
desc: A Roman bridge crossing the Aufidus (modern Ofanto) river at the border between the modern Italian provinces of Campania and Basilicata. The bridge is one of two candidate identifications for the "Pons Aufidi" shown on the Peutinger map (the Ponte S. Venere), a possibility bolstered by recent compar

name: Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta
desc: The Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta on the island of Torcello is a Roman Catholic basilica initially founded in 639. The second basilica was begun in 1008.

name: Church of Santa Fosca
desc: The Church of Santa Fosca on the island of Torcello is a Romanesque church dating initially to the ninth century CE.

name: Casale di Madonna del Piano
desc: A Roman villa with a long occupational arc from the first century BCE to the third century CE.

name: Santuario rupestre di Silvano
desc: The so-called rock-cut sanctuary of Silvanus at Terracina.

name: Casa del Diavolo
desc: A Roman villa (second to fourth centuries A.D.) located near ancient Forentum.

name: Roman baths at Is Bangius
desc: Terme Romane di Is Bangius

name: Domus Romana "delle Entrate"
desc: The remains of a Roman townhouse (domus) at Castra Albana.

name: Etruscan sanctuary of San Lorenzo Nuovo
desc: An Etruscan sanctuary located on Monte Landro northwest of Lake Bolsena.

name: Amiternum (Samnium)
desc: An ancient city in Samnium, located between Interamna Lirenas and Atina, perhaps corresponding to the modern comune of Sant'Elia Fiumerapido (FR).

name: Withdrawn: Untitled
desc: This place resource has been withdrawn because it was created and published due to a technical error.

name: Arch of Augustus (Fano)
desc: A city gate in the form of a triumphal arch with three vaults. The gate marks the entry of the via Flaminia into the city.

name: Cardo Maximus
desc: The Cardo Maximus of Saepinum.

name: Decumanus maximus of Carsulae
desc: The Decumanus maximus of Carsulae.

name: Basilica of Carsulae
desc: The civic Basilica of Carsulae is located on the forum.

name: Arch of Trajan at Ancona
desc: An arch erected to honor Trajan between A.D. 100 and 116.

name: Horti Lamiani
desc: Gardens on the Esquiline Hill that passed into the control of the Iulio-Claudian family from the consul Lucius Aelius Lamia. As imperial property, the gardens were adorned with opulent display architecture and sculpture.

name: Vetricella
desc: An Early Medieval royal property located in the area of Scarlino (Grosseto) in Tuscany.

name: Morgantina, House of Ganymede
desc: The House of Ganymede at Morgantina is a peristyle house with mosaic floor pavements. The earliest phase of the house belongs to the third century B.C.

name: Ekklesiasterion of Morgantina
desc: The monumental central staircase in the agora of Morgantina has been identified as the Ekklesiasterion. They date after the middle of the third century B.C.

name: Albinia Roman villa
desc: The remains of a villa rustica near Orbetello, found to have construction in opus latericium.

name: Thermae Diocletiani
desc: Public baths near the Viminal Hill in Rome constructed under Diocletian from 298-306 CE.

name: Isis Tomb
desc: Now lost, the so-called "Isis Tomb" was excavated at Vulci in the 19th century. Based on finds evidence, the tomb is traditionally dated ca. 625 to 550 B.C. Its traditionally assigned name is likely a misnomer, based on a contemporary identification of a bronze bust as representing the Egyptian godd

name: Ponte di Diocleziano, San Lazzaro di Fossombrone
desc: The so-called "Ponte di Diocleziano" in the local comune of San Lazzaro di Fossombrone was a Roman bridge along the Via Flaminia in the valley of the Metaurus river. The Roman bridge was completely destroyed during the Second World War.

name: Tomba del Sileno
desc: The Tomba del Sileno is an Etruscan tomb at the Sovana Archaeological Park in the province of Grosseto. Dating from the third century BCE, the tomb derives its name from a bas-relief resembling the head of a Silen.

name: Catacombs of San Senatore
desc: A Christian catacomb located at the fifteenth mile of the Via Appia in use from the late third century A.D. until the Middle Ages.

name: Villa Romana ai Cavallacci
desc: A Roman villa first occupied in the Late Republican period and abandoned ca. the fifth century AD.

name: Pantanello necropolis
desc: Burial ground located 3.5 km west of Metaponto containing tombs dated from 600-280 BCE.

name: Nuraghe Appiu
desc: A nuragic complex in northwest Sardinia.

name: Roman amphitheater at Volaterrae
desc: The archaeological remains of an amphitheater were discovered at Volterra in 2015. Preliminary work suggests that the structure measured ca. 70 x 90 meters and had three tiers of seats that could accommodate 8,000 to 10,000 spectators.

name: Portone necropolis at Volaterrae
desc: The so-called Portone necropolis is a major Hellenistic necropolis outside the walls of Volaterrae.

name: Buonconvento, Siena
desc: Numerous instances of ancient ceramic production have been documented in Buonconvento, Siena.

name: Tomba Lattanzi, Norchia
desc: A Hellenistic, rock-cut tomb at Norchia. The site is located within the modern municipal boundaries of Viterbo in Lazio, Italy.

name: Kupinovik Roman Villa
desc: A Roman villa site on the modern Croatian island of Hvar (ancient Pharus).

name: Pago Triopio
desc: The Pago Triopio is a monumentalized area located near the mausoleum of Caecilia Metella between the second and fourth mile of the Via Appia. The residence of Herodes Atticus was located here.

name: Columbarium of the freedmen of Augustus
desc: An early imperial columbarium tomb on the Via Appia.

name: Tomba del Timpano
desc: A rock-cut tomb of the sixth and fifth centuries B.C.

name: Roman amphitheater at Casinum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Casinum was built thanks to the patronage of Ummidia Quadratilla in the first century.

name: Civitas Camunnorum amphitheater
desc: The ruins of a Roman amphitheater.

name: Temple B
desc: A temple vowed by Q. Lutatius Catulus at the battle of Vercellae (30 June, 101 B.C.). The sanctuary is a tholos-type temple and was sometimes referred to as 'aedes Catuli'.

name: Porta Leoni
desc: A Republican gate of Verona dedicated by P. Valerius, Q. Caecilius, Q. Servilius and P. Cornelius.

name: Roman amphitheater at Uthina
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Uthina dates to the reign of Hadrian and seated about 16,000 spectators.

name: Roman amphitheater at Cumae
desc: A Roman amphitheater at Cumae in Campania.

name: Gymnasium at Akragas
desc: An architectural complex in the upper agora of Akragas (modern Agrigento) dedicated to Hermes and Heracles that was probably used as gymnasium. It appears to have been built in Hellenistic time and renovated in the Augustan period.

name: Tomb of Theron
desc: Theron was a fifth-century B.C. tyrant of Akragas. A tomb located near the Porta Aurea of the city is traditionally referred to as that of the tyrant.

name: tribus Velina
desc: The tribus Velina was one of the later rural tribes which was established in Rome in 241 B.C.

name: Lacus Curtius
desc: The Lacus Curtius is an area in medio foro connected with the earliest phases of Rome's occupation. By the late Republican period, it had become a small basin set inside a paved area. Livy relates the famous episode of the Sabine Mettius Curtius in relation to his description of the site.

name: Pian del Vescovo
desc: The Pian del Vescovo is the western necropolis of Blera and perhaps the most extensive. A variety of tomb types dating to the seventh and sixth centuries BCE are attested.

name: Etruscan necropolis of Terrone
desc: A rock-cut Etruscan necropolis located at Blera.

name: Via Flaminia
desc: A major Roman road connecting Rome and Ariminum, by way of Narnia and Nuceria. The road was begun under the censorship of Caius Flaminius Nepos in 220 B.C.

name: Ponte dell'Ospedalato
desc: A Roman bridge located near Praeneste.

name: Villa Sora
desc: A coastal villa in the 'contrada Sora' area of Torre del Greco, a district with a great many archaeological remains.

name: Temple of Jupiter Anxur
desc: A late Republican sanctuary of the city of Terracina that is typically dated ca. 100-70 B.C.

name: Amphitheater of Pompeii
desc: The Amphitheater of Pompeii is the earliest known surviving example of a Roman amphitheater. It was built between 80 and 70 B.C.

name: Tomba del Duce, Vetulonia
desc: An elite tomb at Vetulonia dating to the late eighth century BCE. Among the tomb's occupants was one Rachu Kakanas. The artifact assemblage includes numerous elite objects, among them a bronze boat that is attributed to the Nuragic culture of Sardinia.

name: Barcola
desc: A no-longer-visible villa maritima was identified north of Tergeste in 1887. According to AdriAtlas, a reanalysis by Fontana (1993) places the beginnings of the villa's occupational sequence in the third quarter of the first century BCE.

name: Roman city wall at Telese Vetere
desc: Remains of the fortification wall of the Samnite center of Telese Vetere.

name: House of the Skeleton
desc: The so-called "House of the Skeleton" was constructed in the early first century BCE in the Roman colony of Cosa. It stands an example of the domestic architecture of the Late Roman Republic.

name: Porta Settimiana
desc: The Porta Settimiana is a gate in Rome's Aurelianic walls.

name: Mithraeum at Vulci
desc: A mithraeum was discovered at Vulci in 1975 during excavations of a Roman aristocratic house. The shrine was well preserved with two tauroctony scenes dating to the third century. The site was destroyed in the fourth century A.D.

name: Unnamed spring supplying Thuburbi Minus via aqueduct
desc: Unlabeled feature captured from the Barrington Atlas

name: Unnamed spring supplying Rusicade/Thapsus via aqueduct
desc: Unlabeled feature captured from the Barrington Atlas

name: Temple East of Lavinium
desc: From the 5th century BC.

name: Unnamed spring supplying Hippo Regius via aqueduct
desc: Unlabeled feature captured from the Barrington Atlas

name: Unnamed bridge over the Simbruina Stagna (Anio flumen) at Villa Neronis
desc: Unlabeled feature captured from the Barrington Atlas

name: Dam at source of the Aqua Anio Novus
desc: Unlabeled feature captured from the Barrington Atlas

name: Untitled
desc: Unlabeled feature captured from the Barrington Atlas

name: San Nicola in Carcere
desc: San Nicola in Carcere is a titular church in Rome's historical district (rione) Sant'Angelo, close to the Forum Boarium. The twelfth-century church is built atop the remains of Roman temples of the ancient Forum Holitorium and incorporates their remains into its structure.

name: Cerreto Sannita
desc: A Samnite temple dedicated to Flora.

name: Nuraghe Asusa
desc: A nuraghe standing on a modest hill (502 meters above sea level) on the Brabaciera river. The nuraghe originally had two towers with an intermediary courtyard.

name: Su Fraigu
desc: A Punic necropolis.

name: Adoni
desc: A Late Bronze age nuragic complex composed of a central tower, a quadrilobate bastion, and a village.

name: Cavaturini
desc: Cavaturini, a vicus located in the Ligurian Apennines that is mentioned in the so-called Sententia Minuciorum.

name: Roman cistern (Ladispoli)
desc: Remains of a substantial, two-aisled cistern of the Roman imperial period.

name: Unnamed Roman villa
desc: Ruins of an unnamed Roman villa located near Ladispoli and in the vicinity of the so-called "Villa di Pompeo".

name: Sa Mandra Manna
desc: A fortified site in Sardinia with megalithic architecture.

name: Monte Dell'Incastro (Guidonia Montecelio)
desc: The Monte Dell'Incastro in Guidonia Montecelio, Lazio, is a hill that is the site of ancient construction activity, including villas, a nymphaeum, and a subterranean cult of Hercules.

name: Villa dell'Incastro
desc: An ancient villa in Guidonia Montecelio, Lazio.

name: Porta Mediana necropolis
desc: Porta Mediana necropolis is a necropolis at Cumae containing some 70 tombs, dating from the fourth century BCE to the fifth century CE.

name: Acropolis of Cumae
desc: The Acropolis of Cumae was used across multiple periods, beginning with the foundation of the Greek colony in the eighth century B.C.

name: Mons Faliscorum
desc: Mons Faliscorum (modern Montefiascone) originally a Faliscan settlement, came later to be controlled by the Etruscans.

name: Esquilinus Mons
desc: The Esquiline Hill is one of the seven hills of Rome. The eastern section of the hill lay outside the Servian Wall, and served as a pauper's cemetery during the archaic and Republican periods.

name: Grotta Porcina tumulus
desc: A rock-cut tumulus of the first half of the sixth century B.C.

name: Macchia delle Valli, Vetralla
desc: A rock-cut Etrusco-Roman sanctuary sacred to Demeter that was discovered during rescue excavations in 2006 following looting activity. The sanctuary, set in a grove, remained in use until the second century A.D.

name: Vigna Parrocchiale archaeological area
desc: A complex of civic and sacred buildings in the urban area of ancient Caere, including the so-called "elliptical building".

name: Orcia (river)
desc: The Orcia originates on Monte Cetona and is a major tributary of the Ombrone.

name: Abbazia di Sant'Antimo
desc: The Abbey of Sant'Antimo was a Benedictine monastery located in the comune of Montalcino, Italy, about 9 km from the line of the Via Francigena. The abbey grew around the site of an oratory to Saint Anthimus, whose relics may have been relocated here in the eighth century. The site was formerly occu

name: Pons Sublicius
desc: The Pons Sublicius is traditionally held to be the earliest Roman bridge across the river Tiber. The textual tradition assigns its construction to the king Ancus Marcius in 642 B.C. It crossed the Tiber River near the Forum Boarium just downstream from Tiber Island.

name: Castle of Serravalle
desc: The Castle of Serravalle is a twelfth century castle located in Bosa, province of Oristano, Sardinia. It is connected with the Tuscan Malaspina family.

name: Villa di Tor Vergata, località Carcaricola
desc: An important villa that was excavated during the construction of the University of Rome 'Tor Vergata' in the 1970s, now reinterred. The Carcaricola villa begins in the middle of the second century B.C. and continues in use until the second century A.D.

name: Forum Augusti
desc: The Forum of Augustus at Rome was dedicated in 2 BCE, to the northeast of Julius Caesar's Forum. It contained the Temple of Mars Ultor.

name: Montagna di Gildone
desc: A series of noncontinuous fortifications are extant on Mount Gildone (elevation 902 meters) that enclose part of an upland plateau. A nucleus of 23 Samnite tombs was also discovered in the vicinity.

name: Filitosa
desc: Filitosa is a megalithic site in southern Corsica that was in use from the Neolithic period until Roman times. A number of menhirs have been discovered at the site.

name: Araghju
desc: A prehistoric site of the Torrean civilization in Corsica.

name: Megalithic walls at Telese Terme
desc: Megalithic, polygonal masonry walls atop Mount Pugliano are generally interpreted as Samnite fortifications associated with ancient Telesia.

name: Sant'Angelo Romano
desc: Sant'Angelo Romano is the area of the Castello Orsini-Cesi-Borghese dating from the late fourteenth century onward. The environs of Sant'Angelo Romano are dotted with ancient sites, in particular the ruins of Roman-period platform villas.

name: Casale Sinibalda
desc: The Casale Sinibalda is located on the western side of the Fosso Saina. Located to the north of the casale are the remains of a basis villae of the so-called fourth style, meaning it verges on opus quadratum.

name: Grotta di Seiano
desc: "Grotta di Seiano" or "Cave of Sejanus" refers to a subterranean tunnel dating to the early Roman Imperial period that was excavated into the volcanic tuff. It connected the area of what is now modern Bagnoli and the Campi Flegrei with the Gaiola Valley. Its construction is often attributed to Luciu

name: Lago di Castiglione
desc: An ancient caldera lake near Gabii (ancient name unknown) that has been drained and filled in modern times.

name: Su Nuraxi di Barumini
desc: A nuragic site in Barumini, Sardinia that was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

name: Villa dei Quattro Venti
desc: A monumental villa complex that is known as the “Villa dei Quattro Venti” is situated on a south-eastern offshoot of the Circeo promontory, approximately 100 meters southeast of the historic center of S. Felice Circeo.

name: Mausoleum of Lucilius Peto
desc: A tumulus-type tomb discovered in 1887 belonging to the military tribune M. Lucilius Paetus of the gens Lucilia.

name: Sep. Scipionum
desc: A family tomb of the Cornelii Scipiones near the Porta San Sebastiano in use from the third century B.C. to the first century A.D.

name: Roman amphitheater at Volsinii
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Volsinii dates to the second half of the first century A.D. It measures ca. 86 x 69 meters.

name: Villa di Faragola
desc: A Late Roman villa site near Ausculum.

name: Torre Scribla
desc: The remains of two towers of a Norman fortress near Spezzano Albanese.

name: Greolieres Roman Milestone
desc: A Roman milestone located in France, in the town of Gréolières in the Alpes-Maritimes department in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region. The inscription on the milestone honors the Roman emperor Caracalla and is dated to 213.

name: Wehringen villa rustica
desc: A series of villa rustica located along the road to Cambodunum.

name: Roman amphitheater at Burnum
desc: A Roman amphitheater associated with the legionary establishment of Burnum.

name: Roman amphitheater at Salona
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Salona.

name: Acquoria
desc: A basis villae near Tivoli in opus incertum on the river Aniene measuring 70 x 20 m. Two phases have been identified: second-first century B.C. and first century A.D.

name: Dragoncello
desc: Dragoncello is a modern district of Rome's metropolitan area where archaeological evidence for a series of late republican villas was uncovered. At least four in number, these villa rustica sites have evidence for domestic production.

name: Nymphaeum at Cupra Marittima
desc: The nymphaeum at Cupra Marittima was associated with a Roman villa.

name: Temple of Iuno Moneta at Signia
desc: The remains of the Temple of Iuno Moneta on the acropolis of Segni support the later (tenth century) church of St. Peter.

name: Roman amphitheater at Sutri
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Sutri likely dates to the reign of Augustus.

name: Tofet
desc: The Punic tofet at Sulcis.

name: Villa of Diomedes
desc: A suburban villa of Pompeii located outside the Herculaneum gate, the Villa of Diomedes was excavated between 1771 and 1774 and named after the tomb of Marcus Arrius Diomedes, which faces the entrance on the opposite side of the road.

name: Torvaianica
desc: A Roman villa near Pomezia discovered in 2006. The rich remains of the villa were uncovered along with at least 69 tombs.

name: Iovis Tifatinus
desc: A sanctuary sacred to Jupiter located on the western slopes of Tifata Mons (Monte Tifata).

name: Via Ostiensis viaduct
desc: A viaduct of the ancient Via Ostiensis that purportedly dates to the republican period.

name: Casa dell'Imperatrice di Russia
desc: Dwelling in Pompeii discovered in 1846, likely to have been the house of Inventus.

name: Casa di M. Pupius Rufus
desc: Property in Pompeii excavated in 1895.

name: Casa degli Archi
desc: Also known as the House of the Arches, excavated in Pompeii in 1954

desc: Doublet for https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/541774889

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 G3 Djebel Felfela

name: Giddaba (mountain)
desc: A mountain, probably Chetaibi area.

name: Giddibenses?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 G3 Giddibenses?

name: Hippo? Akra
desc: The modern Cap de Garde (Algeria) is probably the proper identification for "Hippo Akra", attested in ancient sources.

name: Hippo Regius
desc: Hippo Regius (modern Annaba in Algeria) was a colony established by Phoenicians from Tyre as early as the twelfth century BC.

name: Jemmapes
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 G3 Jemmapes

name: Paratianis
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 G3 Paratianis

name: Rusicade/Thapsus
desc: Rusicade/Thapsus was the port of Cirta and a Roman colonia, located at the mouth of the small river Thapsus.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 H2 Sulluctu?

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 G2 Tacatua

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 G4 Thabarbusis

name: Thapsus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 31 F3 Thapsus fl.

name: Zacca
