desc: The remains of the Sanctuary of Sol Indiges are located near Pomezia, Italy. The original phase of the sanctuary dates to the last quarter of the sixth century BCE, with subsequent rebuilding in the late fourth century BCE.

name: Necropoli fenicio-punica di Othoca
desc: The Punic necropolis at Othoca in Sardinia.

name: Unnamed road
desc: An unnamed road included in Barrington Atlas map 42

name: Unnamed road
desc: An unnamed road included in Barrington Atlas map 42

name: Vicus Tuscus
desc: The Vicus Tuscus was a street in the ancient city of Rome. It proceeded southwest from the Forum Romanum to the Forum Boarium, hugging the western flank of the Palatine Hill and passing through the Velabrum.

name: Salve necropolis
desc: A Chalcolithic necropolis with tumulus-type tombs.

name: Cavo degli Zucchi
desc: A Roman necropolis along the Via Amerina.

name: Winningen
desc: A Roman villa rustica.

name: Roman theater of Herculaneum
desc: The Roman theater of Herculaneum was constructed during the Augustan period. The theater was discovered first in 1709 while a well was being dug.

name: Horti Sallustiani
desc: The gardens of Sallust in Regio VI of the ancient city of Rome.

name: Odeon
desc: The Odeon (VIII, 7, 19) is a small roofed theater in Pompeii. It was built between 80 and 75 BC, under commission by two public officials, C. Quinctius Valgus and Marcus Porcius.

name: Samnite Palaestra
desc: The so-called "Samnite Palaestra" (VIII, 7, 29) lies behind the temple of Isis. A dedication in the Oscan language dates to the second half of the second century BC.

name: House of the Ceii
desc: A Roman house in Pompeii (I, 6, 15), also known as the House of L. Ceius Secundus. It is also referred to as the House of Fabia and Tyrannus.

name: House of the Lararium of Achilles
desc: The so-called "House of the Lararium of Achilles" (I ,6 ,4) lies on the Via dell'Abbondanza. Excavated in 1912 and 1913, it is also known as the "House of the Ilion Sanctuary".

name: House of the garden of Hercules
desc: The so-called "House of the Garden of Hercules" (II, 8, 6) is an example of an early "rowhouse" atrium building (third-second centuries BC) that was renovated in the first century BC.

name: Necropolis of Porta Nola
desc: An area with three tombs located outside the Porta di Nola.

name: Quarries at Molara (Grottaferrata)
desc: Stone quarries at Molara (Grottaferrata, Italy). Caves produced by quarry activity were also sites of paleochristian activity.

name: Isera
desc: A Roman villa located in the Alto-Adige region of Italy.

name: San Pietro di Cantoni Italic sanctuary
desc: An extra-urban Italic sanctuary located in the territory of ancient Saepinum.

name: Coriglia, Castel Viscardo
desc: An Etrusco-Roman settlement.

name: The "Auditorium site" at the Auditorium Parco della Musica (Rome)
desc: An Early Republican to Middle Imperial elite complex along the Via Flaminia in the outskirts of Rome.

name: Porta Vesuvio
desc: The so-called "Porta Vesuvio" was damaged in the earthquake of A.D. 62.

name: Castrum Perticae
desc: A fortified site of the later Byzantine period located at Finale Ligure.

name: Ninfeo della Lucchina
desc: A nymphaeum of the third century CE that was identified in 1990 and was likely one component of a larger villa complex in the north-west suburbium of imperial Rome.

name: Tenuta della Lucchina
desc: An archaeological area in the suburbium of ancient Rome, now in the quartiere Ottavia, with multi-phase evidence for tombs of the Etruscan culture, a segment of a Roman road, and evidence for Roman villas.

name: Terme Romane
desc: Roman baths of ancient Luceria

name: Bona Dea Subsaxana, Aedes
desc: An ancient sanctuary of the Aventine Hill in Rome.

name: Nuraghe Santa Barbara
desc: A nuragic site located on Monte Manai in Sardinia.

name: Champigneulles
desc: During archaeological excavations beginning in 1969, Champigneulles (Meurthe-et-Moselle, France) was revealed to be the site of a settled, productive landscape that included the remains of a Gallo-Roman villa. The entry authored by R. Billoret included in the Princeton Encyclopedia of Classical Site

name: So-called Temple of Saturn (Sezze)
desc: The ruins of an architectural complex in Sezze that acquired the misnomer of "Temple of Saturn" in the early modern period. The ruins are likely those of a platform villa and include visible remains in opus incertum and polygonal masonry of Lugli's "fourth" typological category, meaning the blocks a

name: Withdrawn: Basiluzzo
desc: Duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/452336

name: Greek theater, Monte Iato
desc: The Greek theater of Monte Iato was built in the fourth century BCE at a site already inhabited by the Elymians. The theater complex had a long life, used for the same purpose in the Roman period and repurposed as a domestic space by Arab occupiers in the seventh century.

name: Domus Liceo Cavour
desc: An urban domus of the Umbrii located beneath what is now the Liceo scientifico Camillo Cavour in central Rome.

name: Terme Erculee
desc: The largest known bath complex of Roman Mediolanum, built in the late third to early fourth centuries CE.

name: Roman baths, Carsulae
desc: Baths of the early imperial period at Carsulae.

name: Hermeskeil Roman Camp
desc: A late-Republican Roman army camp, located on the eastern outskirts of modern Hermeskeil in the German county of Trier-Saarburg (Rheinland-Pfalz). The site is not visible today.

name: Withdrawn: Tellaro Roman villa
desc: This place resource is a duplicate for http://pleiades.stoa.org/places/462122 and was erroneously created and published. It has been withdrawn and moved to errata.

name: Roman Amphitheater at Syracuse
desc: A Roman Amphitheater at Syracuse, Sicily, that was in use from the first through third centuries. The structure measured ca. 140 x 119 meters.

name: Temple of the Fabri Navales
desc: The Temple of the Ship Carpenters at Ostia dates to the later second century CE.

name: San Felice Roman villa
desc: The villa site is approximately 1 km south of the presumed ancient course of the Via Appia.

name: Ponte di Apollo, Punicum
desc: A Roman bridge.

name: Ponte Romano Di Largo Impero, Santa Marinella
desc: The remains of a Roman bridge located in the comune of Santa Marinella.

name: Villa romana di Acque Fresche a Civitavecchia
desc: Ruins of a Roman coastal villa located at Acque Fresche in the comune of Civitavecchia.

name: Rota
desc: What would become Medieval Rota was once a pagus of Etruscan Caere. Writing in PECS, Mario Torelli describes this an an important Archaic center in the area of Tolfa.

name: Tempio di Grasceta dei Cavallari
desc: The temple of Grasceta dei Cavallari is an Etrusco-Roman sanctuary located in the municipality of Tolfa. This sanctuary sits at the foot of Mount Mazza, above a pass near Tarquinia and Caere's ancient borders. The temple was small, with a rectangular platform and an octastyle arrangement.

name: Roman necropolis at Šempeter v Savinjski Dolini
desc: Šempeter v Savinjski Dolini lies along the former Roman road from Aquilea to Poetovio. The necropolis, dating to the first through third centuries A.D., may be associated with anicent Celeia.

name: Grotta Romanelli
desc: Grotta Romanelli (Lecce, Southern Italy) is a karstic cave in a coastal position that was occupied by humans beginning in the Middle Pleistocene period.

name: Arco Augusteo di Siracusa
desc: The remains of a Roman arch at Syracuse dated soon after the deduction of the Roman colony of 21 BCE.

name: Castelliere di Monte Orve
desc: A fortified pre-Roman settlement near lacus Plestinus.

name: Cabu Abbas
desc: A nuragic complex near Olbia, in the province of Sassari.

name: Nuraghe Cuccurada
desc: A nuragic complex composed of the nuraghe itself, a large wall, and a megalithic structure.

name: Nuraghe Zuras
desc: A later nuragic site, in use from the fourteenth to the twelfth centuries BC.

name: Casteddu de Fanaris
desc: A Late Bronze Age nuragic site.

name: Monte Catalfaro
desc: A rocky plateau located north-east of modern Mineo, overlooking Catania, that was inhabited from prehistoric times to the Middle Ages.

name: San Antonino di Perti
desc: An Early Byzantine fortified settlement in the Liguria Maritima.

name: House of the Ancient Hunt
desc: A well-appointed atrium house with Fourth Style wall paintings (VII,4,48).

name: Lupanar
desc: The Lupanar (or Lupanare Grande) (VII, 12, 18–20) is located east of the forum at the intersection of Vico del Lupanare and Vico del Balcone Pensile. It is the largest of Pompeii's brothels.

name: Doric temple (Pompei)
desc: A temple of the Doric order (VIII,7,30-34) located in the so-called Triangular Forum of Pompeii.

name: Fonteblanda
desc: A planned Etruscan settlement in the Albegna valley along the line of the Via Aurelia founded, perhaps, ca. 570 B.C. The site offers evidence for iron working.

name: Paduline villa
desc: A Roman villa located on the Bruna river that was in use from the third century B.C. until the fifth century A.D.

name: Horrea Vespasiani
desc: A warehouse complex on the Palatine slope adjacent to the Sacra Via.

name: Staranzano, Roman villa “Liberta Peticia”
desc: A Roman villa of the mid-first century A.D.

name: Lago dell'Accesa (lake)
desc: Lago dell'Accesa is a lake located in the Colline Metallifere.

name: Costedt Roman Cemetery
desc: A Roman cemetery was excavated in the late 20th century at modern Costedt in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

name: Marasà Sud
desc: An ancient sanctuary dedicated to Aphrodite located at Locri Epizephyrii.

name: Roman amphitheater of Asisium
desc: In the Porta Perlici of Assisi are the remains of a first century A.D. Roman amphitheater.

name: Arènes de Cimiez
desc: A Roman amphitheater of the second century that was enlarged during the course of the third, the so-called Arènes de Cimiez measures 67 by 56 meters.

name: Porta Venere
desc: One of the six gates of the Roman period fortification wall.

name: Murus Servii Tullii
desc: The Republican city wall of Rome.

name: Necropolis of Montessu
desc: The Necropolis of Montessu is located near Villaperuccio, Sardinia. It is the site of about 40 domus de Janas tombs and dates to the third millennium B.C.

name: Samnite necropolis, Saticula
desc: An area of Samnite tombs near ancient Saticula.

name: Tomba della Fibula d'oro
desc: A corridor-type tomb in the territory of Vetulonia dating to the Orientalizing period.

name: Solestà Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge over the Truentus river.

name: Porta Solestà
desc: The Porta Solestà is one of the gates of Ascoli Piceno.

name: Liverdun
desc: Excavations in and around Liverdun carried out in the 1960s revealed evidence for "fairly dense" habitation from prehistoric to Merovingian times. Notable archaeological features included a Gallo-Roman villa (destroyed in the third century A.D.) at the locality known as Rupt-Chaudron and a Merovingi

name: Ventimiglia Roman Theater
desc: A Roman theater at modern Ventimiglia in Italy, dating to the early second century CE.

name: Giulianello
desc: The site of a minor ancient center of southern Latium.

name: S. Gennaro
desc: A minor settlement.

name: Tomba dei Carri
desc: A mid-seventh century BCE tumulus at Populonia with a diameter of 28 meters; part of the San Cerbone necropolis.

name: Basilica of Lucus Feroniae
desc: The Basilica of Lucus Feroniae communicates with the forum and is linked to the apsidal space identified as the Augusteum.

name: Mausoleum Hadriani
desc: Mausoleum Hadriani (now Castel Sant'Angelo) located on the right bank of the Tiber River was an imperial mausoleum built by Hadrian between 134 and 139 CE. It continued as a tomb for subsequent emperors through to Caracalla, who died in 217 CE. By 401 the tomb had become a fortress with Honorius inc

name: Saepta Iulia
desc: An enclosure in the Campus Martius surrounded by porticoes built by Marcus Agrippa before ca. 26 BCE.

name: Poggio Capalbiaccio
desc: The hill known as Poggio Capalbiaccio is located in the Maremma plain.

name: Mura Greche
desc: The so-called "Mura Greche" are remains of the later third-century B.C. fortifications of Neapolis.

name: Roman theater of Neapolis
desc: The Roman theater of Neapolis is a structure of the first century B.C. that is built atop the pre-existing fourth century B.C. Greek theater.

name: Grotto of the Sibyl
desc: A cave discovered by Amedeo Maiuri in 1932 and connected in the historical tradition with the Cumaean Sibyl. The site features in the sixth book of Virgil's Aeneid.

name: *Via Curia
desc: A Roman road connecting Reate (Rieti) with Interamna Nahars (Terni).

name: Porta Piedimonte
desc: One of the four gates of the fortified castrum of Allifae. The fortifications are thought to date to the Late Republican period on the basis of building techniques.

name: Basilica Julia
desc: The Basilica Julia was built on the south side of the Forum Romanum in 46 B.C. on the site of the former Basilica Sempronia.

name: Castra Bonnensia
desc: The Roman legionary base at Bonna.

name: Temple of Augustus
desc: The Temple of Augustus in Pula is a Roman temple that dates to the time of Augustus. The tetrastyle Corinthian temple sites a high podium.

name: Roman theater at Augusta Bagiennorum
desc: The Roman theater at Augusta Bagiennorum

name: Porta Principalis Dextra, Tulln
desc: The Porta Principalis Dextra of the Roman fortification at Tulln, known in antiquity as Comagena.

name: Velletri-Stimmate
desc: At Velletri the remains of a Late Archaic sanctuary (ca. 530 BCE) were discovered beneath the church of the SS. Stimmate di S. Francesco. The site is often referred to as "Tempio delle Stimmate"; Cardinal Stefano Borgia discovered it in 1784. The architectural terracottas from the sanctuary are part

name: Abbazia San Claudio al Chienti
desc: The church of San Claudio al Chienti is a Romanesque church building located in the municipality of Corridonia in the Chienti valley. It was founded in the eleventh century.

name: Ponte delle Monache sanctuary
desc: A Campanian sanctuary located in the territory of Cales in Campania.

name: Pieve di San Pietro ad Mensulas
desc: A Romanesque church located in the Italian comune of Sinalunga (Siena). Saint Donatus of Arezzo may have founded the church in the fourth century.

name: Tabernae Veteres
desc: The so-called Tabernae Veteres were shops built in the valley of the Forum Romanum. The textual tradition assigns responsibility for this project to Lucius Tarquinius Priscus. The state owned the shops and leased them to tenants.

name: Belmonte Piceno
desc: The Italian comune of Belmonte Piceno is located in the province of Ascoli Piceno. The environs of this modern settlement have produced a range of archaeological evidence of Iron Age populations, including Latin inscriptions.

name: Tomb of Caecilia Agathia
desc: The Tomb of Caecilia Agathia in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis of Pompeii.

name: Tomb of Novia Amoena
desc: The Tomb of Novia Amoena C. L., Lucius Iacellius Virillio, Caius Novius Lupercus G.L., Cnaeus Turranius Primus, and Cornelia Quieta in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

name: Ponte della Mola di San Gregorio da Sassola
desc: A Roman aqueduct bridge that was part of the Aqua Anio Vetus. The remains of the bridge preserve a series of 22 arches stretching approximately 155 meters.

name: Unnamed naiskos tomb, Fondo Pacifico
desc: An unnamed naiskos tomb located in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

name: Torri in Sabina
desc: Torri in Sabina, a comune located in the Province of Rieti, Lazio, lies some 50 km north of Rome. It may succeed the Roman site of Forum Novum.

name: Roman tomb (Allifae)
desc: A tower-type Roman tomb located near Allifae.

name: Porta Napoli (Alife)
desc: One of the four gates of the fortified castrum of Allifae. The fortifications are thought to date to the Late Republican period on the basis of building techniques.

name: Porta Fiume (Alife)
desc: One of the four gates of the fortified castrum of Allifae. The fortifications are thought to date to the Late Republican period on the basis of building techniques.

name: Masseria Caronella
desc: A Roman villa rustica located near Taranto.

name: Via Flaminia militare
desc: The Via Flaminia Militare, or Via Flaminia Minor, was a road constructed by Gaius Flaminius in 187 BCE that connected Arretium and Bononia.

name: Capitolium of Cosa
desc: The so-called Capitolium temple of the Latin colony of Cosa.

name: Ponte Romano di Viale Roma
desc: The ruins of a Roman bridge located in the Viale Roma, Santa Marinella, Italy.

name: Villa Mattonara
desc: A coastal villa and associated necropolis.

name: Fosso Marangone
desc: A small stream that flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea. It now lies in the territory of the municipalities of Allumiere, Civitavecchia, and Santa Marinella and forms the geographical boundary between the latter two. The watercourse originates at Poggio Ombricolo.

name: Greppe S. Angelo necropolis
desc: A rock-cut necropolis of Caere that is noted as the findspot of the Sarpedon krater of the artist Euphronios.

name: Via Aemilia Scauri / Via Aurelia
desc: A Roman road connecting Rome to Placentia begun by Marcus Aemilius Scaurus in 115 B.C.

name: Acquapendente
desc: The modern Acquapendente was settled in pre-Roman times but is known historically from the Middle Ages onward.

name: Freilichtmuseum Römerbad
desc: A Roman bath complex located at Rottweil, Germany.

name: Sorbo Necropolis - Regolini-Galassi tomb
desc: The "Regolini-Galassi tomb" at Caere was discovered in 1836. The well-preserved tomb and its super-elite grave assemblage dates the tomb ca. 680/676-650 BCE. The objects in the assemblage are indicative of the so-called "Orientalizing" phenomenon in Etruria.

name: Area archeologica di Casarinaccio
desc: During archaeological excavations carried out between 1926 and 1934 in Casarinaccio (Ardea), a monumental complex was identified. This consisted of a late republican basilica (first century BCE) and the remains of an archaic temple dedicated to Venus.

name: Santa Maria Maggiore
desc: Santa Maria Maggiore is a major papal basilica as well as one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches of Rome. Located on the Mons Cispius, the origins of the church date to the reign of Pope Celestine I (422–432).

name: Unnamed Pass
desc: An unnamed pass in the Alpes Cottiae near Vesulus Mons

name: Roman theater, Atri
desc: The Roman theater of Atri.

name: Doss Penede (Nago-Torbole, TN)
desc: A pre-Roman and Roman complex at the foot of Castel Penede.

name: Gran Carro (Bolsena)
desc: A Proto-Villanovan settlement at Lake Bolsena. Discovered in 1959, this protohistoric settlement was situated on an island that is now submerged in the waters of the lake.

name: Regio V, Ostia Antica
desc: The fifth archaeological region of Ostia is bounded to the north by the Decumanus Maximus and extends southward.

name: Susa Roman amphitheater
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Segusio.

name: area Apollonis et Splenis et Calles
desc: A trio of toponyms included in the Regionary Catalogues for Regio I. The area Apollonis is otherwise unknown. Topographers debate the trustworthiness of the second and third toponyms.

name: Santa Maria in Tempulo
desc: A deconsecrated Christian church on the flank of Rome's Caelian Hill, Santa Maria in Tempulo is connected with the ancient tradition of the spring and grove of Camenae.

name: Regio II (Caelimontium)
desc: According to the Regionary Catalogues, Regio II contained 7 streets (vici), 7 shrines, 3,600 blocks of flats, 127 houses, 27 grain warehouses (horrea), 85 bath-houses; 65 cisterns; 15 bakeries/mills, and had a circumference of 12,200 paces. The region had 48 vicomagistri and 2 curators.

name: Castra Peregrina
desc: Located on the Caelian Hill, the Castra Peregrina housed Roman soldiers.

name: Cisterns of La Maalga
desc: A group of 15 large cisterns constructed during the late Punic era as a water supply for the city of Carthage.

name: Santuario di Fondo Patturelli
desc: A Samnite sanctuary of ancient Capua that was initially discovered in 1845. Active from the sixth century B.C. until the first century B.C., the Santuario di Fondo Patturelli is noted for its architectural terracotta as well as for the presence of a sacred maternal cult.

name: Samnite House
desc: The so-called "Samnite House" is a domus in Herculaneum that originally dates to the second century B.C., making it one of the oldest buildings discovered at the site.

name: Tomb of Cuccumella
desc: An archaic tumulus-type tomb at Vulci.

name: Tomb of the Dolphin
desc: An early Hellenistic painted tomb at Vulci.

name: Tino (island)
desc: An island in the Ligurian Sea designated as part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, Tino is connected with the life of the seventh-century AD Christian Saint Venerius.

name: Domus de Janas on Monte Crobu
desc: A prehistoric chamber tomb of the third millennium B.C. The 'Domus de Janas' tombs are typical of the Ozieri and Beaker cultures and are found chiefly on Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe la Prisciona
desc: A nuragic site in northeast Sardinia, it was occupied from the fourteenth until the ninth century BC. At its height, the complex covered approximately five hectares.

name: Lucus Furrinae
desc: The Lucus Furrinae or Syrian Sanctuary is a sanctuary site on the Janiculum Hill in Rome. The first known construction at the site took place during the late first century CE, and it remained in use until the mid-fourth century CE.

name: Roman cistern at Largo Zucchi
desc: The Roman cistern at Largo Zucchi dates to the second century A.D. It was discovered in 1957 and had an original diameter of ca. 6.90 meters.

name: Arch of Septimius Severus
desc: The Arch of Septimius Severus is situated at the northwest corner of the Forum Romanum. It was dedicated in A.D. 203 and serves to commemorate the Parthian victories of Emperor Septimius Severus and his two sons against the Parthians (194/195 and 197–199).

name: Roman amphitheater at Noviodunum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Noviodunum was only discovered in 1996 and likely dates to the second century A.D. The arena measures ca. 50 x 36 meters.

name: Square Castan at Besançon
desc: A square containing architectural remains of the Roman city.

name: Theater at Heraclea Minoa
desc: The Theater at Heraclea Minoa dates to the late fourth century B.C.

name: Pula Arena (Roman amphitheater)
desc: The Pula Arena is a Roman amphitheater dating to the first century.

name: Roman aqueduct
desc: The Roman aqueduct of San Giovanni.

name: Temple of Iuno Sospita, Lanuvium
desc: A celebrated cult-place sacred to Iuno Sospita that retained its sacred significance even after a cult to the same divinity was dedicated in the Forum Holitorium in Rome in 194 BCE.

name: House of the Chaste Lovers
desc: The so-called House of the Chaste Lovers at Pompeii is located on the north side of the Via dell'Abbondanza. The site has been the subject of ongoing archaeological excavation since 1987. It is located in insula 12 of Regio IX. It adjoins the so-called House of the Painters at Work which lies to the

name: Archaeological Border complex of Hedeby and the Danevirke
desc: Hedeby was a trading center located between the Frankish Empire and the Danish Kingdom. The Danevirke fortifications separated the Jutland Peninsula from the European mainland.

name: Abbazia di San Vincenzo al Volturno
desc: An historic Benedictine monastery located in the Province of Isernia, near the source of the river Volturno.

name: Mira Lanza
desc: The remains of an Archaic period structure at Mira Lanza, located in Via Luigi Pierantoni.

name: Torcularium villa
desc: A Roman villa of the early second century BCE, constructed in opus incertum and so named because of the presence of a torcularium.

name: Torre del Giudizio
desc: Torre del Giudizio is a Medieval tower built atop a pre-existing Roman site located near the fluvial harbor of vicus Alexandrini.

name: Via Portuensis?
desc: The Via Portuensis is an ancient Roman road that connected Rome and Portus. It proceeded along the right bank of the Tiber river, starting from the Pons Aemilius. In the first part of its course it is identical to the Via Campana.

name: Izola
desc: The remains of a Roman villa maritima.

name: Ager Romanus
desc: The rural hinterland of the ancient city of Rome.

name: Temple G at Selinus
desc: Remains of an octastyle Doric temple begun in the sixth century B.C. but left unfinished.

name: Catacomb of Ponziano
desc: A Paleochristian catacomb at the second mile of the Via Portuensis. The catacomb is noted for containing the original tombs of Pope Anastasius I and his son, Pope Innocent I.

name: Cave di Fosso del Drago
desc: A tuff quarry along the line of the via Tiberina.

name: Via Triumphalis
desc: A road running from the Pons Neronianus toward Monte Mario, eventually joining the Via Clodia some 7 miles from Rome.

name: Tomba di Fadilla
desc: A Roman tomb on the Via Flaminia at Grottarossa that is associated with Annia Aurelia Fadilla, the daughter of the emperor Marcus Aurelius.

name: Roman theater at Grumentum
desc: The Roman theater at Grumentum dates to the Julio-Claudian period.

name: Villa of Lucullus (Neaoplis)
desc: A villa dating to the first century BCE that is associated with Lucius Licinius Lucullus.

name: Pauciuri
desc: An archaeological site located near Malvito in southern Italy, where excavation has revealed a portion of a Roman nucleus of habitation that includes domestic spaces and a bath complex.

name: Pons Aelius
desc: The Pons Aelius or Aelian Bridge (now Ponte Sant'Angelo) was completed by Hadrian in AD 134 to span the Tiber opposite the new mausoleum of the emperor.

name: S'Imbalconadu Roman villa
desc: A multi-phase rustic structure (fattoria) located near Olbia, Sardinia. The quadrangular structure consists of twenty-some rooms arranged around a central courtyard; the built surface covers ca 1,000 square meters.

name: Casa delle Grazie
desc: Dwelling in Pompeii excavated in 1817, 1838.

name: Casa di Diana I
desc: Private dwelling in Pompeii, first excavated in 1763-4.

name: Temple of Hera I (the "Basilica")
desc: An Archaic Doric temple probably dedicated to Hera in the central urban sanctuary of Paestum/Poseidonia.

name: Terrace and altar of M. Nonius Balbus
desc: Marcus Nonius Balbus of Nuceria was an important civic patron of Herculaneum. Balbus was a praetor and proconsul of Crete and Cyrene and served as tribune of the plebs in 32 B.C. This architectural complex near the Suburban Baths included the terrace as well as an honorific statue and altar.

name: Roman theater at Ferentium
desc: The Roman theater at Ferentium dates to the early Imperial period.

name: Tomb of P. Numisius Ligus
desc: A large ara type tomb located outside the Porta di Boiano.

name: Roman theater at Ostia
desc: The Roman theater at Ostia was built under the patronage of Marcus Agrippa.

name: Roman theater at Iguvium
desc: The Roman theater at Iguvium is located within the Guastuglia archaeological area and dates to the late republican period. Sear (2004) notes several important architectural innovations evident in the theater's construction.

name: Villa di Nerone
desc: Nero built a villa and a port at Antium. The villa was subsequently expanded under Domitian and other later emperors.

name: Roman amphitheater at Teate
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Teate dates to the first century.

name: Basilica di Sant'Anastasia al Palatino
desc: The Basilica of Sant'Anastasia al Palatino was founded ca. 325 CE on the slopes of the Palatine. It is now a minor basilica of the Roman Catholic church. It is the national church for the Peruvian community of Rome and the Indian community of the Syro-Malabar rite. The original basilica was adjacent

name: Roman amphitheater at Vindonissa
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Vindonissa was built under the reign of Tiberius.

name: Roman theater at Ferentinum
desc: The Roman theater at Ferentinum is today poorly preserved.

name: Ostia Synagogue
desc: The ancient synagogue located in Ostia Antica is one of the oldest known synagogues in the world. The structure's earliest phase dates to the reign of Claudius and it continued in use until the fifth century.

name: Gallo-Roman theater at Dalheim
desc: The Gallo-Roman theater at Dalheim.

name: Gallo-Roman vicus at Dalheim
desc: Remains of the Roman-era settlement at Dalheim.

name: Roman amphitheater at Falerio Picenus
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Falerio Picenus dates to the first century A.D.

name: Roman theater at Falerio Picenus
desc: The Roman theater at Falerio Picenus was completed during the reign of Tiberius.

name: Roman amphitheater at Tusculum
desc: Today, the Roman amphitheater at Tusculum is poorly preserved. These ruins have never been systematically investigated.

name: Roman theater at Teate
desc: The Roman theater at Teate measures 80 meters in diameter.

name: Porta Collina
desc: The Porta Collina was a gate in Rome's Servian Wall located on the Quirinal Hill. At the Porta Collina the Via Salaria and the Via Nomentana divided. Some remains of the gate were identified in 1872 on the Via Venti Settembre beneath the Italian Ministry of Finance.

name: Praedia Galbana
desc: A tract of suburban land located southwest of the Aventine Hill that would come to be the location of the Horrea Galbae.

name: Caupona and Domus of L. Vetutius Placidus and Ascula
desc: A thermopolium with a marble counter (I.8.8), connected to a private house (I.8.9) in Regio I, insula 8 in Pompeii. The walls of the house show extensive decoration in the Third style.

name: House of the Four Styles
desc: The House of the Four Styles or Casa dei Quattro Stili (I.8.17) is noted for having examples of all four style of Pompeian wall paintings.

name: Roman cistern
desc: A Roman cistern at the Villa Gordiani.

name: Anaktoron at Pantalika
desc: The Anaktoron is an enigmatic megalithic building associated with the prehistoric Sicilian settlement of Pantalica; its polygonal blocks may date to the 12-11th c. B.C., but the current form of the building seems to be the result of Byzantine reconstruction.

name: Necropolis of Pantalica
desc: A large, rock-cut necropolis of over 5,000 tombs dating from the thirteenth to the seventh centuries BC.

name: Monte Inici
desc: A mountain of Sicily located just south of the Golfo di Castellammare.

name: Porta Palatina
desc: A surviving turreted gateway of the Roman circuit wall of Augusta Taurinorum.

name: Nuraghe Mannu, Olmedo
desc: A single-tower nuraghe built in the later second millennium B.C.

name: Castelfusano Paleochristian basilica
desc: Situated along the via Severiana are the remains of an anonymous Paleochristian basilica that was in use between the second and the seventh centuries AD.

name: Castel Fiorentino
desc: The castle was the site of the Holy Emperor Frederick II's death in 1250.

name: Castelvecchio di San Gimignano
desc: The site of Castelvecchio di San Gimignano likely had sacred significance in the first millennium BCE. The area was occupied in the late sixth to early seventh centuries CE, as it provided a location to control movement between southern Tuscany and Piedmont. The site was fortified in the twelfth cen

name: San Manno hypogeum
desc: An Etruscan hypogeum tomb dating either to the third or the second century BCE. The tomb is located beneath the medieval church of San Manno in the comune of Perugia.

name: Cappella di Sant'Antonino (Finale Ligure)
desc: A twelfth-century chapel located near the Castrum Perticae. The site is located in the municipal territory of modern Finale Ligure in Italy's Ligurian Alps.

name: Stele Ponte di Apollo
desc: A stele carrying a Latin inscription that dates to the Severan period (ca. 206 CE) recording the restoration of the bridge that had been destroyed by the "fury of the sea".

name: Castellaccio Europarco
desc: A villa and a number of burials located along the Via Laurentina, dating from the fourth century BC to the second century AD.

name: Temple of Castor and Pollux (Rome)
desc: Located at the southeast corner of the Forum Romanum, the aedes Castoris is a temple of ancient Rome vowed by the dictator Postumius in 499 BCE.

name: Clivus Victoriae
desc: The Clivus Victoriae was a steep street located at or near the southwest corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome.

name: Necropolis of Prato Rosello
desc: An Etruscan necropolis with a number of tumulus-type tombs dating between the eighth and sixth centuries BC.

name: Etruscan necropolis of Dometaia
desc: An Etruscan necropolis dating to the sixth century B.C.

name: Nuraghe Nuraddeo
desc: A Middle Bronze Age nuragic site with a central tower standing ca. 14 m. tall near Suni, Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Sant'Imbenia
desc: A nuragic complex near Alghero, Sardinia, composed of a main, central tower flanked by two minor towers and a bastion, and surrounded by a village. The complex dates from the Middle Bronze Age onwards.

name: Forum of Nerva
desc: A forum complex at Rome begun under Domitian but completed under Nerva and dedicated in A.D. 97. Sometimes referred to as the Forum Transitorium, the complex was the next to last of the imperial fora at Rome.

name: Negrar Roman Villa
desc: Remains of a Roman villa with mosaic pavements located near the modern comune of Negrar di Valpolicella were first discovered in 1922.

name: Accu Sa Pira Nuraghe
desc: A monopteral nuraghe located near Quartu Sant'Elena.

name: Nuraghe Gibe Truttiri
desc: A nuraghe located near the beach of Cala Marina.

name: Colle della Coedra
desc: A small hill in the Alban Hills that was the site of a protourban settlement of Latium covering some 265 square meters.

name: Villa di Rufione
desc: The Villa di Rufione is a villa rustica located along the via Flaminia Vetus, between the hamlets of Montecchio and Bastardo in località Toccioli. The site begins its life in the late republican period and continues in use until the fourth century CE.

name: Terme Romane con Mosaici
desc: These Roman baths in modern Bevagna, Italy, date to the second century CE and were rediscovered in 1891.

name: Domus of Vespasia Polla
desc: A Roman domus traditionally associated with Vespasia Polla, mother of the emperor Vespasian.

name: Roman arch at Spoletium
desc: The so-called "Arch of Drusus and Germanicus" at Spoleto.

name: Tigellio Roman villa
desc: An elite villa dated to the first century B.C.

name: Roman theater at Tergeste
desc: The Roman theater at Tergeste dates to the late first century A.D.

name: Capo la Timpa
desc: Capo la Timpa is an archaeological site in Maratea, Italy, with evidence for human settlement beginning in the Neolithic period.

name: Temple of Herakles, Cora
desc: The Temple of Herakles at Cora was built during the 80s B.C. The temple is tetrastyle in its plan and built following the Etrusco-Italic temple tradition.

name: Santa Maria in Monterone
desc: Santa Maria in Monterone is a Catholic church located in Rome's Sant'Eustachio neighborhood. The church gives its name to the street on which it is located. The church building is situated on first-century BCE ruins in the area of the artificial basin known as the stagnum Agrippae. The present edifi

name: tribus Stellatina
desc: The tribus Stellatina was a later rural tribe of ancient Rome which was established in 387 B.C.

name: tribus Teretina
desc: Established in 299 B.C., the tribus Teretina was one of the later rural tribes of ancient Rome.

name: Chiesa di Sant'Ilario a Port' Aurea
desc: A sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-century Christian church located near the Port'Aurea of Benevento was built during the Longobard period. The church was built atop Imperial remains and was an apsidal hall.

name: Arco del Sacramento
desc: A Roman arch of the second century A.D. that faced on to the forum of Beneventum.

name: La Muculufa (Butera)
desc: An Early Bronze Age village in Sicily.

name: Casa della Regina Carolina
desc: A domus at Pompeii partially excavated in the nineteenth century.

name: Castle of Bominaco
desc: A castle at Bominaco in Italy that originally dates to the twelfth century.

name: Ponte Sereno
desc: A bridge near Ferentinum (modern Ferentino in Italy) that is traditionally dated to A.D. 260 or after. A substructure in polygonal masonry supports the bridge.

name: Necropolis of Porta Vesuvio
desc: A necropolis of Pompeii located outside the so-called "Porta Vesuvio".

name: Castellum aquae
desc: A building in Pompeii serving as the distribution point of water originating from the Acquedotto Serino, Claudio or Augusteo. The structure is also referred to as Castellum Divisorium.

name: Central Baths
desc: A bath complex (IX, 4, 5-18) located at the intersection of the Via Stabiana and Via di Nola that was built following the earthquake of AD 62.

name: Triangular Forum
desc: A triangular plaza with an Ionic propylon that was surrounded by 95 Doric columns. A Doric order temple sits in the forum.

name: Circus Gaii et Neronis
desc: Circus Gaii et Neronis was originally built as a private racecourse for the emperor Caius. In the fourth century A.D., the north side of the circus was destroyed in order to make room for the first basilica of St. Peter.

name: Tomba dei Leoni Ruggenti
desc: The so-called "Tomb of the Roaring Lions" at Veii is considered to be among the earliest, if not the earliest, known example of a painted tomb in Etruria. It is dated ca. 700-690 BCE.

name: Monte Papalucio
desc: The sanctuary of Monte Papalucio was an important Messapian sanctuary. It is located on the mountain of the same name in the territory of Oria in the province of Brindisi. The deities Demeter and Persephone were venerated in this cave sanctuary.

name: Sanctuary of Iuno Gabina
desc: The Sanctuary of Iuno Gabina at Gabii.

name: Via delle Piagge
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Via delle Piagge

name: Vicus Alexandri
desc: A settlement at the third milestone of the Via Ostiensis.

name: Vicus Augustanus Laurentium?
desc: The Vicus Augustanus Laurentium is an ancient settlement in coastal Latium located between the shore and the Via Severiana. The site was first described by Rodolfo Lanciani in 1903. The British School at Rome carried out excavations in the 1980s.

name: Le Vignacce
desc: A Roman villa located on via Lemonia in Rome's suburbium attributed to Quintus Servilius Pudens.

name: Villa Aldobrandini
desc: The Villa Aldobrandini is located on the outskirts of Frascati. The current villa of the site was built in 1550 by a Vatican prelate named Alessandro Rufini. Subsequently, Pope Clement VIII gave the villa to his nephew Cardinal Pietro Aldobrandini in 1598. The Papal villa and gardens occupy the site

name: Villa di Vibio Varo
desc: The so-called Villa of Vibius Varus is located south of the Villa Adriana at Tivoli. The site has three architectural phases stretching from the first century BCE to the fourth century CE

name: Villa Domitiani
desc: Villa Domitiani, a large imperial villa near the Alban Lake, now the site of the Papal retreat at Castel Gandolfo.

name: Villa Esmeade
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Villa Esmeade

name: Villa Hadriani
desc: The Villa of Hadrian (Villa Adriana in Italian) is a sprawling archaeological complex at Tivoli, Italy. The villa complex was designed and used by the emperor Hadrian in the second century A.D.

name: Villa Lucidi
desc: A large villa complex that was built sometime in the first century B.C.E. and remained in use until at least the third century C.E.

name: Villa Maxentii
desc: A complex on the Via Appia constructed by Maxentius in the early fourth century A.D.

name: Villa Muti
desc: The Villa Muti in Grottaferrata occupies, at least in part, the site of a Roman republican villa built on a series of terraces and likely dating to the third and second centuries B.C. Lanciani excavated a series of rooms at the site. The site also had an early to mid-Imperial phase that included ela

name: Villa Neronis
desc: The Villa Neronis was a rural villa of the emperor Nero, likely built early in his reign (perhaps before AD 60).

name: Villa Pamphili
desc: The church of San Pancrazio was founded in the sixth century A.D. by Pope Symmachus. It stands beyond the Porta San Pancrazio on the Ianiculum. Below the church is a massive catacomb referred to as S. Pancrazio or Ottavilla.

name: Villa Torlonia
desc: A Jewish catacomb discovered in 1919 on the grounds of the Villa Torlonia park in Rome.

name: Villa Torlonia
desc: The extant Villa Torlonia occupies the site of an ancient Roman villa, although, as Marzano notes, the interpretation of this villa and its Roman antecedents has been (and continues) to be confused in scholarship, particularly with reference to villas associated with Lucullus.

name: Villamagna
desc: A large imperial Roman villa known from letters of Marcus Aurelius.

name: Aqua Alexandrina
desc: The Aqua Alexandrina was an ancient Roman aqueduct that carried water 22.4 km from Pantano Borghese to the Baths of Alexander in the Campus Martius. It was in use from the third to the eighth century AD.

name: Aqua Alsietina
desc: The Aqua Alsietina was an aqueduct built by Augustus that drew water from the lacus Alsietinus (Lago di Martignano) and conducted it to Rome.

name: Aqua Anio Novus
desc: Aqua Anio Novus is an ancient aqueduct supplying the city of Rome. Begun by Caius in A.D. 38, it was completed and dedicated by Claudius in A.D. 52.

name: Aqua Anio Vetus
desc: Aqua Anio Vetus, an aqueduct serving Rome and built originally during the third century BC. The Anio Vetus carried water to Rome from the Aniene near Vicovaro.

name: Aqua Antoniniana
desc: The Aqua Antoniniana was a branch of the Aqua Marcia that carried water to the Baths of Caracalla.

name: Aqua Appia
desc: The earliest of Rome's aqueducts, the Aqua Appia was constructed in 312 BC by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus. The aqueduct runs a course of 16.4 km, entering Rome at the Porta Maggiore. Frontinus estimated the daily volume at 75,537 cubic meters.

name: Aqua Claudia
desc: The Aqua Claudia was one of the four great aqueducts of the ancient city of Rome. It was begun by Caius in A.D. 38 and completed by Claudius in A.D. 52.

name: Aqua Iulia
desc: A Roman aqueduct built by Marcus Agrippa in 33 BC and expanded by Augustus between 11 and 4 BC.

name: Aqua Marcia
desc: The Aqua Marcia was the longest of Rome's 11 aqueducts.

name: Aqua Tepula
desc: The Aqua Tepula was an aqueduct built in 126 BC by the censors G. Servilius Caepio and L. Cassius Longinus.

name: Aqua Traiana
desc: The Aqua Traiana was an aqueduct built by Trajan and inaugurated in AD 109.

name: Aqua Virgo
desc: The Aqua Virgo was one of the 11 aqueducts supplying the city of Rome and was completed by Marcus Agrippa in 19 BC. The aqueduct was later revitalized by Pope Adrian I in the eighth century.

desc: A now lost unnamed aqueduct supplying Gabii in Latium that was built during the principate of Hadrian.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 unnamed bridge (Ad Turres)

name: Pons Aemilius
desc: The Pons Aemilius was the first stone bridge built across the Tiber River at Rome (241 B.C.). Its remains are known today as the 'Ponte Rotto'.

name: Emissarium of Lake Nemi
desc: An artificial canal originally dating to the fourth century BCE that was built by the inhabitants of Ariccia in order to regulate the waters of Lake Nemi.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D4 unnamed canal group (SW Forum Appii)

desc: unnamed canal group (NW Pomptinae Paludes)

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 no. 2 (bridge over R. Quartaccio)

name: Roman bridge at Palidoro
desc: An ancient Roman bridge along the Via Aurelia.

desc: A feature included on Barrington Atlas map 43 B2 no. 4, an unnamed bridge that crosses the river Arrone.

desc: A villa with beginnings in the early Republican period, continuing in use to the middle Imperial period.

name: Unnamed bridge in the Piazza Eugenio Biffi
desc: The remains of an ancient Roman bridge in the present Piazza Eugenio Biffi in Rome. This bridge is thought to have spanned the Almo river.

desc: M. Cristofani describes terracotta antefixes discovered at Tre Fontane, in the general location of the abbey of the same name. These antefixes form part of a set of evidence relevant to a discussion of the functioning of regional coroplastic workshops in central Italy in the late archaic period. The

name: Ponte di Vallerano
desc: The Ponte di Vallerano is a second-century Roman bridge that carried the via Ostiensis across the fosso di Vallerano.

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 no. 14 (bridge at Mezzocamino)

name: Ponte di Malafede
desc: A Roman bridge that is no longer extant. Quilici notes that the bridge was destroyed both by the Second World War and by urbanization that followed in the post-war period. Blake publishes a photo of E. B. van Deman and indicates that the bridge was built in peperino and of "indeterminate date". She

name: Ponte Ladrone
desc: The so-called Ponte Ladrone was a Roman bridge of the Via Ostiensis located at Acilia. According to L. Quilici, its remaining material vestiges were buried in 1982 by infrastructure works.

name: Unnamed tuff quarry
desc: A tuff quarry located at Castelporziano, to the east of Ostia Antica.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C1 no. 18 (tomb near Nomentum)

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 19 (villa near S. Sinforosa)

name: Cemetery of Gordianus, Epimachus, Apronianus
desc: A burial ground for the the Christian martyrs Gordianus, Epimachus, and Apronianus at the seventh mile of the Via Latina.

name: Parco delle Tombe di via Latina
desc: A cluster of Roman Imperial tombs along the Via Latina excavated in the nineteenth century.

name: Villa del Torraccio, Torrenova
desc: The Forma Italiae notes the presence of drainage channels, foundations, and a cistern that are taken to be indicative of a Roman villa in the locale known today as Torrenova in the eastern portion of modern Rome.

name: Quarries at Aquae Albulae
desc: The quarries at Aquae Albulae were a source of travertine.

name: Bridge over Fosso di Acqua Rossa
desc: The remains of a Roman bridge that once carried a road over the Fosso di Acqua Rossa. Ward-Perkins posits a date of the second or first century BCE based on comparanda in the vicinity.

name: Ponte Ceccara
desc: The Ponte Ceccara, also referred to as the ponte di Terra, is a Republican period bridge located on the fosso di Passerano along the Via Praenestina. It is located within the modern comune of Zagarolo, some 30.5 km southeast of the center of Rome.

name: Ponte dell’Acqua Nera
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 38 (bridge (Ponte dell’Acqua Nera))

name: Ponte Amato
desc: The bridge known as Ponte Amato carries the Via Praenestina near Gallicano nel Lazio.

name: Colle Rasto Settlement
desc: A site to the west of modern Praeneste in Italy where surface material, remains of structures, and graves were discovered in the 19th century. These finds provide evidence for a settlement possibly dating to as early as the fifth or fourth century BCE but with likely occupation throughout the subseq

name: Roman villa near Praeneste
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 no. 41 (villa near Praeneste)

name: Villas on Via Castrimeniense
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 no. 43 (villas on Via Castrimeniense)

name: Vigna Spinabella
desc: A Roman villa located at Vigna Spinabella and included in the Barrington Atlas. In the Barrington Atlas directory, this place is included as a "Numbered Feature" and not given a specific title. It is assigned number 44 on BAtlas map 43 C2.

name: So-called Villa on the Lake
desc: Lugli describes the remains of a sumptuous, porticoed villa in the Doric order facing onto the Alban lake. Marzano clarifies Lugli's earlier summary of the site, which was in turn based on observations made in 1912. The remains of the villa include a 200-m long portico on two levels. About 260 m fro

name: Roman Villa at Lago di Nemi
desc: A Roman Villa on the shores of Lago di Nemi.

name: So-Called Tomb of Clodius
desc: The so-called Tomb of Clodius along the Via Appia near Castel Gandolfo.

name: Unnamed temple near Solforata
desc: An ancient temple located near Solforata, between Lavinium and the Alban Lake in modern Italy.

name: Villas at Castelporziano
desc: Since antiquity, the 6,000-ha estate at Castelporziano has been an elite seaside compound. Where a modern pleasure villa for the Italian president now sits are remains of Roman villas on the Laurentine shore; these remains have been the object of continued study since 1983.

name: Unnamed Roman villa
desc: A villa rustica located near the coast, southwest of Ardea.

desc: The platform, including cryptoporticus, of a republican period villa originally dating to the first century B.C. with evidence for second century A.D. renovations.

desc: The Salinae Romanae at Ostia were said to have been established by Ancus Marcius.

name: Abella
desc: Abella was an ancient settlement of Campania of Samnite origin.

name: Abellinum
desc: Abellinum was a settlement of the Hirpini in Campania.

name: Acerrae
desc: Acerrae was an ancient Oscan city of Campania, perhaps originally named Akeru. The Romans granted it civitas sine suffragio in 332 BC.

name: Acherusia Palus
desc: Acherusia Palus, now known as Lago del Fusaro or Lake Fusaro, is a lake located in the Italian community of Bacoli. The acropolis of Cumae is about 1.5 km from the lakeshore. The lake itself is separated from the sea by a narrow strip of land. The lake has also been noted since antiquity for the pre

name: Acqua Claudia
desc: A Roman villa at Anguillara Sabazia that may have been built in order to take advantage of mineral springs. The villa dates to the Late Republican period but has only been partially excavated. A large hemicycle with ambulatio is extant; this feature may have been coordinated with the villa's garden.

name: Ad Flexum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Ad Flexum

name: Ad Medias
desc: Ad Medias was a mutatio on the ancient Via Appia. It was located at the halfway point of the so-called Decennovium.

desc: Ad Turres Albas lay on the Via Severiana, midway between Circeii and Astura.

desc: Aenaria/Pithekoussai Ins. (modern Ischia) is a volcanic island located in the northern part of the Bay of Naples.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Afragola

name: Agellum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Agellum

name: Agnone
desc: Agnone is a comune in the Italian province of Isernia, in the Molise region. It lies about 53 km (33 miles) northwest of Campobasso. An ancient center of Oscan-Samnite culture, Agnone is known particularly as the namesake of the third-century BCE "Agnone tablet" that was discovered at Fonte di Romit

name: Al(l)ifae
desc: An ancient town of either Oscan or Samnite origin situated in the Volturno river valley.

name: Aletrium
desc: A Hernican hill town that formed part of a sixth-century B.C. defensive league against Volscian and Samnite aggression and allied itself to Tarquinius Superbus. Rome eventually took Aletrium in 306 B.C.; by the first century B.C., the town was a Roman municipium.

name: Alfaterni
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Alfaterni

name: Alfedena
desc: A Samnite settlement occupying a strategic location in the valley of the Sangro river.

name: Amalfitana Civitas
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Amalfitana Civitas

name: Amasenus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 Amasenus fl.

name: Amplero
desc: The toponym Amplero refers to an archaeological area located to the northeast of Collelongo (L'Aquila) in Italy. The Institute of Archaeology at the University of Pisa conducted fieldwork at the site in 1969-1971.

name: Amyclanus Sinus
desc: Amyclanus Sinus, the modern Gulf of Gaeta, is an open body of water along the central-western coast of the Italian peninsula. To the north, Cape Circeo bounds the gulf, while to the south it is bounded by the island of Ischia and the Gulf of Naples. It extends westward to the Pontine Islands.

name: Angitiae Lucus
desc: Angitiae Lucus refers to the grove of Angitia, a divine figure of the Marsi tribe.

name: Antinum
desc: A town of the Marsi in the valley of the Liris River.

name: Apollo et Nymphae Nitrodes (temple)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E4 Apollo et Nymphae Nitrodes, T.

name: Aquae Caeretanae
desc: Therapeutic springs located near Caere.

name: Aquae Sinuessanae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Aquae Sinuessanae

name: Aquae Vescinae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Aquae Vescinae

name: Aquinum
desc: Aquinum was a municipium by the time of Cicero. It was thought to be the place of birth for the satirist Juvenal and the emperor Pescennius Niger.

name: Arpinum
desc: An ancient center that originated as early as the seventh century B.C., which became a civitas sine suffragio in 305 B.C. Arpinum was the birthplace of Caius Marius and Marcus Tullius Cicero.

name: Arx Fregellana
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Arx Fregellana

name: Astura
desc: Astura was once a coastal island of Latium and is now a small peninsula at the southeastern edge of the Bay of Antium.

name: Atella (Campania)
desc: A city of Campania located between Capua and Neapolis.

name: Atessa/Porcari Sanctuary
desc: A small Italic sanctuary, possibly of Vejovis, in a modern area known then as Passo Porcari (between Monte Marcone and Saletti) near Atessa in Italy's Chieti province. It was excavated in the 1970s and is memorialized by the modern street name "Via Veiove". Rescue excavations of purportedly medieval

name: Atina
desc: Atina was a Volscian settlement located at the source of the river Melpis. Atina was located on the via Latina between Casinum and Sora.

name: Aufidena
desc: A probable Samnite center, the Romans captured Aufidena in 298 BC. It only became a municipium after 49 B.C.

name: Aurunci
desc: The Aurunci were an Italic tribe of south Italy. Their territory was incorporated into the Roman territory in the fourth century B.C.

name: Avernus (lake)
desc: A volcanic crater lake located in the Phlegraean Fields, Lake Avernus served a major ritual role for ancient Romans and Greeks as they viewed it as an entrance to Hades.

name: Aversa
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Aversa

name: Baiae
desc: A Roman seaside community on the Bay of Naples that included thermal springs.

name: Baianus Sinus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Baianus Sinus

name: Bauli
desc: Bauli (near modern Bacoli) was an ancient settlement of the Campi Phlegraei.

name: Beneventum/Maleventum
desc: Beneventum/Maleventum (modern Benevento) was an ancient city of Campania of Samnite origin.

name: Boscoreale
desc: A settled area of Campania, especially well known for the Roman country villas of the first century BCE, which were destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE.

name: Boscotrecase
desc: Located on the southern slopes of Vesuvius, Boscotrecase is a Campanian site destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79. Numerous opulent villas are known in the area by way of archaeological exploration.

name: Bovianum
desc: Bovianum was a Samnite center and the capital of the Pentri tribe. It received Roman municipium status ca. 87 B.C. By the late first century A.D., it was occupied by veterans of Legio XI and known as "colonia Bovianum Undecumanorum".

name: Buca
desc: Buca was an ancient settlement of the Frentani.

name: Caecubus Ager
desc: A tract of Latium that bordered the Gulf of Amyclae, lying in the territory of Fundi.

name: Caedicius? Campus
desc: Caedicius Campus is a toponym that ancient sources place in the territory of the Vestini. Pliny praises the high-quality cheese that was produced there.

name: Caiatia
desc: A Samnite town that eventually became a Roman municipium of the tribus Falerna ca. 89 B.C.

name: Caieta
desc: Caieta was a town of ancient Latium located on the Tyrrhenian Sea coast between Tarracina and Formiae.

name: Caieta Pr.
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Caieta Pr.

name: Callifae?
desc: A city of the Samnites that, according to Livy, was captured by the Romans in Republican times. Probably at or in the vicinity of modern Roccavecchia di Pratella in Italy.

name: Calatia
desc: Calatia was an ancient city of Campania located along the Via Appia between Capua and Beneventum.

name: Cales (Campania)
desc: Cales was an ancient city of Campania of Ausonian origins. The Romans captured the town in 335 B.C. and established a colony there.

name: Calor (river)
desc: A river of Samnium and a major tributary of the Volturno river.

name: Campania
desc: Campania was a region of southern Italy.

name: Campanus Ager
desc: The Campanus Ager was the region around Capua that the Romans confiscated in 211 B.C. during the Second Punic War.

name: Campi Phlegraei
desc: The Campi Phlegraei (Phlegraean Fields) is a large caldera (13 km wide) in the Bay of Naples region of Italy. In total, the the area comprises 24 craters, although a good portion of the caldera now lies under water. The area was important in Greek and Roman times; the Greeks established their first

name: Campobasso
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Campobasso

name: Campus Stellas
desc: The name for a region of Campania that adjoined the Ager Falernus.

name: Villa Maritima di Capo di Sorrento
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Capo di Sorrento

name: Capreae
desc: Settlement on the island of Capreae.

name: Capreae (island)
desc: An island of the Bay of Naples off the Sorrentine Peninsula that has, since the time of the Roman Republic, been a popular seaside resort area. The emperor Tiberius maintained twelve villas on the island.

name: Capriati
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Capriati

name: Capua
desc: An important ancient city of Campania with Villanovan and Etruscan origins.

name: Carecini Infernates
desc: Carecini Infernates, one of the four ancient tribes that made up the Samnite population.

name: Carecini Supernates
desc: The Carecini Supernates were a tribe of Samnites.

name: Carovilli
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Carovilli

name: Carsioli
desc: An ancient settlement along the Via Valeria, Carsioli was established as a Latin colony in the territory of the Aequi ca. 298 BC.

name: Cascano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Cascano

name: Casilinum
desc: A settlement located in the border region between the ager Falernus and the ager Campanus, north of Capua.

name: Casinum
desc: A Volscian hilltop settlement that became a Roman colony in 312 B.C.

name: Castellina
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 A1 Castellina

name: Castro dei Volsci
desc: Castro dei Volsci is an Italian comune located in the province of Frosinone. Its name - Castro dei Volsci - dates only from 1816. There is evidence for pre-Roman and Roman settlement in the area, including the polygonal masonry circuit of fortifications on nearby Montenero.

name: Castropignano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Castropignano

name: Castrum Novum
desc: Castrum Novum was a colonia maritima established on the coast of Etruria.

name: Caudium
desc: A city of Samnium located between Capua and Beneventum. In 321 B.C., the Samnites under C. Pontius encamped there before defeating the Romans at the Battle of the Caudine Forks.

name: Cereatae Marianae
desc: Cereatae Marianae, purported to have been the birthplace of Caius Marius, is thought to have been located where the 13th-century abbey church of Casamari now stands (in the modern province of Frosinone, Lazio, Italy).

name: Cerfennia
desc: A settlement of the Marsi and a Roman road station on the Via Valeria.

name: Chiauci
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Chiauci

name: Kirkaion Akron/Veneris Pr.
desc: Kirkaion Akron/Veneris Pr. (Monte Circeo) is a mountainous promontory on the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy.

name: Circeii 1
desc: Circeii received a Latin colony ca. 390 B.C. The remains on the site include an enclosure wall built in polygonal masonry. "Circeii 1" refers to the earlier Roman colony founded at the eastern side of Monte Circeo. The settlement eventually moved to the western side of the peninsula.

name: Circeii 2
desc: A port on the Tyrrhenian coast. In myth, the site was considered to be one of the stopping points of the hero Odysseus.

name: Civitanova
desc: Civitanova del Sannio is an Italian comune located in the present-day province of Isernia. In antiquity, Civitanova was the site of multiple fortifications connected with the Samnites.

name: Clanius (river)
desc: A river of Campania that likely flowed into the Tyrrhenian Sea near Liternum.

name: Cliternia
desc: A city of northern Apulia.

name: Clostra (Romana)
desc: Clostra (Romana) was a place in Latium along the Via Severiana. It was located 15 miles from Circei and 9 miles from Astura.

name: Cluturnum
desc: Cluturnum was a site in Samnium, located near Aesernia. Its exact location cannot be determined.

name: Cocullo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Cocullo

name: Colle Mitra
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Colle Mitra

name: Colle Sparanise
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Colle Sparanise

name: Colle Tassito
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Colle Tassito

name: Colles Leucogaei
desc: A name for volcanic hills of a whitish hue around Puteoli.

name: Cretone
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 C1 Cretone

name: Cumae/Kyme (Campanian)
desc: An ancient settlement of Campania, Cumae was the first Greek colony established on the Italian mainland in the eighth century BC.

name: Cumanus Sinus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E4 Cumanus Sinus

name: Damecuta
desc: An Imperial villa excavated by A. Maiuri in the 1930s, Damecuta was connected to the Iulio-Claudian emperors. The construction of later Medieval and Bourbon fortifications on the site significantly damaged the ancient remains. The Medieval Damecuta tower stands atop part of the Roman villa.

name: Decennovium
desc: Decennovium refers to a 19-mile stretch of the Via Appia from the Forum Appii to Tarracina that continued through the paludes Pontinae.

name: Diana Tifatina (temple)
desc: The Fanum Dianae Tifatinae located on the slopes of Mt. Tifata in Campania.

name: Digentia (river)
desc: A stream in the ager Sabinus.

name: Dikaiarcheia/Puteoli
desc: A maritime city of Campania situated on the Phlegrean Peninsula. The settlement started as a Greek colony and became a Roman colony under the name Puteoli in 194 B.C.

name: Duronia
desc: The compilers of the Barrington Atlas include two ancient places called "Duronia" on map 44. This instance of Duronia corresponds to a fortified Samnite settlement that S.P. Oakley refers to as "Civita di Duronia". This place corresponds to a present-day Italian comune located in the province of Cam

name: Epomeus (mountain)
desc: The highest mountain on the island of Ischia.

name: Eumorfiana? (island)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D4 Eumorfiana? Ins.

name: Fabrateria Nova
desc: Caius Gracchus dispatched a Roman colony to Fabrateria Nova in 124 B.C. The relationship between Fabrateria Nova and the earlier Volscian site of Fabrateria Vetus remains unclear. The favored location for Fabrateria Nova is at S. Giovanni Incarico, where the Liri and Sacco rivers intersect.

name: Fabrateria Vetus
desc: Fabrateria Vetus was a Volscian settlement that surrendered to Rome in 424 B.C.

name: Fagifulae
desc: Fagifulae was a center of the Pentrian Samnites.

name: Falernus Ager
desc: The Ager Falernus comprised the northern portion of Campania from the Massican hills to the Vulturnus river. The area was celebrated for its fertility and, in particular, for its wines.

name: Faustianum?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Faustianum?

name: Ferentinum
desc: A Hernican town along the Via Latina that the Romans captured in 364 B.C. Later in the Republican period (after 195 B.C.), the city received Roman municipal status.

name: Ferrazzano
desc: A fortified ancient hilltop, Ferrazzano is usually identified as a Samnite site.

name: Fibrenus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Fibrenus fl.

name: Fonte Romito
desc: A pre-Roman and Roman settlement of Samnium.

name: Formiae
desc: An ancient settlement of likely Greek origin along the Via Appia. Cicero was assassinated near Formiae (now Formia) in 43 B.C.

name: Forum Popillii
desc: An important town of the Ager Falernus, not to be confused with Forum Popili, the modern Polla.

name: Fratte
desc: The ancient settlement of Fratte is located near Salerno, Italy. The settlement is situated in the valley of the Irno River and was likely first settled by Etruscans in the sixth century BCE. Material remains ascribed to both Etruscan and Samnite cultures have been identified at the site.

name: Fregellae
desc: Fregellae was a city of Latium Adiectum that became a Roman colony in 328 B.C., but was subsequently captured by the Samnites; a Roman presence was re-established in 313 B.C. Loyal to Rome during the Second Punic War, Fregellae revolted in 125 B.C., and the site was razed.

name: Fregellanum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Fregellanum

name: Frentani
desc: An Italic people of eastern Italy occupying a territory between the Apennines and the Adriatic seaboard, the Frentani had a close cultural connection with the Samnites.

name: Frosolone
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Frosolone

name: Frusino
desc: Frusino (modern Frosinone) was a town in Latium along the Via Latina that was originally a Volscian settlement.

name: Fucinus (lake)
desc: A lake of ancient Italy, the site of a major battle of 89 BC. Both Claudius and Hadrian attempted flood and drainage controls in antiquity. The Torlonia family drained the lake in the nineteenth century.

name: Fundanus L.
desc: A brackish lake ca. 90 km southeast of Rome.

name: Fundi
desc: Fundi achieved civitas sine suffragio after the Latin War in 338 B.C.

name: Furculae Caudinae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G3 Furculae Caudinae

name: Gallinaria Silva
desc: An evergreen thicket of the area around Cumae.

name: Gaurus (mount)
desc: An eruptive volcanic vent in the Phlegraean Fields. Modern Monte Gauro (also known as Monte Barbaro).

name: Gianola
desc: The site of a villa associated with Lucius Vitruvius Mamurra.

name: Gioia dei Marsi
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Gioia dei Marsi

name: Giurlanda
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Giurlanda

name: Grottacce
desc: At Grottacce are the remains of a Roman seaside villa or villa maritima.

name: Hamae
desc: Hamae is an ancient site of Campania located between Capua and Cumae, although its precise location is difficult to fix. The people of Capua gathered there for a solemn religious festival.

name: Herculaneum
desc: An ancient Roman town of Campania destroyed by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in A.D. 79. Named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

name: ‘Herculis Rani’?
desc: A large fanum sacred to ‘Herculis Rani’? at Campochiaro, the name of which is then preserved in the station mentioned on the Peutinger Table. Scholars like Adriano La Regina support linking this fanum to a place mentioned by Livy, although see the discussion by Oakley.

name: Herculis Petra
desc: An islet in the Gulf of Naples.

name: Imeus (mountain)
desc: Imeus Mons is the name given in the Peutinger Table to a pass that leads from the Fucine Lake to the territory of the Peligni; the Via Valeria crossed the pass, which is now known as the Forca Caruso.

name: Interamna Lirenas
desc: A Latin colony founded ca. 312 B.C. along the Via Latina. The site was sacked by Samnites (ca. 294 B.C.) and subsequently by Hannibal (212 B.C.). It received Roman municipal status in 90 B.C.

name: ‘Invinias’
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 ‘Invinias’

name: ‘Iovis Lareni’
desc: ‘Iovis Lareni’ is marked as a station on the Peutinger map. It lies 7 miles from Sulmo. This place coincides with the ancient site of Ocriticum, a pre-Roman and Roman settlement. The site, located in the Italian comune of Cansano (province of L'Aquila, Abruzzo), includes the remains of two Italo-Rom

name: Iuvanum
desc: A Roman municipium founded in 87 BC after the Social War, Iuvanum sits on the site of a pre-existing Samnite settlement that occupies an upland plateau.

name: Iuvencus (river)
desc: An ancient river of Italy, identified by modern scholars with the Giovenco River.

name: Kupelternum/Cubulteria
desc: Kupelternum/Cubulteria was an ancient Samnite settlement.

name: La Giostra
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 La Giostra

name: Lactarius (mountain)
desc: A mountain ridge of Campania that is a spur branching off the Apennines. Many Roman villas in this vicinity were destroyed (and thus, preserved) by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius.

name: Lago di Paola
desc: A villa of the emperor Domitian located in the area of Circeii.

name: *Lavernae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 *Lavernae

name: Latium (region)
desc: The territory of the Latins.

name: Latium Adiectum
desc: A region of ancient Italy characterized as an area of Latin colonial expansion; also referred to as Latium Novum.

name: Laurinienses
desc: An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: Vallo di Lauro.

name: Lautulae
desc: Lautulae is a narrow pass (saltus) located above Terracina in Latium.

name: Ligures Baebiani
desc: Ligures Baebiani was a Ligurian settlement in Samnium.

name: Liris/Clanis (river)
desc: A major river of central Italy, originating in the Colles Simbruini and flowing into the Amyclanus Sinus just south of Minturnae. The modern Garigliano.

name: Liternum
desc: An ancient city of Campania located near the mouth of the Volturnus River; a Roman colony was established at Liternum in 194 B.C. The site is most famous as the location of the villa of Scipio Africanus, as described by Seneca.

name: Lucanus? Ager
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Lucanus? Ager

name: Lucrinus (lake)
desc: A small lake near Lake Avernus, the modern Lucrino in Italy.

name: Lucus Feroniae
desc: A sanctuary of Feronia located at a spring on the via Appia near Tarracina.

name: Madonnna del Canneto
desc: The sanctuary site of Madonnna del Canneto is located at Settefrati within the confines of the Abruzzo national park in Italy. It has a long history as a sacred site, beginning with sacred activities dedicated to Mefitis in the later first millennium BCE.

name: Malborghetto
desc: The hamlet of Malborghetto, located on the ancient Via Flaminia, is traditionally linked with Constantine the Great and his visions of victory that occurred prior to the battle of Saxa Rubra on 28 October A.D. 312. The quadrifons arch, dating to the fourth century, marks the intersection of the Via

name: Marcianum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Marcianum

name: Marcianus Fundus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Marcianus Fundus

name: Marica
desc: Marica, an Italic goddess, was worshipped in a sacred grove located between Minturnae and the estuary of the Liris river.

name: Marruvium
desc: Ancient Marruvium was the principal city of the Italic tribe of the Marsi.

name: Massicus (mountain)
desc: Mons Massicus, a mountain ridge of ancient Italy, in the territory of the Aurunci, at the border of Latium and Campania.

name: Matrice
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Matrice

name: Melpis (river)
desc: The Melfa River flows through Lazio, originating from the Monti della Meta and joining the Liri River near San Giovanni Incarico.

name: Mignano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Mignano

name: Minerva temple at Punta della Campanella
desc: An ancient temple of Minerva, located on the ancient cape that also was known by the goddess' name.

name: Minervae (promontory)
desc: The Minervae promunturium is identified by modern scholars with the Punta Campanella, which lies at the western extremity of the Sorrentine Peninsula.

name: Minori
desc: Minori is the site of a major villa located on the Amalfi coast, some 11 km WSW of Salerno. Destroyed by a possible landslide, the villa was in use from the Iulio-Claudian period through to the Flavian period.

name: Minturnae
desc: Originally an Ausonian town that fought against Rome in 314 B.C., Minturnae became a colony in 296 B.C. The site is located on the Garigliano river (ancient Liris) and served an important economic function. The Via Appia passes through the city.

name: Misenum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Misenum

name: Misenum (promontory)
desc: A promontory that sheltered the ancient Portus Julius, the harborage of the Roman western imperial fleet. The feature takes its name from Misenus, one of the sailors aboard Aeneas' ship.

name: Monte Acero
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte Acero

name: Monte Annamunna
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Monte Annamunna

name: Monte Castellone (Torcino)
desc: A fortified center located in the comune of Ciorlano.

name: Monte Castellone 2
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte Castellone 2

name: Monte Cavallerizzo
desc: Monte Cavallerizzo is a fortified Samnite center - perhaps dating to the fourth century B.C. - located in close proximity to the sanctuary at Vastogirardi. According to S.P. Oakley, Monte Cavallerizzo (1,524 meters a.s.l.) is the site of the highest Samnite hillfort. An area of 2.7 hectares is defen

name: Monte Cicoli
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Monte Cicoli

name: Monte Cila
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte Cila

name: Monte del Fico
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Monte del Fico

name: Monte Frascara
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Monte Frascara

name: Monte Monaco di Gioia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte Monaco di Gioia

name: Monte Nero
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D2 Monte Nero

name: Monte S. Angelo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte S. Angelo

name: Monte S. Croce
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Monte S. Croce

name: Monte S. Croce
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Monte S. Croce

name: Monte Saraceno di Cercemaggiore
desc: Archaeological excavations on the area of the summit of Monte Saraceno have documented the remains of an imposing, fortified high-altitude settlement which has a second walled area within it.

name: Monte Vairano
desc: At Monte Vairano are the remains of a fortified center of the Pentrian Samnites.

name: Monteverde
desc: The eleventh century monastery of Santa Maria di Monteverde sits atop and reuses elements of Roman and pre-Roman settlements on the hilltop.

name: Montevetrano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Montevetrano

name: Morroni
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Morroni

name: Mura delle Fate
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Mura delle Fate

name: Mura di S. Stefano
desc: A second century A.D. Roman villa built atop an earlier villa rustica.

name: Neratii
desc: This site of an imperial villa, dating to the first and second centuries, covers an area of ca. 15,000 sq. m. It is located in the southern portion of the modern civic territory of San Giuliano del Sannio in the Província de Campobasso, Italy.

name: Nesis (island)
desc: A volcanic islet of the Phlegraean Islands archipelago, Nesis was in antiquity the site of many elite seaside villas.

name: Nola
desc: The city of Nola (Nuvlana) is considered one of the oldest in Campania. Under Augustus, the settlement became a Roman colony; it was the spot where Augustus died in A.D. 14.

name: Nuceria (Alfaterna)
desc: Nuceria (Alfaterna) (modern Nocera Inferiore) is an ancient settlement in Campania. In pre-Roman times, this was the chief settlement of the Sarnus river valley.

name: *Nuceriola
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G3 *Nuceriola

name: Nymphaeus (river)
desc: The Nymphaeus was a river of Latium. Pliny the Elder seems to be the only ancient author who mentions it, and he has it flowing into the Tyrrhenian Sea somewhere between Astura and Circeii. The compilers of the Barrington Atlas show it flowing across the Pomptinus Ager. Nineteenth-century sources th

name: Oplontis
desc: An ancient place (modern Torre Annunziata in Italy), lying between Pompeii and Herculaneum and buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE. Its ancient name is known only from Peutinger's Roman Map.

name: Oratino
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Oratino

name: Pagus Capriculanus?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Pagus Capriculanus?

name: Pagus Meflanus
desc: Pagus Meflanus was likely located in the Apennines to the northeast of Beneventum.

name: Pagus Sarclanus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Pagus Sarclanus

name: Pagus Vescinus
desc: The Pagus Vescinus is only attested epigraphically.

name: Palazzo a Mare
desc: The site of one of the twelve villas of Tiberius, and perhaps the largest, on the island of Capreae.

name: *Pallanum
desc: An ancient settlement of the Frentani located on Monte Pallano.

name: Palmaria (island)

name: Allia (river)
desc: The Allia river was a tributary of the Tiber, but is now unlocated. It joined the Tiber some 18 km (11 miles) north of Rome and was most famous as the site of a battle in which the Romans were defeated by Brennus and the Gauls ca. 387 B.C.

name: Ameriola
desc: An ancient town of Latium that was a member of the Latin League. It was located to the northeast of Rome, but its precise location cannot be determined today.

name: Bolani
desc: The Bolani were the people of Bola, an ancient city of Latium. Its foundation is ascribed by Virgil to the kings of Alba.

name: Capitulum Hernicum
desc: A Hernican town that still existed in Pliny's time, Capitulum Hernicum received colonists under both Sulla and Iulius Caesar. An inscription found in the area of Piglio mentions the town, but its precise location is uncertain.

name: Carventum
desc: Carventum was an ancient city of Latium, listed by Dionysius as one of the thirty states of the Latin League.

name: Castrum Invi
desc: An Italic site located at the mouth of the Incastro river and in the territory of Ardea.

name: Cominium Ocritum

name: Via Popilia (in Campania)
desc: One of two ancient Roman roads in Italy is named Via Popilia after the magistrate Publius Popilius Laenas. The Campanian instance diverges from the Via Appia at Capua and continues to Rhegium on the Straits of Messina.

name: Via Vitularia

desc: The ancient settlement of Pontecagnano is located on the plain of the Sele river, about 4 km from the sea. Settlement begins in the Chalcolithic period. desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 45 G4 Porto Cesareo

name: Poseideion Akron
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 45 A4 Poseideion Akron

name: Poseidonia/Paestum
desc: Greeks from Sybaris originally founded Poseidonia/Paestum, a major Greco-Roman center of south Italy, in the seventh-century BCE. It was originally named Poseidonia. After the Pyrrhic war, the city became a Latin colony named Paestum ca. 273 BCE.

name: Posta Crusta
desc: The 'villa rustica' at Posta Crusta.

name: Potentia
desc: Potentia was the site of a Roman colonial foundation ca. 184 BCE.

name: Pr(a)etorium Laverianum?

name: Praetorium Publilianum
desc: Praetorium Publilianum was the center of an imperial latifundium in the territory of Teanum Apulum.
