name: Rocavecchia
desc: A fortified coastal site on the Adriatic Sea with a long history of occupation stretching from the Bronze Age (fifteenth to eleventh centuries BC) to the Middle Ages.

name: Roccadaspide
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 45 B4 Roccadaspide

name: Rossano
desc: Rossano di Vaglio, a fourth century BC site dedicated to Mefitis, was a Lucanian federal sanctuary.

name: Rubi
desc: Rubi was a statio in Apulia, located along the Via Minucia.

name: ‘Rudas’/‘Budas’
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 45 D2 ‘Rudas’/‘Budas’

name: Rudiae
desc: An ancient Messapic town, Rudiae was the birthplace of the poet Ennius.

name: Sal(a)pia(i)/Elpia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 45 C2 Sal(a)pia(i)/Elpia

name: Sal(a)pia(i)/Salinae
desc: Sal(a)pia(i)/Salinae was an ancient city of Daunia.

name: Salapina Palus
desc: An ancient coastal lagoon on the coast of Apulia, drained in modern times.

name: Sallentini
desc: Sallentini were a tribe of an ancient Apulia, the 'heel' of the booth of the Italian peninsula. They spoke the Messapian language.

name: Sallentinum/Iapygia
desc: Cape Leuca, known as Sallentinum and Iapygia in ancient sources, is a headland that forms the extreme southeastern point of Italy and separates the Gulf of Tarentum from the Adriatic Sea.

name: Saltus Carminianensis
desc: The Saltus Carminianensis was a large imperial property of northern Apulia mentioned in the Notitia Dignitatum Occidentis. Its precise location and borders are not known today.

name: Castle of Gradara
desc: A castle in the Marche built first in the eleventh century.

name: Aristanis
desc: A Byzantine site in western Sardinia, made important by the location of a bishopric there by Torcotorio in AD 1070; now the modern city of Oristano.

name: Nuraghe Santu Antine
desc: A nuragic structure dating originally ca. 1,600 to 1,450 BC.

name: Via Herdonitana
desc: A Roman road connecting Herdonia and Ausculum.

name: Via Aurelia Aeclanensis?
desc: A road in Apulia leading from Aeclanum toward Vibinum. The Via Aurelia Aeclanensis? intersects the Via Herculia.

name: Via Tiberina
desc: An ancient Roman road.

name: Temple of Juno (Hera Lacinia)
desc: A temple of the Doric order that was built at Akragas ca. 450 BCE.

name: Rocca Calascio
desc: A tenth-century fortress located in the Province of L'Aquila in Abruzzo, Italy.

name: Villa di Monte delle Colonnacce
desc: A Roman villa located near Castel di Guido.

name: Ponte Nomentano
desc: A Roman bridge over the Aniene river.

name: Tomb of Priscilla
desc: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that belonged to one Priscilla, wife of Titus Flavius Abascanto, a freedman of the emperor Domitian.

name: Villa of the Papyri
desc: A suburban villa located northwest of Herculaneum that was originally owned by Lucius Calpurnius Piso Caesoninus.

name: Villa of the Mysteries
desc: A Roman villa located northwest of Pompeii.

name: Via Valeria
desc: An ancient Roman road in Sicilia.

name: Basilica Constantini
desc: The Basilica Constantini, also called Basilica Nova ("New Basilica"), Basilica of Maxentius, or Basilica of Maxentius and Constantine, is a colossal fourth-century basilica along the Sacra Via in Rome. It is considered the largest ancient structure in the valley of the Forum Romanum and is often reg

name: Coriaria Septimiana
desc: A place included the Regionary Catalogues for Rome's Regio XIV, Coriaria Septimiana refers to tanneries in the Transtiberim. name: Ponte Molino
desc: A Roman segmental arch bridge across the Bacchiglione river in Padua, Italy.

name: Ponte di San Lorenzo
desc: An early segmental arch bridge, built between 47 and 30 B.C.

name: Ponte Corvo
desc: A Roman segmental arch bridge across the Bacchiglione river in Padua, Italy.

name: Sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia
desc: The Sanctuary of Fortuna Primigenia at Praeneste is a terraced sanctuary of monumental proportions. The phase visible today dates to the late second century B.C.

name: Roman theater at Brixia
desc: The Roman theater at Brixia was built during the Flavian period.

name: San Salvatore monastery
desc: A monastery founded in A.D. 753 by Desiderius, future king of the Lombards. Located in modern Brescia, Italy.

name: Gastaldaga area and the Episcopal complex
desc: A Longobard complex in Cividale del Friuli.

name: Byzantine arcosolia
desc: Byzantine tombs at the site belong to the sixth century when the Temple of Concordia was converted into a Christian church.

name: Lower Agora
desc: The lower agora of the ancient city of Agrigentum contains shops, a sacred area, and the gymnasium complex.

name: Murgia Lama Rosa
desc: A mountain rising to 485 meters above sea level in the Alta Murgia National Park in Italy.

name: Catacombs of Generosa
desc: A Paleochristian catacomb located at the sixth mile of the via Portuense.

name: Nuraghe Losa
desc: A nuraghe near Abbasanta, Sardinia. The original phase of the site dates to the fifteenth through thirteenth centuries B.C., while the enclosure wall dates to the thirteenth and twelfth centuries B.C. name: Shrine of Venus Cloacina
desc: The Sacrum Cloacina was a small shrine dedicated to Venus Cloacina, patron divinity of the sewer, and was located near the Tabernae novae in the Forum Romanum. The foundation of the sacellum is extant while images of its likely elevation are found on Roman coins.

name: Porta Maggiore
desc: The Porta Maggiore is the ancient Porta Praenestina, an early Imperial gate preserved in the later third century walls built by Aurelian.

name: I Morroni
desc: Morroni dei Marsi, the remains of two mausolea dating to the Roman period.

name: Buffa necropolis
desc: One of the necropoleis of the ancient city of Selinous, on the Buffa hill in contrada Manuzza, to the NE of the ancient city

name: Nuraghe Toscono
desc: A single tower nuraghe standing ca. 7.25 meters.

name: Nuraghe Porcarzos
desc: A complex nuraghe surrounded by a quadrilobate bastion.

name: Santa Maria dell'Orto
desc: The church of Santa Maria dell'Orto is a Roman Catholic church located in Rome's Trastevere district. Its foundation is traced to 508.

name: Ponte Gobbo
desc: A Medieval bridge across the river Trebia that is said to have Roman origins.

name: Pozzo sacro di Sa Testa
desc: An architectural complex dating to Sardinia's nuragic period.

name: Podere Pievina
desc: A farm site with a least two occupation phases - one dating between the second century BC and early first century AD and the second between the fourth and fifth centuries AD.

name: Pauli Stincus
desc: A Punic farm site occupied from the fourth to the second century B.C.

name: Mutatorium Caesaris
desc: An imperial property opposite the Baths of Caracalla that is mentioned in the Regionary Catalogues and also preserved on a fragment of the Severan marble plan.

name: So-called Arco di Druso
desc: The popular toponym associated with this monument - Arco di Druso or Arch of Drusus - is a misnomer and is misleading. name: Porta Neola
desc: A Roman bridge located in the Colle Merulino near Tivoli, Italy.

name: Santa Croce in Montis Vernae
desc: A Benedictine abbey founded in 982 on the Piana di Monte Verna.

name: Crypta Balbi
desc: The Crypta Balbi, mentioned by name only in the Regionary Catalogues, most likely refers to a vaulted passageway built in the Campus Martius by the proconsul Lucius Cornelius Balbus in 15 BC, who also dedicated a theater there in the same year.

name: Roman Mausoleum of Villa Gordiani
desc: The Roman Mausoleum of Villa Gordiani is a two-storey cylindrical tomb with pronaos executed in opus latericium. It fronts on the ancient via Praenestina. The rotunda has a diameter of more than 19 meters. Based on brick stamps, chronology is potentially wide and likely should be assigned anywhere i

name: Octagonal hall, Villa dei Gordiani
desc: A Roman structure with three levels that was re-purposed in the Middle Ages, the so-called Octagonal hall at the Villa dei Gordiani was likely originally either a nymphaeum or part of a bath complex.

name: Teatro Marittimo
desc: The so-called "Maritime Theater" at the Villa of Hadrian in Tivoli is sometimes referred to as the 'island villa'. It served as a kind of inner sanctum within the larger complex of the Villa Hadriana.

name: Örvényes
desc: Örvényes, County of Veszprém, Hungary, was the site of a Roman settlement.

name: Villa Romana di Casalotti
desc: A villa site that includes a bathing complex, dating from the second to fourth centuries CE.

name: Villa di Faonte a Vigne Nuove
desc: The so-called the Villa of Faonte was a Roman villa in Rome located between Via delle Vigne Nuove and Via Passo del Turchino. There are remains of a cistern (approx. 29.5 by 14 meters) now set in a garden area.

name: Colle Lecinone
desc: Remains of a villa built on several terraces.

name: Ianus Quadrifons
desc: A quadrifrons triumphal arch at Rome that is located at a crossroads in the area of the Velabrum and the Forum Boarium. It dates to the early fourth century AD; its construction employed spolia, and it likely honored either Constantine I or Constantius II.

name: Catacombe di San Sebastiano
desc: The catacombs of San Sebastiano located on the Via Appia are located near the church of the same name. These hypogeal tombs emerged in the third century CE and were linked initially to the relics of the apostles Peter and Paul.

name: Römisches Forum Waldgirmes
desc: The Roman Forum at Lahnau-Waldgirmes is the site of a fortified Roman trading outpost. It is located at the edge of the modern village of Waldgirmes.

name: Piazza Pitagora
desc: An in situ segment of the Roman-period paving stones of the Via Salaria was discovered in Piazza Pitagora in 2022 during utility works.

name: Torre Astura
desc: A Medieval coastal fort of the Frangipani.

name: Olevano Romano
desc: Remains of polygonal masonry fortification are extant at Olevano Romano in Italy, which is presumed to be the site of a fortified oppidum of the Aequi. name: Withdrawn: Roccamonfina (volcano)
desc: Unintentional duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/433077

name: Arco di Sant'Ercolano
desc: The Arco di Sant'Ercolano of Perugia is the ancient Porta Cornea of the Hellenistic walls of the city.

name: Arco Etrusco
desc: The so-called "Arco Etrusco" is one of the gates of ancient Perusia. The gate dates originally from the third century B.C. when it was one of seven gates in the Etruscan wall. In 40 B.C. it was refashioned under Augustus.

name: Porta Marzia
desc: The so-called Porta Marzia at Perugia began as a third century B.C. gate of the Etruscan city and was engulfed in the fortifications of the Rocca Paolina in 1540.

name: Porta Eburnea
desc: The so-called Porta Eburnea or the Arco della Mandorla is an ancient gate of the Etruscan walls of Perusia.

name: Montereggi
desc: An Etruscan settlement in proximity to the course of the Arno river that was active from the fifth to the first centuries B.C.

name: Temple of Divus Augustus (Rome)
desc: Caius dedicated a temple to divus Augustus in Rome in the autumn of 37 CE. Based on the sources, the temple should be located between the vicus Tuscus and the vicus Iugarius, just behind the Basilica Iulia. The temple remains unexcavated, and its nature and location are a matter of scholarly debate.

name: Via Aurelia
desc: An ancient Roman road begun ca. 241 B.C. by the censor C. Aurelius Cotta.

name: Casal Bernocchi-Malafede
desc: An archaeological area along the Via Ostiensis with evidence of human activity stretching from the Archaic period to the time of the Roman Empire. SIgnificant archaeological features include an extensive necropolis and a Roman bathing facility.

name: Meta Romuli
desc: The so-called "Meta Romuli" was a pyramidal tomb located in the Ager Vaticanus in Rome. It likely dates to the first century BCE or the first century CE. Its extant superstructure was demolished in 1499. Remains of foundations and pavements that have been associated with the tomb were encountered in

name: Bollendorf
desc: Roman villa rustica in Bollendorf

name: Longuich
desc: Roman villa urbana in Longuich

name: Guglia di Marcello
desc: The so-called "Guglia di Marcello" or "Aguglia d'Agosta" is a Roman funerary monument located along the ancient via Pompei that once connected Syracuse and Messina. It dates to the period from the first century B.C. to the first century A.D.

name: Pons Probi
desc: The Pons Probi across the Tiber is attested in the Notitia and, according to Platner and Ashby, was likely built under Emperor Probus in the third century AD.

name: Mausoleum of Romulus
desc: Tomb of Valerius Romulus (ca. AD 292/295 – 309), son of Maxentius, along the Via Appia.

name: Bidoni
desc: A monumental sanctuary (26 x 20 m) dedicated to Iuppiter.

name: Villa Romana di S. Andrea
desc: The partially preserved structural remains of an Imperial villa dating to the third and fourth centuries.

name: Capitolium of Verona
desc: Excavations have determined the location of the capitolium of Roman Verona, part of an extensive, terraced complex that underpins medieval and later structures of the city. The capitolium itself stretches from the northern end of the modern Piazza Erbe to the via Emilei, lying beneath the Palazzo Ma

name: Nuraghe Cuccuru Ibba
desc: A pre-nuragic village of the Ozieri culture and later nuraghe located in the Laguna di Santa Gilla.

name: Giants' grave of Sa Dom'è s'Orcu (Quartucciu)
desc: A "Giant's tomb" of the fourteenth and thirteenth centuries B.C.

name: Casa Bellezza
desc: The so-called "Casa Bellezza" is a Roman domus located on the flank of the Aventine Hill in Rome. Its remains are found at Largo Arrigo VII, no. 2-4.

name: Nuraghe Nuracale
desc: A quadrilobate nuragic complex located in the territory of Scano di Montiferro.

name: Casa della statuetta indiana
desc: The so-called "Casa della statuetta indiana" (I.8.5) lies on the Via dell'Abbondanza. Excavated between 1930 and 1935, it was named for the fine ivory statuette (thought by some to depict Lakshmi) found inside. The house has a slightly irregular floor plan with some rooms added to the structure from

name: Taberna Pomaria di Felix
desc: A fruit shop in Pompeii (I, 8, 1) with an entrance on to the Via dell'Abbondanza.

name: Pistrinum of Betitius Placidus
desc: A small shop located in Regio I of Pompeii (I, 8, 7).

name: Roman theater of Catania
desc: The Roman theater of Catania was built in the second century CE and remained in use until the fifth or sixth century. It could accommodate approximately 7,000 spectators.

name: Palatine Stadium
desc: "Palatine Stadium" is likely a misnomer when considering the probable function of this architectural complex located on the southeast corner of the Palatine Hill on the flank of the Domus Augustana-Flavia. Originating during the reign of the Domitian, this complex was restored numerous times, includ

name: Temple at Santa Maria in Canale
desc: A temple of Tuscan type with cella and lateral alae built of ashlar masonry and dated to the 3rd century BCE, now built into a rural church and farmstead complex. The temple is situated along the Via Amerina between Ameria and Tuder, and marks the boundary between those two Umbrian communities. A fr

name: Cisterna Acqua Rossa
desc: A Roman cistern located near San Vittorino in Lazio.

name: Ponte Pischero
desc: The ruin called Ponte Pischero was once an aqueduct bridge that was part of the Aqua Anio Vetus aqueduct.

name: Porta Montanara
desc: The Porta Montanara is an ancient Roman gate of Ariminum.

name: Basilica di San Lorenzo Maggiore
desc: A Christian basilica in Milan built in the late fourth and early fifth centuries.

name: Murus Terreus Carinarum
desc: An early earthwork at Rome described by Varro, the Murus Terreus may have been part of the so-called Servian Wall. It was likely located on the Oppian Hill, between the Subura and the Carinae.

name: Tomba delle Anatre
desc: The Tomb of the Ducks at Veii is an early example of a painted Etruscan tomb. It dates to the second quarter of the seventh century BCE and was discovered in 1958 in the Riserva del Bagno necropolis.

name: Tomba Campana
desc: The Grotta Campana at Veii is an Etruscan burial complex discovered by Giampietro Campana in 1843.

name: City walls of Sabucina
desc: The fortification walls of the Classical city.

name: Roman baths of Coriovallum
desc: The site of Coriovallum is known for its well-preserved bath complex. These baths were first built ca. A.D. 40 and then re-built during the reign of Hadrian. They remained in use until the fourth century.

name: Villa del Pastore
desc: A large villa at Stabiae covering more than 17,000 square meters.

name: Villa del fondo Ippolito Zurlo
desc: A Roman villa located in the contrada Giuliana at Boscoreale on a side street of via Grotta II. The site was excavated by Vincenzo De Prisco in 1897 and subsequently reinterred.

name: Villa of Asellius
desc: A Roman villa excavated at Boscoreale in 1903 and 1904 under the supervision of Vincenzo De Prisco and located on the property of one Giuseppe De Martino. Wall paintings and artifacts were recovered from the site, and the villa was subsequently reinterred. Records as to its precise location are less

name: Jensberg Celtic oppidum
desc: Site of the Celtic wall protecting the oppidum from south-west.

name: Temple complex (Petinesca)
desc: A Gallo-Roman sanctuary with an enclosed precinct that was linked to the oppidum.

name: Mülheim-Kärlich
desc: A Roman villa dating to the second and third centuries A.D.

name: Remstecken
desc: Site of a Roman villa rustica, dating from the first to third centuries AD.

name: Haselburg
desc: A second-century AD Roman villa estate.

name: Freimühle
desc: A Roman outpost of the Rhaetian Limes.

name: Spolverino, Alberese
desc: An archaeological site of the Roman period connected with the fluvial harbor of Rusellae.

name: Casa dell'Argenteria
desc: Residential townhouse in Pompeii excavated in the 1830s and 1976.

name: Casa di L. Aelius Magnus
desc: First excavated in 1808, later converted to Sarno baths and gymnasium. Linked to VIII.2.2.23

name: Casa della Soffitta
desc: House in Pompeii, excavated in 1877, 1905, and restored in 1979.

name: House of the Floral Lararium
desc: The so-called House of the Floral Lararium at Pompeii was excavated in 1951, 1954, and 1987. The site was restored in 1988 and reopened to visitors in 2018.

name: Torre del Papito
desc: A Medieval tower in Rome's Largo Argentina.

name: Casa dei Crescenzi
desc: A structure in Rome built between 1040 and 1065 by one Niccolò, son of Crescenzio and Teodora, in order to control the Ponte Emilio, on whose transit the family charged a toll. The building incorporates ancient spolia.

name: Tumulo di Montecalvario
desc: An Etruscan tomb located at Castellina in Chianti in Italy.

name: Alcimoennis
desc: An oppidum located on Michelsberg hill in Bavaria, occupied from ca. 500 BC until the first century BC.

name: Portus Cosanus
desc: The harbor of the Latin colonial city of Cosa in south Etruria.

name: Villa delle Colonne
desc: A late Republican and early Imperial villa in the ager Cosanus noted for its turreted enclosure wall.

name: Ponte Fonnaia

name: Ponte di San Giovanni de Butris

name: Tugurium Romuli
desc: Ancient textual sources, including Dionysius of Halicarnassus and Plutarch, place the purported dwelling place of Romulus near the Scalae Caci at the southwestern corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome. Whether the place cited by ancient texts and maintained in antiquity until at least the fourth centu

name: Roman Villa La Grottaccia
desc: The remains of a Roman villa (first to fourth centuries CE) at Ladispoli. The surviving cryptoporticus gives the site its name.

name: Cascina Torretta
desc: Approximately 41 burials from a Roman cremation necropolis were excavated in 2021 at Cascina Torretta, a locality in the municipality of Calvignasco (southwest of Milan, Italy). The tombs were poorly preserved, appeared to be relatively shallow pit graves, and were likely connected to a rural settle

name: Lake Mezzano
desc: Lake Mezzano is a small crater lake of central Italy that formed 400,000 years ago.

name: Villa Marittima della Tagliata
desc: A maritime villa of the first century A.D. adjacent to the port of Cosa.

name: Abbazia di Santa Maria di Falleri
desc: The Medieval Cistercian abbey church of Santa Maria di Falleri occupies a portion of what was initially the walled area of the ancient town of Falerii, established in 241 BCE. The abbey's name, along with that of the associated hamlet, preserves the ancient toponymy.

name: Cima tumulus
desc: A rock-cut Etruscan tomb dating to the second half of the seventh century B.C.

name: Tumulo del tesoro
desc: An Etruscan tumulus of the seventh century B.C.

name: Cencelle
desc: A Medieval settlement that, according to textual sources, was founded in 854 by Pope Leo IV to provide a more secure position for the citizens of Centumcellae (Civitavecchia). Situated along the ancient Via Aurelia, Cencelle occupies a defensible hill positioned between the Melledra and Mignone rive

name: Pisciarelli necropolis
desc: An Etruscan necropolis with tombs dated to the archaic period located near modern Civitavecchia in Italy.

name: Torre del Pascolaro
desc: The ruins of a Medieval tower in South Etruria.

name: Temple of Vesta at Tibur
desc: The Temple of Vesta in Tivoli dates to the early first century B.C. It was once situated on the acropolis of the ancient city. Its ruins now lie within the grounds of the Villa Gregoriana.

name: Anfiteatro di Bleso
desc: The "Anfiteatro di Bleso" is a second century A.D. Roman amphitheater at Tibur (modern Tivoli in Italy).

name: Monastery of S. Elia Vecchio
desc: A ruined ninth century Christian monastery in Calabria.

name: Podere Marzuolo
desc: Podere Marzuolo was the site of Roman pottery production from the first century B.C. until the early fourth century A.D. The site has yielded evidence for the production of terra sigillata pottery as well as evidence of blacksmithing.

name: Strassen Roman Milestone
desc: A Roman milestone for the twentieth mile from Aguntum was found at modern Strassen in Austria.

name: Basilica of Santa Pudenziana
desc: A palaeochristian church dedicated to St. Pudentiana located in Rome and, perhaps, the earliest site of Christian worship in the city. The church is located along the Via Urbana, which follows the course of the ancient vicus Patricius.

name: Clelia Roman Villa
desc: A Late Roman villa and necropolis located at modern Imola in Italy.

name: Tomba dell'Arciere
desc: An Etruscan tumulus dating to the seventh century B.C. at the locality known as La Collina in the comune of San Casciano in Val di Pesa.

name: Athenaeum of Hadrian (Rome)
desc: The Athenaeum of Hadrian was located in regio VII near the Capitoline Hill in Rome. Founded by the Emperor Hadrian, it was designated for the promotion of literary and scientific studies and named after the city of Athens. Excavations connected to the Metro C line revealed a complex in the vicinity

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: A Roman bridge located in the Parco dei Medici near Rome, Italy.

name: Baths of Pozzo Pantaleo
desc: A public bath (thermae) of the Roman Imperial period.

name: Pozzo Pantaleo
desc: The 'Pozzo Pantaleo' is a Roman mausoleum that re-used a cistern of the early Imperial period. In a third phase, the site was repurposed as a shrine dedicated to the Christian Saint Pantaleon.

name: Via Popilia (in Aemilia)
desc: A road from Ariminum up the Adriatic Coast toward what is now Venice.

name: Gallo-Roman theater of Mandeure
desc: The Roman theater of Mandeure dates to the first century CE.

name: Necropoli Cappella
desc: The Cappella necropolis preserves a complex of underground tombs arranged along the ancient road connecting Misenum and Cumae. The earliest tombs date to the late first century BCE.

name: tribus Sergia
desc: An older rural tribe of ancient Rome.

name: Eumachia Building
desc: Located on the east side of Pompeii's forum (VII, 9, 1), the so-called Eumachia building is a large, public building financed by Eumachia, a public priestess of Venus in Pompeii during the middle of the first century AD.

name: Ekklesiasterion at Poseidonia/Paestum
desc: The seat of the popular assembly of Poseidonia/Paestum, the Ekklesiasterion was built ca. 480-470 B.C. and could accommodate, at most, 1,700 persons. The structure retained its function after the Lucanian conquest but was abandoned, buried, and built over after the Roman conquest.

name: "Basilica" of San Vitale
desc: A church (but not a basilica) in Ravenna, Italy, established by Bishop Ecclesius in 526 AD and consecrated ca. 547 AD.

name: Roman Theater of Minturnae
desc: A theater constructed in Minturnae under Augustus or Tiberius, and further embellished under Hadrian.

name: Litana Silva
desc: The Litana Silva was a forest located in Gallia Cispadana in the territory of the Boii. It was the site of the defeat of the Roman consul L. Postumius Albinus in 216 BC. Its precise location is uncertain, but it probably lay somewhere in the flat land south of the Po river in Italy.

name: Santuario nuragico di Santa Vittoria
desc: A nuragic site near Serri, Sardinia, with a later phase of Christian re-use.

name: House of the Gilded Cupids
desc: A Roman domus that once belonged to Cn. Poppaeus Habitus (VI 16,7).

name: Temple of Asclepius
desc: The Temple of Asclepius (VIII, 7, 25) in Pompeii is located at the intersection of the Via del Tempio di Iside and the Via Stabiana. It is also referred to as the Temple of Jupiter Meilichius.

name: Necropoli del Castellaccio
desc: A necropolis at Falerii Veteres.

name: Villa Arcinelli
desc: The remains of a Roman platform villa, the first phase of which belongs to the first century BCE.

name: Selciatella Roman bridge
desc: Ponte della Selciatella, a Roman-period bridge crossing the Fosso di Acqua Rossa in San Vittorino, Lazio, Italy.

name: Basilica di Santa Balbina all'Aventino
desc: The basilica of Santa Balbina is a paleo-Christian basilica in Rome, located on the "little Aventine".

name: Domus Cilonis
desc: The house of Lucius Fabius Cilo, praefectus urbi in 203, consul in 193 and 204, and a close friend of the emperor Septimius Severus. The house was a gift of the Severans and appears on the Severan marble plan. Its site is now occupied by the basilica of Santa Balbina on the "little Aventine".

name: Caelius Mons
desc: The Caelian Hill in Rome.

name: Domus Aurea
desc: A sprawling palace complex begun by Nero after A.D. 64 that aimed to connect the Esquiline, Caelian, and Palatine hills.

name: Tor de' Schiavi
desc: The Tor de' Schiavi is a medieval tower (thirteenth century) built atop the remains of the octagonal hall of the Villa Gordiani.

name: Temple of Mater Matuta at Satricum
desc: A sanctuary dedicated to Mater Matuta that was in use between the seventh and fifth centuries B.C.

name: Post-Archaic necropolis at Poggio dei Cavallari

name: Porta Querquetulana

name: Terme Romane, Ferento
desc: The Roman baths of ancient Ferentium are located adjacent to the Roman theater.

name: Kastellbad Schirenhof
desc: Extensive Roman bathhouse associated with the Roman fort at modern Schirenhof in the German municipality of Schwäbisch Gmünd, Baden-Württemberg.

name: Jonvelle
desc: The ruins of a Gallo-Roman villa with polychrome mosaic pavement.

name: Roman vicus and harbor at Lousonna
desc: The site is located in modern Lausanne-Vidy

name: Sacred Way at Iuppiter Latiaris, T.
desc: The sacred processional street on Monte Cavo.

name: "Ponte Sanguinario" at Spoletium
desc: The "Ponte Sanguinario" at Spoleto is a late republican to early imperial Roman bridge. The remains of the bridge are now below street level in the Piazza della Vittoria, not far from the Porta San Gregorio.

name: Pimentel, Necropoli di S'Acqua Salida e di Corongiu
desc: A necropolis of the second millennium B.C.

name: Noddule nuragic complex
desc: A multi-period settlement site with occupation stretching from ca. 4000 B.C. to the fourth century A.D.

name: House of the Red Walls
desc: A domus excavated in 1832 and 1882. It is noted for its late-stage wall decoations that may call upon public monuments for inspiration.

name: House of Marcus Lucretius
desc: The House of Marcus Lucretius was excavated in 1846 and 1851.

name: tribus Aemilia
desc: The tribus Aemilia is counted among the twenty-one oldest rural tribes of Rome. Its location is uncertain.

name: tribus Aniensis
desc: The tribus Aniensis was one of the later rural tribes of Rome and was organised in 299 B.C.

name: Thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus
desc: The house and thermopolium of Vetutius Placidus (I,8,8) opens directly onto the south side of the Via dell'Abbondanza.

name: Claudia
desc: A Roman rural tribe that was one of the most ancient of Rome's gentes. The gens Claudia traced its history to the earliest days of the Roman Republic. Appius Claudius Sabinus Regillensis, in 495 B.C., was the first of its members to hold the consulship.

name: Roman theater at Col. Augusta Raurica
desc: The theater at Augusta Raurica is one of the best preserved Roman theaters north of the Alps.

name: Roman theater at Helvia Ricina
desc: Helvia Ricina flourished under Augustus and Tiberius and its theater is the largest in Picenum.

name: Mausoleum of Lucius Pomponius Grecinus
desc: A Roman funerary monument of the first century B.C. that is traditionally associated with the prefect Lucius Pomponius Grecinus.

name: Roman theater at Antium
desc: The Roman theater at Antium is most likely built in the second half of the first century.

name: Roman theater at Cales
desc: The Roman theater at Cales dates to the first century B.C.

name: Roman theater at Carthage
desc: The Roman theater at Carthage was built around the middle of the second century A.D. It was re-discovered in 1904.

name: Odéon at Carthage
desc: The theater and odéon of Roman Carthage stood in the northeast of the city, some three blocks from the cardo maximus.

name: Carthage military harbor
desc: The cothon at Carthage was divided into a rectangular merchant harbor and an inner protected harbor reserved for military use.

name: Casa di Properzio
desc: The so-called "Casa di Properzio" at Assisi is a Roman domus located near the southern curtain of the ancient city walls. The decorations date the house to the first century B.C.

name: Helikon? (river)

desc: The origins of (H)Enna are unclear. Some sources claim it was founded by Syracuse in 664 B.C., but the archaeological record suggests it is likely a Hellenized Sikel settlement.

name: Heraclea Minoa
desc: An ancient Greek city on the south coast of Sicily, located at the mouth of the Halykos River. Founded by Selinus in the sixth century BC, the site was abandoned in the first century AD.

name: Heraia (mountain)

name: Herbessos?

name: Hexapyla

name: Hiera/Maritima (island)

name: Himera
desc: A colony on the north shore of Sicily founded in 649/8 BC by the Myletidai.

name: Himeras (river)

name: Himeras (river)

name: Hippana

name: Hypsas (river)

name: Hannibal's Bridge (Rapallo)
desc: A ruined bridge at Rapallo, Italy, that the local toponymastic tradition links to the third-century BCE military operations of the Carthaginian commander Hannibal.

name: Ponte delle Voze
desc: A Roman bridge with Augustan origins, known either as Ponte Muto or Ponte delle Vozze, associated with the Via Iulia Augusta and located in the Val Ponci in Liguria.

name: funeral monuments of the Via Iulia Augusta
desc: A Roman necropolis located along the course of the Via Iulia Augusta in modern Albenga, Italy. The archaeological area includes the remains of at least nine tombs dating to the first and second centuries CE. These family tombs faced the ancient roadway. Nino Lamboglia carried out the first archaeolo

name: Martini-Marescotti Tomb
desc: The so-called Martini-Marescotti Tomb is an Etruscan tomb located in the Monte Abatone necropolis of ancient Caere. The tomb was built in the late sixth or early fifth century BCE and is composed of a dromos and three funereal chambers covered by a tumulus. The tomb contained a substantial funereal

name: Fosso del Manganello
desc: The stream known as the Fosso del Manganello is a stream that delimits the northern part of the tuff plateau upon which the Etruscan metropolis of Caere developed.

name: Nuraghe Piscu
desc: A multi-phase nuragic complex dating between 1400 and 1000 BC.

name: San Basilio
desc: A Roman bath complex that was reused first as a monastic complex and then as the Medieval church of San Basilio.

name: Nuraghe Santu Milanu
desc: A single-tower nuraghe with a quadrilobate bastion.

name: Santa Maria di Grottaferrata
desc: St. Nilus of Rossano founded what is now known as the Territorial Abbacy of Saint Mary of Grottaferrata in 1004 on the site of a Roman villa that in local tradition was connected to Marcus Tullius Cicero and alleged to be the place where the latter wrote his Quaestiones tusculanae.

name: Circus of Bovillae
desc: The remains of the arcade of the Roman circus remain visible near the site of ancient Bovillae.

name: Le Muracche Roman villa
desc: A villa rustica at Tortoreto, in the province of Teramo, with occupation beginning in the Late Republican period.

name: Ponte di San Francesco
desc: The Ponte di San Francesco or Bridge of Saint Francis is a single-span medieval segmental arch bridge that crosses the River Aniene in Subiaco, Lazio, Italy. It was built in 1358.

name: Area archeologica di Satricum
desc: The remains of an extensive Roman villa have been documented (amongst other phases) in the village of Le Ferriere, on the grounds of the Casale del Giglio winery. This multi-period, multi-phase settlement demonstrates continuity of human activity, albeit with varying loci of focused activity.

name: Mausoleum of Pianura
desc: A Roman mausoleum of two levels executed in opus vittatum.

name: House of the Bronze Herm
desc: The so-called House of the Bronze Herm is a domus in Herculaneum (III, 16) that takes its name from a bronze statue found at the site.

name: Columbarium, Via di Pietralata
desc: A columbarium was discovered by chance in the Via di Pietralata in Rome in 2012.

name: Church of Sant'Urbano alla Caffarella
desc: A tenth-century church built on the site of a Roman structure that was either a temple or a tomb dating ca. 160 CE.

name: Tanella di Pitagora
desc: A third to second century B.C. tomb in the hinterland of Cortona.

name: House of the Faun
desc: A large private residence constructed ca. 180 BCE in Pompeii (VI.12.2). Its modern name derives from a bronze statue of a faun placed in its impluvium. The house also contained the Alexander Mosaic, a large-scale depiction of the Battle of Issus.

name: Cortaillod-Est
desc: Settlement on the northern shore of Lake Neuchâtel in Switzerland containing the inundated remains of a Bronze Age village, inhabited ca. 1010-955 BC.

name: Teatro romano, Aquino
desc: The Roman theater of Aquinum.

name: Tomb of the Nasonii
desc: The tomb of the Nasonii family is an ancient Roman hypogeum-type tomb along the Via Flaminia in Grottarossa in the northern outskirts of Rome. The tomb was exposed during road works in 1674.

name: Temple of Jupiter
desc: The Temple of Jupiter (VII,8,1) in Pompeii sits at the north end of the forum. It was built in the middle of the second century BC.

name: Forum baths
desc: A bath complex adjacent to Pompeii's forum that was built after 80 BC (Reg VII, Ins 5, 2, 5, 7, 24). The baths are publicly financed by the duovir Lucius Caesius and the aediles Caius Occius and Lucius Niraemius.

name: Sorna Roman Villa and Church
desc: Near Parentium (today Porec/Parenzo in Croatia), Cape Sorna (Zorna) first hosted a large villa maritima, and then a small early Christian church.

name: Lio Piccolo Roman Villa
desc: A probable Roman villa site at Lio Piccolo in the Venice lagoon, with a well-preserved, first-century oyster tank made of brick and wood.

name: Forum of Hippo Regius
desc: The Forum of Hippo Regius is one of the largest known Roman fora in north Africa.

name: Labonia (river)
desc: Labonia is a river included on the Peutinger map. It may be identifiable with the modern Lavanestro.

name: Ponte della Concordia, Fossombrone
desc: A bridge over the Metauro River built initially in the thirteenth century. The original bridge was destroyed in 1765 and rebuilt in 1782. The bridge was again destroyed in 1944 and was rebuilt in 1946.

name: Pons Aurelius
desc: The Pons Aurelius is known only from late Roman documents (fourth and fifth centuries CE) and is most likely the same bridge known as pons Antoninus in the early Middle Ages. The present-day Ponte Sisto (built in the fifteenth century) reused some of the ancient Roman bridge piers.

name: Ponte Sisto
desc: The Ponte Sisto is a bridge that spans the Tiber River at Rome. In the present-day city, it links the Via dei Pettinari (Rione of Regola) to the Piazza Trilussa in Trastevere. The bridge was commissioned by Pope Sixtus IV and was built between 1473 and 1479. Its architect, Baccio Pontelli, reused th

name: Grottini Roman villa
desc: A Roman maritime villa located in Santa Severa on Italy's Tyrrhenian coast.

name: Monumental complex of Sant'Ilario a Port' Aurea
desc: An architectural complex associated with the nearby Longobard church of Sant'Ilario. The complex included a monastery and is built atop Roman Imperial remains.

name: Withdrawn: Diomedis (promontory)
desc: Merged into https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/197309

name: Baths of Decius
desc: A bath complex of ancient Rome built on the Aventine Hill in 252 CE.

name: Temple B (Selinus)
desc: The so-called "Temple B" at Selinus is a small temple dating ca. 250 BCE. It measures 8.40 by 4.60 meters. This was a prostyle aedicular building and may have been sacred to a Hellenized Punic cult.

name: Sepolcro dei Calpurni
desc: Sepolcro dei Calpurni is a Roman hypogeum tomb along the Via Latina that dates to the middle of the first century CE.

name: Casinalbo necropolis
desc: A necropolis of the Terramare culture, located in the present-day province of Modena, Italy.

name: Sanctuary of Minerva at Spinera
desc: A site sacred to Minerva with activity from the Early Iron Age onward, the Sanctuary of Minerva at Spinera is located at Breno on the banks of the river Oglio.

name: Carceri Vecchie
desc: The so-called "le Carceri Vecchie" is a first-century CE Roman mausoleum. Its original position on the Via Appia placed it outside the walls of ancient Capua.

name: Posto villa
desc: The so-called "Posto villa" at Francolise was located in the ancient Ager Falernus of Campania. Its remains lie 500 meters from the so-called "San Rocco" villa. This was a small villa rustica whose incipit comes ca. 100 BC.

name: Arch of Marcus Antonius
desc: The so-called "Arch of Marcus Antonius" takes its name from a local tradition that the citizens of Aquinum built the monument in a single day to honor Antonius. In all likelihood, it is a monument connected either to a deductio of veterans sent to Aquinum in 41 BCE or to the work of Caius Calvisius

name: Is Pirois
desc: A sacred well sanctuary, Pozzo sacro Is Pirois, is associated with the Nuragic culture. Is Pirois is located in the municipality of Villaputzu, in metropolitan Cagliari. The well is built of schist, and the covering structure is a pseudo-dome or tholos.

name: Casa dei Grifi
desc: A late Republican domus of the Palatine Hill that was later consumed by the substructures of the Domitianic wing of the Flavian palace. The Casa dei Grifi preserves important wall paintings that are transitional from the First to the Second Pompeian style. Giacomo Boni discovered the domus in 1912.

name: Cati fons
desc: The Cati fons was a spring located on the western flank of Rome's Quirinal Hill. It was the source of the water carried by the brook known as Petronia amnis. The location of the spring remains debated and uncertain.

name: Fortino di Mazzallakkar
desc: A ruined ninth-century Arabic fort on the shores of Sicily's Lago Arancio.

name: Tomb of Publius Aelius Callistion
desc: The tomb of Publius Aelius Callistion, a freedman (libertus) of the emperor Hadrian, is colloquially known as the "Sedia del Diavolo". It is located in a piazza that derives its name from the tomb's occupant (piazza Elio Callistio) in Rome's Trieste neighborhood.

name: Ponte del Diavolo
desc: A bridge in the territory of Blera known as the "Devil's Bridge".

name: Picentino (river)
desc: A river of Campania that is connected to the now-lost settlement of Picentia and the Picentinus Ager.

name: So-called Arch of Hadrian (Capua)
desc: The remains of a triple arch in opus latericium marking the pomerium of Capua. It is perhaps originally constructed under the Flavians.

name: Ponte di Pioraco
desc: A single-arch Roman bridge built during the principate of Augustus.

name: Ponte Funicchio
desc: A Roman bridge dating to the late second century B.C.

name: Tre Ponti necropolis
desc: A necropolis along the Via Amerina, likely in use from the third century BC until the third century AD.

name: Sant'Ilario
desc: A paleochristian site located at the thirtieth mile of the ancient via Labicana, near to the ancient road station 'ad Bivium'.

name: Catacombs of Domitilla
desc: A Christian catacomb located on the via Ardeatina.

name: Satricum, Southwest Necropolis
desc: The Southwest Necropolis located at Satricum.

name: Villa Romana di Caselette
desc: A Roman villa of the first century CE located near Farchetto, Italy.

name: Roman Villa of San Giovanni Del Palco
desc: The remains of a Roman villa located adjacent to the Convent of San Giovanni del Palco in Taurano, Italy. The convent, founded in 1383 at the Niccolò Orsini, utilizes elements of the villa's structural remains in its foundations.

name: Walls of Timoleon
desc: The Greek fortifications of Gela that are credited to Timoleon of Corinth.

name: Via Aemilia
desc: The Via Aemilia was a major Roman trunk road of northern Italy and connected Placentia and Ariminum. Its construction began in 187 BC under M. Aemilius Lepidus.

name: S’Ena ’e Thomes
desc: A well-preserved 'giant's tomb' dating ca. 2000-1600 BC.

name: Incastro River
desc: The Incastro is a river of Latium that drains the waters originating from the Lago di Nemi. Its ancient name is unknown.

name: Paedagogium
desc: The so-called Pedagogium is a building that was part of the Flavian palace complex on the Palatine Hill. It was located below the exedra of the façade of the Domus Augustana. The Paedagogium is thought to have superseded the late-Republican domus known as the Domus Gelotiana.

name: domus Gelotiana
desc: A domus on the slope of the Palatine Hill that Caius incorporated into the Imperial Palace complex.

name: Porta Asinaria
desc: The Porta Asinaria is a gate of the Aurelian Walls on the Caelian Hill, located immediately southwest of the Porta S. Giovanni.

name: Circus Flaminius
desc: Located in the southern Campus Martius, the Circus Flaminius is a large area built by C. Flaminius Nepos in 221 B.C. Various games, including the ludi plebeii, ludi Taurii, ludi saeculares, were celebrated here. The circus was also a place of popular assembly.

name: Parco Archeologico Sommerso di Baia
desc: The underwater archaeological park of Baia is a protected marine and cultural heritage area. Submerged beneath the waters of the Gulf of Naples are various Roman-period archaeological remains, including those of harbors, villas, shrines, and nymphaea.

name: Punta Epitaffio nymphaeum
desc: A now-submerged nymphaeum that dates to the reign of Claudius.

name: Nuraghe Arrubiu
desc: A Middle Bronze Age nuragic site (ca. 1500 BC) near Cagliari, Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Albucciu
desc: A nuragic village dating ca. 1600 BC.

name: Gremanu
desc: A 7-hectare nuragic settlement and sanctuary.

name: Potto Codinu necropolis
desc: A necropolis in use from the Neolithic period through to the Iron Age with numerous hypogeum-type tombs.

name: Fundus Babuleianus
desc: An estate located near Interamna Lirenas.

name: Tomb of Tiberius Claudius Secundus
desc: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia.

name: Via Annia
desc: The Via Annia was a Roman consular road in Cisalpine Gaul that connected (H)Atria to Aquileia. The praetor Titus Annius Rufus constructed the road in 131 BC.

name: Cuccuru Nuraxi
desc: A nuragic site near Cagliari, Sardinia.

name: Mausoleo di Ummidia Quadratilla
desc: A Roman tomb located in the archaeological area of Casinum that dates to either the first or second centuries CE.

name: Roman baths of Aquinum
desc: Roman baths at Aquinum.

name: Santa Liberata
desc: A coastal platform villa conneted with the Domitii Ahenobarbi.

name: Nuraghe Vignamarina
desc: A single-tower nuraghe with an associated village.

name: Ponte Altinate
desc: A late Republican Roman segmented arch bridge in Padua, Italy.

name: Mausoleum of Lucius Sempronius Atratinus
desc: A first-century B.C. circular funerary monument at Gaeta.

name: Vallerano
desc: A necropolis located on the southern outskirts of Rome. The necropolis is located near a villa site along a road running through the suburbium of Rome. Excavated between 1992 and 1993.

name: Acquedotto Anio Novus Ponte S. Antonio
desc: The Ponte S. Antonio carried the Anio Novus aqueduct.

name: Grotte Scalina
desc: A monumental rock-cut Etruscan tomb that dates to the later fourth century B.C.

name: Grotta Scaloria
desc: A cavern discovered in 1931 near Manfredonia with evidence for ritual activity dating to the Neolithic period.

name: Catacomb of Balbina
desc: The Catacomb of Balbina in the suburbium of Rome lies between the via Appia antica and the via Ardeatina in Rome's Ardeatino district. This catacomb is part of the larger Callixtian complex that includes the catacombs of Callixtus and Santi Marco e Marcelliano. The Depositio episcoporum mentions the

name: Small Roman Theater or Odeon at Sisak
desc: Documented in media released by the Croatian Ministry of Culture and Media in 2025, remains of a small theater or odeon of Roman date have been identified and consolidated under the early 20th-century city hall of modern Sisak in Croatia (ancient Segestica/Siscia). name: Samnites
desc: An ancient, Oscan-speaking people who lived in the central southern part of the Apennine mountains in Italy.

name: S. Brancato
desc: At modern San Brancato (Sant'Arcangelo, Basilicata, Italy), multiple excavations since the 1980s have identified a large Lucanian necropolis dating to the 4th-3rd centuries CE.

desc: Scamnum is a road station located in Messapia that is mentioned on the Tabula Peutingeriana. It is perhaps to be identified with excavations at the site of Muro Tenente that have revealed long term occupation levels, beginning from the Neolithic period.

name: Sicalenum?/Kalena
desc: An ancient settlement in the Abruzzo mentioned by Polybius in the account of the Battle of Geronium during the Second Punic War.

name: Silarus (river)
desc: The Sele river.

name: Silvium
desc: Silvium (modern Gravina in Puglia) was founded as a Greek colony. It was a town on the frontier of the Peucetii.

name: Sipous/Sipontum
desc: Sipous/Sipontum was a Greek colony that fell first under Samnite control, then was later taken by Alexander of Epirus. The site became a Roman colony in 189 BC. Legend ascribed its foundation to the hero Diomedes.

name: Soletum
desc: Soletum was a settlement in ancient Calabria.

desc: A Greek colonial city founded in 706 B.C.

name: Taras (river)
desc: An ancient river of south Italy, debouching into the Gulf of Taranto to the northwest of the ancient city. The coastal landscape and river course have seen changes since antiquity, but the modern Fiume Tara is normally associated with its ancient predecessor.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 45 C1 Tatinie

desc: A town in ancient Apulia located between Larinum and and Sipontum. Rome took control of the site in 318 BC, granting it municipal status.

desc: Vibinum/Vibarna was an ancient settlement in Campania that opposed Rome during the Samnite Wars.

name: House of Menander
desc: A large Pompeian townhouse belonging to one Q. Poppaeus Sabinus at the time of its destruction (I, 10, 4, 14-16). The earliest portions of the domus may date ca. 250 BCE.

desc: The remains of a Roman road in southeastern Sardinia.

desc: A monopteral nuraghe located near Nuoro, Sardinia.

name: Graeco-Roman theater at Marina di Gioiosa Ionica
desc: A second-century B.C. theater that represents a point of architectural transition from the Greek-style theater building to the Roman typology.

name: Temple of Hercules Victor
desc: A monopteros in the Forum Boarium at Rome built in the late second century BC, perhaps by L. Mummius Achaicus.

name: Sacred Area of S. Omobono
desc: An archaeological area in the Forum Boarium comprising an ancient ritual precinct with twin temples ranging in date from the Archaic period through the time of the Roman Empire. The Medieval church dedicated to S. Omobono stands atop the remains of one of the two ancient temples.

name: Porta Collina
desc: A gate in Rome's Servian Wall located on the Quirinal Hill.

name: Via Severiana
desc: The Via Severiana was a coastal route running from Ostia to Terracina, a distance of ca. 80 Roman miles.

name: Tunnels of Claudius
desc: An approximately 6 km. long tunnel built under Roman emperor Claudius in 52 CE for the purposes of attempting to drain the Lacus Fucinus.

name: Church of Saint Herculanus
desc: A paleochristian site near Ostia generally dated to the fourth or fifth century CE. It is associated with Claudius II Gothicus and is the findspot of the bulk of the Christian epigraphy known from ancient Ostia.

name: Pantano Borghese
desc: The estate (tenuta) of Pantano Borghese is one of the oldest land holdings in the Agro Romano and was acquired by the Colonna family in 1613. Much of this low-lying area was once marshland at the margins of the crater lakes of this part of Latium. Thomas Ashby's work on the Roman Campagna documented

name: Columbarium in via Luigi Tosti
desc: Excavations in 2022 revealed the remains of a Roman tomb of small dimensions, likely of the columbarium type. The tomb included fragments of a sarcophagus in white marble and an inscribed funerary altar of the second century CE. The altar commemorates the life of one Valeria Laeta, daughter of Publi

name: Lago di Giulianello
desc: The Lago di Giulianello is a lake located in the territory of Giulianello in Lazio, central Italy.

name: Torre dei Capocci
desc: The Torre dei Capocci, together with the Torre dei Graziani, was built in the twelfth century by the Arcioni family as a monumentalized entrance to the Esquiline.

name: Torre dei Graziani
desc: The Torre dei Graziani is a twelfth-century tower on the Esquiline Hill in Rome.

name: Clivus Suburanus
desc: The Clivus Suburanus was a street of the ancient city of Rome. It rose from the Oppian and Cispian Hills and continued to the Porta Esquilina. Some current urban streets - via in Selci, via di San Martino, and via di S. Vito - approximate at least part of its course.

name: Late Antique domus
desc: The structure that now stands at Via in Selci no. 82 in the city of Rome rests on the structural remains of a late Roman building that likely date to the fourth or fifth century. These structural remains are likely those of the basilical hall that often was part of a Late Antique domus.

name: Alta Semita
desc: The Alta Semita was an urban street running along the spine of the Quirinal Hill. The Alta Semita also lent its name to the sixth Augustan region of the city.

name: Roman amphitheater at Urbs Salvia
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Urbs Salvia.

name: So-called House of the Mosaic Columns
desc: Suburban villa outside the Herculaneum gate in Pompeii

name: Porticus Octaviae
desc: A porticus in the area of the Circus Flaminius, the Porticus Octaviae was dedicated by Augustus sometime after 27 B.C. in honor of his sister, Octavia Minor. The porticus replaced the Porticus Metelli. It was restored twice after major urban fires in A.D. 80 and 203.

name: Forre di Corchiano
desc: The Forre di Corchiano is a preserved landscape significant not only for its landforms but also for cultural heritage remains pertaining to many periods.

name: Castellina del Marangone
desc: A small fortified coastal settlement in Etruria occupied from the tenth century B.C. to the first century B.C.

name: Ponte di Traiano
desc: A Trajanic bridge along the Via Appia that crosses the fosso Striscia.

name: Necropolis at Sutrium
desc: Numerous rock-cut tombs are evident at Sutri, most dating from the Hellenistic period and later. In archaeological terms the tombs are poorly understood.

name: Ponte Acque Alte
desc: A Roman bridge along the Via Appia near Cisterna di Latina.

name: Crypta Neapolitana
desc: A rock-cut tunnel of the Via Domitiana built during the first century BC under the direction of Lucius Cocceius Auctus.

name: Castrum Rauracense
desc: A Late Roman fortress located on the southern bank of the Rhine adjacent to Augusta Raurica.

name: Regio VIII, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio VIII, an archaeological subdivision located in the southwestern section of Pompeii, contains a theatre, a sanctuary dedicated to Venus, and a mix of residential, administrative, and commercial structures.

name: Africum Mare
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 1 D3/F3 Africum Mare

name: Alpes (mountains)
desc: The Alps are one of the great mountain ranges of Europe stretching some 1,200 km. (750 miles).

name: Ap(p)enninus M.
desc: The Apennine Mountains extend ca. 1,200 km (750 miles) along the length of peninsular Italy.

name: Casa del Fabbro
desc: Casa del Fabbro or House of the Cabinet Maker is a domus located in Pompeii's Regio I. It derives its modern appellation from an extensive set of carpentry tools found in situ during excavation. The site was excavated in 1914, 1927, and 1933.

name: Tagliata Falisca Cava di Sant'Egidio
desc: An instance of a 'via cava' located near Corchiano, Italy.

name: Villa of Masseria Ciccotti
desc: A Roman villa along the via Herculea near Oppido Lucano.

name: Pollina
desc: Modern town in Sicily, near Cefalù, that has been associated with the ancient settlement of Apollonia.

name: Domus della Fortuna Annonaria
desc: The so-called "Domus della Fortuna Annonaria" (V,II,8) is an ancient peristyle house with a nymphaeum located in Ostia. Its initial construction likely dates to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

name: Prato La Corte
desc: A villa rustica was excavated near Licenza in 1913, the exact position of which is no longer known. This site included a possible granary room, as well as a torcular.

name: Tomb of the Winged Demons
desc: The so-called Tomb of the Winged Demons (Sovana, Italy), a third-century BC Etruscan tomb located in the Poggio Felceto necropolis.

name: Roman amphitheater at Albano Laziale
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Albano Laziale is generally dated to the mid-third century A.D.

name: Roman cistern
desc: A large Roman cistern at Albano Laziale.

name: Caselle in Pittari
desc: An ancient Lucanian settlement located within the territory of the comune of Caselle in Pittari has been explored via archaeological excavation since 2014. This site occupies parts of a large plateau. Evidence for an axial road running north-south and several large structures has been documented.

name: Longola di Poggiomarino
desc: An archaeological site discovered accidentally in 2000 to the east of Vesuvius in the valley of the Sarno River that preserves important Bronze Age occupational contexts.

name: Lateran Basilica, Palace, and Castra Nova equitum singularium
desc: Site of a basilica and palace from early Roman imperial times, as well as an military installation built by Septimius Severus for the Roman imperial cavalry bodyguard. name: Catacomba di San Giovanni
desc: Ancient catacombs in the city of Siracusa, built between AD 315 and 360. The main gallery re-purposes parts of an earlier aqueduct.

name: Forum Traiani
desc: Imperial forum constructed at Rome under Trajan between 105-112 CE.

name: S. Pietro ad centum muros
desc: On the hill of Grignano, located on the outskirts of Montebuono, the remains of a Roman villa were first excavated in the nineteenth century in the area of the church of "S. Pietro ad centum muros". Excavation in the 1990s revealed further villa remains beneath the church and in the vicinity of its

name: San Nicola di Trullas
desc: A Medieval church on the island of Sardinia that is dated to 1133.

name: Mura Abbandonate, Sanctuary of Fondo Decina
desc: A terraced sanctuary of the Samnite culture that was in use from the archaic period to the third century B.C.

name: Avenches Roman amphitheater
desc: The Avenches Roman amphitheater.

name: Porta Pretoria (Albano Laziale)
desc: The principal gateway of Castra Albana.

name: Agora of Halaesa
desc: The agora of the ancient city of Halaesa (second century B.C.), now within the archaeological area of Alesa Arconidea, Sicily.

name: Vacri Italic temple
desc: An Italic temple was identified in 1975 in the locality known as Porcareccia, Vacri (Chieti), Italy.

name: Nuraghe Sa Bosa
desc: The remains of a nuraghe near an industrial zone near Sassari.

name: Loron workshop (Croatia)
desc: Located in the territory of Parentium (Poreč, Croatia), Loron was one of the largest Dressel 6B amphorae workshops in Adriatic (1st-4th centuries CE). name: Pagus Augustus Felix Suburbanus
desc: The ancient Pagus Augustus Felix Suburbanus corresponds to the territory of today's city of Boscoreale and Boscotrecase. Originating around 80 B.C. with the name of Pagus Felix Suburbanus, it included many farms.

name: Giant's tomb at Lu Brandali
desc: A passage grave associated with the nuragic complex at Lu Brandali near Santa Teresa Gallura.

name: Arch of the Sergii
desc: A Roman triumphal arch at Pula commemorating Lucius Sergius Lepidus and the family of the Sergii for service at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC.

name: Malo rimsko kazalište (Roman theater)
desc: The Roman theater in Pula dates to the first century.

name: Underground Shrine (Paestum)
desc: A small, underground tomb-like structure located in the agora of Paestum, thought to be either a shrine or a heroon.

name: Porta Marina tower of Poseidonia/Paestum
desc: The so-called Porta Marina of Paestum is a gate in the Hellenistic fortifications and is located along a main street axis leading to the port of the city.

name: House of Plotilla
desc: The House of Plotilla, also known as Casa di Apollo e Coronide, was excavated in 1815 and again in 1839. It lies in Regio VIII of Pompeii.

name: Workshop of Anteros
desc: A taberna on the Via dell'Abbondanza identified as perhaps the Workshop of Anteros. This location is also linked to the Collegium Aurificum by means of electoral graffiti.

name: Arch of Caius and Lucius Caesar (Pompeii)
desc: An arched entranceway located in the northwest corner of the Forum of Pompeii.

name: Horrea Agrippiana
desc: A set of warehouses in Regio VIII.

name: Domus Lucina
desc: The Domus Lucina was located on the Via Lata, which is the site where a certain widowed matrona named Lucina harbored Marcellus I and then established a church in his name.

name: Tomb of the sons of Sextus Pompeius Justus
desc: A tomb on the Via Appia dated ca. 50 CE.

name: Sanctuary of the Public Lares
desc: A sanctuary located on the east side of Pompeii's forum (VII, 9, 3), the Sanctuary of the Public Lares was likely built after AD 62. The sanctuary measures ca. 18 x 21 m and centers on an open central courtyard.

name: Mensa Ponderaria
desc: The Mensa ponderaria (VII,7,31) was an official public office adjacent to the forum of Pompeii wherein weights and measures were regulated. This location was in use from the late second century BC.

name: Tomb of Septimia Galla
desc: A Roman tomb at the sixth mile of the Via Appia.

name: Thermae of Hippo Regius
desc: The northern bath complex of Hippo Regius.

name: Torrente delle Ferriere
desc: The Torrente delle Ferriere or Fosso della Mola is a stream that bounds the tuff plateau upon which the Etruscan metropolis of Caere developed.

name: Sorgenti della Nova
desc: An eleventh and tenth century B.C. settlement in south Etruria.

name: Guild Temple and Mithraeum of Fructosus
desc: An architectural complex excavated in 1938 at the intersection of Via del Pomerio and Via del Tempio Rotondo in Ostia. The guild temple dates to the reign of Alexander Severus (222 - 235 CE). Based on epigraphic evidence, this shrine may belong to the guild of the stuppatores. A mithraic shrine with

name: Abbey of San Clemente a Casauria
desc: The Abbey of San Clemente a Casauria (Italian: Abbazia di San Clemente a Casauria) is located along the ancient Via Claudia Valeria in the territory of Castiglione a Casauria, province of Pescara, Abruzzo. Louis II (a great-grandson of Charlemagne) founded the abbey in 871. It was dedicated to Saint

name: Roman amphitheater of Virunum
desc: The Virunum Roman amphitheater is located in Maria Saal, Austria.

name: Monumental Mid-Republican Building Complex
desc: This monumental complex of buildings at the city of Gabii was likely constructed in the mid-third century BCE as a public area for feasts, bathing, and ritual activities.

name: Villa Romana di Punta San Limato
desc: The ruins of a Roman villa located in the modern Italian locality of Punta San Limato, province of Caserta.

name: Mithraeum of the Seven Gates
desc: The so-called Mithraeum of the Seven Gates was built at Ostia in the second century CE, repurposing rooms that originally date to the previous century.

name: Ponte Ezzu
desc: Ponte Ezzu or Pont'Ezzu is a Roman bridge of the first century A.D. that crosses the Rio Mannu near Ozieri, Sardinia.

name: Ponte romano di Santa Giusta
desc: A Roman bridge dating between the first century BC and the first century AD.

name: Temple of Vespasian and Titus
desc: A temple in the Roman Forum dedicated to the deified Vespasian that was begun by Titus and completed under Domitian.

name: Mausoleo di San Vito at Puteoli
desc: A mausoleum in the so-called San Vito necropolis that dates to the first century A.D.

name: Mausoleum of Lucius Munatius Plancus
desc: A Roman mausoleum that is associated with Lucius Munatius Plancus.

name: Roman amphitheater at Grumentum
desc: Grumentum's amphitheater (first century B.C.) is the only known example in Lucania. The arena measures ca. 62.5 by 60 meters.

name: Roman theater at Casinum
desc: The Roman theater at Casinum dates to the Augustan period.

name: Roman amphitheater at Marruvium
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Marruvium measures 95 by 75 meters.

name: Roman amphitheater at Frusino
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Frusino measures ca. 78 by 57 meters.

name: Roman amphitheater at Al(l)ifae
desc: Remains of a Roman amphitheater dating to the later first century A.D.

name: Roman amphitheater at Telesia
desc: A Late Republican Roman amphitheater at Telesia.

name: Temple D
desc: The temple referred to as "Temple D" in the Largo Argentina is likely the Aedes Lares Permarini, sacred to the lares who protect sailors. The largest of the temples in this sacred area, "Temple D" dates to the second century B.C. and remains largely unexcavated.

name: Temple A
desc: So-called "Temple A" is a structure of the third century B.C. and is likely the Temple of Juturna that was vowed by Caius Lutatius Catulus following his victory against the Carthaginians in 241 B.C. It was later converted into a church, the apse of which remains visible.

name: Temple C
desc: The so-called "Temple C" of the Largo Argentina sacred area may be dedicated to the Italic goddess Feronia.

name: Roman theater at Verona
desc: The Roman theater at Verona dates from the late first century B.C.

name: Public baths at Saepinum
desc: The public baths at Saepinum are located along the decumanus and date to the first and second centuries.

name: Basilica at Saepinum
desc: The Basilica at Saepinum is positioned at the intersection of the cardo and the decumanus.

name: Roman theater at Carsulae
desc: The Roman theater at Carsulae dates to the Augustan period, pre-dating the amphitheater.

name: Forum of Carsulae
desc: The Forum of Carsulae is supported by terraces and it includes the basilica and a twin sanctuary, in addition to tabernae.

name: So-called twin sanctuary
desc: A double sanctuary on the forum of Carsulae. It is no longer clear to which gods these temples belonged.

name: Forum of Suasa
desc: The Forum of Suasa measures 50 x 100 meters and is surrounded by a portico.

name: House of the Cryptoporticus at Vulci
desc: A well-appointed Roman domus with a large, well-preserved cryptoporticus. The earliest phase belongs to the late second and early first century B.C. with subsequent modifications during the early Imperial period.

name: Church of St. Peter
desc: A twelfth-century AD Christian church was built atop the remains of the Roman temple of Apollo.

name: Busa delle Vette
desc: A hut and some enclosures located in the Dolomites (Veneto, Italy), datable to between the 5th and 11th centuries CE.

name: Valcamonica
desc: Located in the Lombardy plain, the Valcamonica assemblage constitutes one of the world's greatest collections of prehistoric petroglyphs – created over a period of 8,000 years. The site was enlisted by UNESCO in 1971.

name: Ponte Etrusco, Gallese
desc: The so-called "Ponte Etrusco" is an ancient bridge located near Gallese in the province of Viterbo, Italy.

name: Ponte Nepesino
desc: A bridge along the Via Amerina, just south of ancient Nepet (modern Nepi in Italy)

name: Grotta dell'Uzzo
desc: The Grotta dell'Uzzo is an important archaeological site in Sicily with traces of human settlement beginning 10,000 years BP.

name: Ponte Romano di Parco dei Medici
desc: The ruins of a second-century A.D. Roman bridge at Magliana Vecchia.

name: Ponte Sanguinario (Narni)
desc: A Roman bridge located near Narni, Italy.

name: Roman Mausoleum
desc: A Roman tower-type tomb that some local traditions label as the tomb of Cnaeus Pompeius Magnus. The structure is located at the so-called Villa di Pompeo, south of Castel Gandolfo in Italy.

name: Rocca di Cerere
desc: The Rocca di Cerere (Rock of Ceres) is a rocky outcrop located in the city of Enna, Sicily. It was used as a fortified acropolis in antiquity. Roman soldiers are reported to have sacked the temple atop the rocca in 173 BCE.

name: Mithraeum at Fertőrákos
desc: A well-preserved Mithraeum with modern stone vault above ground and site below in Fertőrákos, Hungary, at the site of ancient Scarbantia.

name: Capitolinus Mons
desc: The smallest of Rome's hills and one of its most important, the Capitoline Hill served as the citadel (arx) of the city and as the site of its poliadic temple.

name: Arcus Argentariorum
desc: A commemorative arch located in the Velabrum dedicated to the Severan emperors in AD 204 by the local association of money-changers (argentarii) and merchants (negotiantes). It was later incorporated into the church of S. Giorgio al Velabro.

name: Polygonal masonry wall
desc: An extant segment of a Polygonal masonry wall in Caiazzo.

name: Domus and Mitreo delle Pareti Dipinte
desc: The complex known as "Domus and Mitreo delle Pareti Dipinte" began its life in the later second century BCE and was remodeled during the time of Augustus. A mithraeum is built in the northwest part of the building in the later second century CE.

name: Necropoli del Cavone di Monte Li Santi
desc: A monumental, rock-cut Faliscan necropolis of Narce in use from ca. 750 BCE until the fourth century BCE.

name: Santa Maria in Portuno
desc: A vicus and villa of the Roman period that lay along a route connecting the Via Flaminia to the coast. Archaeological evidence for the production of ceramics and tiles has been identified. A Christian monastery is established in 1090.

name: Tratturo Caniò
desc: Tratturo Caniò is an archaeological site in the territory of the ancient city of Setia, on the Pontine Plain of Lazio, Italy. An archaic temple sacred to Iuno is known at the site, and archaeological prospection in 2009 revealed earlier Bronze Age and Iron Age remains.

name: Villa di via della Magliana
desc: The remains of a Roman villa on land that is now mostly consumed by a golf course connected to a hotel resort.

name: Montefalcone nel Sannio
desc: Two peaks rise in the vicinity of the Italian comune of Montefalcone nel Sannio in the valley of the Trigno River. name: Arpaia milestone
desc: A Roman milestone of the Via Appia located in Arpaia, Italy.

name: Nuraghe Sas Luzzanas
desc: A nuraghe located near Sas Contreddas, Sardinia.

name: Necropolis of Mesu ‘e Montes
desc: The Necropolis of Mesu ‘e Montes contains at least 18 tombs of the domus de janas type. The necropolis dates from the later Neolithic period to the middle Bronze Age.

name: Necropolis of Su Crucifissu Mannu
desc: A prehistoric necropolis at Porto Torres, Sardinia, containing at least 22 domus de ianas type tombs.

name: Nostra Segnora de Mesumundu
desc: Nostra Segnora de Mesumundu ("Our Lady of Mesumundu") is located in the territory of Siligo, Sardinia, Italy. This archaeological site preserves remains of multiple architectural phases. A mid-Imperial (likely second-century CE) Roman complex, which included baths, was reused, in part, for the const

name: Bitti, Complesso di Romanzesu
desc: A 7-hectare nuragic complex.

name: Seruci
desc: A nuragic complex including a central nuraghe and an associated village.

name: Nuraghe s'Ulimu
desc: A two-tower nuraghe located near Ulassai in the province of Nuoro.

name: Vejano
desc: Vejano, located in the Province of Viterbo, is located on the Mignone river approximately 60 km northwest of Rome. While the most visible monument on the site today is the fifteenth century castle known as "La Rocca", the site has a long settlement history reaching back to the Bronze Age.

name: duplicate: Ekklesiasterion
desc: This place resource has been moved to Errata because it is a duplicate for https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/966917974

name: Forum of Vulci
desc: The forum of the ancient town, dating to the Roman period.

name: Roman theater of Lokroi Epizephyrioi
desc: A Roman theater of the first century B.C. was built on the site of the fourth century B.C. Greek theater.

name: Etruscan acropolis at Volaterrae
desc: The multi-phase acropolis of Etruscan Volaterrae has numerous important phases, beginning in the Archaic period. The monumental site continued to develop and grow during the Hellenistic period. It was identified archaeologically only in the nineteenth century. In the twentieth century it was the sub

name: Roman theater at Volaterrae
desc: The Roman theater of Volaterrae was built during the during the Augustan period under the consulship of Aulus Caecina Severus.

name: Pompeii II.3.7 garden entrance
desc: Pompeii II, 3, 7 is a garden entrance linked to II, 3, 8 and II, 3,9. II, 3, 8 is identified as a workshop, either the Officina vasaria or caupona of Nicanor. This complex was positioned across the street from the Palaestra.

name: Necropolis of Anghelu Ruju
desc: A pre-nuragic necropolis discovered in 1903.

name: Gardens of Maecenas
desc: The Gardens of Maecenas or "Horti Maecenatis" were extensive, planned gardens laid out on Rome's Esquiline Hill by Caius Cilinius Maecenas in the mid-30s B.C. These formal gardens occupied what had previously been the agger of the Servian walls and the adjacent necropolis that had an unsavory reputa

name: Mount Fumaiolo
desc: A mountain of the northern Apennines (elevation 1,408 m; 4,619 ft) from which the Tiber River originates.

name: Poggio Colla
desc: An Etruscan settlement located in the Mugello valley.

name: Nuraghe Diana
desc: A single-tower nuraghe located near Quartu Sant'Elena.

name: Algund
desc: A bridge on the Via Claudia Augusta crossing the Adige river near Maiensis Statio.

name: Bagni di Nerone
desc: The so-called "Baths of Nero" are located near the Porta a Lucca in Pisa.

name: Podere S. Mario
desc: A rural site located in the territory of Volterra.

name: La Befa, Carcerelle
desc: The Roman villa rustica of La Befa is positioned at the point where the Torrente di Crevoli joins the river Ombrone. Excavation of the site identified a northern sector and a southern sector, both with multiple architectural phases, likely beginning the later first century CE.

name: Santa Cristina in Caio a Buonconvento (Siena)
desc: An ancient vicus with a thermal complex (first century BCE to fourth century CE) with phases of post-ancient re-use. The site is located in the modern Italian municipal territory of Buonconvento, Tuscany.

name: Pianello di Genga
desc: Pianello di Genga, located in Italy's Ancona province, was the site of a Final Bronze Age settlement, as attested by an extensive necropolis.

name: Early Christian Necropolis of Pécs (Sopianae)
desc: A series of decorated early Christian tombs dating to the fourth century CE is located in the town of Sopianae, in the Roman Province of Pannonia. The Early Christian Necropolis of Pécs was enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

name: Via Julia Augusta
desc: A road begun in 13 BC by Augustus that was, in effect, a merging of the Via Postumia and the Via Aemilia Scauri.

name: Mura Messapiche
desc: Well-preserved remains of the ashlar fortification walls at Manduria.

name: Castello di Decima
desc: The "Castello di Decima" is a fortified complex located in the frazione of Castel di Decima. The fortification is located at the tenth mile of the ancient Via Laurentina. name: Falerna
desc: A rural tribe of Rome, which was established in 318 B.C.

name: Domus Clementis
desc: The remains of a private domus that date to the second and third centuries CE and include a Mithraeum. This complex eventually became incorporated into the fourth-century basilica on the site of the later basilica of San Clemente al Laterano.

name: Tomb of Virgil
desc: The so-called tomb of the Latin poet Virgil.

name: Tomb of Nigidius Alleius Maius
desc: The Tomb of Nigidius Alleius Maius was excavated in 2017. The tomb includes a 'res gestae'-style inscription in Latin that describes the life, career, and patronage of the decedent. Although the name of the decedent is no longer extant, the tomb has been linked to prominent citizen Nigidius Alleius

name: Lago di Fogliano
desc: A shallow, brackish coastal lagoon located in the Pontine plain in central Italy, the Lago di Fogliano has provided archaeological evidence for ancient human settlement in the coastal zone and paleo-climatological data.

name: South Etruria Survey area
desc: The original and pioneering South Etruria Survey was led by J.B. Ward-Perkins of the British School at Rome from the 1950s to the 1970s.
