name: Tor di Mezzavia di Frascati
desc: The Tor di Mezzavia is a Medieval tower located along the modern Via Tuscolana, marking the midway point between Rome and Frascati.

name: Roman amphitheater of Venusia
desc: A Roman amphitheater dating to the first and second centuries.

name: Pottenbrunn burial ground
desc: Burial site near modern Pottenbrunn, Austria, containing 43 burials dated to the Roman period.

name: Torre Chiaruccia
desc: A masonry tower built in the sixteenth century near the ruined site of Castrum Novum (Santa Marinella, Italy).

name: Cancello e Arnone
desc: The ruins of a Roman villa of the ager Falernus were discovered at Cancello e Arnone during work on a green energy facility.

name: Withdrawn duplicate: Roman amphitheater at Volaterrae
desc: This place record has been withdrawn and moved to errata because it is a duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/435476404

name: Temple F at Selinus
desc: Temple F at Selinus is a Doric temple located on the site's so-called "East Hill". Dedicated either to Athena or Dionysus, the temple dates to the middle of the sixth century B.C. The non-canonical ground plan of 6 x 14 columns gives the temple an elongated aspect.

name: Roman bath at Volaterrae
desc: A bath complex located adjacent to the theater of Volaterrae.

name: Mura greche di Hipponion
desc: The Greek walls of the city of Hipponion, later Vibo Valentia, were established in the sixth century BCE. They originally stood to some 10 meters in height and had a circuit of 6 to 7 kilometers. The extant tracts were rediscovered in the early twentieth century and excavated by Paolo Orsi.

name: House of the cithara player
desc: The so-called "House of the cithara player" (I,4,5 and 25) opens both on to the Via Stabiana and the Via dell'Abbondanza. One of the largest aristocratic homes in Pompeii, it was formed from two adjoining properties.

name: House of Octavius Quartio
desc: The House of Octavius Quartio or the House of Loreius Tiburtinus (II,2,2).

name: Porta Nocera
desc: A city gate of Pompeii located at the southern terminus of Strada di Porta Nocera.

name: tribus Arnensis
desc: The tribus Arnensis was one of the later rural tribes of Rome, which was established in 387 B.C.

name: Porta Nola
desc: A city gate located at the eastern terminus of the Strada di Nola. In antiquity, the gate was known as Porta Urbulana.

name: tribus Camilia
desc: The tribus Camilia is one of the sixteen oldest rural tribes of Rome.

name: Monte Li Santi
desc: A Faliscan sanctuary located on the slopes of Monte Li Santi.

name: Gallo-Roman bath complex at Mackwiller
desc: A Gallo-Roman bath complex located at the modern town of Mackwiller in the French commune of Waldhambach.

name: Via Latina
desc: A Roman road running southeast from Rome toward Campania.

name: Vicus Iugarius
desc: An ancient street that led from the Forum Romanum to the porta Carmentalis, passing between the basilica Iulia and the temple of the Castors.

name: Roman theater of Alba Fucens
desc: The Roman theater of Alba Fucens

name: Domus of Titus Macer
desc: The House of Titus Macer at Aquileia dates to the middle of the first century CE when at least two pre-exisiting domus were merged to form a single domus covering more than 1,500 square meters.

name: Ponte degli Arcinelli
desc: The so-called "Ponte degli Arcinelli" is a Roman aqueduct bridge that was part of the Aqua Anio Novus.

name: Ringwall Rentmauer (Weilrod)
desc: A Celtic hill fort from the La Tène period.

name: Temple of Vesta at Rome
desc: The Temple of Vesta, located at the east end of the Forum Romanum.

name: Temple C (Selinus)
desc: The so-called Temple C at Selinus is a Doric temple that dates to the second half of the sixth century B.C.

name: Villa romana di via Carciano
desc: A Roman villa dating to the second century A.D.

name: Pagliano Roman port
desc: A riverine port near the confluence of the Tiber and Paglia rivers.

name: Villa di Formello
desc: A Roman villa dating ca. 50 B.C. located near Monte Gennaro.

name: Antinoeion at Hadrian's Villa
desc: A sacred precinct at the western end of Villa Hadriani, comprising two temples at opposite (north and south) ends of a plaza or garden, and (on the western edge of this complex) a small colonnaded hemicycle. Here, Hadrian may have planned to build a large, semi-circular temple-tomb for Antinous, in

name: Villa Augustea
desc: The so-called “Villa of Augustus” at Somma Vesuviana was first discovered in the late nineteenth century. The villa has been shown to have survived the 79 CE eruption of Mt. Vesuvius but was eventually destroyed by a volcanic event in 472.

name: Casa del Rilievo di Telefo
desc: The House of the Relief of Telephus or Casa del Rilievo di Telefo is one of the largest houses attested in the excavated area of Herculaneum (ca. 1,800 sq. m.). The house was excavated between 1934 and 1936.

name: Funerary Chamber of Manlia Felicitas
desc: A subterranean funerary chamber with three frescoes walls depicting animal and vegetal life, located around the third mile of the Via Appia.

name: Polygonal wall of Signia
desc: The circuit wall of ancient Signia realized in polygonal masonry.

name: Monte Tamburino necropolis
desc: A necropolis with inhumations dating to the fifth and fourth centuries B.C.

name: Santi Quattro Coronati
desc: Santi Quattro Coronati is an early Christian basilica on Rome's Caelian Hill begun by Pope Miltiades in the fourth century A.D.

name: Korčula Neolithic Site
desc: A submerged neolithic site on a former islet connected to the east coast of Korcula island, just southeast of the modern town and port of the same name. name: San Giovanni in Oleo
desc: A sixteenth-century chapel near the Porta Latina that is believed to commemorate the location where the Christian apostle John was reportedly unharmed after being immersed in a vat of boiling oil in 92 CE.

name: Templum Pacis
desc: The Temple of Peace in Rome was vowed by Vespasian following the Jewish War.

name: Roman amphitheater at Album Ingaunum/Albingaunum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Albegna.

name: Arch of Augustus at Aosta
desc: The Arch of Augustus at Aosta is a commemorative arch dedicated to Augustus ca. 25 BC following victories over the Salassi.

name: Roman amphitheater at Bern
desc: The remains of a small Roman amphitheater at Bern, measuring ca. 27.5 x 25.3 meters, are visible on satellite images.

name: Byzantine house
desc: A Byzantine house located at Scylletium/Scolacium.

name: Roman civil amphitheater at Carnuntum
desc: Located outside the city wall, the Roman amphitheater at Carnuntum dates to the later second century. It could accommodate some 13,000 spectators. The amphitheater likely went out of use by the fourth century.

name: Roman baths at Carnuntum
desc: The Roman baths at Carnuntum.

name: Roman theater at Lupia(e)
desc: The precise date of the Roman theater at Lecce is uncertain, but it is generally assigned to the Augustan period.

name: Roman amphitheater at Sipous/Sipontum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Sipous/Sipontum.

name: Diavolino II tomb
desc: An Etruscan tomb of the seventh century B.C.

name: Roman theater at Fiesole
desc: The Roman theater at Fiesole dates to the first century.

name: Decumanus maximus at Vulci
desc: Belonging to Vulci's Roman phase, the Decumanus Maximus is the well-preserved east-west road of the city paved in basalt.

name: Roman theater at Falerii
desc: The Roman theater at Falerii was excavated in 1829.

name: Falerii Novi amphitheater
desc: The Falerii Novi amphitheater is located north of the city walls.

name: Palace of Diocletian
desc: A third-century A.D. fortified palace built by the emperor Diocletian.

name: Capitolium of Brixia
desc: The Capitolium of Brixia was built in A.D. 73.

name: Eremo di San Michele Arcangelo
desc: A rock-cut Christian sanctuary located on Monte Altino in the Monti Aurunci that was begun ca. A.D. 830.

name: Eremo di San Michele (Coli)
desc: The cavern of San Michele was a hermit's dwelling place that is located near a cavern known as the "cave of San Colombano". name: Vaticanus Ager
desc: A district on the right bank of the river Tiber, between the lower course of the river and the territory of Veii.

name: Roman amphitheater at Trier
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Trier dates to the reign of Antoninus Pius and was renovated under Constantius Chlorus. The arena measures ca. 71 x 47.5 meters.

name: Porta Nigra
desc: The so-called "Porta Nigra" is a surviving Roman city gate that dates to ca. A.D. 186-200. It was enlisted as part of the "Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier" UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

name: Ponte delle Chianche, Buonalbergo
desc: A Roman bridge of the second century A.D. along the Via Traiana that crosses the torrente Buonalbergo.

name: Parco Nazionale dell'Alta Murgia
desc: The Parco Nazionale dell'Alta Murgia, a national park in Puglia, southern Italy, preserves a range of natural and cultural features. It covers an area of more than 675 square kilometers and is headquartered in Gravina in Puglia. The park was established in 2004.

name: Mausoleum Campo Barbarico
desc: The Campo Barbarico Mausoleum is a third-century CE Roman "temple tomb" located at the fourth mile of the Via Latina. name: Quirinal Hill
desc: One of the hills of Rome comprises several smaller peaks. According to tradition, its first inhabitants were Titus Tatius and the Sabines; during the Republic, the hill was mostly residential.

name: Chiarone (river)
desc: The Chiarone is a river of the Maremma. It creates one of three major valley systems in the Ager Cosanus.

name: Poggio Evangelista
desc: Poggio Evangelista is a hill located near Latera in the province of Viterbo, Italy. On the highest part of the hill, Bronze Age pottery evidence provides evidence for a naturally defended settlement.

name: Doric temple of Segesta
desc: The Doric temple of Segesta is an incomplete (6 x 14) temple of the Doric order begun in the 420s B.C.

name: Kothon
desc: The so-called "Kothon" is a large, rectangular, artificial pool dating to the Punic period of Sicily and located on the island of Motya. name: Porta Gemina at Asculum
desc: A city gate of the first century B.C.

name: Roman theater at Asculum
desc: The Roman theater at Asculum was discovered during excavations in 1932. The structure dates to the first century A.D.

name: Roman amphitheater at Rusellae
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Rusellae dates to the first century.

name: Roman amphitheater of Martigny
desc: The Roman amphitheater of Martigny likely dates to the reign of Trajan.

name: Porta Praetoria at Aosta
desc: A gate of the city wall of the Augustan colony, ca. 25 B.C.

name: Roman amphitheater at Aosta
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Aosta likely dates to the first century A.D. Its remains are englobed within Medieval structures.

name: Roman theater at Aosta
desc: The Roman theater at Aosta dates ca. 25 B.C.

name: Roman amphitheater at Libarna
desc: The remains of the Roman amphitheater at Libarna are located in Serravalle Scrivia, Italy.

desc: The Roman theater at Libarna dates to the first century.

name: Roman theater at Interamnia Praetuttiorum
desc: A Roman theater dating to the Augustan period.

name: Roman villa
desc: Remains of an early imperial period Roman villa, the so-called "Domus della Madonna delle Grazie".

name: Heidentor
desc: A triumphal monument built at Carnuntum between A.D. 354 and 361, perhaps by Constantius II.

name: Gladiatorial School
desc: The gladiatorial school of Carnuntum was located to the west of the amphitheater.

name: Western necropolis at Egnatia/Gnathia
desc: The western necropolis at Egnatia/Gnathia includes some tombs of the Messapian culture dating from the middle of the fourth to the second centuries B.C.

name: Lucera Castle
desc: A castle originally built by Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor in AD 1233.

name: Pietrera tomb
desc: An Etruscan tholos tomb of the seventh century B.C. at Vetulonia.

name: Mura dell Arce
desc: The so-called "Mura dell Arce" of Vetulonia served as the sixth- and fifth-century B.C. fortifications of Etruscan Vetulonia. These are massive walls built in megalithic technique using limestone.

name: Belvedere tomb
desc: An Etruscan tomb of the seventh century B.C.

name: Pian di Civita, Tarquinii
desc: The Pian di Civita was the ancient urban area of Tarquinia.

name: Tomb of the Shields and Chairs, Caere
desc: The so-called Tomb of the Shields and Chairs at Caere dates ca. 520 - 500 B.C. The organization of this tomb is similar to that of the Tomb of the Capitals and the Tomb of the Cornice. name: Tomb of the Five Chairs, Caere
desc: An Etruscan tomb at Caere dated ca. 625-600 B.C.

name: Porta di Giove, Falerii
desc: A Roman gate in the city's defensive wall.

name: Acropolis of Circeii
desc: The polygonal masonry walls of the Acropolis of Circeii enclose an area of approximately two hectares. The walls likely date to the middle republican period.

name: Tuvixeddu Punic necropolis
desc: A Punic necropolis near Caralis in Sardinia.

name: Necropolis of Filigosa

name: Sanctuary at Lucus Feroniae
desc: The sanctuary and grove of Feronia located at the site of Lucus Feroniae.

name: Doss Trento
desc: Doss Trento is a small hill that lies along the course of the Adige River. A Paleochristian basilica was located on the hillside.

name: Pozzuolo necropolis

name: Scoppieto
desc: An ancient settlement occupied from the fourth century B.C. to the fifth century A.D. noted for an Italic sanctuary and a production center for terra sigillata.

name: Santa Maria in Cosmedin
desc: A minor basilica church in Rome, Italy. Tradition holds that the church was founded in the sixth century to serve the Greek community at Rome. The beginnings of the present edifice lie in the eighth century.

name: San Giorgio in Velabro
desc: A church dedicated to St. George located in Rome's Velabrum. Legend connects the church's location with the spot where the Roman she wolf found the abandoned twins, Romulus and Remus.

name: Basilica Manastirine
desc: An important extra-mural Christian site at Solina. The site includes the basilica and the cemetery of Manastirine, associated with a Christian martyr.

name: Cybele sanctuary
desc: A temple sacred to Cybele located at Neuss am Rhein.

name: Castello D'Evoli

desc: A river of central Sicily: the modern Fiume Dittaino.

name: Chrysas, T.
desc: According to Cicero, the shrine of Chrysas (the god shares a name with the nearby river) was located along the road from Assorus to Henna. A cult image in marble, described as being "beautiful", was to be found there and was ultimately spared from the depredations of Caius Verres.

name: Chydas? (river)

desc: Colle Madore is an archaeological site connected with the Sicanians.

name: Colle Rotondo
desc: At Colle Rotondo (or Collerotondo), Paolo Orsi identified the remains of an area of habitation and an associated necropolis. Surface scatters of Hellenistic pottery were observed.

name: Comiciana?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 C3 Comiciana?

name: Cosconiana
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 D4 Cosconiana

name: Cossyra (settlement)
desc: A harbor settlement on the island of the same name.

name: Pantelleria (island)
desc: An island in the Strait of Sicily with human occupation dating back at least 35,000 years, Pantelleria has evidence for Bronze Age, Punic, Roman, Medieval, and modern phases. The Romans first acquired the island in 255 B.C. They called it Cossyra.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 F5 Dianae Fons?

name: Didyme (island)
desc: One of the Aeolian Islands with Greek occupation from the fourth century B.C.

name: Drepanum
desc: Drepanum, the modern Trapani, Sicily, is an ancient port city. The archaeological remains of the ancient city are meager. During the First Punic War, Hamilcar fortified the site. The Roman Republic lost a naval engagement near Drepanum in 249 B.C. but then prevailed in the battle of the Egadi island

name: Durrueli di Realmonte
desc: A Roman villa rustica dating to the first century A.D. located in the Punta Grande beach, in the territory of Realmonte, province of Agrigento, Sicily.

name: Engyon

name: Entella
desc: Entella was an ancient city in the interior of Sicily, situated on the left bank of the river Hypsas.

name: Epipolai
desc: A substantial plateau that is roughly triangular in shape and extends to the north and west of Syracuse.

name: Erikodes/Ericusa (island)
desc: One of the Aeolian Islands; the island is the site of the extinct Montagnola volcano.

name: Erineos (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 G5 Erineos fl.

name: Eryx
desc: An ancient, indigenous settlement of western Sicily, likely inhabited by the Elymians.

name: Eryx (mountain)
desc: Mount Eryx is a mountain of western Sicily. The mountain is mentioned by numerous ancient authors, notably in the Aeneid, where Virgil discusses it in relation to Venus Erycina.

name: Euboia?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 F4 Euboia?

name: Euryelos
desc: A fortress built by Dionysius the Elder 9 km west of Syracuse, in the modern hamlet of Belvedere (Sicily).

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 E4 Fontana Calda di Butera

name: Francavilla di Sicilia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 G3 Francavilla di Sicilia

name: Gela
desc: A Greek colony of Sicily founded by Rhodians and Cretans ca. 688 B.C. The oikists were the Rhodian Antiphemos and the Cretan Entimos.

name: Gela(s) (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 E4 Gela(s) fl.

name: Gemelli Colles
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 D3 Gemelli Colles

name: Gerace Roman Villa
desc: A fourth century A.D. Roman villa with mosaic pavements. The villa may have extended to some 10,000 square meters in area.

name: Halaesa
desc: Halaesa is located on the north coast of Sicily between between Kalakta and Kephaloidion. The city was founded in 403 B.C. by Archonides of Herbita. The city sided with Rome during the First Punic War and was made "libera et immunis". By the Augustan period it had become a municipium.

name: Halaisos (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 47 E3 Halaisos fl.

name: Halicyae
desc: A town of the Elymians located between Lilybaeum and Entella.

name: Haluntium
desc: An ancient settlement located between Tyndaris and Calacte. Some authors ascribe the foundation of the site to the Acarnanians.

name: Halykos (river)
desc: The Halykos (modern Platani) is the fifth-longest river in Sicily.

name: Heirkte (mountain)
desc: A mountain, probably Monte Pellegrino (contra Manni 1981, 86-87).

name: Strozzacapponi necropolis
desc: The Strozzacapponi necropolis is an assemblage of Etruscan tombs dating from the third to the first centuries BCE. The chamber tomb is the predominant typology. The necropolis is located near Perugia in Umbria.

name: Osteria Cessati Spiriti
desc: In the Notizie degli Scavi di Antichità for 1884, R. Lanciani reports the find of a monolithic, anepigraphic Roman sarcophagus at the Osteria Cessati Spiriti. The sarcophagus had been discovered in a pozzolana quarry and relocated to the grounds of the osteria. Brickstamps dating to 123 CE were repo

name: Sepolcreto Ostiense
desc: The modern toponym "Sepolcreto Ostiense" refers to a portion of what was once a vast ancient necropolis in Rome, located between the Rupe di San Paolo and the bend of the Tiber River. This necropolis was purportedly the place where the apostle Paul was buried and, subsequently, the Basilica of St. P

name: Roman Odeum of Tauromenium
desc: The Roman Odeum of Tauromenium dates to the reign of the Roman emperor Hadrian.

name: Domus Faustae
desc: The Domus Faustae refers to a part of the Lateran Palace. In about 312 CE, Constantine razed the barracks of the imperial horse-guards barracks that adjoined the palace. At that time, the palace was known as Domus Faustae. Since the equites singulares Augusti had supported Maxentius, Constantine des

name: San Pancrazio al Fango
desc: San Pancrazio al Fango is an early medieval abbey built between the eighth and ninth centuries AD.

name: Santa Cristina
desc: A nuragic sanctuary centered on a sacred well that was in use from ca. 1200 to 700 BC.

name: Broglio di Trebisacce
desc: Broglio di Trebisacce is the site of a protohistoric settlement located on the plain of Sibari not far from the Calabrian coast. Discovered in 1978, the site was excavsed by Renato Peroni from 1979 to 1985.

name: Nuraghe Murtas
desc: A single-tower nuraghe dating between 1500 and 1200 B.C.

name: Nuraghe Perda su Luaxiu
desc: A nuraghe located near Quartu Sant'Elena.

name: Corviano
desc: Corviano (Bomarzo) is a protected landscape with evidence of Etruscan, Roman, and Medieval activity.

name: Mithraeum III at Poetovio
desc: The third of five shrines sacred to Mithras found near the site of Poetovio.

name: Roman amphitheater at Sopron
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Sopron dates to the later first century A.D.

name: Halberg Mithraeum
desc: A natural cave in the side of the Halberg hill at Saarbrücken was enlarged for the use of the Mithras cult.

name: Tomb of Gaius Vestorius Priscus
desc: The Tomb of Gaius Vestorius Priscus is located in Pompeii's Porta Vesuvio necropolis. Gaius Vestorius Priscus was an aedile and was granted 2,000 sesterces by the town council for his tomb and funeral. The tomb is decorated with paintings depicting a funereal meal.

name: Tomb of Arellia Tertulla
desc: The Tomb of Arellia Tertulla, daughter of Numerius and wife of Veius Fronto.

name: ad Capita bubula
desc: The toponym "ad Capita bubula" is attested in Suetonius and refers to a place located at the northeast corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome near the Curiae Veteres. Here, there was a domus of one Caius Octavius, a Roman politician who was the biological father of Octavian. It is possible that Octavia

name: Nuraghe Perda Sinnus
desc: A ruined monopteral nuraghe located in the comune of Serrenti, Sardinia.

name: Sepolcro dei Pancrazi
desc: Sepolcro dei Pancrazi is a Roman tomb on the Via Latina dated to the late first or early second century CE. It belonged to a collegium funerarium (funerary college) of the Pancratii, a name attested in two extant inscriptions. The burial chambers are well-appointed with floor mosaics and frescoed wa

name: Colonnacce
desc: Le Colonnacce refers to preserved elements of the lateral, north-south Corinthian-order colonnades that flanked the Forum Transitorium.

name: Aedes Serapis
desc: Caracalla dedicated a temple to Serapis in Regio VI. Its dedication is confirmed via epigraphic elements and some of its architectural elements are also known. It was located on the Collis Latiaris, which is the southern most part of the Quirinal Hill.

name: Aedes Salus
desc: While consul in 311 BCE, Caius Iunius Bubulcus Brutus vowed the temple of Salus; he would later dedicate it as dictator in 302 BCE. While no physical remains of the temple are known, textual and epigraphic testimony suggest that it would have been located near the present-day Piazza del Quirinale.

name: Vicus Patricius
desc: The Vicus Patricius was a street of ancient Rome that crossed both the Cispian and Viminal hills and led, either directly or indirectly, to the Porta Viminalis. The Vicus Patricius bounded both Regio IV and Regio VI of the ancient city. Its course is thought to have been similar to that of the moder

name: Unnamed road
desc: An unnamed road included in Barrington Atlas map 42

name: Eilsleben
desc: Archaeological investigation and geophysical prospection at Eilsleben, Germany, have documented the presence of a notable Early Neolithic settlement dating to the later sixth millennium BCE.

name: Tomb of Lucius Sepunius Sandilianus
desc: The Tomb of Lucius Sepunius Sandilianus is a Roman-period tomb, possibly of tholos typology, located in the Porta Nocera necropolis of Pompeii.

name: Nizzetti
desc: A hamlet in Sicily, located near Acireale, that is the findspot of antiquities possibly related to the ancient settlement of Acium.

name: Mausoleum of Helena
desc: An ancient tomb located on the ancient Via Labicana (now along the Via Casilina) that was built by Constantine I and used as the tomb for his mother, Helena.

name: Vitozza
desc: Vitozza is an ancient settlement located near the village of San Quirico. Its rock-cut habitations were in use by the Etruscans and Romans and again during the medieval period, continuing up to the eighteenth century. Over 200 caves (columbaria) have been cut in the local tufo bedrock.

name: Nuraghe Is Paras
desc: A trilobate nuragic complex of the fifteenth century BC.

name: Phalarium
desc: A fortress named after Phalaris, a tyrant of Acragas and located near the Himera River.

name: Villa Rustica, Loerrach-Brombach
desc: Ruins of a villa rustica, located south of modern Brombach in Baden-Württemberg.

name: Porta Trasimena
desc: The Porta Trasimena or Arco di San Luca is a third-century B.C. gate in the Etruscan wall of Perusia.

name: Grotta Corbeddu
desc: A cave near Oliena, Sardinia, where evidence for the earliest human occupation of the island of Sardinia has been recovered.

name: Nuraghe Poddinosa
desc: A single-tower nuraghe located near Dorgali (NU).

name: Domus della Soglia nilotica
desc: A domus at Privernum dating to the early Imperial period and noted for its mosaic pavements.

name: Stadium-garden at Hadrian's Villa
desc: A garden at the Villa Hadriani imitating the shape of a stadium, situated between the Three Exedras' Hall (to the west) and the Winter Palace (to the east), with a semi-circular nymphaeum at its southern end.

name: Fundus Albianus
desc: An estate located in the Pagus Ambitrebius mentioned on the Tabula alimentaria Traianea.

name: Roman amphitheater at Lupia(e)
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Lupia(e), modern Lecce, was built in the late first and early second centuries A.D.

name: Irno (river)
desc: The Irno river is a river of Campania that flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea. While its ancient name is unknown, the river valley is the site of first millennium B.C. settlement and also the site of numerous clay beds exploited for pottery production.

name: Irru
desc: A nuragic shrine with a sacred well.

name: Fountain of Anna Perenna
desc: Sacred to the goddess Anna Perenna and the nymphs, this rectangular fountain surrounded by rupestral inscriptions was excavated on the modern Via Guidubaldo del Monte in Rome's Pinciano neighborhood during the late 20th century. Rich votive deposits complement the picture of the goddess' worship pai

name: Archaic compound (Gabii)
desc: An archaic compound with evidence for ritual dining that has been identified by its excavators as a "regia".

name: Abbazia di San Faustino
desc: An abbey located in Massa Martana.

name: Greek Theater at Syracuse
desc: Rock-cut theater of Greek form at Syracuse, Sicily, probably in use from the 5th c. BC to the Late Roman period.

name: Madonna del Passo
desc: A modern comune located in the territory of Rieti, Lazio. The Rieti Survey identified this as a likely Roman-period settlement covering more than 5 ha. Material evidence suggests occupation from ca. the sixth century B.C. until the sixth century A.D.

name: Regio III, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio III, a largely unexcavated archaeological subdivision located in the northeastern section of Pompeii, contains a mix of residential and commercial structures.

name: Poggibonsi
desc: Poggibonsi is an ancient and medieval center in the province of Siena on the Elsa river. The city sits along the Via Francigena.

name: Abbey of Monte Cassino
desc: A multi-period hilltop settlement with evidence for ancient terrace construction that now supports an abbey of the Benedictine order.

name: Parco archeologico Griso-Laboccetta
desc: An Archaic to Hellenistic sanctuary sacred to Demeter.

name: Kelten-Wall
desc: An ancient fortification system at the multiperiod Glauberg site in Germany.

name: Valdonega Roman villa
desc: The Roman villa of Valdonega near Verona dates to the first century A.D.

name: Ekklesiasterion/Theater at Metapontum
desc: A building complex located in the city's agora, the Ekklesiasterion/Theater is dated ca. 625-300 B.C.

name: Santa Maria Sopra Minerva
desc: A first century B.C. temple dedicated to Minerva by Gneus Caestius and Titus Caesius Priscus, who were two of the Assisi's quattuorviri. The temple was converted to the church of Santa Maria Sopra Minerva in 1539.

name: Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi
desc: A papal basilica begun ca. AD 1228.

name: Necropolis of Campovalano
desc: A Picene necropolis located near Campovalano (Campli) in the province of Teramo. While more than 600 tombs were identified, there may have been as many as 20,000 originally.

name: Roman amphitheater at Luna
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Luna was built in the second century, perhaps during the Antonine period.

name: Monte Rovello
desc: Monte Rovello was an important Etruscan settlement covering ca. 5 hectares with occupation stretching from the Bronze Age to the Hellenistic period.

name: Stifone
desc: Evidence of a Roman shipyard has been discovered at the locality of Stifone within the comune of Le Mole of the town of Narni. This shpiyard was connected to an artificial canal dug adjacent to the river Nera.

name: House of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus
desc: The House of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus (Regio VII, Insula 16, entrances 12-15) is considered to be the residence and trading center of the gens Umbricia, a Pompeian family involved in producing and selling garum. The house itself is described as a "Samnite-type" house and in the first century B.C. it

name: Gola di S. Andrea, Itri
desc: Located along the course of the Via Appia between Fondi and Itri are the remains of a likely sanctuary of Apollo that dates to the fourth and third century BCE.

name: Werthausen
desc: A Roman fort of the Limes of Germania Inferior.

name: Hypogeum of Trebius Giustus
desc: A tomb of the fourth century A.D. located on the Via Latina.

name: Baths of the Philosopher
desc: The so-called "Baths of the Philosopher" or "Terme del Filosofo" in region V of the ancient city of Ostia take their modern sobriquet from a bust of Plotinus dating to the middle of the third century CE.

name: Shrine of Sabazius
desc: The Shrine of Sabazius was installed in part of a horreum (V, XII, 2) that was initially built ca. 120-125 CE. The Sabazius shrine likely dates to the early third century. Dante Vaglieri excavated the shrine in 1909.

name: Ancient Greek theater at Palazzolo Acreide
desc: The theater at ancient Akrai.

name: Helorine Hodos
desc: An ancient road of Sicily linking Syracuse and Helorus.

name: Ouiriballon Akron
desc: A promontory of northwest Corsica that extends westward and is capped by the Île de Gargalo. It is bounded on the south by the Golfe de Girolata and on the north by the Golfe d'Elbo. Today, the entire promontory is set aside as the Réserve Naturelle de Scandola (a UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site)

name: Ouolerios (river)
desc: The modern Aliso river in northern Corsica.

name: Ourkinion
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 C2 Ourkinion

name: Rhion? Akron
desc: An ancient name for a promontory on the island of Corsica, probably to be identified with the modern Cap Cargese.

name: Rhoition Oros
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 C2 Rhoition Oros

name: Rhopikon
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 C2 Rhopikon

name: Rhotanos (river)
desc: The Tavignano is a river of Corsica that flows into the Tyrrhenian Sea near Aléria.

name: Rhoubra
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 D3 Rhoubra

name: Sacrum Pr. (promontory)
desc: An ancient cape, identified with the Corsican islets now known as the Îles Finocchiarola, which extend from a small, northeastern promontory of the island into the Tyrrhenian Sea.

name: Saone
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 C2 Saone

name: Sardoum Mare
desc: The name given by ancient authors to the part of the Mediterranean Sea adjoining the island of Sardinia on the west and south.

name: Sermigion
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 C2 Sermigion

name: Soubasanoi
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 D3 Soubasanoi

name: Syrboi
desc: A pre-Roman people settled in the interior mountains of Corsica. Their precise territory is not known, but they are thought to have been localized in the Col de Sobra.

name: Syrakousanos Limen
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 D3 Syrakousanos Limen

name: Talkinon
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 D2 Talkinon

name: Tarabenioi
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 D2 Tarabenioi

name: Tikarios (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 C3 Tikarios fl.

name: Tilox Akron
desc: A promontory on the north coast of Corsica mentioned by Ptolemy. Modern scholars identify it with the Punta Cavallata, which is located just west of the Gulf of Saint Florent.

name: Titianoi
desc: A people settled on the coast of south-western Corsica (area of modern Tizzano).

name: Titianos Limen
desc: A settlement on the coast of south-western Corsica, in the territory of the Titianoi.

name: Toutelas Bomos
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 D2 Toutelas Bomos

name: Vanacini
desc: The name of an ancient people inhabiting the northeastern portion of Corscia

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 A2 unnamed bridge (N Hydata Hypsitana)

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 A3 unnamed bridge (N Neapolis)

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: A bridge located north of Usel(l)is in western Sardinia

name: Unnamed bridge north of Aquae Calidae Neapolitanorum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 A3 unnamed bridge (N Aquae Calidae Neapolitanorum)

name: Decimomannu Roman bridge
desc: The remains of a stone, arched Roman bridge at Decimomannu, to the west of Assemini, Sardinia. Three of the original six arches survive today. The bridge may originally have been as much as 160 meters in length. R.J. Rowland considered it to be of Iulio-Claudian date.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge
desc: An unnamed bridge, located northeast of ‘Luguidunec’.

name: Unnamed bridge (E Fundus Moddol(...))
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 B3 unnamed bridge (E Fundus Moddol(...))

name: Ussana Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge located northwest of modern Ussana in Sardinia.

name: Unnamed quarry
desc: An ancient granite quarry located on modern Capo Testa, Sardinia.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 A3 unnamed quarry (W Terr'e Frucca)

name: Annuagras
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 unlocated Annuagras

name: Sousaleos Kome
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 48 unlocated Sousaleos Kome

name: Pollupice
desc: A Roman road station in Liguria, only attested in the Itinerarium Antonini, whose exact location is unknown.

name: Via Gabina villas
desc: Two suburban villa sites and a Late Antique granary were excavated at a site along the Via Gabina 14 km east of central Rome. Walter Widrig and Philip Oliver-Smith directed the excavations.

name: Tomba di Mezzavia
desc: A single-chamber tomb carved in tufo bedrock at Cortona dates from the third and second centuries BCE. The Tomba di Mezzavia was discovered in 1950.

name: Colombarone
desc: An archaeological site that preserves remains of a Late Roman settlement along the Via Flaminia.

name: Herculaneum Gate
desc: The "Herculaneum Gate" was a city gate of Pompeii located at the northern terminus of the Via Consolare. The gate originally incorporated three passageways.

name: Temple of Portunus
desc: A tetrastyle temple dedicated to the god Portunus and dating to the late second century or early first century BC.

name: Ipogeo dei Cristallini
desc: A hypogeum tomb of the Hellenistic period in Neapolis (now Naples, Italy).

name: Porticus Minucia
desc: The Porticus Minucia was a portico that stood in the Campus Martius in Rome. It was initially built by M. Minucius Rufus, consul in 110 B.C.

name: Belvedere Temple, Orvieto
desc: A fifth century B.C. temple that was likely sacred to Tinia.

name: Alpes Cottiae (late Roman province)
desc: The post-Diocletianic province of Alpes Cottiae according to the Verona List (ca. AD 303-324). It was assigned to the diocese of Italia.

name: Pausilipum
desc: Pausilipum was an ancient Graeco-Roman settlement on the Bay of Naples.

name: Pontecorvo (Latium)
desc: Pontecorvo is a comune located in the province of Frosinone, Lazio, Italy.

name: Ponte sul Fosso di Biserano
desc: The Ponte sul Fosso di Biserano is a Roman aqueduct bridge of the Aqua Anio Vetus.

name: Grotta dei Massacci
desc: The so-called Grotta dei Massacci located in Osteria Nuova, municipality of Frasso Sabino, Italy, is a monumental, vaulted subterranean tomb structure that likely dates to the second century CE.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge (Fidenza)
desc: The remains of an unnamed Roman bridge at Fidenza are located in the public square known as "piazza Grandi". The bridge was part of the ancient Via Aemilia and carried the roadway across the Stirone stream. It likely dates to the first century CE.

name: Domus Romane di Palazzo Valentini
desc: The remains of a Roman domus and a bath complex adjacent to the area of the Forum of Trajan.

name: Columbarium of Caius Scribonius Menophilus
desc: The Columbarium of Caius Scribonius Menophilus is located on the grounds of the Doria Pamphili in Rome. The well-preserved columbarium dates to the late republican and early imperial periods and is noted for its wall paintings.

name: Ponte San Stefano
desc: A bridge that leads to the villa of Vibius Varius.

name: Catacomb of the Nunziatella
desc: The Catacomb of the Nunziatella or the Catacomb of the Annunziatella is an ancient catacomb located in Rome's Ardeatina neighborhood in the via di Grotta Perfetta. The catacomb was excavated on the site of a large Republican-period necropolis and does not seem to have been connected with any Christi

name: Column of Marcus Aurelius
desc: The Column of Marcus Aurelius is a monumental victory column erected along the Via Lata between 176 and 193 CE. The monument celebrated victories realized against the Marcomanni and the Sarmatians (172-175 CE).

name: Domus Flavia
desc: The Domus Flavia is a modern appellation that refers to the palace complex built by the emperor Domitian on the Palatine Hill in Rome. The complex was completed ca. 92 CE. The Flavian complex is considered a part of the larger entity known as Domus Palatina.

name: Villa in via Enzo Tortora
desc: A villa site that was active from the middle Republican period to the early Middle Ages was investigated in 2009 and 2010 at via Enzo Tortora, no. 79. The site is located about 500 meters east of the line of the ancient Via Flaminia.

name: House of Argus
desc: The House of Argus at Herculaneum is located on the west side of Cardo III adjacent to the House of Artistides.

name: Voconius Pollio villa
desc: A Roman villa commonly associated with Q. Voconius Pollio that was excavated in the nineteenth century.

name: House of Julius Polybius
desc: The House of Julius Polybius (IX 13,1.3) sits on the north side of the Via dell'Abbondanza and dates from the second century BC.

name: Garden of the Fugitives
desc: The so-called "Garden of the Fugitives" (I, 21,1) is an area of the city that was once given over to habitation but that in the final phase of the city was a vineyard with a summer triclinium. Excavation campaigns of the 1960s and 1970s discovered 13 human victims of the AD 79 eruption that destroye

name: House of Venus in the shell
desc: Located on the Via dell'Abbondanza, the so-called "House of Venus in the shell" is also known as the House of D. Lucretius Satrius Valens.

name: House of the geometric mosaics
desc: The House of the Geometric Mosaics (VIII,2,14-16) is a large domus of more than 60 rooms that was achieved by combining two third to second century BC houses.

name: Church of Saint Eusebius (Ronciglione)
desc: A paleochristian sanctuary located along the Via Francigena.

name: Villa del Cimitero Flaminio
desc: A Roman villa located at the 1.6 km post of the via Tiberina, positioned on a tuff bank, today inside the Prima Porta cemetery.

name: Casetta Etruscan necropolis
desc: The Necropolis della Casetta at Blera contains numerous dado-type tombs.

name: Peschiera necropolis
desc: An Etruscan necropolis at Tuscania in use from the seventh until the first century B.C.

name: Nuragic settlement, Antas
desc: A Nuragic settlement that pre-dates and, in some cases, is re-occupied during the Roman period.

name: Massaciuccoli Romana - Padiglione "Guglielmo Lera"
desc: The site of a Roman imperial-period villa in the modern Italian comune of Massaciuccoli Romana.

name: Ponte di Annibale
desc: An arched Roman bridge across the Titerno near Cerreto Sannita in Campania.

name: Monte Torre Maggiore
desc: An Italic temple complex in Umbria of the first millennium B.C. that includes the so-called "Ara maior".

name: Mausoleo di Monte dell'Incastro
desc: A circular, domed, apsidal subterranean structure of the Hadrianic period that is referred to as a tomb but may have had a cultic function.

name: Nuraghe Coa de Serra
desc: A nuragic complex near Baunei, Sardinia.

name: Rofalco
desc: A fortified Etruscan site located in the territory of Vulci.

name: Hypogeum of the Aurelii
desc: A third-century AD hypogeum tomb on the Esquiline Hill in Rome with both pagan and Paleochristian iconography.

name: Basilica of Iunius Bassus
desc: The Basilica of Junius Bassus (basilica Iunii Bassi) was a civil basilica on the Esquiline Hill in Rome. Its remains were demolished in 1930 to make way for the Seminario Pontificio di Studi Orientali, in via Napoleone III, 3. Junius Bassus held the consulship in 331 CE. The basilica is particularly

name: Porta Flaminia
desc: A gate in the Aurelian Wall from which the Via Flaminia issued, the Porta Flaminia became known as the Porta del Popolo after the fifteenth century. Sixtus IV is credited with building the gateway that stands today.

name: Porta Fontinalis
desc: No longer extant, the Porta Fontinalis is only known via textual and epigraphic references. Presumed to be a gate of the Servian Wall, the Porta Fontinalis lay in the Campus Martius, west of the via Lata. It may have been the original point of issuance for the Republican roads known as the Via Flami

name: Osteria del Gladiatore
desc: A Roman tavern in Pompeii.

name: tribus Maecia
desc: Tribus Maecia (originally Maicia) was a later rural tribe of ancient Rome, established in 332 B.C.

name: Hospitium (I.1.3)
desc: A Hospitium located at the Porta Stabia of Pompeii.

name: Acquedotto dei Sette Bassi
desc: A Roman aqueduct supplying the Villa dei Sette Bassi.

name: Ipogeo delle Ghirlande
desc: The so-called Hypogeum of the Garlands is an ancient tomb located at the tenth mile of the ancient Via Latina. The tomb dates to either the first or second century CE.

name: Cocciano
desc: The archaeological area of Cocciano located in the comune of Frascati, Italy, is the site of an imperial-period villa that is associated with Livia Drusilla and her son, the emperor Tiberius.

name: Ripa Puteolana
desc: A coastal area of Pozzuoli (ancient Puteoli) with numerous ancient remains is now submerged due to the bradyseism of the Phlegraean Fields. The ruins of a Nabataean shrine were documented here in 2024.

name: Fosso di Pratolungo
desc: The Fosso di Pratolungo is a small tributary of the Anio. Its lower course is also known as Fosso di Marco Simone.

name: Basilica di Santo Stefano in via Latina
desc: The now-ruined basilica of Santo Stefano in Via Latina was a fifth-century CE early Christian basilica. It is now located within the confines of the archaeological park of the Via Latina tombs.

name: Nuraghe Orolio
desc: A nuragic monument near Silanus, Sardinia, constructed primarily of granite and rising to a height of ca. 12 m and dating to the Middle to Late Bronze Age (seventeenth to ninth centuries BC).

name: Ponte del Gran Caso
desc: A Roman bridge across the Torrente Gran Caso located south of Ascoli Piceno.

name: Puntone necropolis
desc: An Etruscan necropolis dating to the seventh-fifth centuries B.C. The ancient settlement associated with the site may have been Palmule.

name: Scoglietto
desc: A Roman sanctuary in use from the first century B.C. through fifth century A.D.

name: Siedlung Forschner
desc: A Neolithic archaeological site located in Bad Buchau, Germany, and included in the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Prehistoric Pile Dwellings around the Alps".

name: Aqua Crabra
desc: An aqueduct supplying villas in the area of the city of Tusculum, mentioned by both Cicero and Frontinus.

name: Ponte della Maddalena
desc: A Medieval bridge across the Serchio River. The bridge was built ca. 1080-1100 and was renovated ca. 1300. It is located along the Via Francigena.

name: Thermae Titi (Tïtianae)
desc: Thermae Titi (Tïtianae), or Baths of Titus, were public baths built at Rome in 81 CE under the emperor Titus. Located at the foot of the Esquiline Hill, the baths occupy part of the Domus Aurea of Nero. The Baths of Trajan were constructed immediately adjacent to the Baths of Titus in the early seco

name: Villa of Lucius Nonius Calpurnius Torquatus Asprenas
desc: The remains of a Roman villa on the Via Ostiense have been linked to Lucius Nonius Calpurnius Torquatus Asprenas.

name: Monte Falterona
desc: A peak of the Tuscan-Romagnolo Apennines, rising to 1,654 m. above sea level, Monte Falterona is the source of the Arno River and shows evidence of Etruscan occupation.

name: Le Carrozze-Gravetta
desc: Le Carrozze-Gravetta, the site of a Daunian sanctuary of the fourth century BCE.

name: House of Paquius Proculus
desc: The House of Paquius Proculus at Pompeii, also known as the House of C. Cuspius Pansa, is a domus which was excavated in 1911 and then from 1923 to 1926.

name: Roman forum of Sarsina
desc: The Roman forum of Sarsina has been excavated in its northern reaches.

name: Capitolium of Sarsina
desc: The remains of a first-century BCE temple podium discovered at Sarsina have been identified as the Roman settlement's Capitolium.

name: Venetian Lagoon
desc: The Venetian Lagoon or Laguna di Venezia refers to an enclosed body of water that is linked to the northern Adriatic Sea by three inlets. This body of water is what remains of what was once a system of estuarine lagoons extending from Ravenna as far north as Trieste.

name: San Gervasio, Mondolfo
desc: The Roman Catholic church of San Gervasio dei Bulgari is located in Mondolfo, province of Pesaro and Urbino, Marche, Italy. Built in the Romanesque style, the church was likely founded in the fifth or sixth century.

name: Mura di Monte Giove
desc: A fortification wall on Monte Giove at Terracina that has been interpreted, at various times, in different ways with respect to its chronology.

name: Manganello Sanctuary
desc: The Manganello Sanctuary is located at the northern edge Caere's urban plateau.

name: Largo di Torre Argentina
desc: A square in the Campus Martius of Rome, at the center of which lies an archaeological site that includes the remains of four temples of the Republican period, as well as elements of the first century B.C. theater complex of Cnaeus Pompeius.

name: Complesso di Sant'Imbenia
desc: A Bronze Age settlement on the northwest shore of the Bay of Porto Conte in western Sardinia. Excavations revealed a nuraghe and associated village, as well as indigenous, Phoenician, Levantine, and Greek ceramics. Activity at the site seems to have started as early as 1500 BCE and continued until t

name: Banjole Roman villa
desc: A Roman maritime villa located at the southwest corner of the Istrian peninsula, about six kilometers south of Pola. According to Matijašić 1982, the remains of the villa are visible beneath the waters of Paltana Bay.

name: Sep. Bibuli
desc: The tomb of C. Publicius Bibulus, a plebeian aedile, located at Rome at the foot of the Capitoline Hill. It most likely dates to the close of the Republican period.

name: Corre
desc: A Gallo-Roman site located near the junction of the Saône and Coney rivers.

name: Necropoli del Fusco
desc: The Fusco necropolis is the largest and oldest burial area in Greek Syracuse. Located within contrada Canalicchio, the site was excavated by Paolo Orsi in 1893.

name: Tomb of Eumachia
desc: A monumental exedra-type tomb built at the Porta Nocera between ca. A.D 1-30 that served as the tomb for the family of Eumachia.

name: Nuraghe Sa Jua
desc: A monopteral nuraghe.

name: Baptistry of Neon
desc: An octagonal brick structure erected by Bishop Ursus (late fourth or early fifth century AD) as part of a Basilica (destroyed in 1734). Bishop Neon completed the baptistry at the end of the fifth century AD.

name: Ciota Ciara
desc: A cave in Northern Italy, inhabited in the Late Roman and Early Medieval period.

name: Forum of Col. Augusta Raurica
desc: The Forum of Augusta Raurica.

name: Theater at Saepinum
desc: The intramural theater at Saepinum is one of the best preserved structures at the site. Located in the northern part of the walled area, it is likely built between 2. B.C. and A.D. 4.

name: The Forum of Corporations
desc: A key commercial center occupying the quadriporticus of the theater of Ostia, the Forum of Corporations dates initially to the Augustan period but is substantially rebuilt in the second century.

name: Area della Guastuglia
desc: The archaeological site "Area della Guastuglia" at Gubbio is an architectural complex likely connected with civic religion during Gubbio's Roman phase.

name: Roman theater at Tusculum
desc: The Roman theater at Tusculum was first excavated in 1839.

name: Roman temples at Chieti
desc: Structures thought to be temples set within a sacred area that includes a sacred well.

name: Tophet de Salammbô
desc: A hybrid sanctuary and necropolis sacred to Tanit and Baal.

name: Roman harbor at Carthage
desc: Roman engineers began modifying the Punic harbor by the late second century B.C.

name: Baths of Antoninus at Carthage
desc: The Baths of Antoninus at Carthage date to the middle of the second century and are the largest of the Roman public bath complexes in North Africa.

name: Roman theater at Utica
desc: The Roman theater at Utica.

name: South-Western Baths
desc: A bath complex at Herculaneum that was discovered in the excavations of the so-called "Insula Occidentalis". It was not in use as a bath at the time of the 79 CE eruption as it had been repurposed as a ship-shed.

name: Temple of Concord
desc: The Temple of Concord at Rome was located at the western margin of the Forum Romanum. Its origins are sometimes linked to a vow made by Marcus Furius Camillus in 367 BCE, but the vow may not have been fulfilled until 218 BCE under Lucius Manlius. The sanctuary was rebuilt in 121 BCE and again in 10

name: Tarpeian Rock
desc: The Tarpeian Rock (Tarpeius mons) is a steep rocky cliff on the south side of the Capitoline Hill in Rome. Certain adjudicated criminals were tossed from the Tarpeian Rock to their deaths in antiquity. According to Varro, Tarpeius mons may be the earliest name of the Capitoline Hill.

name: House of Aufidia Cornelia Valentinilla
desc: Archaeological excavations in the area of the Aqua Marcia and the Basilica of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem (Rome) in 1887 and 1888 uncovered the remains of lead water pipes identifying this domus as that of one Aufidia Cornelia Valentinilla.

name: Domus dei Ritratti
desc: The so-called "Domus dei Ritratti" is located in the archaeological area surrounding Santa Croce in Gerusalemme in Rome. The domus dates to the later Roman Empire.

name: Grotta della Vipera
desc: The so-called "Grotta della Vipera" is the hypogeum tomb of a Roman woman named Atilia Pomptilla. It dates to the first century CE.

name: San Trifone in Posterula
desc: San Trifone in Posterula is a no-longer-extant titular church of Rome. It was located at the corner of Via dei Portoghesi and Via della Scrofa in the Campus Martius. The church likely originates in the eighth century; it appears in documentary records beginning in 1006. The ancient church was destro

name: villa del Cavalcavia di Salone
desc: The so-called "Villa of the Jurist" was discovered in 2013 during salvage excavations connected with the expansion of Italy's A24 motorway. A significant villa of the Late Republican period was documented and attributed to the jurist Quintus Mucius Scaevola.

name: Temple of Diomedes (Ploča)
desc: Archaeological evidence in the vicinity of the 14th-century Church of St. John of Trogir on the Croatian Ploča peninsula indicates the presence, in Hellenistic times, of at least a small temple and associated pottery dump. Epigraphic evidence ties the temple to Diomedes, presumably as a protector of

name: Temple O (Selinus)
desc: Temple O at Selinus is a Doric-order temple dating to the early fifth century BCE. It is similar in design to Temple A. The temple measures 16.2 x 40.2 meters with a 6 x 14 columnar arrangement (6.23-meter order height).

name: Mozia necropolis
desc: An archaic period necropolis located on the north shore of Mozia.

name: Roman furnaces in Alcamo
desc: A productive site in Alcamo Marina was discovered in 2000 and includes kilns from the Roman period.

name: Via Berneri columbarium
desc: The Via Berneri columbarium was discovered in 2021 during utility work. This Roman tomb contained two sarcophagi, one of which carried a Latin inscription.

name: Monte di Terra tomb
desc: A monumental Roman tomb located at the ninth mile of the Via Appia, the Monte di Terra tomb rests on a quadrangular podium in peperino stone that supports a circular concrete core and an earthen tumulus.

name: Tomb of the Greek Cross
desc: A tomb located at the tenth mile of the Via Appia.

name: Porta Ardeatina
desc: The Porta Ardeatina was a gate in the city walls of Rome. While it is presumed that the Via Ardeatina exited the walls at this point, debates remain over the nature of the gate; the possibility that it was a postern has been raised.

name: Lacus Iuturnae
desc: The Lacus Iuturnae was a pool built near a spring sacred to Iuturna. Legend held that the Dioscuri watered their horses there after the Battle of Lake Regillus in 495 BCE.

name: Tomb of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus
desc: A tomb at Pompeii's Herculaneum gate that may be that of Aulus Umbricius Scaurus.

name: via Taranto columbaria
desc: Two Roman columbaria are located under the present via Pescara, 2. This accounts for the tomb being referred to interchangeably with two modern, street-derived toponyms, namely "via Taranto" and "via Pescara". These tombs are situated near the ancient crossroads of the via Latina and the via Labican

name: Monte Gentili
desc: A villa associated with Aulus Vitellius Germanicus.

name: Nuraghe Nolza
desc: The Nuraghe Nolza consists of a central, quadri-lobate tower. The tower still stands to ca. 13 m and the complex covers 2.5 ha.

name: Roman theater at Castrum Novum
desc: The Roman theater at Castrum Novum (Santa Marinella, Italy).

name: Roman quarry of Antas
desc: A Roman quarry located approximately 800 meters from the Temple of Antas.

name: Ponte Leproso
desc: A bridge of Roman origins crossing the Sabato river on the outskirts of Benevento.

name: Sepolcro dei Veienti
desc: The so-called "Sepolcro dei Veienti" is a ruined tomb of Roman imperial date. Built in opus caementicium and travertine, only the core of the rectangular structure remains. Likely located along the ancient Via Veientana, the tomb today stands in the modern Parco Papacci.

name: Carrara
desc: The quarries at Carrara in northern Tuscany produced a range of white marbles that saw limited local use until being widely exploited and exported by the Romans from the first century B.C. onward.

name: Unnamed road
desc: An ancient road linking Nomentum and Eretum. Portions of the road are extant, particularly within an archaeological area at Monterotondo.

name: Nuraghe Asoru o Basoru
desc: Nuraghe Asoru o Basoru located in San Vito, Sardinia, Italy

name: Porta Trigemina
desc: Now lost, the Porta Trigemina was one of the main gates of the Servian Wall.

name: Horti Largiani
desc: Gardens that were located in regio VII, but whose precise location is uncertain. They could have been in the Campus Martius or on the slopes of the Pincian Hill.

name: Regio XIV (Transtiberim)
desc: The fourteenth regio of imperial Rome was created by the Augustan administrative reform of 7 BCE. This region contained, in addition to the named monuments, the statio of the seventh cohort of the Vigiles, 78 shrines (aediculae), 150 townhouses, 22 warehouses (horrea), 86 bathhouses, and 180 fountai

name: Unnamed Roman villa
desc: The cryptoporticus of an Augustan-period villa that later came to be incorporated in the substructure of the abbey of Santa Maria Maddalena in Armillis.

name: Castel Malnome (Ponte Galeria)
desc: An imperial necropolis with at least 326 tombs was identified at modern Castel Malnome (Ponte Galeria) in Italy. Archaeological evidence marks these as burials belonging to working-class people of the Roman imperial period, with most graves having either no grave goods or very few. The osteoarchaeol

name: House of Anicetus
desc: The House of Actius Anicetus (I.3.23) at Pompeii is best known as the site where the fresco painting depicting the battle between the Nucerians and the Pompeians in the amphitheater of Pompeii was discovered.

name: Piazza Ronchi Roman cistern
desc: A Roman cistern dating to the second-third centuries CE.

name: Basilica di Santa Sinforosa
desc: A minor Paleochristian basilica located in Guidonia Montecelio that was dedicated to the patron saint of Tivoli.

name: Santa Susanna
desc: The current Church of Saint Susanna at the Baths of Diocletian located on the Quirinal Hill in Rome dates from 1585. A titular church has existed on the site since ca. A.D. 280. The remains of an elite house (domus) are preserved beneath the church.

name: Ponte Lupo
desc: Remains of a portion of the Aqua Marcia aqueduct located near Gallicano nel Lazio.

name: Palazzo Barberini Mithraeum
desc: The Palazzo Barberini Mithraeum numbers among the best-preserved mithraic shrines in Rome. It is situated in via delle Quattro Fontane. Construction work revealed the site in 1936. A portion of the original structures of the second century CE was transformed into the mithraeum in the third century.

name: Sepulcretum
desc: A modern appellation of the ancient Iron Age necropolis uncovered along the Sacra Via adjacent to the Temple of Antoninus and Faustina in April 1902. Giacomo Boni and others conducted extensive excavations at the site.

name: Monte Solaro
desc: Monte Solaro is the tallest mountain on the island of Capri with an elevation of 589 meters.

name: City wall of Pompeii
desc: The city walls of Pompeii surround the ancient urban center and have several architectural phases.

name: House of Romulus and Remus
desc: The so-called House of Romulus and Remus in Pompeii is a domus located at VII.7.10. The site was originally linked to VII.7.13 and was excavated in 1859 and again in 1864. During World War II, the site was bombed and significantly damaged on August 24, 1943, and September 13, 1943. Many of the extan

name: Tomb of Quintus Sulpicius Maximus
desc: The tomb of the boy poet Quintus Sulpicius Maximus on the Via Salaria in Rome. He died in 94 CE, aged just 11 years.

name: Via della Monachina necropolis
desc: A necropolis at the thirteenth kilometer of the Via Aurelia excavated between 2007 and 2011. A total of 332 tombs were identified at the site.

name: Eastern sanctuary
desc: An extra-mural sanctuary located at the eastern gate of Gabii

name: Via Ardeatina
desc: The Via Ardeatina connected Rome and Ardea.

name: Castello di Venere
desc: A Norman castle founded in the twelfth century atop Mount Eryx in Sicily.

name: House of the Mosaic Atrium
desc: A domus in Herculaneum. The mosaic "chessboard" decoration of its atrium distinguishes it from neighboring domus.

name: Villa Poppaea
desc: A seaside villa located in Oplontis, possibly owned by Emperor Nero, based on decorations, date of construction, and pottery fragments inscribed with the name of a freedman of Poppaea Sabina.

name: Castello di Agira
desc: Castello di Agira is situated atop Mount Teja in the province of Enna, approximately 820 meters above sea level.

name: Stadium Domitiani
desc: Domitian built the Stadium Domitiani in the Campus Martius at Rome.

name: Li Schiavoni (Nardò, Lecce)
desc: Li Schiavoni is the site of a fortified Messapic center that flourished in the mid-first millennium BCE.

name: Borg Roman villa
desc: A large Roman courtyard villa covering ca. 7.5 ha.

name: Auf Schiffels
desc: A Roman road station.

name: St. Ulrich
desc: An archaeological site first excavated between 1894 and 1897 that has yielded remains of several villas, including a luxury villa of more than 117 rooms, and a sanctuary.

name: Donon
desc: A sanctuary of the god Mercury in the Vosges Mountains.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge on the Rio Murtazzolu near Birori, Sardinia.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge
desc: Located in the Comune Pabillonis in Sardinia.

name: Crustuminus Ager
desc: The territory of the city of Crustumerium.

name: Collepardo
desc: A sixth-century CE city founded in the time of Theodoric the Great that shows traces of first millennium BCE habitation in the form of polygonal masonry walls.

name: Monte San Giovanni Campano
desc: Monte San Giovanni Campano is the site of ancient first millennium BC fortifications, atop which was built the eleventh century fortress, Castello di Monte San Giovanni Campano, where Thomas Aquinas was imprisoned.

name: Roman villa on viale Alfredo Ottaviani
desc: The ruins of a Roman villa were discovered along viale Alfredo Ottaviani at Acilia Nord in 2011.

name: Posta Vecchia
desc: Remains of a Roman imperial villa incorporated into a post office that later became a hotel.

name: Porta Naevia
desc: The now-lost Porta Naevia was a minor gate in the Republican-period wall of the city of Rome. It was located on the Little Aventine and its position may correspond to the modern Largo Enzo Fioritto.

name: House of the Gorgons
desc: The so-called House of the Gorgons at Ostia originally dates to the late republican period. It has an unusual trapezoidal plan and is divided into 17 rooms.

name: Caseggiato di Bacco e Arianna
desc: The House of Bacchus and Ariadne at Ostia dates to the Hadrianic period and adjoined the Serapeum.

name: Quadriporticus of the theatre
desc: A four-sided portico standing behind the large theater of Pompeii (VIII, 7, 16-17). The complex was constructed ca. 80 BC.

name: Necropolis of San Germano
desc: Burial ground containing 28 burials dated to the Etruscan period.

name: Forte Michelangelo
desc: A fortress at modern Civitavecchia in Italy. It was begun in 1508 and completed in 1537 during the reign of Pope Paul III. Antonio Sangallo the Younger designed the fortress.

name: San Potito Sannitico
desc: A Roman villa in the locality of Torelle at San Potito Sannitico.

name: Castello di Agropoli
desc: A Medieval castle built atop Byzantine foundations.

name: Passo di Corvo
desc: A large, neolithic enclosure

name: Regio VII, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio VII, an archaeological subdivision located in the central western section of Pompeii, contains a mix of residential and commercial structures, as well as the Stabian Baths.

name: Orridroxiu
desc: Two nuraghi located in the valley of Riu Accu 'e Nius.

name: Masseria De Carolis
desc: A Roman villa with an associated bath complex destroyed by the AD 79 eruption of Vesuvius, the Masseria De Carolis site is located in the comune of Pollena Trocchia near Naples, Italy.

name: Via cava del Cavone, Sovana
desc: A hollowed roadway created by cutting the natural tufaceous bedrock. These roads link necropoleis and settlements in the area between Sovana, Sorano, and Pitigliano.

name: Costone della Folonia necropolis
desc: The Costone della Folonia necropolis of Sovana.

name: Valle Bona-Monte Rosello necropolis
desc: A Hellenistic necropolis of Suana.

name: Euphrasian Basilica
desc: An Early Byzantine Christian basilica located in Poreč, Croatia.

name: Larinum Roman amphitheater
desc: An amphitheater of the first century A.D.

name: Arco di Trevi
desc: An opus quadratum monument with an arched gateway perhaps marking a boundary between the territory of the Equi and the Hernicans.

name: Italic temple of Castel di Ieri
desc: The remains of an Italic temple, in the locality known as "Pié di Francia". The sanctuary dates from the fourth to first centuries B.C.

name: Dornburg
desc: A Celtic oppidum.

name: Volcanal
desc: The Volcanal was an open-air sanctuary of Vulcan located in the valley of the Forum Romanum on the slopes of the Capitoline Hill. The earliest phases of the sanctuary likely predate the forum itself.

name: Chalcidicum
desc: Augustus uses the generic term Chalcidicum to describe a porch he built as an approach to the Curia Iulia.

name: Aedicula Concordia
desc: The Aedicula Concordia was a bronze shrine of Concord located on the Graecostasis in Rome. Cn. Flavius erected it when he was aedile in 304 B.C. It is presumed to have been destroyed when the later Temple of Concord was dedicated in 121 B.C.

name: Monte Croce Guardia
desc: Monte Croce Guardia (province of Ancona) was a site of human settlement in the Recent Bronze Age (first half of the twelfth century BCE) that went on to flourish during the Final Bronze Age (ca. 1150-925 BCE). The settlement once covered an area of more than 22 ha.

name: Montefalco
desc: Montefalco is a hilltop town in Italy's present-day Umbria region. Its ancient toponymy and settlement history remain debated, although it is the findspot of several municipal inscriptions in Latin.

name: Temple of Augustales at Centuripae
desc: An early Imperial (first to third centuries) temple at Centuripae that has been associated with the priestly college of the Augustales.

name: Amphitheater of Thizica
desc: The small Roman amphitheater of Thizica.

name: Temple of Hercules, Lanuvium
desc: The Temple of Hercules at Lanuvium.

name: Temple of Jupiter Tonans
desc: A small temple to Jupiter the Thunderer, most likely located in the Area Capitolina. Vowed by Augustus in 26 BCE and dedicated in 22 BCE.

name: Bouleuterion at Ietas
desc: The Bouleuterion at Ietas dates to the later second century B.C.

name: Le Sparne archaeological area
desc: An ancient urban area at Poggio Buco in Italy with a defensive wall that included an agger. Also evidence for an elite building of the archaic period.

name: Theater at Sybaris/Thurii/Copia
desc: The Roman Theater at Sybaris/Thurii/Copia dates originally to the Augustan period.

name: Monte Testaccio
desc: An artificial mountain on the banks of the Tiber River at Rome composed of 580,000 cubic meters of broken amphorae.

name: Via Praenestina
desc: A consular road running from Rome to Praeneste.

name: Salemi
desc: The modern town of Salemi, near Trapani, has been associated with the location of the ancient settlement of Halicyae.

name: balneum Caesaris
desc: A bath complex known from the Severan marble plan and perhaps also referred to in the Historia Augusta.

name: Basilica Argentaria
desc: The toponym "Basilica Argentaria" is a descriptor that appears in fourth-century CE sources for a porticoed complex that dates to the reign of Trajan. This complex was built between the slope of the Capitoline Hill and the Forum Iulium during the terraforming of the Quirinal Hill that created space

name: Ponte Taulella
desc: The ruin called Ponte Taulella was once part of the Aqua Anio Vetus aqueduct.

name: San Giovanni de Butris
desc: A church of the eleventh and twelfth century built along the line of the Roman Via Flaminia. The church incorporates Roman remains, including those of a bridge.

name: Varignano Vecchio
desc: A villa maritima in eastern Liguria, inhabited from ca. 100 BC to the fifth century AD.

name: Domus Aventino
desc: The so-called "Domus Aventino" is located near the Piazza Albania on the Aventine Hill in Rome. This archaeological site was identified in 2014 and preserves multiple phases of human activity, including elements of Rome's archaic fortifications and the remains of a well-appointed domus.

name: tomb of Cerberus
desc: A painted tomb located at Giugliano in Campania, the so-called tomb of Cerberus, was discovered in 2023 during utility work. This is a hypogeum tomb built in tuff blocks with an opus incertum facade. A stepped dromos led to the tomb itself.

name: Temple D (Selinus)
desc: The so-called "Temple D" at Selinus dates ca. 540 BCE. It is a Doric-order temple dedicated to Athena. Its peristylar plan (56 by 24 meters ) has a columnar arrangement of 6 x 13 (order height of 7.51 m high). The building has a pronaos in antis.

name: Temple A (Selinus)
desc: Temple A (Selinus) was built between 490 and 460 BCE. It is a peristyle temple with a plan of 6 x 14 columns (order height of 6.23 m).

name: Ipogeo di San Bartolomeo
desc: A system of caves located in Mazara del Vallo, Sicily, on the right bank of the Mazaro River. Human occupation of the caves began with the Diana Culture (ca. 3500 BCE) and continued into modernity. A paleochristian catacomb was also identified here in the 19th century.

name: Grotta Mangiapane
desc: Grotta Mangiapane is the largest of the so-called Scurati Caves, a series of caverns in Sicily's Trapani province. These caves became a site of human settlement in the Upper Paleolithic. Human settlement activity continued there through the middle of the twentieth century.

name: Teatro di Solunto
desc: A small theater at Soluntum, first erected in the middle of the fourth century BCE and then revitalized in the first century BCE.

name: Castello della Pietra (Vobbia)
desc: The Castello della Pietra is a Medieval fortificaiton located in the comune of Vobbia in the province of Genova. The castle is occupies a position some 540 meters above sea level. It dates to ca. 1252.

name: Vigna Cartoni cistern
desc: A monumental cistern located in what is now the Caffarella park that was likely once part of the estate of Herodes Atticus.

name: Basilica Opimia
desc: A civil basilica built in the Forum Romanum ca. 121 BCE by Lucius Opimius. This basilica was likely razed in 7 BCE.

name: Basilica Porcia
desc: The Basilica Porcia is considered the first named civil basilica in Rome. The elder Cato is responsible for its construction in 184 BCE. It seems to have been a small structure that took the place of several earlier private atria located between the Clivus Argentarius and the Curia Hostilia. The Bas

name: Tomb of Marcus Antonius Antius Lupus
desc: The Tomb of Marcus Antonius Antius Lupus is located at the third mile of the via Ostiensis.

name: Macellum of Hippo Regius
desc: The Macellum of Hippo Regius originates in the early imperial period and is then renovated in Late Antiquity.

desc: Doublet for https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/208942910

name: Withdrawn: Untitled
desc: Withdrawn duplicate for https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/208942909

name: Ponte Genga
desc: A stone bridge at Genga, Italy, that is purportedly of Roman origin.

name: Ponte Tufillo
desc: A bridge that crosses the Tronto River at Ascoli Piceno that dates from the later eleventh century.

name: Atrium Vestae
desc: The Atrium Vestae or House of the Vestals refers to an architectural complex on the northwest slope of the Palatine Hill.

name: Via Basiliano necropolis
desc: An ancient necropolis located in the modern Parco della Serenissima that was initially discovered via construction works in 1997. The necropolis is located, in ancient terms, in a landscape between the line of the via Collatina and that of the via Praenestina. The excavations also revealed traces of

name: Large Theater
desc: The so-called "Large Theater" at Pompeii was built in the Greek style during the second century B.C. Its capacity was approximately 5,000 spectators.

name: Basilica
desc: An important civic building in Pompeii and an early example of the building type, built between ca. 120 and 78 B.C. (VIII, 1, 1).

name: Ager Cosanus survey area
desc: The term "Ager Cosanus" refers to the territorium (territory) of the Latin right colony of Cosa, reportedly established by Rome in south Etruria in 273 B.C. following conflict with the Etruscan city of Vulci. The colonial center of Cosa has been the subject of ongoing archaeological inquiry since th

name: Masseria Ponte
desc: Roman bridge, Masseria Ponte

name: Pollenzo Roman amphitheater
desc: The Roman amphitheater at ancient Pollentia (modern Pollenzo).

name: Emporium
desc: The river port of the ancient city of Rome that was located between the Aventine Hill and the Rione Testaccio, formally established perhaps in 193 BCE.

name: Vignale
desc: A Roman villa, mansio, and Late Antique settlement along the Via Aemilia Scauri.
