name: Italia, Regio IV
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Samnium. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Italia, Regio X
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Venetia and Histria. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Grotte dell'Acqua
desc: Architectural remains near Lago Fusaro that may have been associated with a so-called "villa maritima".

name: Casale Vignale necropolis
desc: An Etruscan rock-cut necropolis of San Giovenale.

name: Grotte di Catullo
desc: Located on the Sirmione peninsula on the southern shore of Lake Garda, "Grotte di Catullo" is the name given to the ruins of a Roman villa dating to the late first century B.C. and the beginning of the first century A.D.

name: Casal Bertone necropolis
desc: Casal Bertone is named for the modern Roman neighborhood where it was discovered, about 2 km east of the Porta Maggiore. The site of Casal Bertone covers more than 3,000 square meters. The eastern portion of the site comprised a residential area that was occupied from about the first century B.C. to

name: Palatium Sessorianum
desc: Palatium Sessorianum is of unknown origins. It was situated at the extreme south-east of Region V and it adjoined the amphitheatrum Castrense. It pre-dated the Aurelian wall. The portions of the complex within the line of the walls was an imperial residence by the time of Constantine.

name: Curia Iulia
desc: Construction of the Curia Julia was begun by Julius Caesar and completed by Augustus in 29 BCE. It replaced the former senate house, the Curia Hostilia.

name: Nuraghe Corbos
desc: A Middle Bronze Age nuragic monument in Silanus, Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe S. Cadrina
desc: A nuragic village of the Middle Bronze Age (ca. 1700-1350 BC), Nuraghe S. Cadrina has a central tower with an original diameter of 11.70 m.

name: Nuraghe Mannu (Doragli)
desc: A nuragic archaeological site in eastern Sardinia that overlooks the village of Cala Gonone.

name: Esaro River (Calabria)
desc: The Esaro River in Calabria is a tributary of the Coscile River.

name: Raviscanina
desc: A pre-Roman center located in the territory of Allifae.

name: Patriarchal Basilica of Santa Maria Assunta of Aquileia
desc: The Basilica di Santa Maria Assunta, Aquileia dates originally to the fourth century.

name: Port-sur-Saône
desc: Port-sur-Saône may be the ancient “Portus Abucinus” included in the Notitia Galliarum. This may have been the location of the martyrdom of Saint Valerius.

name: Poggio La Croce
desc: A fortified Etruscan settlement.

name: Cresta di Gallo
desc: The hill in the province of Trapani known as Cresta di Gallo has evidence for Bronze Age occupation in the form of a necropolis that is linked with the nearby site of Mokarta.

name: Odèon/Ekklesiasterion
desc: The Bouleuterion of ancient Region (modern Reggio Calabria).

name: Escragnolles
desc: A commune in the Alpes-Maritimes department of southeastern France in which a number of ancient sites have been identified.

name: Montebuono
desc: The remains of a villa were excavated near the church of San Pietro ad centum muros in the nineteenth century. Based on epigraphic evidence, the site is connected with M. Vipsanius Agrippa.

name: Christian Basilica, Ostia
desc: The so-called Christian Basilica, located in Regio III of ancient Ostia, was discovered by Guido Calza in 1939. The structure likely dates to the fourth and fifth centuries CE. The interpretation of the structure and its remains has proven difficult, resulting in numerous theories that are often at

name: Necropoli de La Petrina
desc: The "La Petrina" necropolis is associated with ancient Narce and was in use from the eighth to the third centuries BCE.

name: Pompeii I.14.1
desc: A building complex in Regio I of ancient Pompeii that in its final phases was devoted to commercial use that included the production of woven mats.

name: Odeon at Pausilipum
desc: The Roman odeon at Pausilipum.

name: Amphitheatrum Castrense
desc: The Amphitheatrum Castrense is a Roman amphitheater built in the third century AD. Its structure was later incorporated into the Aurelianic Walls. Adjacent to the amphitheater is the Christian church of Santa Croce in Gerusalemme.

name: Nymphaeum divi Alexandri
desc: A monumental nymphaeum on the Esquiline Hill dating to the Severan period; commonly known as "Trofei di Mario". The complex is located at a fork between the Via Tiburtina and the Via Labicana.

name: Roman amphitheater of Milan
desc: The Roman amphitheater of Milan was built near the Porta Ticinese during the second and third centuries. It was destroyed by the time of the Gothic Wars, most likely during the fifth century.

name: Mausoleum of Galla Placidia
desc: An ancient funerary chapel, part of the Santa Croce complex in Ravenna, Italy, possibly built as an imperial mausoleum (ca. AD 417 - 425). The empress Galla Placidia (d. AD 450 ) is the presumed, likely patron of the building, though she is very unlikely to have been entombed within one of three sar

name: Jouy-aux-Arches aqueduct
desc: Remains of a Roman aqueduct that originally served Divodurum Mediomatricum.

name: tribus Clustumina
desc: The tribus Clustumina (or Crustumina) was a rural tribe of Rome which was established in 495 B.C.

name: House of Marcus Lucretius Fronto
desc: The House of M. Lucretius Fronto (V, 4, a, 11), situated off the north side of the Via di Nola, is an example of a refined domus that is small in size but with opulent Third and Fourth style wall paintings.

name: Necropolis of San Giuseppe
desc: The Necropolis of San Giuseppe is located along a cut tufo road or via cava near Pitigliano.

name: Etruscan necropolis of Malignano
desc: An Etruscan necropolis south of Sovicille in the province of Siena. The tombs date from the fifth century B.C. onward.

name: Etruscan necropolis of Pianacce
desc: An Etruscan necropolis located near the center of Sarteano with tombs dating from the sixth to the second centuries B.C. In 2003, the fourth-century painted tomb of the 'infernal quadriga' was discovered.

name: Podere Cannicci (Civitella Paganico - GR)
desc: The site of Podere Cannici has been investigated by means of both non-invasive geophysics and by excavation. Data reveal multiple phases of activity and occupation.

name: Torre di Centocelle
desc: A Medieval tower that was originally built in the twelfth century and is located near the crossroads of the present-day via Casilina and viale Palmiro Togliatti in the city of Rome.

name: Cisterna delle 36 colonne
desc: A large Roman cistern associated with the so-called Villa di Marmura at modern Gianola in Italy.

name: Roman Forum of Catania
desc: The remains of a colonnaded square located near the Cortile di San Pantaleone in Catania are identified as those of the ancient Roman forum.

name: House of Livia
desc: The so-called "House of Livia" on the Palatine Hill in Rome is a multi-phase domus with both Republican and Imperial phases.

name: Domus Augustana
desc: Domus Augustana, a topographic appellation for the central block of the Flavian palace complex on the Palatine Hill attributed to the emperor Domitian.

name: Vatican necropolis
desc: The Vatican necropolis lies beneath Vatican City, specifically beneath the present St. Peter's Basilica, at depths ranging from 5 to 12 meters. The necropolis was partially exposed by means of archaeological excavations in 1940-1949. The necropolis was an open-air burial ground that included both ma

name: Casa della Farnesina
desc: An opulent Roman domus in the Transtiberim with a complex plan and an extraordinary program of painted and stuccoed decorations, the so-called "Casa della Farnesina" lies beneath the gardens of the Renaissance Villa della Farnesina. One hypothesis holds that it was built following the wedding of Mar

name: Unnamed domus in Via Graziosa
desc: A domus excavated in Via Graziosa in Rome, Italy (now the Via Cavour) on 7 April 1848 produced a sequence of wall paintings depicting scenes from Homer's Odyssey.

name: Tomb of Servius Sulpicius Galba
desc: A tomb of the late second century BCE originally located near the Via Ostensis in the district of Rome now known as Testaccio. In antiquity, this was the area known as the Emporium. The tomb is visible on a fragment of the Severan marble plan of Rome and it lies between the Horrea Galbana and the “P

name: Tomb of Marcus Alleius Minius
desc: The Tomb of Marcus Alleius Minius is located outside the Porta Stabia of Pompeii. It is a schola-type tomb, excavated 1888-1890. The tomb carries a Latin inscription and it was buried by debris following the 62 CE earthquake.

name: Ägelmoos
desc: Ägelmoos is an archaeological site located in Beinwil am See in the Swiss canton of Aargau. It is a now-submerged site that was once a lakeside settlement and was occupied between ca. 4500 BCE and 850 BCE.

name: Sepulcra Salaria
desc: The area known as "Sepulcra Salaria" corresponds to the current-day Piazza Fiume, a public square adjacent to the intersection of the Corso d'Italia and Via Piave. Beginning in the later republican period, this funereal area developed. A range of tomb typologies has been identified here.

name: Pranu Muttedu
desc: Pranu Muttedu is a pre- and protohistoric archaeological site located near Goni, Sardinia. The complex includes standing stones (menhirs) and prehistoric built tombs (domus de janas). The site dates to the Late Neolithic (3200 – 2800 BC) and Early Chalcolithic (2800 – 2600 BC) periods.

name: Necropolis of Sant'Andrea Priu
desc: A prehistoric necropolis in Sardinia associated with the Ozieri culture and dating to the Final Neolithic period (ca. 3500-2900 BC).

name: Nuraghe S'Ortali 'e su Monti
desc: A nuragic complex dating ca. 1500 BC near Tortolì in Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Serbissi
desc: A nuragic complex located near Osini, Sardinia.

name: Malchittu nuragic temple
desc: A sacred structure with an 'in antis' plan located near Arzachena in Sardinia.

name: Santa Maria in Legarano
desc: Site of a large Roman villa, the remains of which were incorporated into the church of Santa Maria in Legarano. The early phases of the villa likely date to the early imperial period. At some point the villa became an Imperial property as it was donated to Pope Sylvester by Constantine.

name: Antro delle Sorti
desc: The "Cave of the Fates" at Praeneste is a sanctuary at the base of the city's terraced sanctuary of Fortuna. It was said to contain wooden oracular tablets.

name: Arco dei Gavi
desc: A Roman arch built by the gens Gavia.

name: The Sassi and the Park of the Rupestrian Churches of Matera
desc: A series of rock-cut dwellings and buildings.

name: Hellenistic and Roman quarter archaeological area
desc: The Hellenistic and Roman area is orthogonally planned and covers more than 15,000 square meters. It is located near Poggio San Nicola.

name: Bouleuterion at Akragas/Agrigentum
desc: A bouleuterion complex at Akragas (modern Agrigento in Sicily).

name: Upper Agora at Akragas/Agrigentum
desc: The Upper Agora at Akragas at Poggetto di San Nicola is the site of the ekklesiasterion, the so-called "Oratory of Phalaris", and the bouleuterion.

name: Fortifications at Civita di Artena
desc: The polygonal masonry fortifications of the ancient settlement now known as Civita di Artena. These fortifications today measure more than 2.5 km in length.

name: Monte Rocche
desc: A settlement of the Iron Age and Roman period in western Liguria.

name: Circuit wall of Rusellae
desc: The megalithic defensive circuit of Rusellae dates to the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. and represents an important early example of stone-built fortifications in central Italy.

name: Roman amphitheater at Alalie/Aleria
desc: A Roman amphitheater located in eastern Corsica.

name: Roman amphitheater at Thermae Himeraeae
desc: Roman amphitheater at Termini Imerese was of modest size and is today poorly preserved.

name: Roman amphitheater at Hydata Hypsitana/Forum Traiani
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Forum Traiani, modern Fordongianus

name: Roman baths at Hydata Hypsitana/Forum Traiani
desc: The Roman baths Fordongianus dates to the first through third centuries.

name: Roman theater at Ocriculum
desc: The Roman theater at Ocriculum dates to the early imperial period.

name: Monte Cornacchia
desc: Monte Cornacchia is the highest peak in the Daunian Mountains and the region of Apulia region (1,151 m (3,776 ft)).

name: Trebbio
desc: An Iron Age settlement covering some 20 ha was identified at Trebbio, located to the south of Sansepolcro.

name: Via Sublacensis
desc: The Via Sublacensis was built in order to connect the Villa Neronis (Nero's villa at Sublaqueum) to Rome. It split from the Via Valeria near Varia.

name: Via Herculia
desc: A Roman road known through epigraphic attestations, the Via Herculia connected Aquilonia and Aequum Tuticum.

name: ager Mutycensis
desc: The territory of Motyca in the Roman province of Sicilia that, according to Cicero, supported 187 farmers.

name: Prehistoric pile dwellings around the Alps
desc: A series of prehistoric pile-dwelling settlements in and around the Alps built from around 5000 to 500 B.C. on the edges of lakes, rivers or wetlands; 111 sites in all.

name: Acropolis of Aletrium
desc: The Acropolis of Aletrium, often referred to as the "Civita", is the fortified citadel of the ancient city. Surrounded by polygonal walls, it is accessed via two gates.

name: Forum Romanum
desc: The ancient Roman forum.

name: Casale dell’Infernaccio
desc: A Roman villa located at Magliana Vecchia that dates to the second century A.D.

name: Domus of Publius Confuleius Sabbio
desc: The domus of the freedman P. Confuleius Sabbio at Capua.

name: Arch of Augustus (Susa)
desc: An arch dedicated to Augustus at Susa in the late first century BC that records the renewed alliance between the princeps and Marcus Julius Cottius.

name: Segusio aqueduct
desc: A Roman aqueduct of Segusio.

name: Castrum Caetani
desc: A Medieval fortification that incorporates and repurposes the Roman mausoleum of Caecilia Metella.

name: So-called "Temple of Augustus"
desc: A temple dedicated to Octavian by a Lucius Calpurnius. It replaced a temple of ca. 194 B.C. that had in turn been restored by Sulla.

name: Canicella necropolis
desc: An Etruscan necropolis located to the south of the city of Orvieto with tombs ranging in date from the eighth to the third centuries B.C.

name: Roman amphitheater of Catania
desc: The Roman amphitheater of Catania is the largest known ancient amphitheater in Sicily. Its external dimensions measure ca. 125 x 105 meters. It likely dates to the second century.

name: Roman baths at Fundi
desc: Imperial baths located on Fundi's decumanus maximus.

name: Roman amphitheater at Eporedia
desc: The extramural Roman amphitheater at Eporedia is evidence of the expanding suburbium of the Roman settlement.

name: Forum of Iuvanum
desc: The Roman forum of Iuvanum.

name: Roman theater at Iuvanum
desc: The Roman theater at Iuvanum is located at the foot of the acropolis.

name: Villa urbana
desc: A Roman villa that has now been reconstructed.

name: Roman amphitheater at Veleia
desc: The Roman amphitheater of Roman Veleia.

name: Roman amphitheater at Spoletium
desc: The remains of the early Imperial amphitheater were discovered within the Caserma Minervio during the early nineteenth century.

name: Arch of Augustus at Ariminum
desc: The Arch of Augustus at Ariminum was dedicated in 27 B.C. and marked the end of the Via Flaminia.

name: Roman amphitheater at Verona
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Verona dates to ca. A.D. 30.

name: Porta Borsari
desc: A first century A.D. gate at Verona, the point at which the Via Postumia entered the city.

name: Roman amphitheater at Abella
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Abella has been compared to the amphitheater of Pompeii.

name: Santa Lucia in Selci
desc: The church of Santa Lucia in Selci was founded by the eighth century and perhaps as early as the sixth century.

name: San Martino ai Monti
desc: San Martino ai Monti is a minor basilica in Rome. The basilica was founded on a site donated by Equitius during the reign of Pope St. Sylvester I in the fourth century.

name: Lago di Burano
desc: A coastal lacustrine basin near Capalbio Scalo, Italy.

name: Fluvius Vulpis
desc: A river included on the Peutinger map.

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: This bridge in Liguria is also colloquially referred to as "the Roman bridge". The current 10-arched structure could have Roman origins and could be the place where the Via Iulia Augusta crossed the Merula.

name: Sa Sedda 'e sos Carros
desc: A middle Bronze Age (ca. 1300 B.C.) nuragic settlement.

name: Daunian Mountains
desc: A mountain range of southern Italy that constitutes the eastern appendix of the Campanian Apennines.

name: Aquas volaternas
desc: A place named on the Peutinger map, possibly to be associated with modern Monte Cerboli, Italy.

name: Troculu
desc: A megalithic "giant's tomb" in proximity to a nuragic settlement.

name: Nuraghe Cabudbbene
desc: Nuraghe Cabudbbene I is a single tower nuraghe built of trachyte.

name: Odeon at Catania
desc: The small, covered odeon at Catania likely dates to the second century CE and is located adjacent to the open-air theater.

name: Temple of Magna Mater
desc: The Temple of Magna Mater, also known as the Temple of Cybele, was dedicated near the Clivus Victoriae on the Palatine Hill on 11 April 191 BCE. The original temple was destroyed by fire in 111 BCE. Following another series of destructive fires, Augustus restored the temple, as he records in his Res

name: Aedes Apollinis Palatini
desc: The temple sacred to the god Apollo on the Palatine Hill in Rome.

name: Shop with dwelling (VII.4.22)
desc: The ruins of VII.4.22 at Pompeii are identified as a shop with an associated dwelling and are linked to VII.4.21. The site was excavated in 1822 and again in 1833 and was bombed during the Second World War (13 September 1943). Among the themes depicted in the wall paintings of the structure are thos

name: Cispius Mons
desc: Cispius Mons, a spur of the Esquiline Hill wedged between the Viminal and the Oppian.

name: Forum of Cosa
desc: The forum of Cosa functioned as the administrative center of the town and was the site of key administrative and ritual structures.

name: Tullianum
desc: Prison located at the foot of the Capitoline Hill, named either for Servius Tullius (578–535 BCE) or for the spring (tullus) on which it was constructed. Also known as the Mamertine Prison. The church of San Giuseppe dei Falegnami was constructed on the site in the 11th century CE.

name: Temple of Hadrian
desc: The Temple of Hadrian at Rome, also referred to as the Hadrianeum, was a temple located in the Campus Martius dedicated to the deified Hadrian by Antoninus Pius in 145 CE. Some of the temple's substantial remains were incorporated into a 17th-century building designed by architect Carlo Fontana in R

name: College of the Augustales
desc: The so-called College of the Augustales at Herculaneum was built at the end of the first century BC. The brothers A. Lucius Proculus and A. Lucius Iulianus served as patrons of the project.

name: House of the Hotel
desc: The so-called House of the Hotel (Casa dell'Albergo) is an opulent Augustan-period domus that occupies the bulk of the southern end of Insula III at Herculaneum.

name: House of Aristides
desc: A domus at Herculaneum that earned its modern sobriquet thanks to the misidentification of a statue found in its ruins. The statue in question was thought to be Aristides, one of the ten Attic orators, when, in fact, it is a statue of Aeschines.

name: Via Pompeia?
desc: An ancient road of Sicily linking Syracuse and Messina.

name: Elephas herbarius
desc: Elephas herbarius (Elefantum herbarium), a place included in the Notitia, is mentioned only once and must lie at the southern limit of Regio VIII. Coarelli concludes that this place must have been located on the lower slopes of the Capitoline Hill facing the Forum Holitorium. Its coincidence with La

name: François Tomb
desc: An important painted Etruscan tomb dating to the final quarter of the fourth century B.C.

name: Vagnari
desc: A villa, vicus, and necropolis site in modern Puglia, Italy, located near the modern city of Gravina. The site was active from the first to fourth centuries CE.

name: Nuraghe Loelle
desc: A nuragic site near Caput Tyrsi.

name: Roman villa at Maasbracht
desc: A Roman villa near the modern village of Maasbracht, Limburg, Netherlands, famous for its murals. The earliest structures on the site are dated to the second century CE, and the villa was abandoned by the middle of the third century.

name: Casa dell'Impluvium at Rusellae
desc: The so-called "Casa dell'Impluvium" at Rusellae was excavated in the 1980s. It may present an important, early example of an Italic courtyard house. It dates to the sixth century B.C.

name: Roman amphitheater at Interamnia Praetuttiorum
desc: A Roman amphitheater of the first century A.D.

name: Forum of Scylletium/Scolacium
desc: The Roman Forum of Scylletium/Scolacium.

name: Roman amphitheater at Scylletium/Scolacium
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Scylletium/Scolacium.

name: Byzantine necropolis
desc: A necropolis of Scolacium dating to the fifth through seventh centuries.

name: Roman amphitheater at Egnatia/Gnathia
desc: The so-called Roman amphitheater at Egnatia/Gnathia dates to the Iulio-Claudian period. It is an elliptical structure with walls in opus Africanum that were revetted with painted plaster.

name: Roman amphitheater at Rudiae
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Rudiae is part of the complement of Roman buildings dating to the imperial period.

name: Roman amphitheater at Carsulae
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Carsulae dates to the first century A.D.

name: Amphitheater Birten
desc: A Roman amphitheater located at Castra Vetera (modern Birten Germany)

name: Roman amphitheater at Ocriculum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Ocriculum lies outside the city walls.

name: Aedes Ceres Liber Liberaque
desc: The Temple of Ceres, located on the slope of the Aventine Hill in Rome, was originally dedicated by Sp. Cassius in 494/3 B.C.

name: Costa Murata archaeological area
desc: A site with votive activity from the Archaic period and a later Roman house in addition to the basalt-paved Roman road.

name: Roman baths at Fiesole
desc: The Roman baths at Fiesole date to the time of Sulla in the first century B.C.

name: Drususstein (Drususstone) at Mogontiacum
desc: The remains of a Roman monument at Mainz, perhaps a cenotaph erected in 9 B.C.

name: Römersteine im Zahlbachtal
desc: Site of the remains of the Roman aqueduct, Römersteine im Zahlbachtal, in the district of Mainz-Bretzenheim.

name: Grutenhäuschen
desc: The Grutenhäuschen is a Roman funereal temple of the third or fourth century A.D. It has been reconstructed on site.

name: La Temple de la Madeleine, Geneva
desc: The oldest Christian church in the city of Geneva, the Temple de la Madeleine site has been in continuous use as a church since the 5th century. The current structure on the site dates to the 15th century.

name: Marino Mithraeum
desc: A Mithraic shrine of unusual size discovered at modern Marino, Italy in 1963.

name: Ninfa
desc: Ninfa is now a garden landscape covering more than 100 hectares in the territory of Cisterna di Latina. In archaeological terms, this landscape includes many remains stretching from protohistory to the Middle Ages.

name: Praetorian Guard Barracks at Amba Aradam Metro Station
desc: Excavations for Rome's Metro C public transit line at the Amba Aradam Station revealed the remains of a second century A.D. barracks connected with the Praetorian Guard, along with a domus identified as that of a praetorian commandant. Although ruinous, the architectural complex demonstrates good pr

name: Via Veientana
desc: The ancient Via Veientana led from Etruscan Veii to the Tiber river.

name: Nuraghe Sa Domu 'e s'Orcu (Sarroch)
desc: A bilobate nuraghe located to the east of Sarroch, Sardinia.

name: Columbarium, Via del Casale Ferranti
desc: Roman columbarium tombs in the Via del Casale Ferranti.

name: Roman forum of Iulium Carnicum
desc: The Roman forum and civic basilica at Iulium Carnicum (modern Zuglio)

name: Portus Iulius
desc: The so-called "Portus Iulius" is an ancient Roman port complex on the Bay of Naples. Its remains are now submerged due to the bradyseism of the Phlegraean Fields. The archaeological remains were first rediscovered in 1956.

name: Crocifisso del Tufo necropolis
desc: A major necropolis of Volsinii that reaches its maximum extent between 550 and 450 BC. The necropolis is especially noteworthy on account of its orthogonal layout.

name: Tomba dei giganti di Laccaneddu
desc: A Bronze Age "giant's tomb" in Sardinia.

name: Moregine
desc: Moregine, immediately to the south of the archaeological site of Pompeii, is the findspot of an important archaeological assemblage buried by seismic activity that preceded the final eruption of Vesuvius in A.D. 79.

name: Casa del pomarius Felix
desc: This house (I.8.2) opens onto the Via dell'Abbondanza and is connected to the taberna at I.8.1 and the shop at I.8.3. It was named the "Casa del pomarius Felix" from electoral programmata painted on its facade. It has a typical atrium-peristyle plan.

name: Chiesa Ipogea di San Nicola
desc: A poorly understood paleochristian site located on the grounds of the Inviolata park in the comune of Guidonia-Montecelio in the greater metropolitan area of Rome. The cave site may originally have functioned as a mithraeum.

name: Chiesa di Santa Pudenziana, Narni
desc: The church of Santa Pudenziana near Narni, Italy, dates from the ninth to eleventh centuries CE and reuses spoliated architectural elements from a Roman villa.

name: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus
desc: The chief temple of the city of Rome was located on the Capitoline Hill.

name: Columbarium of Tiberius Claudius Vitalis
desc: A columbarium tomb located on the grounds of the Villa Wolkonsky in Rome, Italy.

name: Villa Romana Baláca
desc: The site of a Roman villa that was discovered in 1904 in the Balácapuszta field of Vámos village in western Hungary.

name: Welzheim: Ostkastell
desc: One of two Roman forts located at modern Welzheim in Germany, the excavated remains of the "Ostkastell" are largely preserved. The west gate and a portion of the associated defensive wall was reconstructed in the 1970s.

name: Auguratorium
desc: An augural area on the Palatine Hill mentioned in the Regionary Catalogues for Regio X.

name: House of the Surgeon (Rimini)
desc: The so-called House of the Surgeon in Rimini may have been the home of a Roman doctor by the name of Eutyches.

name: Boucheporn
desc: A significant center in eastern Gaul producing sigillate pottery.

name: Regio IX (Circus Flaminius)
desc: The ninth administrative region of the city of Rome was created under the Augustan reforms of 7 BCE. According to the Notitia et Curiosum, this region contained 35 shrines (aediculae), 140 townhouses (domūs), 25 warehouses (horrea), 63 bathhouses, and 120 fountains). The region was subdivided into 3

name: Regio X (Palatium)
desc: Regio X (Palatium) is one of the Augustan regions of the city of Rome. The Regionary Catalogues indicate that this regio contained 20 shrines (aediculae), 89 townhouses (domūs), 48 warehouses (horrea), 44 bath houses, and 89 fountains. Its perimeter was recorded as 11,510 Roman feet (approx. 3.4 km)

name: Arcus Novus
desc: A now-lost arch on the ancient Via Lata. It was dedicated to Diocletian either in 293 CE (marking the occasion of his decennalia) or in 303-304 (joint triumph with Maximian). The present church of Santa Maria in Via Lata occupies the site of the arch.

name: Circus Varianus
desc: A circus that was part of the Sessorium palace next to the Amphitheatrum Castrense. The obelisk currently situated on the Pincian Hill was discovered on the site in the sixteenth century. It had been moved to the spina of the circus during the reign of Elagabalus.

name: Aedes Fauni
desc: A temple dedicated to Faunus located on Tiber Island, the Aedes Fauni was dedicated in 196 BCE by Gnaeus Domitius Ahenobarbus and Gaius Scribonius Libo.

name: Roman bridge over Rio S'Adde
desc: Remains of a Roman bridge, north of Makopsisa (modern Macomer in Sardinia).

name: Villa di Podere Anna
desc: The ruins of a Roman villa rustica were discovered in the 1990s along via Diego Fabbri. The site dates to the first century B.C. and remained in use at least until the fifth century A.D. The remains of a bath complex are substantial.

name: Punta di Zambrone
desc: Excavations at the site of Punta di Zambrone have documented indigenous settlements of the early Iron Age in Calabria.

name: Baths of the Old Convent, Tharros
desc: Roman baths at Tharros known as the "Baths of the Old Convent".

name: Su Coddu
desc: A prehistoric settlement covering some 10 hectares with evidence for approximately 150 huts located in Selargius, Sardinia.

name: Insula Volusiana
desc: The Insula Volusiana in the Forum Boarium is an archaeological site with evidence for multiphase occupation, including craftworking evidence from the fifth and sixth centuries CE.

name: Ponte sul Fosso Tre Ponti
desc: A Roman bridge on the Via Amerina between ancient Nepet and Falerii.

name: Casa dell’ Amore punito
desc: A domus excavated in 1844 and 1867.

name: Roman necropolis at Melano
desc: Roman necropolis in the modern town of Melano, Switzerland, containing 29 burials dated to the 1st-2nd centuries CE.

name: Anfiteatro laterizio
desc: A Roman amphitheater located to the northwest of Nola and dating to the first century BCE.

name: Santa Savinilla catacomb
desc: A Late Imperial catacomb located in the territory of Nepet. The Christian church of San Tolomeo alle Sante Grotte developed at the site of the catacomb.

name: Tempio della Tosse
desc: The so-called "Tempio della Tosse" is an ancient Roman building along the river Anio. Its dating is problematic, but it is likely a building of late antiquity that is built on the site of an earlier villa. It has been interpreted as a nymphaeum, a temple, and also as a tomb.

name: Temple of the Sibyl
desc: A second-century B.C. Roman temple located on the acropolis of ancient Tibur. The so-called Temple of the Sibyl is a pseudo-peripteral building executed in the Ionic order. Some portions of the structure, including the side walls and rea wall, survive to the height of the capitals.

name: Minor Acropolis, Norba
desc: The so-called Minor Acropolis is located on the hill to the south of the Porta Maggiore. This area is surrounded by the urban enclosure wall and is terraced in polygonal masonry. Two platform temples of unknown assignation are to be found here.

name: Forum of Norba
desc: The forum of Norba measures ca. 125 x 63 m.

name: Dam over the Simbruina Stagna
desc: Between Sublaqueum and Villa Neronis

name: Dam over the Simbruina Stagna
desc: East of Sacro Speco

name: Bridge
desc: Within the Villa Neronis

name: Capo di Bove
desc: An archaeological site located at the fourth milestone of the Via Appia Antica.

name: Valbandon Roman Villa(s)
desc: Architectural remains consistent with a Roman-era villa maritima have been identified on both the north and south sides of a small bay at modern Valbandon in Croatia. Originally thought to represent a single establishment that wrapped the entire bay, more recent interpretations would see two separat

name: Torre delle Milizie
desc: A fortified Medieval tower built adjacent to the Forum of Trajan in Rome.

name: Sambracitanus Sinus
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 C3 Sambracitanus Sinus

name: Sanremo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 E2 Sanremo

name: Tavia (river)
desc: A river flowing from Alpes Maritimae and emptying into the Ligusticum Mare near Costa Bellene.

name: Tropaeum Augusti/Alpium Tropaeum/Alpis Summa/Alpis Maritima
desc: A victory monument built by Augustus (5 B.C.) to commemorate the subjugation of the tribes of the western Alps. The Romans considered the spot to be "In Alpe Maritima".

name: Varus (river)
desc: The Var river.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 16 D2 Vaugrenier

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: Located between Costa Balenae and Portus Maurici (at or near modern San Lorenzo al Mare, over the Rio della Torre, Italy).

desc: A monastery founded in late antiquity on the island then known as Lerina/Planasia (modern Île Saint-Honorat, France; BAtlas 16 D2 unnamed monastery)

name: Alpes Cottiae
desc: Alpes Cottiae (Cottian Alps) are a mountain range located the southwestern part of the Alps. They take their name from Marcus Julius Cottius.

name: Alpes Graiae (region)
desc: The mountainous area around the Little St Bernard Pass, conquered by the Romans and organized by Augustus into the province that took its name (q.v.). desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 17 H2 *Alpis Graia

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 17 I2 Arebrigium

name: Ariolica
desc: Ariolica was a Roman road station located at or near modern La Thuile, Italy.

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 17 H2 Axima/Forum Claudii Ceutronum

name: Bergintrum
desc: Bergintrum (Bourg-Saint-Maurice) was a settlement located to the west of the Alpes Graiae along the road connecting Mediolanum (modern Milan) and Vienna (modern Vienne).

desc: Octodurus/Forum Claudii Vallensium (modern Martigny).

desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 17 H4 Le Plan de Phazy

name: Poeninus (mountain)
desc: Great St. Bernard.

name: Pondel
desc: A Roman aqueduct dating to 3 B.C.

name: Semo Sancus, Aedes
desc: A sanctuary on the Quirinal Hill in Rome sacred to the cult of Semo Sancus Dius Fidius, a cult of Sabine origin said to have been introduced to Rome by Titus Tatius. The dedication of the temple is generally attributed to Sp. Postumius on 5 June 466 BCE.

name: La Marmotta
desc: An Early Neolithic settlement that is now submerged beneath the waters of Lake Bracciano. Settlement activity begins ca. 5750 BCE.

name: via Pedana
desc: The via Pedana, known only from epigraphic evidence, led presumably from Rome to Pedum. It was likely a branch of the via Praenestina.

name: Nuraghe Sa Mandra 'e Sa Giua
desc: A nuraghe and associated village.

name: Grotta Mora Cavorso
desc: Cave site in the Aniene Valley in central Italy with signs of human activity from the Early Neolithic period to the early Bronze Age.

name: Steinerner Steg - Ponte Romano
desc: A two-arched, stone-built footbridge across the Passer in Merano, South Tyrol.

name: House of the Thunderbolt
desc: A Vespasianic domus in Ostia Antica, built ca. 70-75 CE, situated outside the Porta Marina, and north of the continuation of the Decumanus Maximus. It had a slightly concave façade, comprising six shops and an entrance corridor leading to an interior peristyle garden.

name: Garden Houses
desc: A large residential complex, built in ca. 128 CE as part of the Hadrianic remodeling of Ostia. Its central area was occupied by two blocks, each comprising four houses, surrounded by a garden furnished with six fountains.

name: House of the Fishes
desc: A domus in Ostia Antica, whose two building phases have been dated, respectively, to the middle and last quarter of the third century CE.

name: Honos et Virtus, Aedes
desc: The Temple of Honour and Virtue (aedes Honoris et Virtutis) was a double temple founded by Q. Fabius Maximus Verrucosus in 234 BCE. The temple and mentions of it seem to have disappeared after the fourth century CE. It was located outside the Porta Capena (ad portam Capenam), likely on the north sid

name: Mars, Aedes
desc: A temple sacred to Mars located on the Via Appia. The shrine was located between the first and second milestones and was dedicated in the fourth century BC. According to Livy, Titus Quinctius dedicated the temple on 1 June 387 BC.

name: Porta Metronia
desc: Porta Metronia, a gate in the Aurelian Walls of Rome.

name: Porta Portuensis
desc: The Porta Portuensis was one of the gates of the Aurelian Wall of Rome, located in the Transtiberim. The original gate carried an inscription of Honorius and was destroyed during the reign of Pope Urban VIII. The present Porta Portese, built by architect Vincenzo Maculani in 1644, occupies its site.

name: Roman bath at Fregellae
desc: A two-phase complex of public baths at Fregellae dating to the third and second centuries BCE represents an important point in the transition from "Greek" bathing culture to "Roman" bathing culture.

name: Serra del Cedro (Basilicata)
desc: The hill of Serra del Cedro in Basilicata (858 meters above sea level) is occupied already in the archaic period. By the fourth century BCE the settlement covers some 30 ha.

name: Western gate and walls of Peltuinum
desc: The Western gate and walls of Peltuinum.

name: Botzdorf Roman villa
desc: The remains of a Roman villa dating to the first century CE were discovered in the Botzdorf district of the city of Bornheim in the Rhein-Sieg district of Germany in 2002. It is also referred to as the "Villa Fortuna".

name: Porto romano
desc: The remains of the ancient port area of San Marco (Comune di Castellabate) date from the first century BCE.

name: Cuccureddus
desc: A Phoenician port of southeastern Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Rumanedda
desc: A nuraghe located near Tottubella in the territory of Sassari.

name: Basilica di Santa Restituta
desc: The Basilica of Santa Restituta is a Christian church in Naples, Italy. It is considered the oldest Christian basilica in the city. Tradition assigns its foundation to Constantine I, and the Liber Pontificalis identifies him as patron in a passage from the life of Pope Sylvester I. The Christian chu

name: Privata domus Traiani
desc: The so-called "Privata domus Traiani" was an opulent townhouse on the Aventine Hill in Rome. Its foundations were eventually coopted in the third century CE for the construction of the Baths of Decius. Evidence from brickstamps dates the building to the Trajanic to early Antonine period, leading som

name: Arch of Titus (Circus Maximus)
desc: A triple-bay triumphal arch was erected at the eastern end of the Circus Maximus in honor of Emperor Titus' role in the victory in the Jewish War. The arch is known from architectural and sculptural fragments and from an inscription recorded in the Einsiedeln sylloge.

name: Porta Nord
desc: The so-called "north gate" of Selinus dates to the fifth century BCE.

name: Catacombs of Villagrazia
desc: A paleochristian catacomb dating to the fourth century CE.

name: Castello di Lombardia
desc: Local tradition holds that the Castello di Lombardia, located at Enna, was established on the site of a fortified acropolis of the Sicani. The castle is located on a mountain top some 970 meters above sea level.) The castle remains that are visible in the present day belong to a construction phase i

name: Tomb of the Servilii
desc: A tomb known as the "Tomb of the Servilii" which pre-dates the Mausoleum of Romulus, was incorporated into the porticus surrounding the latter. This tomb dates to the late first century BCE or early first century CE.

name: Punta Milazzese
desc: A prehistoric village was situated on the promontory of Punta Milazzese at Panarea in Sicily. This Middle Bronze Age village (fourteenth to thirteenth centuries BCE) was identified in 1948 by Luigi Bernabò Brea. Excavations were carried out in 1949-1950 and again in 2008-2009. The material culture o

name: Catacomb of Apronianus
desc: Antonio Bosio discovered the paleochristian Catacomb of Apronianus in 1596. It is located two miles from the Porta Latina.

name: Argiletum
desc: The Argiletum was a street of ancient Rome that passed from the Forum Romanum and crossed the Suburra. Its route more or less followed that of the modern streets Via Leonina and Via della Madonna dei Monti.

name: La Celsa
desc: At La Celsa (12.7 km of the Via Flaminia) are the remains of a cylindrical drum mausoleum that was likely once part of a larger funereal complex.

name: Sanctuary at Fondo Iozzino
desc: An extra-urban sanctuary located outside of the Porta Nocera of Pompeii. Excavations at the sanctuary have revealed votive activity in multiple periods, including the pre-Roman phases of Pompeii. Inscribed bucchero pottery indicates connections with leading Etruscan families of central Italy.

name: Sette Sale
desc: Cisterns of the imperial period on the Oppian Hill that once supplied the Baths of Trajan.

name: Basilica Neptuni
desc: A building in the Campus Martius that originally dates to ca. 25 BCE.

name: Mithraeum at Riegel
desc: A temple once sacred to Mithras located in Riegel am Kaiserstuhl (Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany).

name: House of the Bicentenary
desc: A domus at Herculaneum that occupies a large area in the northern section of the insula.

name: Neapolis of Syracuse
desc: A district of the ancient city of Syracuse.

name: San Gimignano
desc: San Gimignano, which originated as an Etruscan settlement, is best known as a Medieval town renowned for its fortified towers.

name: Flavian Amphitheater at Puteoli
desc: The Flavian Amphitheater at Puteoli is an amphitheater constructed in the port town of Puteoli under the Flavian dynasty around 80 CE.

name: Velabrum
desc: The Velabrum is a valley in Rome that connects the Forum Romanum to the Forum Boarium.

name: Pantheon
desc: A temple in the Campus Martius of Rome that was first built by Marcus Agrippa (ca. 27-25 B.C.) and then rebuilt by the emperor Hadrian (after A.D. 126). In A.D. 609, the structure was consecrated as a Christian church, S. Maria ad Martyres.

name: Villa dei Casoni
desc: The Villa dei Casoni is sometimes referred to as the Villa di Varrone, based on some scholarly assumptions that it once belonged to Marcus Terentius Varro. This late republican to early imperial platform villa is located near Poggio Mirteto, Montopoli di Sabina, Italy.

name: Monte Amiata
desc: Monte Amiata is a lava dome located about 20 km northwest of Lake Bolsena in Italy.

name: Gran Sasso d'Italia
desc: The Gran Sasso d'Italia is a mountain located in the Abruzzo region of central Italy.

name: Herculaneum Gate
desc: A city gate of Pompeii that dates to the time of Sulla.

name: Terrace of Zeus
desc: The so-called "Terrace of Zeus" or "Terrazza di Zeus" at Elea-Velia.

name: Aequimelium
desc: The Aequimelium was an open area on the southeast slope of the Capitoline Hill. This space may have once been the site of the house of one Spurius Maelius, a Roman citizen of the fifth century BCE who was slain for the crime of wanting to be a king (adfectatio regni).

name: Necropoli Fondo Scataglini
desc: An Etruscan necropolis at Tarquinia with more than 175 tombs.

name: So-called Early Christian Basilica
desc: A small basilica located outside the walls of the ancient Greek city of Akragas, at the foot of the so-called Temple of Juno, on the eastern slopes of the Hill of the Temples, in an area previously occupied by the necropolis of the late Roman period.

name: City wall of Ugento - Mura Messapiche
desc: The so-called "Mura Messapiche" at Ugento.

name: Necropolis of Porta Ercolano
desc: The Porta Ercolano necropolis, excavated between 1763 and 1838, is the best known of Pompeii's necropoleis, in use from the middle of the first century BC until the first century AD.

name: St. Pauls villa
desc: A Late Roman villa discovered ca. 2005.

name: Sillian milestone
desc: An uninscribed Roman milestone discovered in 1970 at Sillian, Tirol, Austria. The milestone corresponds to the 24th mile from Aguntum.

name: Susegana bridge
desc: A Roman bridge along the Via Claudia Augusta.

name: Terme Achilliane
desc: Thermal baths at Catania dating to the fourth and fifth centuries CE. The archaeological remains are located near the present-day Piazza del Duomo of Catania.

name: Porta Santo Spirito
desc: The Porta Santo Spirito is a gate of the Leonine Wall.

name: Scalae caci
desc: A stairway located at the southwest corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome, the Scalae caci led from the hilltop down to the valley of the Circus Maximus. If the amended manuscript of Plutarch's biography of Romulus is to be followed, then the Scalae caci provide a point of orientation for location of

name: Castello di Pieve del Vescovo
desc: The present late fourteenth-century castle on the site is first mentioned in a papal bull of 1206.

name: House of the Golden Bracelet
desc: The so-called "House of the Golden Bracelet" is a domus at Pompeii located on the Vicolo del Farmacista. It takes its name from the discovery of the remains of a woman wearing a thick gold bracelet.

name: Etruscan Pyramid of Bomarzo
desc: The so-called Etruscan Pyramid of Bomarzo is a megalithic, rock-cut monument at Bomarzo. It likely dates to the late Archaic period.

name: Miersch
desc: A Roman villa rustica discovered at Miersch in the early twentieth century. It was abandoned ca. 400 CE.

name: Zingsheim
desc: A Gallo-Roman temple of the Matronae Aufaniae.

name: House of Leda and the Swan
desc: The so-called House of Leda and the Swan at Pompeii (Regio V 6,12) is located along the street referred to as Via del Vesuvio. The domus is well-appointed with Fourth Style wall paintings.

name: Tomb of Marcus Veius Marcellus
desc: The Tomb of Marcus Veius Marcellus at Pompeii.

name: Comitium of Pompeii
desc: The complex referred to as the Comitium of Pompeii is located in the southeast corner of the square of the Forum and was built during the second century BC.

name: tribus Pollia
desc: The tribus Pollia was one of the older rural tribes of Rome.

name: Ponte d'Arli
desc: A Roman bridge along the Via Salaria near Ascoli Piceno.

name: Pian della Conserva
desc: An Etruscan necropolis located 5 km from Tolfa with tombs stretching from the Orientalizing period to the later Hellenistic.

name: Tomb of the Ottavii
desc: The mid-third century CE tomb of the Ottavii was discovered beneath the Villino Cardani (now at Via della Stazione di Ottavia, 73) on 17 August 1921. Based on epigraphic evidence, the tomb was occupied by the remains of one Octavia Paolina, her father Octavius Felix, and two other relatives. The arc

name: Basilica Hilariana
desc: A basilica erected on the Caelian Hill in Rome under the patronage of Manius Publicus Hilarus and connected to the cult of Cybele and Attis.

name: Basilica Benedettina di S. Michele Arcangelo
desc: An abbey church located in Capua on the western slopes of Monte Tifata.

name: Tempio di Venere, Baiae
desc: The so-called "Tempio di Venere" is likely part of a bathing complex dating to the reign of Hadrian. The surviving structure has an octagonal plan.

name: Vacone Roman villa
desc: A Roman villa site near Rieti known initially from several cryptoporticus structures. More recent excavations have revealed a series of rooms, including some with mosaic pavement.

name: Piazza d'Armi
desc: The site of the arx of ancient Veii located on the southern spur of the volcanic plateau on which the city is located. There is archaeological evidence for an initial occupation phase of the ninth century B.C. By the seventh century B.C., the area shows evidence for adoption of rectilinear huts and

name: Archaeological area of Piano della Comunità
desc: The archaeological area of Piano (or Quarto) di Comunità is an area of Etrusco-Roman Veii where there is evidence for a Republican domus that is modified during the Augustan period. The area is then used as a necropolis in Late Antiquity (fourth and fifth centuries).

name: Campetti - Decumano
desc: At Campetti - Decumano, in the southwestern part of Veii near the "Portonaccio" gate, there is evidence for a sacred complex that includes a therapeutic bath dating to the Roman period. Some residential functions emerged in Late Antiquity.

name: Archaeological area of Villa di Campetti
desc: The site of a Roman villa complex covering ca. 10,000 square meters. The villa was built in the late republican period (second-first centuries B.C.) on the hillside adjacent to the Archaic Portonaccio sanctuary.

name: Roman baths at Trier
desc: The Imperial Baths at Trier (also referred to as "Kaiserthermen") are a large Roman bath complex in Trier, Germany. The site was designated as part of the "Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St. Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier", a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The complex dates to the fourth century

name: Barbarathermen at Trier
desc: Dating to the second century, the so-called "Barbara Baths" (Barbarathermen in German) are the largest Roman bath complex known north of the Alps. The bath complex was reused first as a Medieval castle and then as a seventeenth century Jesuit college. The ruins were designated as part of the "Roman

name: Aula Palatina
desc: The Aula Palatina is a Roman Imperial Basilica of the emperor Constantine (German: Konstantinbasilika) located at Trier, Germany. It was built ca. A.D. 310 as part of a Roman palace complex.

name: Tomb of Lucius Verginius Rufus
desc: The Tomb of Lucius Verginius Rufus was located at ancient Alsium. Lucius Verginius Rufus (d. 97 CE) was a colleague of Nero and guardian of the younger Pliny, with the latter recording Verginius Rufus' epitaph.

name: Santi Nereo e Achilleo
desc: The basilica of the two Roman martyr saints Nereus and Achilleus has its origins in the fourth century as the Titulus Fasciolae. This church was listed as titulus Sanctorum Nerei et Achillei in 595. The titulus was rebuilt under Leo III in 814 but was abandoned by 1320. For the Jubilee of 1475, Pope

name: Sanctuary of Hercules Victor
desc: The Sanctuary of Hercules Victor in Tivoli is a significant cult place of the second century B.C. The sanctuary is composed of a vaulted, terraced platform that support the temple, its porticoes, and a theater.

name: Porta Maggiore, Norba
desc: The main gate, defended by a bastion, of the Middle Republican fortifications of the city. The gate still stands to a height of ca. 13 m.

name: Castello Savelli Torlonia
desc: A castle at Palombara Sabina that originates in the eleventh century.

name: Monte d'Accoddi
desc: A ramped, megalithic structure in Sardinia dated to around 2700-2000 BC.

name: Tomb of the Tassinara
desc: A painted Etruscan tomb at Chiusi that dates ca. 170-150 BCE. The tomb has acquired a constellation of modern appellations, including "tomba della Tassinaie", "tomba della Tassinara," and "tomba della Tassinaia".

name: Altheim-Weirading villa rustica
desc: A Roman "villa rustica" occupied from ca. 80 - 240 CE, located in the Innviertel region, northeast of the Austrian town of Altheim, village of Weirading (Kiriberg district). This is one of three such sites in the general vicinity of Altheim.

name: Altheim-Wagham villa rustica
desc: A Roman "Villa rustica" site dating to the second century.

name: Ponte Lucano Roman Bridge
desc: A Roman bridge over the modern Aniene river adjacent to the Tomb of the Plautii, which is located north of the Villa of Hadrian at Tivoli.

name: villa of Q. Volconius Pollio
desc: A villa associated with Q. Volconius Pollio was excavated near Marino in 1884.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge crossing the Rio Mannu stream in Sardinia.

name: Tomb of Numerius Agrestinus Equitius Pulcher
desc: A schola tomb at Pompeii located near the Porta Nocera necropolis. The inscription on the tomb's hemicycle honors Numerius Agrestinus Equitius Pulcher, a Roman who had an illustrious military career, including holding the role of praefectus of the Autrigones, an Iberian tribe.

name: Porta Marina
desc: A city gate at the western terminus of the Strada della Marina.

name: Temple of Venus
desc: The Temple of Venus (VIII,1) is located adjacent to Pompeii's Porta Marina. The site was cleared in the early years of the colony to make way for the temple. Seriously damaged by the AD 62 earthquake, the sanctuary was still being rebuilt at the time of its ultimate destruction.

name: Sa Carcaredda
desc: A nuragic complex consisting of a 'megaron-type' temple and a giant's grave.

name: Rocca Guidonesca di Rocchettine
desc: A ruined twelfth-century castle located in the Italian comune of Torri in Sabina

name: Greek Temple at Taras
desc: A Doric temple dating to the sixth century B.C., located in the modern piazza Castello in Taranto, Italy. It was initially attributed to Poseidon, but may have been dedicated to a different deity.

name: Farfa Abbey
desc: A Benedictine abbey located ca. 60 km from Rome.

name: Tappino (river)
desc: The Tappino river is located in the modern Molise region of Italy.

name: Val d'Orcia
desc: A cultural landscape in the agricultural hinterland of Siena, Italy, the Val d'Orcia was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004.

name: Malvaccaro Roman villa
desc: An imperial Roman villa located near Potenza.

name: Santa Maria in Domnica
desc: The Minor Basilica of St. Mary in Domnica alla Navicella, also known as Santa Maria in Domnica, is a Roman Catholic church in Rome, Italy. The basilica has ancient origins, with likely foundations in the fifth century A.D.

name: Contrada Diana
desc: A prehistoric settlement and Greco-Roman era necropolis underlying the modern city of Lipari, with burials dating from the bronze age through the Roman period.

name: Monte Luna Necropoleis
desc: Two adjacent funerary landscapes located south of modern Senorbì on the island of Sardinia, with burials ranging from the 6th century BCE to the 6th century CE.

name: Temple of Victory
desc: A Greek temple of the Doric order (peripteral hexastyle), built in the fifth century BC, possibly to celebrate a victory against the Carthaginians. Its ruins are still visible in the archaeological site of Himera.

name: Ponte Ettori
desc: A Roman bridge crossing the river Temo; the bridge is said to have originally had a five-arch span.

name: Col di Marzo, Perugia
desc: Survey and excavation at Montelabate overlooking the upper Tiber valley in the territory of Perugia have revealed evidence for an Etruscan settlement on the hill of Col di Marzo (Perugia). This place is located some 10 km from Arna and rises to 645 meters above sea level.

name: Domus dei Coiedii
desc: The so-called Domus dei Coiedii is a domus located at Suasa. It dates to the first century B.C.

name: Arch of Malborghetto
desc: A fourth-century A.D. tetrapylon arch stands at the intersection of the Via Flaminia and a road linking the Via Tiberina and Veii.

name: Forum Holitorium
desc: The Forum Holitorium was the vegetable market of ancient Rome, situated outside the Porta Carmentalis in the southern Campus Martius. This area was bounded by the Forum Boarium and the Circus Flaminius.

name: Poggio all'Aglione
desc: A cistern likely connected with a Roman villa.

name: Tomb of Hilarus Fuscus
desc: The Late Republican tomb of the freedman Hilarus Fuscus along the Via Appia (ca. 30 B.C.).

name: tribus Ramnes
desc: The name of a Roman tribe dating from the earliest period of Roman history.

name: House of the Vettii
desc: The so-called House of the Vettii (VI, 15, 1) is a luxurious townhouse (domus) located in Pompeii. The house's owners in its final phase were the freedmen brothers Aulus Vettius Conviva, an Augustalis, and Aulus Vettius Restitutus. Among other features. the house is important for its Fourth Style wa

name: The Temple of Janus (Rome)
desc: The now destroyed Temple of Janus near the Forum Romanum, Rome, was originally built in the reign of Numa, according to Livy.

name: Castello di Filissano
desc: A fortification located in the valley of the Treja River, in use from the tenth century until its abandonment in 1431.

name: Via Francigena
desc: The Via Francigena is a Medieval pilgrimage route connecting Canterbury (England) and Rome.

name: Villa del Vergigno, Montelupo Fiorentino
desc: A large villa rustica inhabited from ca. 100 B.C. to A.D. 500, located near Montelupo Fiorentino in the mid-Arno Valley of northern Tuscany, approximately twenty km west of Florence.

name: Marina di Palo Roman villa
desc: An Imperial maritime villa located in Ladispoli, Italy.

name: Poggino necropolis
desc: An Etruscan necropolis in Chianti in use between the seventh and fifth centuries BC.

name: Roman theater at Fréjus
desc: The Roman theater at Fréjus dates to the reign of Tiberius.

name: Porta Salaria
desc: A gate of the Aurelian Walls of Rome (ca. 271-275 CE) by means of which the Via Salaria exited the city, heading northward. The date was damaged during the bombardment of Rome in 1870 and was subsequently replaced (1873). The replacement gate was demolished in 1921. The site of the Porta Salaria is

name: Bacino Termale Euganeo
desc: A key element of a well-known area of thermal spas and springs already in use in Roman antiquity, located in modern Italy's Veneto region.

name: Roman Baths of Como
desc: The Roman Baths of Como were in use from the later first century until the third century CE.

name: Roman baths, Spoleto
desc: Roman baths located at Spoletium.

name: Terme romane (Regium)
desc: The excavations carried out following the earthquake of 1908 revealed a number of baths dating to the early centuries of the Roman Imperial period.

name: Twann
desc: The village of Twann, Switzerland located on Lake Biel. The site has been occupied since the Neolithic period.

name: Temple de Saint-Gervais
desc: Church in Geneva, Switzerland that has existed in some form since the 4th century CE. The 4th century building was followed by a 10th century Romanesque church which was destroyed by fire in the 14th century. The current church was constructed in the 15th century.

name: Tomb of Derecia Methe
desc: The Tomb of Derecia Methe is a house-type tomb located at the Porta Nocera.

name: Tomb of Annedia and Lucius Caesius
desc: The Tomb of Annedia and Lucius Caesius is an aedicula tomb in the Porta Nocera necropolis.

name: Castello Piccolomini
desc: A castle of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries located in Celano, the Province of L'Aquila (Abruzzo), Italy.

name: Porta Capuana
desc: A Roman gate of Aquinum located on the Via Latina.

name: Mausoleum of C. Ennius Marsus
desc: C. Ennius Marsus was duovir at Saepinum.

name: Arch of Lucius Neratius Priscus
desc: An arch dedicated to Lucius Neratius Priscus, suffect consul of A.D. 97 and governor of Germania Inferior.

name: Arch of Trajan
desc: An arch dedicated to Trajan on the Via Flaminia at Carsulae, also known as the Arco di San Damiano.

name: Porta Bovianum
desc: The western gateway of Saepinum.

name: Roman amphitheater at Ancona
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Ancona could accommodate 8,000 to 10,000 spectators.

name: Berretta del Prete
desc: A circular Roman mausoleum with a distinctive cupola located at the ninth mile of the Via Appia.

name: Punic-Roman Sanctuary, Kamart
desc: A Punic-Roman sanctuary, possibly of Hygieia/Salus or Aesculapius/Eshmun was identified to the northwest of Carthage in the direction of Cape Kamart (Tunisia), mostly on the basis of an assemblage of extremely fragmentary polychromatic terracotta statues, numbering at least 30.

name: Mercurius, Aedes
desc: A temple dedicated to Mercury and Maia that was located on the slopes of the Aventine Hill overlooking the Circus Maximus.

name: Tomb of Marcus Servilius Quartus
desc: A Roman tomb on the Via Appia dating ca. A.D. 100.

name: Torre Maggiore
desc: A place located at the 21st km of the via Ardeatina, Torre Maggiore is likely built on the site of a domusculta and is connected to key Roman families, including the Savelli, Altieri, Capodiferro, Serlupi, and Maddaleni families. The tower has a square plan and rises to 34 meters.

name: Tomb Garden of Aur(elius) Inachus
desc: An inscription found beside the Via Appia near the tomb of Caecilia Metella in 1851 identifies a cepotaphium, i.e., a tomb in a garden, belonging to one Aur(elius) Inachus.

name: Castel San Pietro Romano, polygonal walls
desc: Polygonal masonry walls at Castel San Pietro Romano are likely remnants of an ancient defensive circuit, possibly dating to the later first millennium BCE.

name: Santuario dei Tre Santi (Alfio, Filadelfio e Cirino)
desc: A church of ca. 1200 AD onwards, containing ancient material from the site of Apollonia in re-use.

name: Castello di Vicalvi
desc: The ruined castle of Vicalvi is an eleventh-century fortification that remained in use until the sixteenth century. The Medieval fortifications re-use elements of ancient, pre-Roman polygonal masonry architecture that is presumed to date to the fifth or fourth centuries BCE.

name: Necropoli di Montarano
desc: A necropolis located to the north of ancient Falerii Veteres containing more than 67 tombs.

name: Mattonara necropolis
desc: The Etruscan necropolis of La Mattonara near Civitavecchia, Italy.

name: Santa Maria delle Vigne
desc: A Paleochristian church (fifth century CE) located near ancient Lavinium.

name: Italia, Regio VII
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Etruria. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Italia, Regio IX
desc: One of the administrative regions from Augustus's division of Italy, comprising Liguria. Described by Pliny the Elder in Book III of his Natural History.

name: Roman aqueduct, Spello
desc: An aqueduct carrying water to Spello from the hills below Collepino.

name: Mausoleum of Diocletian
desc: A mausoleum built to entomb Diocletian at his retirement palace that was constructed around 295 CE and is located in modern day Split, Croatia.

name: Ascoli Satriano Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge crossing the Carapelle stream in the territory of Ascoli Satriano.

name: Area di Monte Giulio e Capitaneria
desc: The low hill known as Monte Giulio is anthropic, formed by the accumulation of sediment atop an ancient quay. Archaeological investigation beginning in 1968 revealed numerous architectural remains, including a cistern and a bath complex along the via Guidoni. The ruins of the so-called Capitaneria,

name: Temple of Mars Ultor
desc: The Temple of Mars Ultor was dedicated in the Forum of Augustus in 2 B.C., fulfilling a vow that Octavian had made to the god in 42 B.C.

name: Almo (river)
desc: A small river of the Ager Romanus that once joined the Tiber River just below the walls of Rome. Almo, the eldest son of Tyrrhus, who is one of the heroes in Virgil's Aeneid, shares the river's name.

name: Lapis Niger
desc: A shrine in the Forum Romanum adjacent to the Republican comitium, recognizable by the distinctive black paving stones that covered it in the later republican period. The shrine has been associated, in tradition, with the tomb of Romulus and/or of Faustulus. Giacomo Boni excavated the site between 1

name: Arco di San Lazzaro
desc: The so-called Arch of Saint Lazarus is part of a ruined arcuated structure located in Rome along Via Marmorata. Since this is the general vicinity of the ancient Emporium, these remains may belong to an ancient horreum. Medieval folklore associated the building with Horatius Cocles.

name: Tomb Garden of Claudia Semne
desc: Latin inscriptions unearthed in 1792 between the second and third mile of the Via Appia near S. Sebastiano identify the tomb garden complex of one Claudia Semne.

name: Insula dei Dipinti
desc: A Hadrianic insula in Ostia Antica between the north wall of the castrum and the Tiber, comprising the houses of Jove and Ganymede, of the Infant Bacchus, and of the Paintings, arranged according to an L-shaped plan. Its façade faced onto two streets, forming a corner, while its inner sides looked o

name: Masseria Muro
desc: Masseria Muro (comune di Mesagne, province of Brindisi, south Italy) is the findspot of a hoard of ancient coins. In 1976, a deposit of coins originating from a number of Greek cities of south Italy was discovered. The coins range in date from the Archaic to the Hellenistic periods.

name: Umbilicus urbis Romae
desc: The remains of a monument marking the symbolic navel of the city of Rome that dates to the reign of Septimius Severus.

name: Murus Romuli
desc: "Murus Romuli" refers to a fortification wall alleged to have surrounded the Palatine Hill in Rome, Italy. Legendary tradition claims it was built by the founder-hero Romulus during the eighth century BCE. The historicity of the wall remains hotly debated.

name: Excubitorium
desc: A barracks of the seventh cohort of the Vigiles, Rome's urban fire brigade, was located in the Transtiberim.

name: Castello degli Accarigi
desc: A ruined castle located in the Montagnola Senese, about 10 kilometers from Siena, Italy, that was once part of the defenses of the Republic of Siena.

name: Alpes Graiae (province)
desc: A small Alpine province of the Roman Empire organized around the Little St Bernard Pass, roughly corresponding to the eastern portion of the modern-day French department of Savoie. Augustus annexed the territory in 15 BCE; under Diocletian, the periodically joint administration of the province toget

name: Colonne di San Lorenzo
desc: Sixteen columns in the Corinthian order that once belonged to a Roman temple were relocated to the square adjacent to the Basilica of San Lorenzo in Milan.

name: Temple of Demeter and Kore
desc: A Punic and Roman temple sacred to Demeter and Kore located at Bagoi, Perdaxius, Sardinia.

name: Lucretilis Mons
desc: A mountain in the ager Sabinus.

name: City wall of Ameria
desc: The polygonal masonry circuit wall of ancient Ameria.

name: Nuraghe Biunisi
desc: A single-tower nuraghe with a likely associated village.

name: Ponte Papaloppe
desc: A ruined bridge located near Nuoro in Sardinia.

name: Vižula Maritime Villa
desc: An extensive maritime villa of the Roman period occupied the western and southern coasts of the Vižula peninsula, located near modern Medulin in Croatia.

name: Catacombs of Praetextatus
desc: A vast Roman catacomb along the Via Appia that began to be used at the close of the second century A.D.

name: House of the Painters at Work
desc: The House of the Painters at Work or Casa dei pittori al lavoro is a ruined domus at Pompeii that was undergoing renovations and repairs at the time of the city's final destruction.

name: Roman amphitheater at Augusta Raurica
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Augusta Raurica accommodated ca. 13,000 spectators and was built ca. A.D. 170.

name: Roman amphitheater at Hispellum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Hispellum dates to the first century.

name: Porta Consolare
desc: The Porta Consolare was likely the primary gateway in Hispellum's Roman-era fortification wall.

name: Vigna Pia necropolis
desc: An imperial necropolis with columbarium tombs and a family tomb connected with the gens Atilia Romana.

name: Via Gemina
desc: The Via Gemina was a Roman road linking Aquileia and Emona.

name: Santa Croce in Gerusalemme
desc: A minor Catholic basilica in Rome, Santa Croce in Gerusalemme is also a titular church in rione Esquilino and one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches. The church was consecrated ca. 325 to house relics of the Passion of Jesus Christ brought to Rome from the Holy Land by Empress St. Helena.

name: Via Domitiana
desc: A Roman road of Campania built during the reign of Domitian.

name: House of Amor and Psyche
desc: A domus in Ostia Antica on the Via del Tempio d’Ercole, between the Via della Foce to the south and the Tiber to the north. Installed in late antiquity, and incorporating large parts of a preexisting tenement, this house had a wide central corridor, which opened through an arcade onto a small garden

name: Regio I, Ostia Antica
desc: The first archaeological region of Ostia includes the area of the forum and elements of the original Republican castrum.

name: Regio III, Ostia Antica
desc: The third region of ancient Ostia comprises the western sector of the archaeological area.

name: Regio IV, Ostia Antica
desc: The fourth region of the city of Ostia includes the Porta Marina and its surroundings, as well as extramural baths, tombs, and the Ostia Synagogue.

name: Regio I (Porta Capena)
desc: Regio I (Porta Capena), one of the administrative regions of the city of Rome instituted by Augustus in 7 BCE. name: templum divi Claudii
desc: A temple dedicated to the emperor Claudius who was declared divus (deified) after his death in 54 CE. The platform temple occupied a large area of the Caelian Hill in Rome. The construction project was ultimately completed by the Flavians.

name: antrum Cyclopis
desc: A curious toponym that comes from the Regionary Catalogues for Regio I, the antrum (or atrium) Cyclopis is thought to have been a cave or grotto, perhaps in the flank of the Viminal Hill. It seems to lend its name to the vicus Cyclopis (CIL 6, 2226) that ran south and west to join the via Appia.

name: Cento Camerelle (Bacoli)
desc: The so-called Cento Camerelle at Bacoli is an archaeological site that dates initially to the late republican period. name: Santa Maria Antiqua
desc: A fifth-century A.D. Christian church built in the Forum Romanum at the foot of the Palatine Hill.

name: Castello di Arechi
desc: A sixth-century fortification overlooking Salerno, Italy.

name: Castello di Montevetrano
desc: The castle of Montevetrano is a Medieval fortification atop the Montevetrano hill (258 meters above sea level) in the present-day comune of San Cipriano Picentino, Italy. While the origins of the Medieval fortifications lie in the eleventh century, the hill was fortified as early as the third centur

name: Tomb of the Sempronii (Palazzo San Felice, Rome)
desc: A late-Republican tomb located on the slope of the Quirinal Hill at Rome, now built into Palazzo San Felice (via della Dataria 21).

name: Thammes (mountain)
desc: A mountain, possibly Djebel Tegma.

name: Tractus Umbriae
desc: According to Pliny the Elder, the Tractus Umbriae was the coastal territory near the mouth of the Umbro that was originally settled by the Umbri. It was located between Saena and Telamo.

name: Casacce necropolis
desc: A rock-cut necropolis at Blera with tombs of the Hellenistic period.

name: tribus Tromentina
desc: A later rural tribe of ancient Rome, which was established in 387 B.C.

name: tribus Voturia
desc: The tribus Voturia was an older rural tribe of ancient Rome.

name: La Torricella
desc: A Medieval watch tower (thirteenth to fourteenth centuries) that is part of a system that appears to follow the line of the ancient Via Amerina.

name: Grociana piccola
desc: A Roman fortification on the modern Mt. Grociana piccola, east of Trieste. The structure seems to date to the late second and early first centuries BCE, and may have been part of a military fortification network in the area that developed over time.

name: San Rocco Military Complex (Trieste)
desc: A Roman military fortification at modern Trieste, dating from the third to the first centuries BCE.

name: Monte Savello (Rome)
desc: Monte Savello is an area located in Rome's Sant'Angelo district, between the pons Fabricius and the Capitoline Hill. name: Monte Baranta
desc: A pre-nuragic architectural complex near Olemdo, Sardinia.

name: Necropolis near Randazzo, Sicily
desc: A necropolis with remains dating to the fifth century B.C.

name: Roman city gate, Mainz
desc: A preserved gate of the Roman city wall in the district Mainz-Kästrich.

name: Villa San Marco
desc: The Villa San Marco originates in the Augustan period and was subsequently expanded during the reign of Claudius. Its owner may have been a freedman of Claudius.

name: Villa Arianna
desc: The so-called "Villa Arianna" at Stabiae is typically considered one of the earliest villas at the site and is often dated to the second century B.C.

name: Villa of Publius Fannius Synistor
desc: The Villa of Publius Fannius Synistor was built after the middle of the first century B.C. and was ultimately destroyed by the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius. The villa may have been owned by P. Fannius Synistor and/or L. Herennius Florus.

name: Villa of Numerius Popidius Florus
desc: The Villa of Numerius Popidius Florus dates to the early first century B.C. It was modified several times before its destruction in A.D. 79.

name: Villa Regina, Boscoreale
desc: A villa rustica at Boscoreale discovered in 1977. This is the only villa site currently visible and has been subjected to more modern excavation and analysis.

name: Villa in via Casone Grotta
desc: A Roman villa at Boscoreale discovered in 1986 and only partially excavated.

name: Villa on the Property of D'Acunzo
desc: A villa rustica excavated and reinterred in 1903, located near the Boscoreale train station.

name: Nuraghe Conca Niedda
desc: A nuraghe that is located atop a trachytic rock at a bend in the Rio d'Aridda, a river that has carved a deep valley.

name: Circus of Maxentius
desc: The Circus of Maxentius is part of a complex of buildings built by emperor Maxentius on the Via Appia between A.D. 306 and 312.

name: Capalbio
desc: Capalbio is a municipality in the Province of Grosseto. It is first attested in A.D. 805 when Charlemagne donated the locality to the Abbey of the Tre Fontane.

name: Lago di San Floriano
desc: The lake of San Floriano is located in the Maremma plain near Capalbio.

name: Selvicciola Roman villa
desc: The Selvicciola Roman villa is the site of a vast Roman rural complex as well as a Longobard cemetery.

name: Greek theater of Morgantina
desc: The Greek theater of Morgantina was built during the third century B.C.

name: Greek theater of Taormina
desc: The Greek theater of Taormina was built originally in the third century B.C.

name: Greek theater of Tyndaris
desc: The Greek theater of Tyndaris dates originally to the fourth century B.C.

name: Roman baths of Taormina
desc: The Roman baths of Taormina are built atop a public building of the Hellenistic period. The Roman baths originally fronted on the forum and were expanded in the second century.

name: Selvasecca di Blera
desc: A Republican period villa located near Blera.

name: Lemovii?
desc: The Lemovii were a Germanic tribe whose territory was close to that of the Rugii and the Gutones, all of which lie near the Vistula river delta. Tacitus mentions the tribe in his treatise on Germania.

name: House of the Skeleton
desc: The so-called "The House of the Skeleton" at Herculaneum is a Roman domus that owes its name to the discovery of a human skeleton during excavations. Carlo Bonucci initially explored it between 1830 and 1831. Amedeo Maiuri completed the excavation in 1927.

name: Ad Malum Punicum
desc: Ad Malum Punicum describes a street on the Alta Semita in ancient Rome, likely corresponding to the modern Via delle Quattro Fontane. Vespasian owned a domus in this street and it was here that the future emperor Domitian was born.

name: Graecostasis
desc: The Graecostasis was located at the margin of the comitium in the Forum Romanum. It was a tribunal where foreign ambassadors would wait.

name: Basilica of Saint Augustine in Campo Marzio
desc: The Basilica of Saint Augustine of Hippo in Camp Martius is a titular minor basilica of the Roman Catholic church located in the Campus Martius of Rome. The basilica was conceived in 1286 and the current basilica was completed in 1483.

name: Capalbiaccio Tricosto
desc: The fortified site of Tricosto di Capalbiaccio is located in southern Tuscany, some 6 km inland from the ancient Latin colony of Cosa (Ansedonia). The archaeological site was initially identified by means of a field survey led by Stephen L. Dyson (1976-1980). Beginning in 2009 the site was again inv

name: Fondo Pacifico necropolis
desc: A necropolis of Pompeii. The eastern sector was excavated in 1886-7 and is now reinterred.

name: Tomb of the Lollii
desc: The Tomb of the freedman Marcus Lollius Lucrio and his familia at Pompeii.

name: Tomb of the Blaesii
desc: North Tomb H in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

name: Unnamed tomb
desc: An unnamed tomb, funeral enclosure, or perhaps ustrinum in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

name: Santa Maria Nova
desc: A multi-period site with medieval and modern remains atop Roman levels, including a medieval farmhouse built atop a Roman cistern. Excavations revealed multi-phase evidence, including a bath building decorated with mosaics. The structures may have been related to the nearby Villa dei Quintilli.

name: Mausoleum of Gallienus
desc: A mausoleum on the Via Appia that has been identified conventionally as that of the emperor Gallienus.

name: Tombs of the Festoons and Frontespizio
desc: Two collocated tombs on the Via Appia - a Republican tomb belonging to the time of Sulla known as the 'Tombs of the Festoons' and a second tomb called the 'Tomb of the Title Page' by Luigi Canina who studied and restored it.

name: Constantinian Columbarium
desc: The so-called Constantinian Columbarium is actually a second-century A.D. tomb on the Via Appia.

name: Tomb of Gaius Rabirius Postumus Libertus and family
desc: A tomb of the Republican period belonging to the freedman family of the Rabirii.

name: House of Pansa
desc: The House of Pansa (VI,6,1) is an atrium house in Pompeii that occupies an entire insula. Architectural elements date the structure ca. 140-120 BC in its original phase. The merchant and duumvir Cn. Alleius Nigidius Maius owned the property.

name: Monkodonja
desc: A Bronze Age fort of the Castellieri culture in Istria with megalithic architecture.

name: tribus Quirina
desc: The tribus Quirina was one of the last later rural tribes, established in 241 B.C.

name: House of the Actors
desc: A Roman domus in in Pompeii overlooking the via Stabiana, with shops on both sides of the entrance. The site was excavated in 1872 and bombed in 1943. Located at I,2,6.

name: tribus Scaptia
desc: A later rural tribe of ancient Rome, which was established in 332 B.C.

name: Grotta Paglicci
desc: The Paglicci cave or Grotta Paglicci is located near Rignano Garganico, Apulia, in southern Italy. Discovered in the 1950s, the cave is an important archaeological site documenting life in the Paleolithic period. In addition to artifact finds and zooarchaeological information, the cave provides evid

name: Castello di Monte Sant'Angelo
desc: The castle of Monte Sant'Angelo was built in 837 by the Doge of Venice Orso I. It is located in the comune of Monte Sant'Angelo in Apulia.

name: La Salata necropolis
desc: An early Christian necropolis with tombs dating to the fourth through sixth centuries CE in the Italian comune of Vieste.

name: Ponte di Pietra
desc: A Roman segmental stone arch bridge located near Augusta Praetoria.

name: Dalmatia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 101 K3 Dalmatia

name: Raetia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 101 J2 Raetia
