desc: The Late Roman Province of Sicily as defined by BAtlas 101 J4 Sicilia. Deprecated in favor of place 981549.

name: Poggio la Guardia
desc: The site of a Roman villa.

name: Porta Romana
desc: The so-called Porta Romana of Saturnia was once part of the Roman wall of the second century B.C.

name: Savignano sul Rubicone Roman bridge
desc: A Roman bridge on the Rubicon at Savignano sul Rubicone.

name: Arae incendii Neroniani
desc: A series of altars commemorated the "Great Fire of 64" that occurred during the reign of the emperor Nero. These so-called "Arae incendii Neroniani" are assigned to the reign of Domitian. The original number of altars is unknown and debated. Epigraphy aids greatly in a reconstruction of this distrib

name: Mokarta
desc: A Bronze Age settlement located near Salemi, Sicily. The site has multiple settlement phases, including the Medival ruins referred to as the Castello di Mokarta. A combination of excavation and geophysical prospection has revealed the remains of Bronze Age settlement atop the plateau as well as evid

name: Temple of Isis
desc: The Temple of Isis in Pompeii (VIII, 7, 28) is a sanctuary sacred to Isis that dates from the second century BC.

name: Torre degli Embrici
desc: An imperial Roman villa with a bath complex that emerged in the first and second centuries AD, transitioning to a fortified site after the sixth century AD.

name: Trebiates
desc: An ancient tribe of Umbria that Pliny places in the sixth Augustan region.

name: Nuraghe Antigori
desc: A nuragic complex with artifact evidence showing trade linkages between Sardinian peoples and Mycenaean Greeks, along with Cypriots.

name: Torrione di Micara
desc: A Roman tomb that was adapted for use as a medieval fortification. It is located near modern Frascati, southeast of Rome.

name: Montione
desc: A large villa platform, perhaps measuring 150 meters square, located near Grottaferrata, southeast of Rome. The earliest phase belonged to the first century B.C.

name: Mursia
desc: A modern village on the northwest coast of the Mediterranean island of Pantelleria. Mursia lies atop a settlement of late Bronze Age date that is associated with the cemetery (Sesi) that lies immediately to its south.

name: Bronze Age Cemetery at Mursia
desc: A cemetery (referred to collectively in Italian as "sesi") consisting of multi-burial stone cairns associated with the Bronze Age settlement at Mursia on Mediterranean island of Pantelleria.

name: Duino Mithraeum
desc: A Mithraeum near Duino, in the province of Trieste, north-eastern Italy, that is located within a natural cave.

name: Casa di Bacco
desc: The House of Bacchus at Pompeii takes its name from a wall painting featuring the god Bacchus. Excavations were carried out in 1824 and 1826. The site was bombed during World War II in 1943.

name: Domus of A. Octavius Primus
desc: The so-called House of A. Octavius Primus was excavated in 1859 and again in 1872.

name: House of the Silver Wedding
desc: The so-called House of the Silver Wedding was built in the second century BCE and remodeled in the first century CE. It is noted for its particularly elegant tetrastyle atrium executed in the Corinthian order. Excavated between 1891 and 1893, it earned its modern moniker due to the celebration of th

name: Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere
desc: Sometimes referred to as the "Anfiteatro Campano", the Roman amphitheater at Santa Maria Capua Vetere is the second largest in the Roman world. Begun under Augustus, it was further renovated under Hadrian and Antoninus Pius.

name: Ponte del Diavolo
desc: Site of an ancient Roman bridge across the Raganello near Civita. The ancient bridge was largely rebuilt in 2005.

name: Macellum of Puteoli
desc: A macellum of Roman Puteoli. The discovery of a statue of Serapis at the site led to a misidentification of the building as a Serapeum.

name: Rione Terra
desc: The original urban nucleus of Puteoli, dating from the second century B.C. onwards.

name: Torre dei Conti
desc: A fortified Medieval tower located in Rome, dating to AD 1238, and built by Richard Conti, brother of Pope Innocent III.

name: Torrione di Poli
desc: A Republican-period tower tomb located in the Comune di Poli in Lazio, Italy.

name: Monte Sant’Angelo (Tarracina)
desc: A hill at Tarracina where, in Roman times, the sanctuary complex of Jupiter Anxur was built. In the medieval period, it was occupied by a monastery. Secondary deposits displaced by Roman and medieval construction indicate that Monte Sant’Angelo was the site of significant human activity from prehist

name: Roman theater of Fioccaglia
desc: Crop marks, confirmed by a magnetometer survey reported in 2026, demonstrate the location and footprint of a monumental theater at the archaeological site of Fioccaglia di Fumeri.

name: Castello di Mussomeli
desc: A 14th-century fortification, built on a hill called Monte Raffe, which is located east of the modern Sicilian town of Mussomeli. The hill was previously the site of a long-lived fortified settlement, dating back at least to the early iron age.

name: Theater at Pausilipum
desc: A small Roman theater with a capacity of approximately 2,000 spectators.

name: Roman forum at Cupra Maritima
desc: The Roman forum at Cupra Maritima.

name: Terme di Cavascura
desc: A site of ancient thermal baths.

name: Stoa at Lokroi Epizephyrioi
desc: A large U-shaped stoa dating to the seventh and sixth centuries BCE.

name: Santa Prisca
desc: A titular church on Rome's Aventine Hill dedicated to Saint Prisca. A Mithraeum dating to the late first century A.D. was discovered on the site in 1934.

name: Via Ostiensis
desc: An ancient road running from Rome to Ostia, exiting the city walls of Rome at the Porta Trigemina.

name: Via Nomentana
desc: The ancient road connecting Rome and Nomentum.

name: Civita di Artena
desc: The remains of an ancient fortified center close to the town of Artena, Italy. The original settlement, of uncertain name, may have been established by the Volsci; both Ecetra and Fortinum have been suggested. The modern village was known as Monte Fortino until 1873.

name: Roman amphitheater at Trebula Mutuesca
desc: The archaeological remains of the Roman amphitheater at Trebula Mutuesca are located at Monteleone Sabino in the Province of Rieti, Italy.

name: Polygonal wall of Roman castrum
desc: The polygonal masonry wall of the Roman castrum at Pyrgi encloses an area of ca. 5.7 ha.

name: Hypogeum of via Dino Compagni
desc: A Christian catacomb on the ancient Via Latina used during the fourth century.

name: Temple of Olympian Zeus, Syracuse
desc: The Temple of Olympian Zeus is located approximately 3 km southwest of Syracuse on the Cyane river.

name: Tempio di Matzanni
desc: The remains of a Punic temple located in the Matzanni archaeological area.

name: Roman amphitheater of Carthage
desc: A Roman amphitheater built at Carthage.

name: Tophet of Carthage
desc: The Tophet of Carthage, also known as tophet de Salammbô, is a hybrid sanctuary-necropolis of Punic Carthage.

name: Santuario di Santa Maria di Barbana
desc: The Santuario di Barbana is an ancient Marian shrine that dates ca. 582. It is said that Elia, the Patriarch of Aquileia, built a church near the hut of a hermit from Treviso by the name of Barbanus.

name: Tomba di Boschetti
desc: An archaic Etruscan tumulus located near Comeana, Italy.

name: Montefortini
desc: A monumental Etruscan tumulus that covers two chamber tombs that were looted in antiquity but that likely dated to the seventh and sixth centuries B.C.

name: Villa di Teodorico
desc: A palatial Roman villa and bath complex that has been connected with Theodoric the Great, with twentieth century interpretations labeling it as Theodoric's "hunting lodge". More recent excavations have uncovered evidence for earlier building phases, dating from the first century B.C. through the thi

name: Fosso Saina
desc: A minor tributary of the Anio river in the vicinity of Guidonia.

name: Cellarulo
desc: An area in the Contrada Cellarulo of Benevento that is designated as an archaeological area with evidence for the later phases of ancient Benevento's history.

name: Villa di Fralana
desc: The remains of the so-called villa of Fralana belong to the villa rustica type. Mosaic floors have been discovered at the site, in addition to a productive area that may have included a Torcularium.

name: Nuraghe Cobulas
desc: A pentalobate nuraghe.

name: Sacred well of Predio Canopoli
desc: The sacred well of Predio Canopoli is a monument of the nuragic culture located in Perfugas, Sassari province, in front of the present parish church of Santa Maria degli Angeli. The well is built of isodomic blocks of limestone

name: Withdrawn duplicate: Marcellinus and Peter
desc: This place resource was withdrawn and moved to "errata" because it is a duplicate of https://pleiades.stoa.org/places/281289039

name: Arènes de Fréjus
desc: A 12,000 seat Roman amphitheater located in Fréjus, France.

name: Oppidum du Castellas de St Martin
desc: An oppidum located in the vicinity of the modern commune in the Alpes-Maritimes department of southeastern France.

name: Is Calas menhir
desc: A menhir located near the Is Calas nuragic complex near Monte Nai, Sardinia.

name: Terme di Tito
desc: The so-called "Terme di Tito" is a terraced Roman villa site located in the modern comune of Castel Sant'Angelo near Lago Paterno.

name: Necropolis of Selva Miccia
desc: The Necropolis of Selva Miccia, located along the road leading to Vulci, contains tombs of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C., corresponding in phase to the elite structure excavated at località Le Sparne.

name: Doric temple at Kaulonia
desc: The Doric Temple at Caulonia has been dated ca. 420 B.C.

name: Casa Matta at Kaulonia
desc: The so-called "Casa Matta" at Kaulonia is an elite domestic building of the Hellenistic period that includes mosaics in the remains of its bathing rooms.

name: Tomba de Tre Camini
desc: An ancient tomb located along the via di Terrano on the outskirts of Falerii Novi.

name: Rostra
desc: A large platform erected in the Forum Romanum for senators to deliver orations to a crowd.

name: Via Valeria
desc: An ancient road from Rome to Corfinium.

name: House of the outdoor triclinium
desc: A Roman domus in Pompeii facing on to the Via Nocera.

name: tribus Horatia
desc: The tribus Horatia was a rural tribe of ancient Rome.

name: tribus Oufentina
desc: The tribus Oufentina was a later rural tribe of Rome, established in 318 B.C.

name: House of the Tragic Poet
desc: The so-called "House of the Tragic Poet" (VI, 8, 3, 5) was built in the first century BC and has the plan of a classic "Samnite" house. The house was excavated in 1824. It lies at the corner of the Via delle Terme and the Via della Fullonica, across from the Forum Baths.

name: Forum of Pompeii
desc: Main forum of the Roman city of Pompeii (VII, 8).

name: Porta Mugonia
desc: The Porta Mugonia was one of the three gates of the original Palatine city of Rome (often referred to as "Roma quadrata"). Its precise location can no longer be established and it remains a hotly debated issue for topographers.

name: Aurelian Walls
desc: The Aurelian Walls of Rome began as a fortification system built by Aurelian and Probus between 271 and 275. They enclose an area of approximately 1,400 hectares.

name: Portonaccio sanctuary at Veii
desc: The extraurban sanctuary of Minerva at Portonaccio is an important Etruscan cult center. The temple dates ca. 510 B.C. and was adorned with acroterial sculptures, notably the famous "Apollo of Veii".

name: San Saba, Rome
desc: The Basilica of San Saba is located on the "Piccolo Aventino" in Rome. The basilica's origin is traced to 645 when fugitive monks from Mar Saba in Palestine traveled to Rome to attend the Lateran Council. They subsequently remained on the Aventine.

name: Pietrarossa di Trevi
desc: Excavations at the archaeological site of Pietrarossa (Trebiae) revealed materials pertaining to a Roman domus in the territory of the ancient municipium. The site shows a long occupational history.

name: Santa Costanza
desc: A fourth century AD structure along the Via Nomentana that was built by Constantine I as a mausoleum, originally housing the remains of his daughters Constantina and Helena. It was dedicated as a Christian church in the Middle Ages.

name: Arch of Caligula (Pompeii)
desc: The so-called Arch of Caligula has been referred to by various names and is unlikely to be connected with the emperor Caius. It is located near the intersection of the Via di Mercurio with Via delle Terme and Via della Fortuna.

name: Macellum (Pompeii)
desc: The Macellum of Pompeii is located just outside the northeast corner of the Forum of the city.

name: San Marcello al Corso
desc: The church of San Marcello al Corso is located adjacent to the Via del Corso (the ancient Via Lata) in Rome. Originally known as the Titulus Marcelli, it was established by Pope Marcellus I before 418 CE. The current edifice was completed in the seventeenth century following a destruction by fire of

name: Peschiera
desc: The so-called Peschiera is an architectural complex on the grounds of Hadrian's Villa at Tivoli.

name: Greek theater of Segesta
desc: Remains of a Greek theater at Segesta that was first built in the first half of the third century B.C.

name: Rocca San Silvestro, Campiglia Marittima
desc: The Rocca San Silvestro is a tenth century fortified village on Monte Rombolo near Campiglia Marittima in the Alta Maremma. The village was built in order to exploit rich mineral resources in the area.

name: Ara Pacis Augustae
desc: The "Altar of Augustan Peace" was located in the Campus Martius of Rome. It was originally situated to the west of the Via Lata, near the eastern end of Augustus' Horologium. The reconstructed fragments of the altar are now housed in a museum located on the Tiber's banks in the Piazza Augusto Impera

name: Necropoli di San Placido
desc: A large Roman necropolis in Messina, uncovered in 1914 during the works to build the modern Palazzo della Prefettura.

name: Circus Maximus
desc: An ancient chariot-racing venue at Rome and a major location for public entertainments (ludi), the Circus Maximus is located between the Aventine and Palatine hills.

name: Porta Saracena
desc: A gateway in the polygonal masonry circuit wall of Segni.

name: House of Caecilius Jucundus
desc: The House of Lucius Caecilius Jucundus in Pompeii takes its name from one of its latter-day owners, the banker Lucius Caecilius Iucundus who may have perished in the earthquake of A.D. 62.

name: Villa romana della Standa a Fiano Romano
desc: A Roman villa located along the Via Tiberina in present-day Fiano Romano, the footprint of which is preserved within a commercial complex.

name: Roman bridge (via Salvator Rosa)
desc: A Roman bridge at Naples that was rediscovered and conserved ca. 2000. Its original phase may place it along the ancient road connecting Neapolis and Puteoli.

name: Palazzo degli Spiriti
desc: A seaside architectural complex of the Roman period in the Marechiaro locality of the greater metropolitan area of Naples, Italy.

name: Funerary monuments in piazza del Corso (Nocera Inferiore)
desc: A series of Roman tombs along the road leading from Nuceria to Stabiae.

name: Paleochristian baptistry of Santa Maria Maggiore
desc: The Paleochristian baptistry of Santa Maria Maggiore dates to the sixth century and was built on the site of an early imperial building; its construction made significant use of architectural spolia.

name: Shop of Acastus
desc: The so-called "Shop of Acastus" was a taberna in Pompeii that stood to at least two stories. It is located in the same block as the public bath complex at VII, 5, 24.

name: Ponte Tufaro
desc: A bridge of Roman origins located near Montesarchio.

name: Nuraghe Chentu Istradas
desc: A central nuraghe and associated settlement.

name: Nuraghe Trochesia
desc: Nuraghe Trochesia is a monopteral nuraghe located at Aidomaggiore, Sardinia, Italy.

name: Honorific arch
desc: An honorific arch built in Pompeii near the Temple of Jupiter.

name: House of Iphigeneia
desc: The House of Pinarius Cerialis and Cassia or Casa dell’orefice or Casa di Ifigenia (III, 4, b).

name: House of Obellius Firmus

desc: A Medieval fortification of the Colonna family located in the Italian municipality of Castel San Pietro Romano, the Rocca dei Colonna was in use from the thirteenth century until ca. 1800.

name: Devia (San Nicandro Garganico)
desc: A casale first attested in 1032, Devia is located on Monte Devio (also referred to as Monte d'Elio). This mountain is situated between the coastal lakes of Lesina and Varano, in the northern Gargano.

name: Santa Maria di Devia
desc: The church of Santa Maria di Devia is a Romanesque church of the eleventh century with Byzantine frescoes dating to the twelfth through fourteenth centuries.

name: Sant'Annea
desc: At Sant'Annèa are the remains of an extensive Roman villa located near the port of Gargano, about 3 km south of Lake Lesina. The villa probably originates in the late republican period and flourishes in the third and fourth centuries CE.

name: Church and early Christian necropolis at Vaste
desc: An early Christian complex that included a cult building with several construction phases and a vast cemetery.

name: Quarries at Aquae Albulae
desc: Travertine quarries in the vicinity of Tibur and Aquae Albulae.

name: Sacriportus
desc: Sacriportus is an ancient site of Latium located between Signia and Praeneste, although its precise location is no longer known. It was the site of a decisive battle between Caius Marius and Lucius Cornelius Sulla.

name: Clivus Capitolinus
desc: The principal road leading to the Capitolium and the Arx in the city of Rome.

name: Roman theater of Suasa
desc: The Roman theater of Suasa was discovered in 2003 during excavations near the amphitheater. The semicircular structure measures ca. 55 meters in diameter and dates to the first century A.D.

name: Thermopolium
desc: A dining establishment that served drinks and hot food in antiquity. There are several well-preserved wall paintings in the interior.

name: Porta Nocera necropolis
desc: The Porta Nocera necropolis at Pompeii.

name: Republican-period temple, Fabrateria Nova
desc: A Late Republican temple at Fabrateria Nova.

name: Torre Dell'Angelo
desc: A Roman columbarium tomb located on the Via Latina.

name: Church of the Annunziatella
desc: The church of the Annunziatella is a Catholic church located in Rome's Ardeatino district. It is situated between the via Ardeatina and via di Grotta Perfetta. The church was established in the thirteenth century, as an inscription of Pope Honorius III attests.

name: Villa Cuomo
desc: The so-called Villa Cuomo in the modern Italian comune of Sant'Antonio Abate in greater metropolitan Naples is a Roman villa rustica of the first century CE.

name: Schola Praeconum
desc: The so-called Schola Praeconum is located at the foot of the Palatine Hill near the church of S. Anastasia. A black-and-white floor mosaic discovered during excavations depicts public heralds known as praecones, thus the name of the site.

name: Osteria di Centocelle
desc: An nymphaeum located at Osteria di Centocelle dating to the Roman Imperial period.

name: Horti Lucull(i)ani
desc: An elite villa and garden on the Pincian Hill in Rome laid out originally by Lucius Licinius Lucullus ca. 60 BC. The present day Villa Borghese gardens still cover a portion of the Gardens of Lucullus.

name: Arco Felice Vecchio
desc: The so-called "Arco Felice Vecchio" is a city gate of the first century A.D. built under the administration of Domitian.

name: Via Celle necropolis
desc: A Roman necropolis with 14 tombs constructed during the first and early second centuries A.D.

name: Grotta di Cocceio
desc: A 1-km long ancient tunnel connecting Lake Avernus with Cumae. It dates ca. 38-36 B.C.

name: Tisia
desc: An ancient place in Bruttium mentioned by Appian. Its precise location is unknown today.

name: Park of the Roman Villas at Carthage
desc: An excavated section of Roman Carthage containing blocks (insulae) of townhouses organized on a grid.

name: Villaggio di Tramontana
desc: The “Faraglioni Village” is a Middle Bronze Age settlement located on the northern coast of the volcanic island of Ustica (Palermo, Sicily, Italy).

name: Columbarium of Pomponius Hylas
desc: A Roman columbarium on the Via Appia close to the Porta Latina. The columbarium was excavated in 1831 by Pietro Campana.

name: Güglingen Mithraeum
desc: A sanctuary dedicated to Mithras located near modern Heilbronn, Germany, in use during the second-third centuries CE.

name: Dugali Alti
desc: Dugali Alti or Dugali Alti di Ostiano is an archaeological site located near Ostiano in Cremona, Italy, that has provided evidence of agricultural practices in the Neolithic period of northern Italy.

name: Santa Marina (Villa)
desc: A large seaside villa on two terraces overlooking the modern Santa Marina bay near Varbiga, Croatia. The villa lies on the northern coast of a headland; the major amphora workshop at Loron occupies the southern coastal site.

name: Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres
desc: The so-called Mithraeum of the Seven Spheres is located in ancient Ostia near to the theater-cum-quadriporticus complex. The so-called Quattro tempietti screen it from the Decumanus Maximus.

name: Sanctuary of the Bona Dea
desc: The Sanctuary of the Bona Dea at Ostia dates to the republican period (second century BCE?) and was renovated in the second century CE.

name: Quattro tempietti
desc: The sanctuary along the Decumanus Maximus of Ostia known as the "Quattro tempietti" dates from the Republican period. desc: The remains of a Roman bridge at Tramatza cross the Riu di Mare Foghe. name: Civic forum of Praeneste
desc: The so-called civil forum of ancient Praeneste served as the center of the ancient city and was used across multiple periods. name: Rocca Abbaziale
desc: The Rocca Abbaziale at Subiaco was built by Giovanni V in the eleventh century.

name: Ödes Schloss bridgehead fort
desc: A Roman bridgehead fort, located near Carnuntum (modern Bad Deutsch-Altenburg in Austria).

name: Basilica di San Marco
desc: The ruins of a Christian basilica located near the Via Ardeatina on the grounds of the Calixtian complex have been connected with the Basilica of Saint Mark. The site was discovered accidentally in 1991 and is associated with the Catacomb of Balbina.

name: Cugno Case Vecchie
desc: The area of Cugno Case Vecchie is located about 3 km north-west of Canicattini Bagni, in the province of Siracusa, Sicily. There is archaeological evidence for human activity, including rock-cut burials, from the prehistoric to early modern periods.

name: Temple of Hercules
desc: Remains of the fourth-century BCE Temple of Hercules are preserved in the edifice of San Marco d'Alunzio.

name: Roman villa of Capo di Massa
desc: A villa at the Capo di Massa that has frequently been associated with Pollius Felix, a magistrate from Puteoli.

name: tribus Pomptina
desc: The tribus Pomptina (or Pontina) was a later rural tribe of Rome, which was established in 358 B.C.

name: Hospitium of Hermes
desc: A Roman hospitium located near the Porta Stabia in Pompeii (I, 1, 8).

name: tribus Romilia
desc: An older rural tribe of ancient Rome that was located at the edge of Etruscan territory, across the river Tiber.

name: Stabian Gate
desc: A Roman city gate at the southern terminus of Strada Stabiana in Pompeii.

name: tribus Sabatina
desc: The tribus Sabatina (or Sabatia) was a later rural tribe of ancient Rome, which was established in 387 B.C.

name: Grotta dei Cervi
desc: A karstic cave located near Porto Badisco in southern Apulia, Italy, the so-called Grotta dei Cervi was first discovered in 1970. name: Serra Lustrante
desc: Writing in PECS, D. Adamesteanu notes that Serra Lustrante was found to be the site of a Hellenistic sanctuary.

name: Regio II, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio II, an archaeological subdivision located in the eastern section of Pompeii, includes the Amphitheater and the Large Palaestra, as well as a number of residences and commercial structures.

name: House of Messius Ampliatus

name: Sardinia et Corsica (Roman province)
desc: The province of Sardinia et Corsica was the second Roman province and came under Roman control after the First Punic War.

name: Sicilia (Roman province)
desc: The Roman province of Sicilia (Sicily) was initially organized in 241 BC as a territory with a proconsular governor. The territory fell to the Vandals in AD 440 but was reclaimed by the Byzantines.

name: Alpes Graiae et Poeninae (Roman province)
desc: Alpes Graiae et Poeninae, a small Alpine province of the Roman Empire. There were three such provinces in the western Alps. Alpes Graiae et Poeninae comprised the Val d'Aosta region and the Canton Valais in Switzerland.

name: Alpes Cottiae

name: Tyrrhenum/Inferum Mare
desc: The Tyrrhenian Sea is part of the Mediterranean Sea off the western coast of Italy. It takes its name from the Tyrrhenian people, another name for the Etruscans.

name: Ustica (island)
desc: An island in the Tyrrhenian Sea occupied since the middle of the second millennium B.C. when Phoenician traders were present there.

name: Camars
desc: An Etruscan settlement covering some 17 ha located near the modern village of Gonfienti (Prato).

name: Stadium of Antoninus Pius (Puteoli)
desc: A stadium of ancient Puteoli constructed under Antoninus Pius in the second century A.D. that was revealed by excavation in 2008.

name: Aqueduct of the Arcioni, Rocca di Papa
desc: The remaining segment of a Roman aqueduct in the valley of the Arcioni stream, comune of Rocca di Papa (Italy).

name: Villa Rufinella
desc: Also known as the Villa Tuscolana, this structure was built in the 16th century on the site of a terraced Roman villa. The site occupies one of the most commanding positions on the slope above what is now Frascati, placing it in the environs of ancient Tusculum.

name: Römische Villa
desc: A 'villa rustica' located to the west of Höflein, Austria, on the Danube frontier.

name: Monumenti Funerari Romani
desc: An archaeological area at Avella includes a sector of the ancient monumental necropolis that was in use between the late Hellenistic period and the early imperial period. It lies along an extra-urban road axis. Remains of four Roman mausolea are presently visible.

name: Tomba di Tulliola
desc: The so-called tomb of Tulliola is a Roman mausoleum located at Formiae. Situated about 100 meters from the so-called tomb of Cicero, this tomb is held to be that of Cicero's father.

name: Torre di Pietra Pertusa
desc: A Medieval tower along the Via Flaminia near Prima Porta.

name: Porta Rosa
desc: An arched gateway built using the Lesbian polygonal masonry technique at Velia.

name: Via Postumia
desc: A Roman road (via publica) of northern Italy begun in 148 B.C. by Spurius Postumius Albinus Magnus.

name: Murgia Timone
desc: The site of a Neolithic village located in the territory of Matera in southern Italy. The site was initially discovered in the 1890s by Domenico Ridola.

name: Rocca Sillana
desc: A Medieval fortress in the modern territory of Pisa, Italy.

name: Pieve di San Giovanni Battista a Sillano
desc: A ruined church that was once part of the diocese of Volterra, San Giovanni Battista a Sillano is unique in Tuscany for having a Romanesque-Norman façade. The ruined edifice likely dates to the twelfth and thirteenth centuries although the parish exists as early as the mid-tenth century.

name: Montesei di Serso
desc: A hilltop settlement with a long-term habitation, stretching from ca. 2000 BC to the first century BC. The archaeological site preserves the remains of 4+ mid-first millennium BC dwellings.

name: Roman temple, Capo Mulini
desc: The remains of an early Imperial Roman temple on Sicily's Cape Mulini.

name: Colossus Neronis
desc: The "Colossus Neronis" or "Colossal Statue of Nero" was a monumental bronze statue of the first-century CE emperor reportedly created by Zenodorus. The statue was originally an element of the sprawling Domus Aurea of Nero but the monument endured long after Nero's reign. The statue's original positi

name: Sororium Tigillum
desc: Sororium Tigillum describes a wooden beam that stretched across a branch of the Sacra Via that climbed the Oppian Hill near the Compitum Acilii. The monument was flanked by altars of Iuno Sororia and Iuno Curiatius. It is an ancient monument about which there are many stories, the primary one being

name: Nuraghe Lugherras
desc: A nuragic site of the Middle Bronze Age near Oristano, Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Ruju
desc: A hilltop nuragic complex with a central tholos tower dating to the Middle and Final Bronze Age (1600-1000 BC).

name: Tomb of Marcus Venerius Secundio at the Porta Sarno (Pompeii)
desc: A tomb dating to the first century CE, excavated in 2021 in the necropolis of Porta Sarno at Pompeii.

name: Anfiteatro Fausto
desc: The "Anfiteatro Fausto" or "Amphitheater of Faustus" refers to a Roman amphitheater that was built during the reign of Tiberius (likely 30 or 32 CE) at Terni.

name: Nuraghe di Sant'Itroxia
desc: A Middle Bronze age nuragic site with evidence of a giant's tomb and a nuragic tower.

name: Funtana Coberta
desc: A sacred well of the Nuragic civilization dated between 1200 and 850 BC. The well is located between the modern Sardinian settlements of Escalaplano and Ballao near the junction of highways S6, S13, and S23.

name: Regia
desc: The Regia is an ancient complex along the Sacra Via in Rome at the margin of the Forum Romanum, adjacent to the Temple of Vesta. It is understood as a sort of ritual headquarters of Rome's early kings and, later, as a structure connected with the office of the pontifex maximus.

name: Augusteum, so-called Basilica at Herculaneum
desc: The Augusteum, or so-called "Basilica", at Herculaneum, was partially investigated in the eighteenth century. This large complex (68 by 40 meters) had colonnades on three of its sides and faced onto the Decumanus Maximus across from the Basilica Noniana and the College of the Augustales.

name: Via Cassia
desc: An ancient Roman road branching off from the Via Flaminia and continuing to Luna, where it joined the Via Aurelia. The Via Cassia post-dates the Via Amerina and was built after 240 B.C. It combined new construction with re-use of pre-existing roads and tracks.

name: Via Clodia
desc: An ancient Roman road.

name: Arch of Gallienus
desc: The Arch of Gallienus marked the Porta Esquilina, a gate in the Servian Wall of Rome. The via Labicana and via Tiburtina issue from Rome at this point. The arch was erected in A.D. 262.

name: Thermae Antoninianae
desc: The Thermae Antoninianae, commonly known as the Baths of Caracalla, were built in Rome between AD 212 and 216.

name: Withdrawn: Untitled
desc: This place resource has been withdrawn because it was created and published due to a technical error.

name: Capitolium
desc: The so-called Capitolium of Aquinum is found in the northwest part of the site. It may predate Roman colonization, and it is perhaps sacred to Iuno Regina.

name: Forum of Saepinum
desc: The Forum of Saepinum assumes a trapezoidal shape and is aligned with the decumanus.

name: Roman amphitheater at Suasa
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Suasa dates to the first century A.D.

name: Insula Erkronis (island)
desc: The island marked "Insula Erkronis" on the Peutinger map may be the island in the Adriatic Sea now known as Silba (Croatia).

name: Rödgen
desc: A Roman fortification founded during the principate of Augustus that was located some 50 km from the legionary fortress at Mainz-Mogontiacum.

name: Frattocchie diverticulum
desc: An ancient side road (diverticulum) connecting the Via Appia to ancient Bovillae was rediscovered in 2014 construction work in modern Frattocchie. A section of the road was conserved and can be visited beneath the McDonald's restaurant now occupying the site. Other remains of the road have been iden

name: Castel Lagopesole
desc: Castel Lagopesole was situated along the line of the ancient Roman Via Herculea between Melfi and Potenza in southern Italy. During the eighth through tenth centuries, the site played a strategic role in the region. The castle's construction between 1242 and 1250 is linked to Frederick II. The castl

name: Torre Romana, Novaria
desc: A surviving Roman defensive tower.

name: Basilica of Saint-Pierre-aux-Nonnains
desc: A Christian basilica that incorporates the remains of a fourth-century AD Roman gymnasium.

name: Ponte Cardona
desc: An aqueduct bridge near Nequinum dating ca. A.D. 24 - 33.

name: Caudini
desc: A Samnite tribe that was subjugated in 275 BC by L. Cornelius Lentulus.

name: Frattura Vecchia
desc: Frattura Vecchia is a hamlet located in the town of Scanno now in the Abruzzo National Park. This small village is located about 1260 meters above sea level and has ancient origins, perhaps as early as 1106.

name: Nymphaeum of Egeria
desc: A nymphaeum connected with Egeria, the divine advisor of Numa Pompilius. This iteration of Egeria's spring dates to the time of Herodes Atticus in the second century A.D.

name: Via Livenza hypogeum
desc: A painted hypogeum tomb of the fourth century A.D. discovered in 1923 between the via Livenza and the via Po.

name: Unnamed Roman bridge
desc: An unnamed Roman bridge over the Fosso della Mola.

name: Torre Valca
desc: A Medieval tower (12th or 13th century) is now located within the grounds of the Caffarella park.

name: Roman cistern
desc: A Roman cistern of the early second century A.D.

name: Catacombs of Commodilla
desc: A catacomb along the Via Ostiensis that contains, among other wall paintings, the earliest depiction of a bearded Jesus Christ.

name: Necropoli di San Vito
desc: A Greek necropolis located at Puteoli.

name: Anfiteatro minore
desc: The so-called "Anfiteatro minore" is a small amphitheater at Puteoli dating to the early Imperial period.

name: Roman amphitheater at Lucus Feroniae
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Lucus Feroniae was financed by one M. Silius Epaphroditus, who in turn received the title patronus. The structure dates to the reign of Tiberius.

name: Roman amphitheater at Flavia Solva
desc: The Roman amphitheater of Flavia Solva.

name: Roman amphitheater at Vercellae
desc: An extramural Roman amphitheater was to be found at Vercellae.

name: Roman amphitheater at Lucera
desc: An amphitheater dating to the time of Augustus.

name: Roman amphitheater at Ariminum
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Ariminum is dated to the second century, perhaps during the reign of Hadrian.

name: Roman amphitheater at Patavium
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Patavium dates to the Augustan period.

name: Roman amphitheater at Trebula
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Trebula dates to the Augustan period.

name: San Crisogono
desc: San Crisogono (sacred to San Crisogono) is one of Rome's early parish churches (tituli). Pope Sylvester I (314–335) likely builds the first iteration in the fourth century AD; later reworkings occur in the twelfth and seventeenth centuries, respectively.

name: Lacus Orphei
desc: A fountain on the Esquiline (Regio V) that was perhaps located just outside the porta Esquilina.

name: Fufidianum
desc: The name of an estate near Arpinum that once belonged to Q. Tullius Cicero.

name: Quadrato di Torre Spaccata (Rome)
desc: A Late Neolithic to Chalcolithic settlement in the vicinity of the Medieval Torre Spaccata in Rome. The earlier settlement remains were truncated by activity in the Roman period that included road pavement.

name: Grotta del Tasso di Sofignano
desc: The Grotta del Tasso di Sofignano (also referred to as Buca del Tasso) is a cave located near Camaiore in the province of Lucca in Italy. The cave is an archaeological site where the presence of Homo neanderthalensis is attested ca. 40,000 years ago.

name: Casa di Trittolemo
desc: The so-called Casa di Trittolemo at Pompeii was excavated in 1859 and again in 1871.

name: House of Thiasus
desc: A domus at Pompeii located on Via Nola in insula 10 of Regio IX. Partial excavation at the site occurred in 1888; scientific excavations resumed in 2023. Epigraphic evidence suggests that one of the domus' owners was connected to the duovir Aulus Rustius Verus. In February 2025, a mid-first-century

name: Domus di Faustus
desc: The so-called House of Faustus at Pompeii was excavated in 1844 and 1875. It is linked to V.1.24 and VI.1.26.

name: Villa of Agrippa Postumus
desc: The Villa of Agrippa Postumus was discovered at Boscotrecase in 1903 on land owned by Cavaliere Ernesto Santini. Works for the Circumvesuviana railroad line brought the site to light. Excavations supervised by Matteo Della Corte were carried out from 1903 to 1905. In 1906, however, a new eruption of

name: Villa romana del Torchio
desc: A Roman "villa rustica" with an olive-oil press (torcularium, hence "Torchio") was discovered in 2006.

name: Via *Quinctia
desc: A road named Via *Quinctia linked Florentia (Firenze) to Pisae (Pisa) in northern Etruria. Its construction is ascribed to the consul Titus Quinctius Flamininus starting in 123 BCE.

name: Tigurini
desc: A sub-tribe of the Helvetii.

name: Dangstetten
desc: Dangstetten was the site of a Roman military camp.

name: Palatinus Mons
desc: The central hill of Rome, Italy. Legend held that Romulus founded the city of Rome on the Palatine Hill following an augural contest with Remus, his brother.

name: Cloaca Maxima
desc: The Cloaca Maxima drained the valley of the Forum Romanum. The sewer originates as a canalized drain in the late sixth century BCE. It would eventually be vaulted and interred. It drains into the Tiber River.

name: Schwarzenbach
desc: Celtic settlement site in eastern Austria inhabited during the 1st-2nd centuries CE.

name: Terme del Nuotatore
desc: The so-called "Baths of the Swimmer" or "Terme del Nuotatore" (V,X,3) in region 5 of the ancient city of Ostia takes its modern name from a partially preserved black-and-white mosaic pavement. These baths were built in the late first century CE during the reign of Domitian. The complex was rebuilt d

name: Aventinus mons
desc: One of the seven hills of Rome. Until the reign of the emperor Claudius, the hill lay outside the pomerium of the city.

name: Villanovaforru, Nuraghe Genna Maria
desc: A multi-period nuragic site that began as a single tower ca. the Middle Bronze Age (1500 BC).

name: Lu Brandali
desc: A nuragic settlement dating to the latter part of the second millennium BC.

name: Nuraghe Maiori
desc: A single-tower nuraghe with a central corridor.

name: Ludus Magnus
desc: A gladiatorial training school adjacent to the Flavian Amphitheater in Rome. The structure is attested on the Severan marble plan of Rome.

name: Pons Cestius
desc: A Roman stone bridge on the Tiber River, spanning the river channel from the Tiber Island westward to the Transtiberim (Trastevere). The original bridge dates to the first century BC.

name: Horrea Piperataria
desc: A portion of a warehouse complex dating to the Flavian period, the Horrea Piperataria, was likely destroyed in the fire of 192 CE. Its remains were later incorporated into the substructions of the Basilica Nova (a.k.a. Basilica of Maxentius).

name: Tolfa
desc: The modern Italian comune of Tolfa is 24 kilometers northeast of Cerveteri. Its environs contain several ancient sites, dating from prehistory as well as the time of the Roman Empire.

name: Capanna dell’Elceto
desc: The so-called Capanna dell’Elceto was part of a fortified Protovillanovan settlement located near Monte Rovello, Italy.

name: Temple of Hera II (Neptune)
desc: A fifth century B.C. Doric temple, the so-called Temple of Hera II is also sometimes referred to as the Temple of Neptune.

name: Roman theater at Benevento
desc: A Roman theater of the second century A.D. constructed during the reign of Hadrian.

name: Vatican City
desc: Vatican City is an independent state, established following the Lateran Treaty of 11 February 1929. Its sovereign territory measures 44 hectares in area. There is a long and complex settlement history associated with this center of Christendom, beginning from the establishment of the Basilica of Sai

name: Hedemünden
desc: An early Imperial fort located on the river Werra.

name: Tomb of Aulus Hirtius
desc: A tomb located in Rome's Campus Martius. Its remains are now submerged in the channelized waters of the Euripus canal beneath the Palazzo della Cancelleria.

name: Roman villa at Artena
desc: A Roman villa built atop the terraced platform of the so-called "Civita di Artena".

name: Roman amphitheater at Luca
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Luca dates to the second half of the first century.

name: Poggio di Moscona
desc: The Poggio di Moscona is a hill on the northeastern edge of the plain of Grosseto and the basin of the ancient lake Prile.

name: Carmine Roman tomb
desc: A Roman tomb of the later second century incorporated into the former Convento del Carmine in Catania, Sicily.

name: Ekklesiasterion at Akragas
desc: Located in the Upper Agroa, the Ekklesiasterion at Akragas dates to the fourth and third centuries B.C.

name: Porta Roma
desc: One of the four gates of the fortified castrum of Allifae. The fortifications are thought to date to the Late Republican period on the basis of building techniques.

name: Sepolcro del Casale di Gregna
desc: A Roman tomb of the fourth century C.E. built in opus listatum.

name: Tomba della Mula
desc: A tomb near Sesto Fiorentino, that dates to the seventh century B.C.

name: Tomba della Montagnola
desc: A tholos-type tomb dating to the seventh century B.C.

name: Bocca di Magra Roman villa
desc: A villa maritima of the first century B.C.

name: Via Appia
desc: An early Roman road (via publica) originating at Rome and terminating at Brundisium, the Via Appia was begun in the fourth century B.C. by the censor Appius Claudius Caecus. The Latin author Statius described the Via Appia as "queen of the long roads".

name: Oppius Mons
desc: The Oppian Hill is the southern spur of Rome's Esquiline Hill.

name: Ponte Fabio Massimo
desc: The so-called "Ponte Fabio Massimo" or "Ponte del Diavolo" originally dates to the third century BC with subsequent reworking and reuse continuing to the Middle Ages.

name: Ponte di Capua
desc: A Roman bridge crossed the Volturno river at Capua, some elements of which remain in the site of modern bridge.

name: Divorum
desc: A porticus constructed by Domitian in A.D. 80 on the eastern Campus Martius on the site of the Villa Publica, whose northern entry—a triumphal arch—was flanked by two small temples in honor of Titus and Vespasian.

name: Ponte Fratto
desc: The remains of a late Republican bridge near Benevento (in Località Serretelle).

name: Capitolium Vetus
desc: The Capitolium Vetus was located on the Quirinal Hill and was an earlier shrine to the triad of Iuppiter, Juno, and Minerva than the famous Capitoline Temple. It was likely perched on the northern edge of the Quirinal.

name: Via Labicana
desc: An ancient Roman road connecting Rome and Labicum.

name: Regio I, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio I, an archaeological subdivision located in the southeastern section of Pompeii, contains a mixture of residences and commercial structures.

name: Regio IV, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio IV is a largely unexcavated archaeological subdivision located in the northeastern section of Pompeii.

name: Regio V, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio V, a largely unexcavated archaeological subdivision located in the northern section of Pompeii, contains a mixture of commercial and domestic structures, including a gladiators' barracks.

name: Regio VI, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio VI, an archaeological subdivision located in the northwestern section of Pompeii, contains shops and residential buildings, including the House of the Faun.

name: Regio IX, Pompeii
desc: The so-called Regio IX, an archaeological subdivision located in the central section of Pompeii, contains a mix of residential and commercial structures.

name: Corvey
desc: The abbey was first founded in 815 by Charlemagne's cousins, Wala and Adelard.

name: Aphrodision at Akrai
desc: Temple dedicated to Aphrodite constructed in the 6th century BCE at the Greek colony of Akrai.

name: Casa di Pane
desc: A domus in Pompeii excavated in 1818. It is linked to VIII.3.28 and VIII.3.30.

name: Arch of Augustus (Pompeii)
desc: The brick core of an arch monument stands immediately to the west of the Temple of Jupiter in the Forum of Pompeii. It has had various appellations including "Arch of Drusus", referring to Drusus Iulius Caesar the son of emperor Tiberius.

name: Nymphaeum of via degli Annibaldi
desc: An elaborate nymphaeum on the Oppian Hill discovered in 1895. The complex dates to the Late Republican period. The ancient nymphaeum was partially obliterated by the construction of the Neronian Domus Aurea.

name: House of the Centenary
desc: A Pompeian domus re-discovered in 1879, the so-called House of the Centenary is among the largest domus in Pompeii.

name: Pani Loriga
desc: A fortified Phoenico-Punic settlement on Sardinia with two necropoleis.

name: Arch of Trajan at Canosa
desc: The Arch of Trajan at Canosa dates to the second century CE.

name: S. Passera hypogeum
desc: A hypogeum connected with the S. Passera complex.

name: Roman amphitheater at Arretium
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Arretium was built during the late first and early second centuries. It measures 121 by 68 meters.

name: Roman forum of Luna
desc: The forum of Luna, founded as a colony in 177 B.C.

name: Porta Tiburtina
desc: The Porta Tiburtina is a gate in the Aurelianic Walls through which the Via Tiburtina passes. It is also known today as the Porta San Lorenzo.

name: Mehring
desc: Roman villa rustica in Mehring

name: Grotta del Mortale
desc: A Republican period cistern located along the present-day Via Polense in the Comune of Poli in Rome's eastern suburbs.

name: Isola de San Lazzaro degli Armeni
desc: Small island in the Venetian Lagoon. A church and monastery were constructed on the site during the 9th century CE, and it was used as a leper colony in the medieval and early modern periods. Since 1717 CE, it has been home to an Armenian Catholic (Mkhitarist) monastery, from which the island derive

name: Felceto
desc: An amphora production site with kiln was identified in the 1990s at a place called Felceto, approximately 10km south of ancient Tifernum Tiberinum (modern Città di Castello) and 2km east of the Tiber on a tributary (i.e., somewhere to the east of modern Cinquemiglia and Promano). The site has not be

name: Hellenistic Baths (Syracuse)
desc: A Hellenistic bath complex at Syracuse, located near the Greek theater.

name: Catacombe San Marcellino e Pietro
desc: The Catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter lies some 3 km southeast of Rome along the ancient Via Labicana. They date to the fourth century A.D.

name: Tagliata Etrusca
desc: A rock-cut canal located at the port of ancient Cosa.

name: Sarresdorf
desc: Roman villa rustica

name: La Loggia
desc: "La Loggia" refers to a squared tower that is a part of the polygonal masonry curtain wall of Norba.

name: Porta Nomentana
desc: The Porta Nomentana was a single-arch gateway in the Aurelianic Walls of Rome built between 270 and 273 AD by the emperor Aurelian.

name: Porta Pinciana
desc: The Porta Pinciana is a gate passing through Rome's Aurelianic wall and was added during the principate of Honorius in the fifth century.

name: House of Julia Felix
desc: The so-called House of Iulia Felix (II, 4, 3) is situated on the south side of the Via dell'Abbondanza, near the Palaestra and the Amphitheater. The estate was formed from two complete insulae that were merged. About one-third of the area was occupied by the house, the remainder by a large garden. F

name: Monte Bibele
desc: A massif of the middle Bolognese Apennines rising 617 meters above sea level,

name: Monte Tamburino
desc: A peak rising to 594 meters above sea level.

name: Villa of Horace
desc: The archaeological remains of a villa near Licenza, Italy, that are traditionally connected with the Latin poet Horace.

name: Nuraghe Ponte, Dualchi
desc: Nuraghe Ponte, Dualchi is located near the archaeological complex of Frenegarzu. The site consists of a single circular tower (diameter 13.25 m; height 11.80 m) built upon a foundation of large roughly-hewn polyhedral blocks that support the structure built of neatly squared ashlars.

name: Nuraghe Biriola
desc: A Nuraghe with a complex plan located near Dualchi, Sardinia.

name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria di Amiternum
desc: The ruins of the cathedral of the fifth century are located in an area of the archaeological site of Amiternum that was occupied in the second and third centuries CE.

name: Mithraeum at Mundelsheim
desc: A second-century Mithraeum is located in the area of the municipality of Mundelsheim in the Ludwigsburg district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany.

name: Torcello (island)
desc: Torcello is an island located at the northern end of the Venetian Lagoon that was first settled in 452 CE.

name: Mazzorbo (island)
desc: Mazzorbo is an island in the Venetian Lagoon. It is sparsely populated in the present day. In antiquity, it may have received displaced persons from Altinum following its sacking in the fifth century CE.

name: Burano (island)
desc: Burano is an island in the Venetian Lagoon. It may have been settled in Roman times by refugees from Altinum.

name: Roman villa of Torre di Pordenone
desc: A Roman villa and bath complex located in the valley of the Noncello River. The villa complex, whose original construction dates to the first century BCE, was likely rebuilt during the second century CE.

name: Domus of the figurative emblem
desc: The so-called "Domus of the figurative emblem" is a well-appointed domus at Privernum.

name: Pieve a Bozzone
desc: The ruins of an ancient Roman villa were discovered in the Italian comune of Pieve a Bozzone (Siena) in 2023.

name: Aedes Hercules Musarum
desc: Marcus Fulvius Nobilior likely built this temple in Rome's Circus Flaminius ca. 187 B.C. following his campaigns in Ambracia. In 29 B.C., the temple was restored by L. Marcius Philippus and included in the new porticus bearing his name.

name: Temple of Romulus (Rome)
desc: A temple along the Sacra Via dedicated to Valerius Romulus, son of Maxentius.

name: Arch of Titus
desc: A triumphal arch erected in summa Sacra Via and dedicated to the deified emperor Titus by his brother Domitian, ca. 81 CE.

name: Poggio Murella
desc: A large, rectangular cistern (Castellum aquarum) located near Poggio Murella was built in opus reticulatum.

name: S'Arcu 'e is Forros
desc: A significant nuragic complex with major occupational phases during the middle Bronze Age and during the Bronze- to Iron Age transition. A 17 meter long megaron with its temenos is a main feature of the site.

name: Nuraghe Succoronis
desc: A single-tower nuraghe located near Macomer, Sardinia.

name: Nuraghe Sa Ucchiusura
desc: A monopteral nuraghe built of trachite. The ruined walls stand to at least four meters in height.

name: Nuraghe Maronzu
desc: Remains of a nuraghe in the territory of the comune of Olbia.

name: Nuraghe Terra Tenera
desc: A single-tower nuraghe located near Sassari, Sardinia.

name: Abini nuragic sanctuary
desc: A nuragic sanctuary.

name: Tamuli
desc: A Middle Bronze Age nuragic complex near Macomer, Sardinia.

name: Su Tempiesu
desc: A nuragic spring sanctuary in use from the thirteenth to ninth centuries BC.

name: Mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa
desc: The so-called mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa stands along the Via Nomentana.

name: Offemont
desc: A Roman-period pottery production workshop dating to the second century CE, located in the modern French commune of Offemont (Territoire de Belfort).

name: Cavalupo Necropolis (Vulci)
desc: Excavated in the nineteenth century and only recently re-assessed, this cemetery is located east of Vulci itself, across the modern river Fiora from the ancient acropolis. The cemetery was in active use from the Villanovan period through Hellenistic times.

name: Chancy
desc: The fortification located at Chancy dates initially to the reign of Valentinian.

name: Saint-Saphorin
desc: A Roman villa located near the shores of Lake Geneva.

name: Csopak
desc: Roman ruins were discovered on the shores of Lake Balaton.

name: Tempa Cortaglia
desc: An Archaic settlement in Lucania located near moderm Oliveto Lucano.

name: Olten
desc: A vicus and fort on the Aare river.

name: Metubarbis
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 21 A4 Metubarbis

name: Savus (river)
desc: A river of Central Europe and a right tributary of the Danube.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 21 A4 unnamed bridge (Mursa)

name: Ouakontion
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 21 unlocated Ouakontion

name: Nuraghe Baccu Idda
desc: A nuragic site located near Chia, Sardinia, Su Nuraxi de Baccu Idda is located atop a 78 m hill close to the course of the Riu di Chia, a stream that irrigates the plain south-east of the nuragic complex.

name: Castello di Corradino
desc: A mausoleum dating to the Roman Imperial period located at Centuripe in Sicily.

name: Castellu di Cucuruzzu
desc: Castellu di Cucuruzzu is a Torrean archaeological site in Corsica.

name: Santu Misirinu
desc: An octagonal structure covered by a cupola, dating between the second and sixth centuries A.D.

name: Grotta della Dragonara
desc: A rock-cut Roman cistern.

name: Tombs of the Buccii and Melissaei
desc: The Grave enclosure of the Buccii and the Melissaei located on the west side of Pompeii's Herculaneum Gate.

name: Odeon at Hadrian's Villa
desc: The Odeon at Hadrian's Villa is also referred to as the South Theater. It is located at the southern end of the Villa Adriana.

name: Funerary Grove of Q. Cervonius Chryseros
desc: A now-lost inscribed altar of a probable Iulio-Claudian date was found by T. Mommsen among the stones of Aquileia. The inscription described the dedication of a grove.

name: Nuraghe Cubalciada
desc: A Bronze Age nuraghe re-used and re-fortified during the Second World War.

name: Nuraghe Flumenelongu
desc: Nuraghe Flumenelongu (Alghero-Sassari) is an important archaeological site for considerations of prehistoric maritime commerce in the Mediterranean.

name: Covili sa Serra su Sipiri nuraghe
desc: Remains of a single tower nuraghe.

name: Timpone della Motta
desc: The Timpone della Motta is an archaeological site located near Francavilla Marittima. The site was inhabited from the Middle Bronze Age onward. During the Iron Age, an Oenotrian settlement flourished here, one that developed into an important sanctuary. The site passed into Greek control in the late

name: House of the Ship Europa
desc: The so-called "House of the Ship Europa" is a large house in the city of Pompeii (I,15,3) that takes its conventional, archaeological name from a large graffito of ship bearing the legend 'Europa'.

name: Ponte di Nona
desc: A Roman-period bridge along the via Praenestina built of lapis Gabinus.

name: Tor Boacciana
desc: A Medieval tower, perhaps of the twelfth century, connected with the Bobazani family.

name: Molino San Vincenzo
desc: Field surveys, geophysical prospection, as well as targeted research and training excavations, have revealed the remains of a mid- to late- imperial rural settlement with evidence for agricultural activity. However, the earliest finds (e.g., bucchero) date to the sixth/fifth century B.C., indicating

name: Ager Venusinus
desc: The Ager Venusinus is the territory of ancient Venosa, located in the Basilicata region of Italy.

name: Torre d'Ischia, Vejano
desc: The archaeological site of Torre d'Ischia was identified in 1982, with evidence for Proto-Villanovan occupation.

name: Circus Maximus Mithraeum
desc: A mithraeum adjacent to the Circus Maximus and facing the carceres of the same was located at the margin of the Forum Boarium and now situated beneath a building in the via dell'Ara Massima. The site was excavated in 1931.

name: Temple of Quirinus
desc: The Temple of Quirinus was located near the Capitolium Vetus. The temple was built ex manubiis by Lucius Papirius Cursor in 293 B.C., fulfilling the vow made by his father in 325 B.C. Tradition holds that the republican-period temple was sited on an even earlier altar dedicated by the Sabines. The t

name: San Menna
desc: The church of San Menna in Rome was recorded by the anonymous pilgrim author of the Einsiedeln in the eighth century CE.  It was located along the Via Ostiensis, most likely between the Porta San Paolo and the Basilica of Saint Paul. Likely founded in 589, the church is not attested after the tenth

name: Bir Massouda
desc: An archaeological site in Carthage showing signs of continuous habitation from ca. 760 BCE-700 CE.

name: Forum Aemilianum
desc: The Roman forum of Terracina, entered by a quadrifons arch, sits along the line of the Via Appia.

name: House of Lucius Cornelius Diadumenus
desc: The House of Lucius Cornelius Diadumenus (VII, 12, 26) is a small domus noted for its wall paintings.

name: Santa Maria della Libera
desc: An eleventh century church near Aquinum built largely from spolia.

name: Manoppello Roman Villa
desc: A Late Republican villa in Abruzzo that later became a productive estate. The archaeological remains of the villa are located in the locality of Piano S. Maria Arabona in Manoppello, Italy.

name: Santa Sabina
desc: A Christian basilica on the Aventine Hill in Rome was founded in the fourth century A.D. The church takes its name from a Christian martyr who was said to have lived on the Aventine. The church is the oldest extant Roman basilica structure that preserves its original plan in the city of Rome.

name: Frontone
desc: An Umbro-Roman temple of Iuppiter on the slopes of Monte Catria.

name: Alpes Maritimae (late Roman province)
desc: The post-Diocletianic province of Alpes Maritimae according to the Verona List (ca. AD 303-324). It was assigned to the diocese of Viennensis.

name: Villa della Pisanella
desc: A Roman villa rustica at Boscoreale that was first discovered in 1868 by Modestino Pulzella. The villa is best known as the findspot of the so-called "Boscoreale Treasure". Following excavation, the remains of the villa were reinterred.

name: Monte Catria
desc: A mountain of the central Apennine range; the highest peak rises to 1,702 metres (5,584 ft) above sea level.

name: Costia dei Lippi
desc: The archaeological area of Costia dei Lippi is located near the contemporary cemetery of Vetulonia. Excavations in this area began in the 1960s and revealed a series of stone walls built in a squared technique, as well as a system of terraces and a paved road. The area has been interpreted as a dome

name: Ras ben Sakka
desc: The northernmost point of the continent of Africa.

name: Castel del Monte
desc: A 13th-century castle near Andria in the Apulia region of southeastern Italy built during the 1240s by the Emperor Frederick II. The castle was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1996.

name: Tumulo del Principe etrusco
desc: A seventh-century B.C. Etruscan tumulus is located near Pisa.

name: Temple of Concordia, Agrigento
desc: The Temple of Concord, located in the so-called "Valle dei Templi" of Agrigento, dates ca. 440-430 B.C.

name: Radicofani
desc: Radicofani, located ca. 60 km southeast of Siena, is the site of the tenth-century AD castle of the Carolingian Ghino di Tacco.

name: Torre di Donoratico
desc: An Etrusco-Roman fortified hilltop settlement that later served as a fortress of the Della Gherardesca family from the twelfth to the fifteenth centuries.

name: Area Scheibler
desc: An extramural, suburban area of Pisa that has been the focus of both rescue excavation and geophysical prospective. This fieldwork revealed a long arc of occupation activity stretching from the Iron Age to the Middle Ages.

name: Roman amphitheater at Nuceria (Alfaterna)
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Nuceria (Alfaterna) likely dates to the Augustan period.

name: Roman amphitheater at Caralis
desc: The Roman amphitheater at Cagliari dates to the first and second centuries.

name: Sacellum of the Augustales
desc: The so-called "Sacellum of the Augustales" at Misenum is an architectural complex located near the theater that was first built during the Iulio-Claudian period and dedicated to the Imperial cult. The complex was renovated during the second century, at which time one Cassia Victoria re-dedicated the

name: Roman forum at Tergeste
desc: The Roman forum of Tergeste.

name: Lago di Massaciuccoli
desc: The Lago di Massaciuccoli appears on Map 41 of the Barrington Atlas (grid square C2), but it is not named. In the introductory essay for Map 41 in the Map-by-Map Directory, W.V. Harris mentions the lake in the context of a brief discussion about the ancient hydrography of the territory around Pisa.

name: Vico Pancellorum
desc: In the introductory essay for Map 41 of the Barrington Atlas published in the Map-by-Map Directory, Vico Pancellorum is mentioned as a toponym with likely ancient origins, but absent is any specific evidence to that effect. Vico Pancellorum is a small Tuscan village located in the Province of Lucca.

name: Vicopisano
desc: Vicopisano is located in the Province of Pisa, some 50 km west of Florence and 15 km east of Pisa. In the Middle Ages, Vicopisano was a fortified center of the Republic of Pisa that was conquered by Florence in 1406. W.V. Harris asserts in the introductory essay for Map 41 of the Barrington Atlas th

name: Augusta Bagiennorum amphitheater
desc: The Roman amphitheater of Augusta Bagiennorum.

name: Lobaos
desc: The site of two monopteral nuraghi.

name: Castello di Attimis
desc: A twelfth-century castle

name: Shrine of Strenia
desc: The Shrine of Strenia was located in the valley of the Colosseum and is mentioned as the starting point of the Sacra Via.

name: Sudelfels
desc: The site of a Gallo-Roman sanctuary.

name: Via Caecilia
desc: The Via Caecilia left the Via Salaria at the 35th mile and continued to the Adriatic coast.

name: Vigna Randanini
desc: A Jewish catacomb along the Via Appia discovered in 1859.

name: Auditorium Maecenatis
desc: An early Imperial building on the Esquiline Hill in Rome, the Auditorium Maecenatis has been connected with Maecenas as it stands in the area of his gardens (horti). While its precise function is unknown, the building may have served as a conservatory.

name: Porte des Gaules
desc: The point of entry of the Via Aurelia.

name: Camp du Château
desc: The Camp du Château in Escragnolles, France

name: Oppidum de Conrouan
desc: The Oppidum of Conrouan in Escragnolles.

name: Passo Lombardo
desc: A villa rustica in Rome's suburbium with evidence for domestic production in the form of vats made from peperino tuff.

name: Villa romana delle Grotte
desc: A villa dating to the final quarter of the first century BC located on a headland overlooking Portoferraio on the island of Elba.

name: Basilica Damous el-Karita
desc: A Christian basilica of the Byzantine period located in Carthage.

name: Villa Area 5-7 a Tor Vergata
desc: An imperial villa located at Tor Vergata in the suburbium of Rome.

name: tribus Galeria
desc: The tribus Galeria was one of the older rural tribes of ancient Rome

name: Forum Boarium (at Pompeii)
desc: The so-called "Forum Boarium" in Pompeii was erroneously named by its 1755 excavators who discovered the bones of large bovids and assigned the name that still is used to describe this insula in Pompeii's Regio II (II, 5).

name: House and caupona of Epagatus
desc: Roman villa and caupona in Pompeii.

name: Temple of Apollo
desc: The Temple of Apollo (VII,7,32) in Pompeii is one of the city's oldest cults, dating to the sixth century BC. The sanctuary assumed its present appearance in the second century BC.

name: Porta Ostiensis
desc: The Porta Ostiensis, now known as the Porta San Paolo, is a gate in Rome's Aurelian Wall from which the Via Ostiensis issues.

name: Apollo, Aedes
desc: The likely site of the original sanctuary to Apollo at Rome. The visible remains belong to the Augustan phase.

name: San Teodoro al Palatino
desc: A church on the Palatine Hill in Rome, sacred to Saint Theodore of Amasea, dating originally to the sixth century AD.

name: Arcus Dolabellae et Silani
desc: Situated on the Caelian Hill, the Arcus Dolabellae et Silani sits at the northern corner of the Castra Peregrina. The gate dates to A.D. 10 and is likely a rebuilding of an earlier gate that was part of the so-called Servian Wall, perhaps the Porta Querquetulana (or Querquetularia) or the Porta Cael

name: Domus delle bestie ferite
desc: The Domus delle Bestie Ferite (“House of the Wounded Animals”) in Aquileia is an elite townhouse with at least two architectural phases: the first belonging to the Augustan period and the second to Late Antiquity. The house is well-appointed with elaborate mosaic pavements.

name: Fundus Appianus
desc: The estate of Aurelius Appianus, located near Beneventum and Ligures Baebiani (Circello). It's precise location is not known.

name: Sant'Agata di Militello
desc: A modern town in Sicily that has been associated with the location of the ancient settlement of Agathyrnum.

name: Lateran Obelisk
desc: The Lateran Obelisk is a monumental Egyptian obelisk, completed during the reign of Thutmose IV (ca. 1400 BCE) and looted from Karnak in the early fourth century CE.

name: Canneto sul Trigno
desc: The remains of a Roman "Villa rustica" located adjacent to the Sanctuary of the Madonna di Canneto.

name: Piscina romana (Acqui Terme)
desc: A Roman water feature at Acqui Terme dating to the Imperial period.

name: Peschiera di Castrum Novum
desc: Artificial fishponds of the Roman period at Castrum Novum.

name: Fosso delle Guardiole
desc: A stream that drains into the Tyrrhenian Sea at Santa Marinella, Italy.

name: Abbazia di San Giovanni in Venere
desc: A Christian monastic complex that is located in the municipality of Fossacesia, Italy. The site occupies a hilltop at 107 m above sea level on the Adriatic Sea coast. The basilica dates originally from the thirteenth century.

name: Roman theater at Amiternum
desc: The Roman theater at Amiternum could seat approximately 2,000 people. It was abandoned after the fourth century and became a necropolis.

name: Roman amphitheater at Amiternum
desc: A Roman amphitheater dating to the first century A.D.

name: Tino di Moscona
desc: The remains of a fortification located in the territory of Grosseto. While the visible architectural remains date to the Medieval period, the hilltop likely was occupied earlier by Etruscans and Romans.

name: Unnamed villa
desc: Remains of an extensive urban villa were discovered in 1886 during construction work at the intersection of what is now the Via Cavour and the Via dei Quattro Cantori.

name: House of the Wooden Shrine
desc: The so-called House of the Wooden Shrine may have been owned by one Lucius Autronius Euthymius. Its remains include a notable wooden shrine.

name: Central Baths
desc: A public bath complex at Herculaneum, dating to the first century A.D. It was subdivided into "male" and "female" sectors.

name: Basilica Noniana
desc: An architectural complex at Herculaneum that was renovated following the earthquake of A.D. 62 thanks to the patronage of Marcus Nonius Balbus. The site is only partly excavated. It faced onto the Decumaus Maximus, and lies directly across Cardo III from the College of the Augustales.

name: House of the Gem
desc: The so-called House of the Gem at Herculaneum was once linked to the House of the Relief of Telephus when Marcus Nonius Balbus owned the complex. After the Augustan period, the two domus were separated, and the House of the Gem was restored following the earthquake of A.D. 62.

name: Podere Cosciano
desc: Etrusco-Roman farm site

name: Sulcis Iglesiente
desc: A territory located in the southwestern part of Sardinia.

name: Grotta delle Veneri
desc: In the Grotta delle Veneri, human occupation can be documented from the Mousterian Age until the Neolithic and Bronze Ages.

name: Théâtre antique de Tarquimpol
desc: The ancient theater of Tarquimpol is located at the ancient settlement of Decempagi, present-day Tarquimpol, in the Moselle department. The theater was revealed by aerial photography in 1981; the theater measures approximately 117 meters in diameter and could accommodate up to 16,000 people.

name: Tomba della Vaschetta
desc: The so-called "Tomba della Vaschetta" is a Roman tomb located in the Portuense necropolis.

name: Ferrone Necropolis
desc: An Etruscan necropolis located on a tufaceous plateau overlooking the valley of the Fosso della Lenta. The tombs in the necropolis date between the seventh and fifth centuries BCE.

name: Necropolis of Grottini di Rota
desc: An Etruscan necropolis located in the middle of the Mignone river valley in the comune of Canale Monterano.

name: House of the Botanical Garden
desc: The site of a domus (VIII.5.38) in Regio VIII where modern botanical gardens of the ancient Vesuvian flora present in Pompeii are maintained.

name: House of the Moralist
desc: The so-called House of the Moralist, also known as the House of M. Epidius Hymenaeus, is located on the Via dell'Abbondanza. The house was formed from two connecting properties that belonged to two related wine merchants, T. Arrius Polites and M. Epidius Hymenaeus ( III, 4, 2-3).

name: Castronuovo di Sicilia
desc: A modern location in Sicily that has been associated with the location of the ancient settlement of Krastos.

name: Cancellone necropolis
desc: Rock-cut tombs located along the remains of a road dating as early as the sixth century B.C.

name: Necropolis of Santa Maria in Borraccia
desc: A seventh- and sixth-century B.C. Etruscan necropolis located in the territory of Heba.

name: Tanella Angori
desc: A circular Hellenistic tomb of the second century BC.

name: Villa of Furius Octavianus
desc: A Roman villa associated with a Caius Furius Octavianus who was a member of the Senatorial order during the Severan period. The villa was identified along the via Aurelia in the locality of Massimina - Casal Lumbroso. Excavations were carried out between 2011 and 2017.

name: Tomb of C. Veranius Rufus
desc: The tomb of the freedman of Caius Veranius Rufus and freedman Verania Clara in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis at Pompeii.

name: Unnamed tomb
desc: An ancient Roman tomb located in the Fondo Pacifico necropolis of Pompeii.

name: Tombs of the Calventii
desc: Burial ground of the gens Calventii in the Porta Nocera necropolis of Pompeii.

name: House of Minucius
desc: The so-called House of Minucius is located in Regio I of the city of Pompeii at the intersection of Vicolo del Menandro and Vicolo del Citarista. It is noted for two plastered benches flanking the fauces as well as painted electoral graffiti.

name: Luxeuil Abbey
desc: Located in France's Burgundy region, the Luxeuil Abbey was founded ca. 585–590 by the Irish missionary Saint Columbanus.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C4 unnamed bridge (near Compitum ad Confluentes)

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C4 unnamed bridge (over Sapis fl., near Caesena)

name: Roman bridge of San Vito
desc: The remains of a Roman bridge that once crossed the river known as Uso are located at San Vito, Italy, in the environs of Rimini.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 D1 unnamed bridge (at Ad Sanos (near S. Anastasio))

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 D1 unnamed bridge (at Fiumicino, nearer to (H)Eraclia)

name: Ponte romano – Ceggia
desc: Excavated remains of a Roman bridge located on the modern Via Ponte Romano about 2km southest of Ceggia (Veneto), Italy. Aerial/satellite photographs often show crop marking corresponding to the associated Roman road and now-diverted watercourse spanned by the bridge.

name: Fossa Augusta
desc: A canal connecting the Po river to the harbor of Ravenna.

name: Fossa Flavia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C3 Fossa Flavia

name: Centuriation near Vicetia
desc: Roman centuriation to the northwest of Vicetia (modern Vicenza in Italy)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A2 unnamed centuriation (near Cadianum (Verona))

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A2 unnamed centuriation (N Castello del Tartaro (Verona))

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A2 unnamed centuriation (near Fabbrica dei Soci (Verona))

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A3 unnamed centuriation (Bononia)

name: Centuriation located near Mutina
desc: BAtlas 40 A3 unnamed centuriation (near Forum Gallorum (Mutina))

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B1 unnamed centuriation (Acelum)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B1 unnamed centuriation (N Patavium)

name: Untitled

desc: Populonia likely derives its name from the Etruscan god 'Fufluns' and was an important maritime and commercial center of Etruria located in the Colline Metallifere.

name: Gallunianum
desc: A Praedium or estate located in Etruria near Siena; the modern Galognano.

name: Hellana
desc: Hellana was a road station along the via Cassia in Etruria, located between Florentia and Pistoriae.

name: Igilium
desc: An ancient settlement at modern Giglio Porto on the Italian island of Giglio. It abutted a massive Roman maritime villa.

name: Igilium (island)
desc: An island in the Tyrrhenian Sea with Etruscan and Roman occupation.

name: Ilva/Aethalia (island)

name: Luna

name: Vada Volaterrana
desc: Vada Volaterrana was an Etruscan port city located north of the mouth of the Cecina River.

name: Valvata

name: Vatl/Vetulonia
desc: The Etruscan Vatluna resisted Rome's influence in the seventh century BCE, although the city may have been the source of Rome's adoption of the curule chair and the fasces.

desc: A major Etruscan city of North Etruria.

name: Virle
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 D2 Virle

desc: A first century A.D. Roman aqueduct that carried water from the locality known as "Caldaccoli" to baths in Pisa.

name: Aquae Populoniae
desc: Remains of an Etrusco-Roman thermal complex, dating from the third century B.C. to late antiquity, were documented between 2000 and 2003.

desc: An Umbrian town that became a colonia civium Romanorum under the name of Aesis in 247 B.C.

name: Aesis (river)
desc: Aesis fl. (modern Esino river) is a river of the Marche region of Italy and flows into the Adriatic Sea.

name: Ager Gallicus (region)
desc: A region of Italy in which Gallic settlement had taken place after 400 BC. This territory was captured by Rome following the battle of Sentinum in 295 BC.

name: Alba Fucens
desc: A town of the Aequi along the Marsic frontier where the Romans established a Latin colony in 304/3 B.C. name: Albinia (river)
desc: The Albegna is a river of southern Tuscany and flows from Monte Amiata to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

name: Albula (river)

name: Alsietinus lacus
desc: The Alsietinus lacus, modern Lago di Martignano, is a small volcanic crater-lake in southern Etruria. The lake was the source of the Augustan aqueduct aqua Augusta Alsietina that served non-potable water to the Transtiberim and Ianiculum.

name: Alviano Scalo
desc: Occupation of the Roman villa at Alviano Scalo begins in the first century BCE and continues until the fourth century CE.

name: Ameria (Umbria)
desc: Ameria, claimed by Cato the Elder (quoted by Pliny) as the oldest town in Umbria, was an important center that may have gained Roman municipal status as early as 338 B.C., following the Latin War.

name: Amiternum
desc: Amiternum was an ancient settlement of the Sabines that Rome captured in 293 BC. The settlement was situated at the intersection of four Roman roads: the Via Caecilia, the Via Claudia Nova, and the two branches of the Via Salaria. The historian Sallust was born at Amiternum in 86 B.C.

name: Ancon(a)
desc: A port city founded by colonists from Syracuse in 387 BC.

name: Anguillara
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Anguillara

name: Anneianum
desc: Anneianum was located in the Etruscan Apennines, along the road from Faventia to Florentia.

name: Anxanum
desc: City of the Frentani, situated on a hill about 5 miles from the Adriatic Sea, and 8 miles from the mouth of the river Sagrus or Sangro in Italy.

name: *Aprutium
desc: An ancient region of eastern Italy (modern Abruzzo).

name: Aqua Viva

name: Aquae Apollinares Novae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Aquae Apollinares Novae

name: Aquae Cutiliae
desc: Roman city situated on mineral springs known today as Terme di Cotilia or Terme di Vespasiano in the Sabina region, Italy

name: Aquae Passeris
desc: Located in Etruria, Aquae Passeris was frequented in antiquity for its thermal springs, as noted by Martial. The site is included on the Tabula Peutingeriana, placing it on the road from Rome to Volsinii. Its location likely corresponds to that of Bacucco, a comune to the north of Viterbo.

name: Aquae Tauri
desc: A thermal site in Etruria northeast of Centumcellae.

name: Armenta (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Armenta fl.

name: Arna
desc: Arna was an ancient city of Umbria that was controlled by Etruscans in the fourth century BCE.

name: Arretium
desc: Arretium (the Etruscan Aritim) was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae and described by Livy as one of the "Capitae Etruriae". The Romans captured the city in 311 B.C. and it became a station on the via Cassia.

name: Asciano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Asciano

name: Asculum
desc: Asculum (modern Ascoli Piceno) was the principal city of the Piceni.

name: Asisium
desc: A Roman settlement built atop an earlier Umbrian one on a western foothill of the Apennines, Asisium received municipal status and was assigned to the Tribus Sergia. Totila destroyed most of the city in A.D. 545.

name: Aspia (river)
desc: The Aspio river.

name: Aternum
desc: Aternum (modern Pescara) was a settlement at the mouth of the Aternus River.

name: Aternus (river)
desc: The Aterno-Pescara river.

name: Attidium
desc: An ancient settlement of Umbria mentioned only by Pliny the Elder. Numerous inscriptions discovered at the site indicate that Attidium achieved the status of a municipium.

name: *Aufenginum

name: *Aurinia/Saturnia
desc: *Aurinia/Saturnia was a settlement in Etruria. Dionysius of Halicarnassus claimed it was founded by the Pelasgians. Saturnia received a Roman colony in 183 BC.

name: Auximum
desc: Auximum (modern Osimo) is an ancient settlement of Picenum. The original foundation was likely carried out by Greeks from Ancona. The Romans made it a base for military operations from 174 B.C.

name: Aveia
desc: Aveia was a settlement of the Vestini in the valley of the Aterno River.

name: Avens (river)
desc: A river of the Sabine territory.

name: Axia
desc: Axia was an Etruscan center located to the west of Viterbo.

name: Baccanae

name: Badies

name: Balneum Regis

name: Batinus (river)
desc: The Batinus flumen is mentioned by Pliny and may correspond to the modern Tordino river.

name: Blera
desc: Blera was a significant Etruscan settlement in the vicinity of Tarquinii. It lay along the line of the Roman Via Clodia. It received Roman municipal status and was enrolled in the tribus Arnensis. The city flourished in the sixth and fifth centuries BCE.

name: Caelanum

name: Camerinum

name: Campovalano

name: Capena
