name: Cetamura
desc: Cetamura is an ancient hilltop settlement with occupation phases stretching from the Etruscans to the Romans to the Medieval period. The site is located near Gaiole, Radda and Castellina in Chianti, Italy.

name: Chianciano Terme
desc: Chianciano Terme begins as an Etruscan site, with a temple located near the natural springs. By the first century B.C. the site was popular with Romans as a healing spa.

name: Le Ciliegeta

name: Ciminius (lake)

name: Ciminius (mountain)

name: Cingulum

name: *Cingulus (mountain)

name: Civita

name: La Cività di Spedino

name: Civitalba

name: Clanis (river)

name: Clasius? (river)
desc: Clasius? fl., a river of Umbria and part of the basin of the Tiber River.

name: Cliternia

name: Clitumnus (river)

name: Clocoris (river)

name: Cluana
desc: Cluana was an ancient settlement in Picenum.

name: *Cluentus (river)

name: Clusinus (lake)
desc: The modern Lake Chiusi in Italy.

name: Clusium
desc: Clusium, the Etruscan Clevsin (modern Chiusi), was a major city of Etruria. Lars Porsena was a sixth century B.C. king of Clusium.

name: Cluviae
desc: A city of the Carricini Samnites. Its site was surveyed and partially excavated in the 19th and 20th centuries in the vicinity of modern Piano La Roma, a locality to the northwest of modern Casoli.

name: Colle delle Fate
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Colle delle Fate

name: Colle Plinio
desc: A hilltop villa near Tifernum Tiberinum commonly associated with one of the villas of Pliny the Younger.

name: Collepezzuto
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Collepezzuto

name: Contrada Altavilla
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada Altavilla

name: Contrada S. Rustico
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada S. Rustico

name: Corchiano
desc: Corchiano was the site of a wealthy settlement in the Ager Faliscus that was in proximity to the Via Amerina.

name: Corciano
desc: The environs of Corciano were inhabited by Etruscans and, later, there is evidence for Roman villas. In 1812, a series of bronze panels from an Etruscan parade chariot was discovered at Castel San Mariano di Corciano.

name: Corfinium
desc: Corfinium was the principal city of the Paeligni in the valley of the Aternus river. The site becomes the capital of the breakaway Italic groups that oppose Rome during the Social War.

name: Cortona
desc: An Umbrian city that, under Etruscan influence, expanded and came to be called 'Curtun'. Later it became the Roman colony of Cortino.

name: Cosa
desc: A Latin colony in south Etruria founded ca. 273 B.C.

name: Crustumius (river)
desc: Crustumius fl. (Conca river)

name: La Cuma, Monte Rinaldo
desc: The principal archaeological remains found in the "La Cuma, Monte Rinaldo" site are those of a late Republican sanctuary dating to the third through first centuries B.C.

name: Cumara? (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Cumara? fl.

name: Cunerum (promontory)
desc: A promontory on the Adriatic coast of Italy, south of Ancona near Monte Conero.

name: Cupra Maritima
desc: Cupra Maritima was a coastal city of Picenum (regio V) assigned to the tribus Velina.

name: Cupra Montana
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Cupra Montana

name: Cures
desc: Cures (also Cures Sabini) was a Sabine city in the Tiber River valley along the Via Salaria. The Romans conquered Cures in 290 B.C. under M'. Curius Dentatus and granted it status as a municipium in the tribus Sergia.

name: Cutiliensis (lake)
desc: A lake located near ancient Reate.

name: Doganella
desc: Doganella was an important Etruscan settlement of the Albegna valley, occupied between ca. 600 and 400 B.C. The city may have comprised as many as 240 ha.

name: Eretum
desc: Eretum was a settlement of the Sabines and is involved in legendary accounts of early Rome.

name: Etruria/Tuscia (region)
desc: Etruria/Tuscia was an ancient region of Central Italy inhabited by the Etruscans. Its spatial footprint was roughly equivalent to the modern Italian regions of Toscana and northern Lazio.

name: Faesulae
desc: Faesulae (modern Fiesole) was an Etruscan foundation called Viesul, Viśl, or Vipsul. The city was conquered by Romans in 283 B.C. Sulla would settle Roman veterans there. Citizens of the town supported the conspiracy of Catiline.

name: Falerii
desc: A fortified town located some 6 km from Falerii Veteres and established by the ancient Romans ca. 241 B.C.

name: Falerii Veteres
desc: Falerii Veteres was the principal city of the Faliscans. It is located on a tuff outcropping at the point where several tributaries of the Treia join to flow into the Tiber. After rebelling against Rome in 241 B.C., Falerii suffered serious reversals of fortune.

name: Falerio
desc: Falerio was the site of a substantial ancient settlement on the left bank of the river Tinna. Under Augustus, a colony of veterans assigned to the tribus Velina was established there.

name: Falisci
desc: The name for a group of Italic people who occupied the Ager Faliscus within Etruria.

name: Fanum Fortunae
desc: Fanum Fortunae, the site of a shrine to Fortuna, is first mentioned in the ancient sources in 49 B.C. when Iulius Caesar held the town. An Augustan colony was established at the site and the Romans prevailed in the Battle of Fano in A.D. 271. The town was eventually destroyed by the Ostrogoths.

name: Fanum Fugitivi
desc: A road station on the Via Flaminia, located between Interamna and Spoletium.

name: Farfarus (river)
desc: The Torrente Farfa is a small stream in central Italy. It is located in the Province of Rieti in Italy and flows through the Sabine Hills en route to its confluence with the Tiber River. The valley has been a protected nature reserve since 1979. The Latin poet Ovid refers directly to the river using

name: Ferentium
desc: Ferentium (modern Ferento) was a city of Etruria first mentioned in the Liber Coloniarum ca. 123 BC that became a Roman municipium after the Social War. Substantial remains of the city remain; the site was the birthplace of Otho and is noted for its fine stone monuments and statues.

name: Fescennium
desc: Fescennium is the ancient name of a Faliscan settlement located ca. 5 km south of Falerii Veteres. The site, which was inhabited from the second millennium to the third century BCE, is often also called by the modern Italian name Narce (derived from an associated peak).

name: *Firmidianum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 *Firmidianum

name: Firmum Picenum
desc: Firmum Picenum was founded as a Latin colony in 264 B.C. with 6,000 colonists. It received municipal status after 48 B.C.

name: Fisternae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Fisternae

name: Flaminia (region)
desc: An ancient region of Roman Italy, located in the modern Marche region, north of the river Aesis (modern Esino).

name: Florentia
desc: Florentia (modern Florence / Firenze) was founded as a colony for military veterans ca. 80 B.C. by Lucius Cornelius Sulla.

name: Flusor (river)
desc: The Potenza river.

name: Fons Clitumni
desc: Originally the site of a shrine dedicated to the river god Clitumnus and later a paleochristian shrine. The temple was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2011.

name: Fontecchio
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Fontecchio

name: Foruli
desc: Foruli was a Sabine town located between Amiternum and Interocrea.

name: Forum Aurelii
desc: A settlement in Etruria situated on the Via Aurelia between Centumcellae and Cosa according to the Antonine Itinerary.

name: Forum Cassii
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Forum Cassii

name: Forum Clodii
desc: An ancient road station on the Via Clodia.

name: Forum Decii
desc: A town of the Sabines mentioned by Pliny the Elder.

name: Forum Flaminii
desc: Caius Flaminius founded Forum Flaminii in 220 B.C. during the construction of the Via Flaminia.

name: Forum Novum (Vescovio)
desc: Forum Novum was a Roman town and an early medieval bishopric. It is located in the Sabine hills and was likely founded as a market center during the Republican period. It had achieved the status of municipium by the first century A.D. The market center seems to have remained active until at least th

name: Forum Sempronii
desc: An ancient Roman colony, founded in the time of Gaius Sempronius Gracchus.

name: Fulginiae
desc: Fulginiae was an ancient town of Umbria, Italy, on the later line of the Via Flaminia, ca. 20 km south of Nuceria.

name: Furfo
desc: A vicus of the Vestini located in the upper Aterno valley in Abruzzo. The ancient settlement was located some 15 km south of modern L'Aquila, in the vicinity of S. Maria di Forfona near Barisciano. Furfo lay on the Via Claudia Nova between Amiternum and Peltuinum.

name: Galeata
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Galeata

name: Ghiaccio Forte
desc: Ghiaccio Forte was an Etruscan settlement, most likely founded in the fourth century B.C., that was sacked by the Romans ca. 280 B.C.

name: Graviscae
desc: The port of the Etruscan city of Tarquinia.

name: Grotte di Castro
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Grotte di Castro

name: Grotte di S. Nicola
desc: The so-called Grotte di S. Nicola, the remains of the platform and cryptoporticus of a late republican Roman villa.

name: Grotte di Torri
desc: Grotte di Torri is located on the left bank of the Tiber river in the modern comune of Montopoli di Sabina. It has been inhabited since pre-Roman times.

name: Hatria (Picenum)
desc: An ancient city of Picenum that may have originated as a colony established by Etruscans from Adria in the Veneto region. An alternate narrative suggests the city may have originated as a late sixth-century B.C. colony founded by Aegina.

name: Heba
desc: A Roman colony that was established in the third or second century B.C., Heba lay near modern Magliano. Funerary evidence indicates previous Etruscan occupation at the site.

name: *Hercules Curinus
desc: A sanctuary in the territory of the Paeligni dedicated to Hercules Curinus situated on an artificial terrace on the slopes of Mount Morrone. The terrace sanctuary looks over Sulmo in the valley below.

name: Helvia Ricina
desc: An ancient settlement in Picenum at modern Villa Potenza in Marche, Comune di Macerata, Italy.

name: Helvillum
desc: Helvillum was a vicus in Umbria located about 10 Roman miles from Aesis (Jesi).

name: Helvinus? (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F2 Helvinus? fl.

name: Himella (river)
desc: The Himella River was located in the Sabina, and its modern equivalent is the Fiume Salto. Virgil mentions the river along with the sites of Casperia and Foruli. The Himella debouched into Lacus Velinus.

name: Hispellum
desc: Hispellum (modern Spello) is an ancient settlement of Umbria that became a Roman colony in the first century BC.

name: Histonium
desc: Histonium, on the Adriatic coast, was a chief town of the Frentani.

name: Horta
desc: The Etruscan settlement of *Hurta (the modern Orte) was close to the Vadimonis Lacus where the Romans fought, and won, two engagements against Etruscan armies.

name: Iguvium
desc: An Umbrian hilltown, Iguvium is best known as the find-spot of the Iguvine Tables.

name: *Incerulae
desc: *Incerulae, an ancient sanctuary site in the territory of the Vestini.

name: Interamna Nahars
desc: An Umbrian center founded in the seventh century B.C. that became an important Roman municipality along the Via Flaminia.

name: Interamnia Praetuttiorum
desc: Originally a settlement of the Praetuttii located at the confluence of the rivers Tordino and Vezzola (modern Teramo).

name: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa
desc: Intercisa/Petra Pertusa was a road station on the Via Flaminia. The toponym derives from the rock-cut tunnel or galleria that dates to the reign of Vespasian.

name: Interocrium
desc: A Sabine town that was later known as a mansio on the course of the Via Salaria.

name: Interpromium
desc: A village of the Marrucini, forming a station on the Via Claudia Valeria between Corfinium and Teate.

name: Lucus Feroniae
desc: A sanctuary and grove of Feronia and an associated settlement located along the Via Tiberina in the territory of Capena.

name: Lugnano
desc: Lugnano in Teverina is a comune located in the Province of Terni in the modern Italian region of Umbria. It lies about 60 km south of Perugia and 25 km west of Terni. Archaeological investigation has documented important examples of villa culture as well as Late Antique funereal evidence.

name: Luni sul Mignone
desc: Luni sul Mignone is a site with archaeological evidence for habitation in the later second millennium BC, continuing into the Italian Iron Age. Excavations conducted by the Swedish Institute in Rome (1960-1963) exposed three phases of settlement activity.

name: Magliano Sabina
desc: Magliano Sabina is located in Lazio, some 50 km north of Rome and some 30 km west of Rieti.

name: Manliana
desc: One of two Roman road stations with this name in Italy attested in ancient sources. The Barrington Atlas Directory localizes this one at modern Torrita di Siena.

name: Marrucini
desc: The Marrucini were an Italic tribe centered around Teate in the Abruzzo. In conflict with Rome through the end of the Second Samnite War, the Marrucini became allied with Rome thereafter. Their language was likely in the Sabellic family.

name: Marsi
desc: The Marsi were an ancient Italic tribe. Their chief center was located at Marruvium.

name: Marsiliana d’Albegna
desc: An ancient settlement located near the confluence of the rivers Albegna and Elsa.

name: Marta (river)
desc: The Marta river flows from Lake Bolsena to the Tyrrhenian Sea. Its course flows past both Tuscania and Tarquinia and enters the Tyrrhenian Sea near Lido di Tarquinia.

name: Martanum
desc: An ancient harbor of the city of Tarquinia.

name: Maternum
desc: Maternum was a settlement of ancient Etruria that is known from the Peutinger Table. It is located along the Via Clodia between Saturnia and Tuscana.

name: Matilica
desc: Matilica was a municipium in Umbria located near the source of the river Aesis and close to the borders of Picenum. The Liber Coloniarum identifies the settlement as one of the “Civitates Piceni.”

name: Matrinum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G3 Matrinum

name: Matrinos (river)
desc: An ancient river of Picenum, mentioned by Strabo and Ptolemy, which is to be identified with the modern Torrente Piomba. The ancient Latin name is reflected in that of a coastal road station labeled on the Peutinger map (Macrinum), whence (correcting "c" to "t" after the Greek sources) BAtlas "Matri

name: Metaurus (river)
desc: Metaurus fl. (Metauro river) flows from near Monte dei Frati in the Apennine Mountains to the Adriatic Sea. The Metaurus was the site of two key battles in antiquity. The first, in 207 B.C., saw the defeat of Hasdrubal Barca by the consuls Marcus Livius Salinator and Gaius Claudius Nero. The second,

name: Mevania
desc: Mevania (modern Bevagna) was a Roman municipium in Umbria located on the Via Flaminia. The town was enrolled in the tribus Aemilia.

name: Mevaniola
desc: Mevaniola was a Roman city located in the Bidente valley. Its inhabitants were of Umbrian extraction, connected with the settlement of Mevania (Bevagna).

name: Minio (river)
desc: A river that flows some 62 km from the Monti Sabatini to the Tyrrhenian Sea. The modern Mignone.

name: Misco? (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Misco? fl.

name: Misus (river)
desc: A river that flows from just south of Arcevia to the Adriatic Sea. The Nevola river joined the Misa before it drains into the sea near Senigallia.

name: Mola di Monte Gelato
desc: An ancient settlement 30 km north of Rome that was excavated from 1986-90. An imperial villa existed on the site up until the third century AD.

name: Montariolo
desc: The tumulus of Montariolo originally measured some 4 meters in height and 50 meters in diameter. It included more than 350 tombs. It was used during several phases, stretching from the ninth to the fifth centuries BCE.

name: Monte Calvo
desc: The remains of a Roman villa that belonged to the family of the Bruttii Praesentes were found in the locality known as 'Madonna dei Colori' near the ancient road station Vicus Novus/Ad Novas, modern Osteria Nuova, some 53 km northeast of Rome.

name: Montedoro di Scapezzano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E1 Montedoro di Scapezzano

name: Monte S. Angelo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monte S. Angelo

name: Monteferetra
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Monteferetra

name: Montefortino
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Montefortino

name: Montelibretti
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Montelibretti

name: Monterano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monterano

name: Monti della Tolfa
desc: Monti della Tolfa, a volcanic group of mountains in the Anti-Apennines in the northern part of Lazio in central Italy.

name: Mucella
desc: Mucella, a region of north Etruria located north of Florentia.

name: Poggio Civitate (Murlo)
desc: An Etruscan elite complex of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. located at Poggio Civitate, a hill adjacent to the medieval town of Murlo and about 25 km south of Siena.

name: Musarna
desc: Musarna is an ancient Etruscan settlement discovered in 1849 just west of Viterbo, Italy. The École française de Rome has been conducting excavations at the site since 1983.

name: Naharcer
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Naharcer

name: Nar (river)
desc: The Nera river, a tributary of the Tiber.

name: Nelurus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Nelurus fl.

name: Nemora Vacunae
desc: Shrine dedicated to a rural divinity of the Sabina.

name: Nepet
desc: Nepet had become a Roman town before 396 B.C. when Livy dubs it, along with Sutrium, as one of the "keys" to Etruria. It became a Roman colony in 383 B.C. and a municipium after the Social War.

name: Nequinum/Narnia
desc: Nequinum/Narnia (modern Narni) was an ancient settlement in Umbria. It became a Latin colony in 299 BC.

name: Novilara
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Novilara

name: Nuceria
desc: Nuceria (modern Nocera Umbra) is an ancient town in Umbria, perhaps founded in the seventh century B.C. by Camerinum.

name: Numana
desc: Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.

name: Nursia
desc: Nursia was the northernmost city of the Sabines.

name: Ocriculum
desc: An ancient Umbrian city that became allied with Rome in 308 B.C.

name: [Orcla]
desc: [Orcla] or Norchia is an ancient Etruscan settlement located near Tarquinia and along the line of the Roman Via Clodia.

name: Ortona
desc: An ancient site in Italy that most likely originates with the Frentani.

name: Osa (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A3 Osa fl.

name: Ossaia
desc: Site of a Late Republican and Imperial Roman villa (first to fifth centuries A.D.)

name: Ostia Aterni
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Ostia Aterni

name: Ostra
desc: Ostra was an ancient town of Umbria.

name: Paeligni
desc: The ancient Oscan tribe of eastern Italy, the Paeligni, is first mentioned in historical sources in the fourth century BC, when they opposed Rome during the Second Samnite War. The Paeligni came into alliance with Rome at the end of the fourth century BC, but again took sides against Rome in the Soc

name: Paganica
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Paganica

name: Pallanum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Pallanum

name: Pallia (river)
desc: The Pallia is a tributary of the Tiber River.

name: Palmensis Ager
desc: Pliny the Elder discusses the Palmensis Ager in connection with his description of the Praetutii.

name: Passo Corese
desc: Passo Corese is located near Cures (Fara in Sabina). The site is often connected with Titus Tatius' march on Rome in 747 B.C.

name: Pausulae
desc: Pausulae was a town of Picenum mentioned by Pliny the Elder. It was a Municipium of Regio V.

name: Peltuinum
desc: Peltuinum was a settlement of the Vestini located along the Via Claudia Nova. The town is notable as the birthplace of the Roman general Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo.

name: Perusia
desc: A city of ancient Umbrian and Etruscan origin, Perusia aided Rome during the Second Punic War but was sieged and reduced by Octavian in the first century B.C. during campaigns against Lucius Antonius. It was rebuilt by Augustus and became Colonia Vibia Augusta Perusia quite late, in A.D. 251-3, unde

name: Pescara
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Pescara

name: Phalacrinae
desc: A Roman town where the emperor Vespasian was born in A.D. 9.

name: Piano Tondo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Piano Tondo

name: Picenum (region)
desc: Picenum was a region of Central Italy, extending along the coast of the Adriatic Sea from the mouth of the Aesis to that of the Matrinus, and inland as far as the central Apennines.

name: Pieve Socana
desc: Pieve di Sant'Antonino a Socana, a Medieval parish church, is built atop the remains of an Etruscan sanctuary.

name: Pinna
desc: Pinna (modern Penne) was a center of the Vestini. The site came under Roman control after the Social War (89 BC).

name: Pisaurum
desc: Pisaurum (modern Pésaro) was founded as a Roman colony in the territory of the Picentes in 184 BC.

name: Pisaurus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pisaurus fl.

name: Pitigliano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Pitigliano

name: Pitino
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Pitino

name: Pitinum
desc: An ancient center of the Vestini.

name: Pitinum Mergens
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pitinum Mergens

name: Pitinum Pisaurense
desc: An ancient settlement in Umbria, known mostly via its inclusion in the texts of Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy, as well as by means of various epigraphic evidence.

name: Planina
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Planina

name: Plestia
desc: Plestia was a municipium of the tribus Ufentina.

name: Plestinus L.
desc: In antiquity, the lacus Plestinus was located in Umbria and was the site of a military engagement during the Second Punic War.

name: Poggio Buco
desc: Poggio Buco was a pre-Roman site located in the valley of the Fiora River. Its archaeological remains include those of a circuit wall and a necropolis. The archaeological site is located ca. 9 km west of Pitigliano.

name: Poggio Sommavilla
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Poggio Sommavilla

name: Polimartium
desc: An late Roman settlement associated with modern Bomarzo in Italy with nearby Etruscan antecedents.

name: Ponte a Buriano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Ponte a Buriano

name: Ponte Capo d’Acqua
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Ponte Capo d’Acqua

name: Potentia
desc: A city settled in an area subjugated by Rome during the fourth century B.C. The local populace rebelled against Rome after the defeat at Cannae (216 B.C.), however the defeat of the Carthaginians eventually led to Potentia's reincorporation into the Roman sphere.

name: Praetuttii
desc: The Praetuttii were an ancient tribe of central Italy.

name: Prolaqueum
desc: A statio on the road from Nuceria to Ancona.

name: Punta La Penna
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Punta La Penna

name: Quintianum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Quintianum

name: Quinto Fiorentino
desc: Quinto Fiorentino is a place located in the plain of the Arno River to the west of Florence. Its location corresponds to the fifth mile of the Roman road. The site is especially known for two Etruscan tholos-type tombs a thòlos, one of which is the Tomba della Mula, and the other the Tomba della Mon

name: Raiano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Raiano

name: Rapinium
desc: Rapinium is located on the coast of Etruria between Centumcellae and Graviscae, at modern Bagni Sant'Agostino.

name: Reate
desc: Reate (modern Rieti) was a major Sabine center that came to be captured by Manius Curius Dentatus in late third century B.C.

name: Regis Villa/Regae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Regis Villa/Regae

name: Respampani
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Respampani

name: Rosia Campus
desc: A plain in the territory of the Sabines near Reate, reputed to have the most fertile soils in Italy.

name: Rostrata Villa
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Rostrata Villa

name: Rusellae
desc: An Etruscan city captured by Rome in 294 B.C., Rusellae's >2 mile circuit of megalithic walls represent an important early instance of stone fortification walling in the Italian peninsula.

name: Sabatinus lacus
desc: A volcanic lake in Latium north of Rome (modern Lago di Bracciano).

name: Sabini
desc: The Sabini (Sabines) were an Italic tribe of central Italy and belonged to the Osco-Umbrian language group. Their territory straddled parts of the modern regions of Lazio, Umbria, and the Abruzzo. Ancient writers connect them with Rome at the time of its foundation, as represented by the episode of

name: Sacraria
desc: A station on the Via Flaminia near Le Vene.

name: Saena
desc: Saena was an Etruscan city that received a Roman colony (Saena Iulia) in the time of Augustus.

name: Sagrus (river)
desc: A river of eastern Italy (modern Sangro).

name: S. Anatolia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 S. Anatolia

name: S. Casciano dei Bagni
desc: The village of San Casciano dei Bagni, located south of Siena, Italy, has been frequented since at least the first millennium BCE on account of its thermal springs with supposedly healing properties.

name: S. Erasmo di Cesi
desc: An ancient settlement, architectural complex featuring polygonal masonry, and associated burials at modern S. Erasmo di Cesi dates to the archaic period and has evidence for activity through the third century BCE.

name: San Giovenale
desc: The archaeological remains of an Etruscan settlement were discovered at San Giovenale, close to Blera, Italy, by the Swedish Institute at Rome in the 1950s and 1960s. The ancient name of the site is unknown.

name: San Giuliano
desc: An Etruscan settlement evidenced by its extensive, surviving necropolis, which now lies within the Parco Naturale Regionale Marturanum in the administrative territory of Barbarano Romano, Italy. Its modern name is transferred from a nearby medieval church.

name: S. Pier Maggiore
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 S. Pier Maggiore

name: S. Valentino
desc: Remains of at least two Roman villas have been identified in the frazione of San Valentino, part of the larger comune of Poggio Mirteto. One is the so-called Villa dei Casoni, while this site is sometimes known as the Bagni di Lucilla. This villa was the findspot in 1801 of a mosaic pavement now in

name: S. Vittore
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 S. Vittore

name: Sappinates?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Sappinates?

name: Sarsina
desc: Sarsina was a town of the Umbri that was captured by Cornelius Scipio in 271 B.C. and was the birthplace of the Latin author Plautus. The necropolis at Sarsina has been extensively studied.

name: Sarteano
desc: Sarteano is located between the Val d'Orcia and the Valdichiana. It is known in particular for its rich evidence of Etruscan funerary culture.

name: Sena (river)
desc: The Nevola river.

name: Sena Gallica
desc: Senonian Gauls founded Sena Gallica at the mouth of the Misa River in the fourth century B.C. This place became the site of Rome's earliest colony on the Adriatic seaboard before 280 B.C. Pompeius Magnus destroyed the city in 82 B.C.

name: Senones
desc: An ancient Gallic tribe that entered Italy after 400 BC and settled on the Adriatic coast from Forlì to Ancona, marking the so-called Ager Gallicus.

name: Sentinum
desc: An ancient town in the region of Italy now known as Le Marche, Sentinum is perhaps best known for the pivotal Battle of Sentinum of the Third Samnite War that took place nearby in 295 BC.

name: Sepernates?
desc: An ancient people of Etruria inhabiting the area around Nazzano Romano.

name: Septempeda
desc: Septempeda was an ancient settlement of Picenum. Its Roman phase began as a conciliabulum in the third century B.C.

name: Sestinum
desc: Sestinum was an ancient place in Umbria near the headwaters of the river Pisaurus. Pliny mentions the site, and its ancient name is preserved in modern toponymy.

name: Settefinestre
desc: A Late Republican Roman slave-run villa owned by the senatorial family of the Volusii.

name: Soracte (mountain)
desc: Soracte M. (Monte Soratte) is a mountain near Rome, Italy, the highest peak of which rises to 691 meters above sea level (2,267 ft). A site of ritual activity in antiquity, the mountain was sacred to Dis Pater.

name: Sorano
desc: Sorano was a Villanovan and, later, Etruscan settlement.

name: Sorrina
desc: Sorrina was a small Etruscan settlement on Viterbo's Colle di San Lorenzo, of which some traces remain. Epigraphic evidence also attests to a Roman municipium - Surrina Nova - that was likely located between Viterbo and Lake Bullicame.

name: Spoletium
desc: An ancient city along the route of the Via Flaminia; an initial colony was established there in 241 BCE.

name: Piammiano
desc: Site of an ancient settlement that flourished between the seventh century BCE and the early sixth century CE, located west across the Tiber from the modern village of Attigliano in Italy. Piammiano is probably to be identified with "Statonia", which is mentioned in ancient sources.

name: Statulae
desc: Statulae is a station marked on the Peutinger map. It was located in the territory of the Paeligni, 7 miles from Corfinium.

name: Suana
desc: Suana (Sovana) has Etruscan origins but later became a Roman municipium. In the fifth century A.D. it became an episcopal see.

name: Suasa
desc: Suasa was the site of a Roman municipium in Umbria. It lies in the Piano Volpello along a road from Cales to Sena Gallica. Alaric razed the settlement in 409.

name: Succosa
desc: Succosa was located between the Portus Cosanus and the Via Aurelia Antica to the north. It is mentioned in the Itineraries and located on the Tabula Peutingeriana. Frank E. Brown suggests that Succosa, derived from "sub-Cosa", emerges in the first century B.C. following the decline of the hill-top c

name: Superaequum
desc: One of three towns of the Paeligni which possessed municipal rights.

name: Sutrium
desc: An ancient settlement along the line of what would become the Roman Via Cassia and described by Livy, together with Nepet, as one of the keys to Etruria. A Latin colony was founded at the site after the fall of Veii.

name: Tadinae
desc: Tadinae (Sant'Antonio della Rasina to the west of Gualdo Tadino) is an ancient municipium of Umbria and was a road station on the Via Flaminia.

name: Talamone
desc: Located along the road from Talamone to Cannelle are the archaeological remains of one of the largest maritime villas known in the Albegna valley. Referred to colloquially as Villa le Terme at Santa Francesca di Talamone, the remains of this site can be divided into four sectors: the cistern, in a l

name: Tarchna/Tarquinii
desc: An ancient city of Etruria and the leading city of the doudecim populi Etruriae, Tarquinia (called Tarch(u)na or Tarchna in Etruscan) was a major urban center of ancient Italy.

name: Teate
desc: Originally named Teate Marrucinorum, Teate (modern Chieti) was the principal settlement of the Marrucini. Strabo attributes its origins to Arcadian Greeks.

name: Tessuinus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Tessuinus fl.

name: Tetricus (mountains)
desc: A mountain group in Italy, part of the central Apennines, the Tetricus mons is known today as the Monti Sibillini (Sibylline Mountains).

name: Tifernum Mataurense
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Tifernum Mataurense

name: Tifernum Tiberinum
desc: An Umbrian hilltown in the floodplain of the Tiber river north of Perusia.

name: Tinea (river)
desc: The Topino river in Umbria.

name: Tinna (river)
desc: The Tinna (modern Ténna) flows from the eastern slopes of the Sibillini Mountains into the Adriatic Sea between the municipalities of Porto Sant'Elpidio and Fermo. The Latin toponym Tinna may derive from that of Tinia, the Etruscan sky-god who was equivalent to the Greek god Zeus and the Roman god I

name: Tiora Matiene
desc: Tiora Matiene was the site of an ancient oracle of the god Mars. The Barrington Atlas tentatively placed it at modern Teora, near Barete.

name: Tirinus (river)
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Tirinus fl.

name: Tolentinum
desc: Tolentinum was a town of Picenum that is listed as having municipal status in the Liber Coloniarum.

name: Tolenus (river)
desc: A river of Lazio and Abruzzo that is a tributary of the Velino.

name: Traianus?
desc: A Roman villa that is typically associated with the emperor Trajan.

name: Trasumennus (Lake)
desc: Trasumennus lacus (modern Lake Trasimeno) is the largest lake of the Italian peninsula and the site of a major engagement of the Second Punic War on June 21, 217 B.C.

name: Trea
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Trea

name: Trebiae
desc: Trebiae was an ancient city of Umbria (regio IV) located near the line of the Via Flaminia. It is identified with modern Trevi, north of Spoleto in Italy.

name: Trebula Mutuesca
desc: Trebula Mutuesca or Trebula Mutusca was one of two Sabine cities bearing the name Trebula.

name: Tres Tabernae
desc: An ancient people, tribe, or cultural group. Located: near Trevi.

name: Trevignano
desc: Trevignano Romano, located on the shores of Lake Bracciano, lies some 47 km from Rome. Archaeological evidence for Etruscan occupation, in the form of tombs dating to the eighth - sixth centuries B.C., has been discovered to the north of the modern town. A medieval castle was built there under Innoc

name: Truentus (river)
desc: A river of Picenum that flows from its source on the Gran Sasso d'Italia to the Adriatic Sea at Porto d'Ascoli.

name: Tuder
desc: Tuder, modern Todi, is an ancient city of Umbria. Its foundation likely occurred during the eighth/seventh centuries BC, although legendary traditions associate the site with the activities of Herakles.

name: Tuficum
desc: Tuficum was an ancient city of Umbria located on the Aesis River. It became a municipium of the tribus Oufentina.

name: Tuscana
desc: An ancient city that traced its legendary origins to Ascanius, son of Aeneas. The site became an important Etruscan mercantile center and eventually achieved Roman municipal status in 88 B.C.

name: Umbria (region)
desc: The eponymous region of the Umbri, an ancient Italic people who spoke the Umbrian language. The physical geography of the landlocked region is hilly and dominated by the Appennine Mountains.

name: *Umbro (river)
desc: The Ambra flows from the foot of Monte Luco to the Arno river.

name: Urbs Salvia
desc: An ancient city of Regio V (Picenum) where a Roman colony was founded in the second century B.C.

name: Urvinum Hortense
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Urvinum Hortense

name: Urvinum Mataurense
desc: Urvinum Mataurense (modern Urbino).

name: Vacchereccia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Vacchereccia

name: Vadimonis (lake)
desc: A partially dry lake of ancient Etruria near Orte. The Romans were victorious in two battles fought against the Etruscans there (310 and 283 BC).

name: Velini L.
desc: In the Roman period, the Lacus Velinus was a larger body of water than the surviving remnant that is now known as Lake Piediluco. Modern intervention drained water away from the lake into the lower Nera River.

name: Velini (lake)
desc: A lake formed by three rivers (Avens, Himella and Tolenus) in the territory of the Sabines.

name: Velzna/*Volsinii Veteres/Urbiventus
desc: Volsinii Veteres was one of the most powerful and important cities of Etruria, as it was the location of the important federal sanctuary located at the Fanum Voltumnae.

name: Verucchio
desc: Around the modern Italian town of Verucchio (Emilia-Romagna), a number of ancient necropoleis provide evidence for iron-age civilization and craft at a presumed settlement on the site lasting into the Roman period.

name: Vespasiae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vespasiae

name: Vestini
desc: The Vestini were an ancient tribe of Italy and lived in the southern part of the modern Abruzzo, between the Gran Sasso and the northern bank of the Aterno river. A major center was located at Pitinum.

name: Vettona
desc: Vettona (modern Bettona) is an ancient settlement of Umbria located between Perusia and Mevania. Pliny the Elder lists it among the municipalities of Umbria, and it also numbered as one of the “xv Populi Umbriae".

name: Vicarello
desc: A large, Roman imperial estate covering ca. 2,000 ha on the shores of Lake Bracciano. The name may derive from Vicus Aurelius, suggesting a connection with Marcus Aurelius.

name: Vicus Martis
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vicus Martis

name: Vicus Matrini
desc: Vicus Matrini was a mansio along the Via Cassia, located between Sutri and Forum Cassi. The site's name is attested on the Peutinger Table.

name: Vicus Novus/Ad Novas
desc: Vicus Novus/Ad Novas

name: Vignanello
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Vignanello

name: Villa S. Silvestro
desc: The remains of a Republican temple podium now support a Christian church at Villa S. Silvestro in Umbria. The temple's podium likely dates, in its first phase, to the third century B.C.

name: Villalfonsina
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Villalfonsina

name: Visentium
desc: Visentium (Bisenzio) was an Etruscan settlement located on the shores of Lago di Bolsena. The site has yielded especially important evidence for Iron Age and Etruscan period burials.

name: Vittorito
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Vittorito

name: Volsiniensis L.
desc: A volcanic lake of northern Latium formed by the collapse of the Vulsini volcano. Roman sources record volcanic activity at the site as late as the second century B.C.

name: Volsinii
desc: Volsinii, also referred to as Volsinii Novi, is thought to be the settlement where Rome resettled the survivors of the Volsinian rebellion of 264 BCE. This episode is discussed by Zonaras (8. 7. 8). A late republican center at Bolsena, Italy, with civic architecture (forum) and domus has been excava

name: Volusii
desc: A villa associated with the Volusii Saturnini built ca. 50 B.C.

name: Vomanus (river)
desc: The Vomano river in Abruzzo flows into the Adriatic Sea.

name: Vulci
desc: Vulci (originally Velch or Velx in Etruscan) was an Etruscan city 80 km northwest of Rome. Vulci was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae.

name: Zerninus (river)
desc: An ancient river, probably to be identified with the modern Salinello.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 unnamed aqueduct (Florentia)

name: Roman aqueduct at Arretium
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 unnamed aqueduct (Arretium)

name: Untitled
desc: An aqueduct located near the sulphurous springs at Aquae Tauri, northeast of Centumcellae.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 unnamed aqueduct (Spoletium)

name: Unnamed aqueduct near Amiternum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 unnamed aqueduct (near Amiternum)

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: An unnamed ancient bridge located on the Via Aurelia over the Osa river at Telamon.

name: Ponte Buriano
desc: The bridge known as Ponte Buriano is located at the hamlet of Ponte a Buriano, Italy. The bridge spans the Arno River and dates initially from 1277.

name: Ponte Romito
desc: An ancient bridge, now known as "Ponte Romito" crosses the Arno River to the west of Ponte a Buriano.

name: Ponte di Pogi
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 unnamed bridge (over *Umbro fl., W Arretium at Pogi)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 unnamed bridge (near Aquae Apollinares? on road to Tarquinii at La Mola)

name: Ponte dell'Abbadia
desc: An ancient bridge over the Fiora river (the ancient Armenta) near Vulci. Ancient name unknown.

name: Bridge on Via Cassia near *Volsinii Veteres
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 unnamed bridge group (on Via Cassia, near Sorrina)

name: Ponte della Rocca, Blera
desc: The so-called Ponte della Rocca located on the Via Clodia at Blera is situated adjacent to the Necropolis of San Giovenale and Terrone. Some sources suggest an original date in the third or second centuries BCE.

name: Unnamed bridge over the Nar river near Terni
desc: An ancient bridge near the *Via Curia.

name: Unnamed bridge
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1-C4 unnamed bridge (on Via Flaminia (20))

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 unnamed bridge (S Camerinum)

name: Ponte di Quintodecimo
desc: The Ponte di Quintodecimo is located near Acquasanta Terme.

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A1 unnamed centuriation (Florentia)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A3 unnamed centuriation (Heba)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A4 unnamed centuriation (Cosa)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 unnamed centuriation (Hispellum)

name: Untitled
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E1 unnamed centuriation (Fanum Fortunae)

name: Unnamed centuriation near Potentia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F2 unnamed centuriation (Potentia)

name: Ad Nonas
desc: Ad Nonas is the name of a now unlocated road station near Cosa; the name is attested in the Peutinger Table.

name: Ad Novas
desc: An unlocated Roman road station in Italy. As represented on the Peutinger Map, it was at least a minor hub in the road network, connected to Ad Grecos (unlocated), Arretium, Clusium, and Manliana. The Barrington Atlas Directory describes its likely general localization as "between Saena and Clusium"

name: Castellum Amerinum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 unlocated Castellum Amerinum

name: Ceios
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 unlocated Ceios

name: Cingilia
desc: A settlement of the Vestini, now unlocated, that, according to Livy, Iunius Brutus captured in 325 B.C.

name: Fanum Voltumnae
desc: A shrine of Voltumna that served as the chief religious center of Etruria. The Etruscan League (duodecim populi Etruriae) was said to meet annually at the shrine. Archaeological excavations of the site of Campo della Fiera have been posited as the definitive location of the Fanum Voltumnae.

name: Fiscellus M.
desc: A high mountain forming part of the central and most elevated chain of the Apennines. Pliny indicates that it was the source of the river Nar.

name: Flosis (river)
desc: A small coastal river in Picenum located between Ancona and Firmum.

name: Frusteniae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 unlocated Frusteniae

name: Iabuscer
desc: An ancient people whose territory is unlocated.

name: Nersa
desc: Referred to by Virgil, Nersa was a vicus of the Aequiculi. Its precise location is not known, but some 19th century scholars identified it with the modern village of Civitella di Nesce in Italy.

name: Pollition
desc: Mentioned only by Diodorus, Pollition is described as "a city of the Marroukinoi" against which Rome conducted military operations ca. 312 BCE. The Marrucini were an Italic tribe centered around Teate in the Abruzzo, but the precise location of Poliltion cannot be determined today.

name: Sabate
desc: An ancient settlement, attested by literary or documentary sources, whose precise location cannot be determined today

name: Sacrata
desc: Attested on the Peutinger Map, this road station near the Adriatic coast in Italy cannot be located with certainty today.

name: Salinae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 unlocated Salinae

name: Septem Aquae
desc: A now-unlocated pagus in the territory of the Sabines. Septem Aquae was known for springs and lakes that were popular with tourists. Cicero visited the area in 54 B.C.

name: Severus (mountain)
desc: A mountain probably near Mt. Tetricus.

name: Surpicanum
desc: An ancient settlement along the Via Salaria, the exact position of which remains unknown.

name: Tabellaria
desc: A road station located on the via Aurelia between Centumcellae and Graviscae in Etruria, now unlocated.

name: Testruna
desc: Testruna is now unlocated, although it may have been located near Amiternum. Dionysius of Halicarnassus names it as the original settlement of the Sabines.

name: Acqua Acetosa
desc: A settlement along the Via Laurentina that has yielded significant evidence for protohistoric occupation, including funereal evidence of the eighth and seventh centuries B.C.

name: Acquafredda
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Acquafredda

name: Ad Aquas Salvias
desc: Ad Aquas Salvias was a place on the Via Laurentina.

name: Ad Bivium
desc: A statio in Latium located at the intersection of the Via Latina and the Via Labicana, near the modern Valmontone.

name: Ad Decimum
desc: The road station of Ad Decimum corresponds with the archaeological area of Castel di Decima where archaeological excavations in the 1970s identified the remains of a settlement covering some 11 hectares that dates to the eighth through sixth centuries BCE. Excavations revealed not only habitation ev

name: Ad Decimum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Decimum

name: Ad Duas Lauros
desc: The toponym 'Ad Duas Lauros' refers to a large imperial property at the third mile of the Via Labicana and today comprising the archaeological park of Centocelle. The site is mentioned in the Liber Pontificalis as that of a large imperial villa in which Helena, mother of Constantine I, lived. Archae

name: Ad Gallinas Albas
desc: Ad Gallinas Albas refers to a location along the Via Flaminia.

name: Ad Nonum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Nonum

name: Ad Nonum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ad Nonum (1)

name: Ad Pictas
desc: Ad Pictas is a road station east of Rome, known mostly for its role in Sulla's march on Rome in 88 B.C. The precise location of the statio continues to be debated.

name: Ad Quintanas
desc: Ad Quintanas is the name of a road station on the Via Labicana.

name: Ad Sextum
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Ad Sextum

name: Ad Sponsas
desc: Ad Sponsas was a road station on the Via Appia.

name: Ad Statuas
desc: Ad Statuas was a road station on the Via Labicana located east of Rome.

name: Ad Turres
desc: Ad Turres was located on the Via Aurelia, some 10 miles from Lorium and 12 miles from Pyrgi.

name: Adriano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Adriano

name: Aeflanus (mountain)
desc: Colle Ripoli-Monte S. Angelo.

name: Aefula
desc: Aefula was an ancient settlement of Latium that had disappeared by the time of Pliny the Elder, although the cult of Bona Dea there continued to flourish.

name: Aequi
desc: The Aequi were an ancient Italic tribe of northeast Latium in the first millennium BC.

name: Afilae
desc: Located in the Anio river valley to the south of Subiaco, Afilae was a municipium that was likely assigned to the tribus Aniensis.

name: Alba Longa
desc: Alba Longa, located in the Alban Hills southeast of Rome, was the chief city and founder of the Latin League. Conflict with Rome caused Alba's destruction in the seventh century B.C. The legendary history of Romulus and Remus connects them to the royal lineage of the city. The ancient city is probab

name: Albanus (lake)
desc: A volcanic lake in ancient Latium at the foot of Albanus Mons, Albanus Lacus (Alban Lake) is connected with the site of the city of Alba Longa and, later, with imperial properties of the Flavian house.

name: Albanus M.
desc: The second-highest summit of the Alban Hills, Mons Albanus, is an extinct volcano with an elevation of 950 m (3,117 ft). In the middle of the first millennium B.C., there may have been volcanic activity, as noted by the historian Livy. The mountain was sacred for Latin peoples who held important fes

name: Albuccione
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Albuccione

name: Albunea (river)
desc: A toponym connected to the semi-legendary topography of Latium as described in the Aeneid.

name: Algidus
desc: An ancient settlement of Latium located in the territory of the Aequi.

name: Algidus (mountain)
desc: Algidus (mons) refers to the eastern rim of the dormant Alban volcano in the Alban Hills of central Italy, known today as Monte Artemisio.

name: Alsium
desc: Alsium served as a port for Caere, together with Fregenae. A Roman colony was established ca. 245 BCE. The Antonine Itinerary places it 18 Roman miles from Portus at the mouth of the Tiber.

name: L’Altare
desc: A small site in Latium (?1.2 hectares) that may have been fortified as early as the eighth century BCE.

name: Anagnia
desc: Anagnia was a Hernican town that sided with Rome against the Volscians and later became civitas sine suffragio. By Cicero's time it received the status of municipium.

name: Anio (river)
desc: The Anio river (modern Aniene) is a river of northern Latium.

name: Annunziatella
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Annunziatella

name: Antemnae
desc: Antemnae is an ancient Latin settlement located north of Rome near the point where the Anio and Tiber rivers intersect. Connected with Rome's early history, Antemnae was involved in episodes such as the 'Rape of the Sabine Women' and Romulus is said to have celebrated a triumph over the Antemnates i

name: Antium
desc: Antium ranked as one of the most important and most powerful centers of Latium and was captured by Rome at the close of the Latin War in the fourth century B.C. Imperial Antium was well known for its number of coastal villas.

name: Villa degli Antonini
desc: The so-called 'Villa of the Antonines', located near Genzano di Roma in the Alban Hills, lies just south of the Via Appia between the road's 18th and 19th milestones.

name: Aquae Albulae
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Aquae Albulae

name: Aquae Albulae
desc: A group of springs located west of Tibur (modern Tivoli). The main spring, known as Lago della Regina, preserves traces of an ancient Roman bath.

name: Arcinazzo
desc: An imperial villa of the Trajanic and Hadrianic periods located on the Altipiani di Arcinazzo.

name: Ardea
desc: Ardea was an ancient settlement of the Rutuli in Latium.

name: Aricia
desc: Aricia was an ancient Latin settlement and a member of the Latin League.

name: Artena
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Artena

name: Astura (river)
desc: The Astura is a river of Latium that flows from the Alban Mount to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

name: Baebiana
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Baebiana

name: Il Barco
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Il Barco

name: Il Barco
desc: The so-called "Barco Borghese" is an archaeological site located in Monte Porzio Catone (Roma) in Italy. This multiperiod site began as a Roman terracing or substructure, perhaps originally meant to support a villa (basis villae). Subsequent modification and reuse converted the Roman structure into

name: Bel Poggio
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Bel Poggio

name: Bovillae
desc: A town of ancient Latium along the line of the Via Appia, Bovillae is traditionally considered to be a colony of Alba Longa and was one of the thirty cities of the Latin League.

name: Bruto e Pisoni
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Bruto e Pisoni

name: Buglioncino
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Buglioncino

name: Buon Riposo
desc: Buon Riposo is a small, fortified settlement covering some 2 hectares. Its fortifications date to the seventh century BCE or later.

name: Cabum?
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cabum?

name: Caere
desc: Caere (also known as Cisra or Cerveteri) was a major Etruscan polis located ca. 50 km north-northwest of Rome in southern Etruria.

name: Calepodius
desc: A Christian catacomb originally containing the tombs of Pope Callixtus I and Pope Julius I, along with that of the eponymous Saint Calepodius.

name: Campo del Fico
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Campo del Fico

name: Campoverde
desc: Campoverde (Lazio) lies some 60 km south of Rome. In 1977-1978 a quantity of votive material was recovered from a body of water known as the "Laghetto del Monsignore". This spring-fed body of water was interpreted as an open-air votive depository.

name: Campus Martius
desc: The Campus Martius or "field of Mars" is the name given to the level ground between the slopes of the Capitoline, the Quirinal, and Pincian hills, and the Tiber river.

name: Capannacce
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Capannacce

name: Capitolium
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Capitolium

name: Cappellette
desc: The site of a villa located between Frascati and Monte Porzio Catone. It is associated with Matidia Augusta on account of an inscribed fistula discovered there in 1888.

name: I Cappuccini
desc: The church and convent "I Cappuccini" in Frascati was the site of a Roman villa.

name: Careiae
desc: An ancient town on the Via Clodia.

name: Casal Rotondo
desc: A Roman tomb that supports a Medieval farmhouse (casale) at the sixth mile of the Via Appia. The tomb originally dates ca. 30 BC; it was a large, circular tomb with a diameter of approximately 35 m.

name: Casale del Cavaliere
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Casale del Cavaliere

name: Casale di Gregna
desc: A villa at the seventh mile of the Via Latina.

name: Casale Martellona
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Casale Martellona

name: Casale Morena
desc: A villa located at the eighth mile of the ancient Via Latina. The villa was first built in the first century B.C. and continued in use until the fourth century. During its life span there were several phases of architectural modification and expansion.

name: Casali
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Casali

name: Casali Vitriano
desc: T. Ashby notes the presence of a villa platform to the west of the "upper Casale Vitriano". This platform seems to be a terrace at least 34 m in length.

name: Case Nuove 1
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Case Nuove 1

name: Case Nuove 2
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Case Nuove 2

name: Case Rosse
desc: Ashby describes a rich archaeological landscape that once included the remains of Roman-period tombs and villas, the latter appointed with mosaics. The modern toponym "Case Rosse" is said to derive from a well-preserved Roman tomb executed in brick that was purposefully destroyed in 1824.

name: Cassio
desc: A villa in Tibur that has been incorrectly linked to Gaius Cassius Longinus. In the eighteenth century, the site produced a cache of Egyptianizing sculpture that likely dates to the reign of Hadrian and is now held in the Vatican Museums.

name: Castel Campanile
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Castel Campanile

name: Le Castella
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Le Castella

name: Castel Madama
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Castel Madama

name: Castelporziano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Castelporziano

name: Castel Savello
desc: Castel Savello takes its name from a fifteenth-century fortress of the Savelli family at Albano Laziale. Funerary evidence associated with the Latial culture has been documented here.

name: Castra Albana
desc: Castra Albana was a permanent, fortified camp of the Legio II Parthica constructed during the Severan period.

name: Castrimoenium
desc: A Latin settlement that became a Roman municipium.

name: La Cecchina
desc: The so-called "Torraccio della Cecchina" is a Roman funereal monument dating to the second century A.D. It is located at the ninth kilometer of the modern Via Nomentana.

name: Centroni
desc: The Villa dei Centroni, located on the modern via Anagnina, lay at the ninth mile of the ancient via Latina. It dates from the first century B.C. onward.

name: Ceres et Faustina (temple)
desc: The Roman temple dedicated to Ceres and Faustina received patronage from Herodes Atticus. Its remains were eventually repurposed in the construction of the church of Sant'Urbano.

name: Cervara 1
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cervara 1

name: Cervara 2
desc: In the vicinity of Tor Cervara are anio tuff (tufo d'Aniene) quarries.

name: Cessati Spiriti
desc: A ruined Roman mausoleum on the grounds of the Caffarella regional park. The so-called Cessati Spiriti mausoleum was once clad in travertine.

name: Ciciliano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Ciciliano

name: Cimitero Maggiore
desc: A major Roman necropolis and catacomb along the Via Nomentana.

name: Cinecittà
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Cinecittà

name: Civitana
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Civitana

name: Clodio
desc: Cicero describes the villa of Publius Clodius Pulcher as being located at the thirteenth mile of the Via Appia near Bovillae.

name: Collatia
desc: Collatia was an ancient city of Latium located between Gabii and the Anio River. A colony of Alba Longa, Collatia was one of the most ancient cities of Latium. Subjugated by Rome under the Tarquins, Collatia would decline during the Republican period and numbers among the lost Latin cities by the ac

name: Colle Gentile
desc: Colle Gentile is a naturally defensible hill with good visibility located in the environs of Norba. While the site has not been scientifically excavated, it has been surveyed. The Groningen Institute of Archaeology identified traces of polygonal masonry fortification walls as well as surface ceramic

name: Colle Medico
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Colle Medico

name: Colle Monitola
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Monitola

name: Colle Nocello
desc: A plaform villa at Colle Nocello.

name: Colle Rosa
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Rosa

name: Colle Rotondo
desc: Colle Rotondo was the site of a prehistoric settlement inhabited from the Bronze Age until the early Iron Age.

name: Colle Tasso
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Colle Tasso

name: Colle Vitriano
desc: Colle Vitriano is the site of a Roman villa supported on two artificial terraces that utilize megalithic walling in the polygonal masonry technique as well as caementicium.

name: La Colombella
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 La Colombella

name: Compitum
desc: A multi-period sanctuary near Anagnia.

name: Cora
desc: A Latin center in the Monti Lepini that was already a Roman municipium by 211 B.C.

name: Corniculum
desc: An ancient town of Latium connected with the origins of Servius Tullius.

name: Corzano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Corzano

name: Cremera (river)
desc: The Cremera is a small stream in Lazio that played a role in the fourth century BC war between Rome and the Etruscan city-state of Veii.

name: Crepaddosso
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Crepaddosso

name: Crustumerium
desc: An ancient town of Latium located at the headwaters of the Allia river, very close to the territory of the Sabines, Crustumerium figures in Rome's early history. The Romans conquered the site in 500 B.C. and formed the tribus Crustumina or Clustumina in 471 B.C.

name: Dea Dia (temple)
desc: The Arval Brethren cultivated the cult of the Dea Dia. The remains of this Augustan era temple, located at La Tavernaccia restaurant in the Magliana Vecchia neighborhood of Rome, are subterranean and not open to the public.

name: Temple of Diana at Nemi
desc: A site sacred to Diana near Lake Nemi, comprised of a Tuscan-style sanctuary and a sacred grove.

name: Ficana
desc: An ancient city of Latium that was said to have been conquered by Ancus Marcius, Ficana was located near the eleventh mile of the Via Ostiensis. Excavation at the site has produced important evidence for the urban center beginning from the eighth century BC. Pliny the Elder mentions Ficana as one of

name: Ficulea
desc: Ficulea was an ancient city of Latium situated between Rome and Nomentum.

name: Fidenae
desc: Fidenae was an ancient city of Latium.

name: Forte Tiburtina
desc: At Forte Tiburtina the remains of a Roman villa located on the northern edge of the Parco della Serenissima in the eastern suburbium of the city of Rome.

name: Fortuna Muliebris, T.
desc: A sanctuary dedicated to Fortuna Muliebris along the Via Latina. Tradition holds that it was dedicated in 487 B.C.

name: Forum Appii
desc: An ancient road station on the Via Appia located 69 km southeast of Rome.

name: Fosso della Crescenza
desc: John Ward-Perkins identified the archaeological site at Fosso della Crescenza during the South Etruria Survey. Excavations of a Iulio-Claudian mausoleum were undertaken in 1962. Additional excavation revealed portions of the Via Veientana. Post-excavation work did not occur until the 1980s, by which

name: Frascati
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Frascati

name: Fregenae
desc: An ancient town of Etruria, Fregenae was located between Alsium and the mouth of the river Tiber.

name: Gabii
desc: An ancient Latin city located on the line of the Republican Via Praenestina connecting Rome to Praeneste. Gabii is allied to Rome from an early date and flourished during the archaic period, declining by the time of Augustus.

name: Giordani
desc: A fourth-century A.D. catacomb along the via Salaria at Rome.

name: La Giostra
desc: A fortified site on the Via Appia dating to the Republican period.

name: Villa Gordiani
desc: A third century A.D. villa complex along the Via Praenestina connected with Gordian I, Gordian II, and Gordian III.

name: Grotta del Mortale
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Grotta del Mortale

name: Grotta di Paris
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Grotta di Paris

name: Grotta Papale
desc: The site of a Roman villa situated on two terraces. The modern toponym "Grotta Papale" derives from a partially subterranean apsidal nymphaeum. The villa was extensive, covering some 23,000 square meters and has both a late republican and an imperial phase.

name: Grottaferrata
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Grottaferrata

name: Grottarossa
desc: Grottarossa is located at the intersection of key roadways in northern suburbium of Rome, lying along the Via Flaminia as well as at the point where the Via Veientana separated from the Via Cassia and thereby connected Rome with Veii. There is archaeological evidence for tombs, both built tombs and

name: Grotta Oscura
desc: The quarries at Grotta Oscura were an important source of high-quality tuff located in the territory of Veii. This was the "tuffo giallo della via Tiberina" that was used at Rome from the Archaic period onward.

name: Hernici
desc: The Hernici (Hernicans) were an Italic tribe of first millennium B.C. Latium. Their territory was bounded by the Trerus fl. (Sacco) and the Lacus Fucinus (Fucine Lake).

name: Inviolata
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Inviolata

name: Isola Sacra
desc: An extensive second and third century A.D. necropolis located between the city of Ostia and Portus.

name: Iuppiter Latiaris, T.
desc: An important Latial sanctuary of Iuppiter located on Mons Albanus (modern Monte Cavo).

name: Temple of Jupiter?, Via Appia
desc: A temple located at the fourth mile of the Via Appia.

name: Labicum
desc: Originally a member of the Latin League, the city of Labicum was taken by the Romans ca. 418 B.C. By the time of Augustus, the site was almost certainly deserted and its precise location remains debated today.

name: Ladispoli
desc: Ladispoli is a modern toponym; it is a comune of the Metropolitan City of Rome and is situated 35 kilometers (22 miles) west of Rome, on the Mediterranean Sea coast. In terms of the ancient landscape, present-day Ladispoli lies in the environs of ancient Alsium. Based on archaeological remains, Ladi

name: Laghetto di Colonna
desc: Based on T. Ashby (1902), the compilers of the Barrington Atlas include a Roman villa site identified as "Laghetto di Colonna". Ashby discusses this toponym in relation to the discussion about the location of Lacus Regillus; he posits that Laghetto di Colonna and Lacus Regillus are, in fact, differe

name: Lamnae/Ad Lam(i)nas
desc: Lamnae/Ad Lam(i)nas, a road station located 33 miles from Rome and 13 miles from Tibur.

name: Lanuvium
desc: Lanuvium was an important city of Latium located south of the Alban Hills. After opposing Rome at the battles of Aricia (504 B.C.) and Lake Regillus (496 B.C.), Lanuvium was captured by the Romans in 338 B.C.

name: Largo Preneste
desc: A Roman tomb of the second or third century CE.

name: Latium Vetus (region)
desc: Latium Vetus is an historical region of Italy. Latium Vetus begins south of the Tiber river and extends as far as Circeo, at which point the boundary of Latium Adiectum is reached.

name: Lavinium
desc: An ancient city of Latium on the Numicus River that was founded, according to Virgil, by Aeneas.

name: Lepinus (mountain)
desc: Lepinus M., a mountain range of central Italy that belongs to the Anti-Apennines.

name: Lolli Paolini
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Lolli Paolini

name: Lorium
desc: An ancient town on the Via Aurelia.

name: Lucio Vero
desc: A Roman villa located at Acquatraversa on the Via Cassia that is frequently attributed to Lucius Verus.

name: Lucullo
desc: Plutarch describes a villa owned by Lucullus near Tusculum.

name: Magliana Vecchia
desc: "Magliana Vecchia" is the name of the 40th urban administrative zone of the Comune di Roma. It is located to the southwest of the city center and straddles the Grande Raccordo Anulare (Ring Road) line that circles the city. The compilers of the Barrington Atlas noted that this place includes a "brid

name: Marco Pedonio
desc: The villa of Marcus Pedonius.

name: Marina di S. Nicola
desc: Marina di S. Nicola is located close to Alsium.

name: Marmenia
desc: The Domus Marmeniae is a villa located on the Via Appia near the fourth milestone. The villa grounds hosted a pagan necropolis and tradition holds that the matrona, Marmenia, relocated the body of St. Urban to a mausoleum built on the grounds.

name: Mondragone
desc: A Renaissance villa (Villa Mondragone) was built atop the platform of a Roman villa dating to the first century B.C.

name: Monte del Grano
desc: Monte del Grano is a popular name that was assigned to a mausoleum once thought to belong to Alexander Severus, although that assignation is no longer supported. The archaeological remains are now part of the Parco XVII Aprile 1944.

name: Monte dell'Oro
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Monte dell'Oro

name: Montedoro
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Montedoro

name: Monteroni
desc: Monteroni, near Ladispoli, is the site of an Etruscan necropolis.

name: Monte Tosto
desc: An Etruscan and Roman site lying 4 km to the west of Caere along the monumental road leading to Pyrgi. Until the early 1960s, the site was known for the monumental tumulus that Mengarelli had excavated in the 1920s. Subsequent excavation revealed other evidence, including an elite compound that serv

name: Monteverde
desc: The hill of Monteverde, a part of the Ianiculum hill to the west of the Tiber river, was a source of a brown, lithoid tuff (tufo di Monteverde) that was quarried for use as a building material from the second century BC.

name: Montioni
desc: Ashby describes the area of the Vigna Montioni as the findspot of numerous funereal inscriptions and funerary altars. This vineyard of the early twentieth century seems likely to have been the location of the villa of the Iavoleni.

name: Munazio Planco
desc: Munazio Planco, the so-called Villa of Munatius Plancus and villa on Via delle Piagge.

name: Muraccio dell’Omo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Muraccio dell’Omo

name: Naumachia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Naumachia

name: Nemorensis (lake)
desc: Nemorensis Lacus (modern Lake Nemi) is a small, volcanic lake in Latium located south of Rome. The lake is known for its adjacent sanctuary of the goddess Diana and for the recovery of several sunken Roman ships of the first century AD.

name: Nettuno
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Nettuno

name: Nomentum
desc: The Latin town of Nomentum and Rome were linked by means of the Via Nomentana. In Livy's history the town, a member of the Latin League, is captured by Lucius Tarquinius Priscus. Nomentum was one of a number of towns captured by Tarquinius. The Romans granted the town civitas sine suffragio after 33

name: Norba
desc: Norba, located in the Monti Lepini, was a member of the Latin League (ca. 499 B.C.) and became a Latin colony ca. 492 B.C. The city was destroyed in the early first century B.C.

name: Numicus (river)
desc: The Numicus was a river of Latium connected to the legendary history of Aeneas. Modern Fosso di Pratica in Italy.

name: Villa of the Octavii
desc: The archaeological remains of a Roman villa on the hill of San Cesareo are speculatively identified as belonging to the gens Octavia, according to Della Portella 2004 op. cit.

name: Opimiano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Opimiano

name: Ospedale di S. Camillo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Ospedale di S. Camillo

name: Osteria dell’Osa
desc: The site of a major Iron Age necropolis (Latial chronology) composed of over 600 burials.

name: Ostia
desc: The port city of ancient Rome located at the mouth of the river Tiber.

name: Pedum
desc: The Barrington Atlas Directory indicates that an ancient place called Pedum could correspond to the modern Corcolle in Lazio, Italy.

name: Pianabella
desc: A large Christian basilica discovered in 1976 several hundred meters southeast of the Porta Laurentina of Ostia. The original phase dates to the end of the fourth century A.D.

name: Pianelle
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Pianelle

name: Pietra Papa
desc: In terms of modern toponymy, Pietra Papa describes a place on the right bank of the Tiber River where today a riverside avenue (Lungotevere di Pietra Papa) links the Lungotevere Vittorio Gassman to Piazza Augusto Righi. Palmer asserts that the toponym "Pietra Papa" dates to the Middle Ages. Excavati

name: Pietralata
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Pietralata

name: Piscina Torta
desc: Piscina Torta is a place located in the Tyrrhenian coastal zone to the south of Ostia. The ancient place would have been part of the southern Tiber River delta. There would have been several natural ridges parallel to the coast and a coastal lagoon. The site has been connected with salt production s

name: Plinio
desc: The so-called villa of Pliny the Younger, also known as the Villa della Palombara. The villa's first phases date to the Iulio-Claudian period. It continues in use, and continues to undergo modifications, through the second century A.D.

name: Pometia
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Pometia

name: Pompeo
desc: A villa attributed to Cnaeus Pompeius at Albano Laziale.

name: Pons Mulvius
desc: Pons Mulvius (the Milvian Bridge) is a Roman bridge over the Tiber River. The original phase of the bridge dates to the consulship of Gaius Claudius Nero in 206 B.C. The bridge is most famous as the site of a decisive battle between Maxentius and Constantine I fought in A.D. 312.

name: Ponte di Tuscolo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Ponte di Tuscolo

name: Ponte Mammolo
desc: Ponte Mammolo is the modern name of an ancient bridge over the Aniene river. It gives its name to a neighborhood and metro station in the northeast part of the modern city of Rome. Archaeological evidence of ancient quarrying and a settlement have also been found in the vicinity of the bridge.

name: Ponte Salario
desc: The Ponte Salario is a Medieval bridge with Roman origins. It is located at the point where the Via Salaria crosses the Anio, about 3 km north of the Colline Gate.

name: Portus
desc: The great ancient maritime port of Rome, located on the right-hand bank of the Tiber River.

name: Praeneste
desc: An ancient city of central Italy, the eighth and seventh century B.C. origins of which demonstrate high-level trade contact with the Eastern Mediterranean world. The city withdrew from the Latin League (499 B.C.) and opposed Rome in the Latin war; Cincinnatus eventually subdued Praeneste. Sulla foun

name: Prati Fiscali
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Prati Fiscali

name: Prima Porta
desc: Prima Porta, located to the north of Rome, allegedly derives its modern name from the remains of a Roman aqueduct whose presence signaled to travelers on the Via Flaminia that they had reached Rome. The site is best known for an Imperial villa that belonged to the family of Livia Drusilla.

name: Priscilla
desc: A Christian catacomb within an ancient quarry on the Via Salaria that was in use from the second to the fourth centuries AD. The Catacomb of Priscilla was likely named for Priscilla, a member of the gens Acilia, and contains the oldest known Marian painting (third century AD).

name: Quadraro
desc: A Roman villa near the line of the Aqua Claudia located in the modern Via del Quadraro. The villa is dated to the first century B.C. or first century A.D. Following remodelling in the third century, the villa's occupation ends in the fourth century.

name: Quintilii
desc: A suburban villa built by Sextus Quintilius Maximus and Sextus Quintilius Condianus (consuls in A.D. 151).

name: Quintilio Varo
desc: A villa located near the sanctuary of Madonna di Quintiliolo (Tivoli) that is traditionally associated with Quintilius Varus. The remains of the basis villae may date as early as the third century B.C.

name: Redicolo
desc: The Tomb of Annia Regilla (vix. A.D. 125-160), the wife of Herodes Atticus. The tomb is also erroneously known as the "Temple of the God Rediculum" and was used in the Middle Ages as a hay barn.

name: Lacus Regillus
desc: An ancient lake in Latium that was the site of a Roman military victory in 496 BC; the precise location of the lake cannot be determined, although some scholars place its location at Pantano Secco near Frascati, Italy.

name: Robigo?, T.
desc: The sanctuary of the god Robigus, located at the sixth mile of the Via Cassia. The Romans celebrated the festival of Robigalia on 25 April.

name: Roma
desc: The capital of the Roman Republic and Empire.

name: La Rustica
desc: La Rustica was a Latin site located along the Via Collatina.

name: Sabina
desc: The one-time territory of the ancient Sabine people of central Italy.

name: Sacer Mons
desc: Sacer Mons is a hill on the banks of the Anio River and is connected, traditionally, with the episode of the secession of the Roman plebs of 494 BC.

name: Sacro Speco
desc: The Monastery of Saint Benedict or Monastero di San Benedetto Sacro Speco. The Shrine of the Sacred Cave of St. Benedict (Sacro Speco di San Benedetto) at Subiaco is a significant monastic shrine connected to the Roman Catholic saint Benedict. At the site is found a fresco-adorned cave linked to the

name: Salinae
desc: Salt pans located to the east of Ostia and to the north-east of Portus around the Tiber river estuary.

name: Salone
desc: Ancient tuff quarries and a bridge at Salone on the Anio River.

name: S. Agapito
desc: S. Agapito, the Palestrina Cathedral also known as the Cattedrale di Sant'Agapito martire, was built atop the ruins of Praeneste's civic forum and its temple. The relics of Saint Agapitus were transferred to this location in 898. The present basilica was consecrated on 16 December 1117 by Pope Pasqu

name: S. Agata
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Agata

name: S. Agnese
desc: A titular church on the Via Nomentana, S. Agnese houses the remains of the eponymous saint. The present church was built by Pope Honorius I in the seventh century AD, on the site of a fourth century basilica built by Constantine I.

name: S. Alessandro
desc: The basilica and catacombs of S. Alessandro are located at the seventh milestone of the Via Nomentana.

name: S. Antonio
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Antonio

name: S. Callisto
desc: A large catacomb on the Via Appia south of Rome notable especially for its so-called 'Crypt of the Popes'. The catacomb covers approximately 15 hectares.

name: S. Carlo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Carlo

name: S. Cesareo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 S. Cesareo

name: S. Clemens
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 E2 S. Clemens

name: S. Ermete
desc: S. Ermete is the site of a Paleochristian basilica and catacomb; the catacombs are also referred to as the Catacombs of Bassilla, and both names occur in the documentary sources.

name: S. Felicita
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Felicita

name: S. Ippolito
desc: A catacomb connected with the Christian Saint Hippolytus of Rome along the Via Tiburtina.

name: S. Laurentius
desc: The Papal Basilica of Saint Lawrence outside the Walls (Basilica Papale di San Lorenzo fuori le Mura) is one of the Seven Pilgrim Churches of Rome. The basilica serves as the shrine and tomb dedicated to Saint Lawrence and its earliest phases likely belong to the fourth century AD.

name: S. Lidano
desc: The so-called "Archi di San Lidano" are the remains of a Roman stone bridge in the Pontine plain, near the modern locality of Sezze Scalo. The bridge likely dates originally to the second century B.C. Evidence of an ancient sanctuary have also been detected in the vicinity.

name: SS. Marcellino e Pietro
desc: The church of Saints Marcellinus and Peter is a Roman Catholic church located on the Via Merulana in Rome. Pope Siricius built the original church in the fourth century A.D., close to the catacombs of Marcellinus and Peter. The relics of the saints were deposited in the church in 1256.

name: S. Maria di Galeria
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B1 S. Maria di Galeria

name: S. Martino
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 S. Martino

name: S. Passera
desc: S. Passera is a Christian church on the Tiber river in Rome, opposite the Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls. The current church dates to the ninth century and incorporated the remains of a Roman tomb. The church is traditionally connected to a community of local miners.

name: S. Paulus
desc: One of Rome's four major papal basilicae, S. Paulus was founded by Constantine I in the early fourth century A.D. and expanded by Valentinian I in the 370s. The basilica, with many renovations, repairs, and improvements, stood until the 19th century, when it was destroyed in a fire. The reconstructe

name: S. Petrus
desc: The Basilica of St. Peter in Vatican City is currently a Renaissance edifice standing on the site of Old St. Peter's Basilica, a church built by Constantine I between 319 and 333 CE. The holy site is located on the Mons Vaticanus in connection with the purported site of the burial of the Christian S

name: S. Rufina
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Rufina

name: S. Scholastica
desc: A convent founded within the area of the Villa Neronis.

name: S. Sebastianus
desc: S. Sebastianus (San Sebastiano fuori le mura) is a Christian basilica outside the walls of Rome; the earliest phase belongs to the fourth century AD.

name: S. Sinforosa
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 S. Sinforosa

name: S. Valentino
desc: A Christian catacomb along the Via Flaminia dedicated to S. Valentino.

name: S. Vincenzo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D1 S. Vincenzo

name: Satricum
