desc: An ancient settlement on the right bank of the river Astura, Satricum has a mixed heritage of Latins and Volscians. In 499 B.C. Satricum was a member of the Latin League, but was under Volscian control in 488 B.C. The site is noted for its sanctuary of Mater Matuta.

name: Saxa Rubra
desc: Saxa Rubra (modern Grottarossa) is the name of a road station on the Via Flaminia, nine Roman miles from the center of ancient Rome. It was at Saxa Rubra that Constantine I defeated Maxentius in A.D. 312.

name: Scalzacane
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Scalzacane

name: Sep. C. Maenius Bassus
desc: The tomb C. Maenius Bassus is located along the Via Valeria. This podium tomb with superstructure is dated to either the reign of Caius or that of Claudius. Epigraphic evidence mentions that C. Maenius C. f. Cam. Bassus was an Augustalis, an aedile, and praefectus fabrum.

name: Mausoleum of Caecilia Metella
desc: A tomb on the Via Appia south of Rome belonging to Caecilia Metella, a daughter of Metellus Creticus. She was born ca. 100 BC. In 1303, the tomb was incorporated into the Castrum Caetani, serving as the main tower of the fortification.

name: Sep. Geta
desc: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that is traditionally believed to be that of Publius Septimius Geta, the younger son of Septimius Severus.

name: Sep. Plautii
desc: The Mausoleum of the Plautii dates to the first century B.C. It is located near Ponte Lucano at Tibur.

name: Serrone di Bove
desc: The small hill that is known as "Il Poggio di Serrone di Bove" is located in the hinterland of ancient Norba and was the site of ancient settlement activity. Architectural remains on the site include those of a polygonal masonry sub-struction or platform as well as an ancient roadway that may be par

name: Setia
desc: A Volscian settlement of the fifth century B.C. that became a Latin colony in 382 B.C.

name: Sette Bassi
desc: A large, suburban villa complex on the Via Tuscolana. The villa was in use from the reign of Antoninus Pius until the fourth century A.D.

name: Settebagni
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Settebagni

name: Settecamini
desc: An archaeological site located at the midpoint of the Via Tiburtina linking Rome and Tibur.

name: Signia
desc: A city of Latium Adjectum established as a Latin colony ca. 494 B.C.

name: Simbruina Stagna
desc: A series of three artificial lakes created along the river Anio.

name: Solforata
desc: At Solforata along the Via Ardeatina activity related to the extraction of sulfur has been identified.

name: La Storta
desc: A station on the Via Cassia attested in an inscription dated to A.D. 379-383.

name: Sublanuvio
desc: Sublanuvium was an ancient station (statio) along the Via Appia, located between Aricia and Ad Sponsas. While its precise location is unknown, the site is located at the twentieth milestone of the Appia.

name: Sublaqueum
desc: An ancient settlement, located at modern Subiaco in Italy, Sublaqueum was located in the territory of the Aequi that was annexed by Rome in 304 B.C.

name: Tiberis (river)
desc: The Tiber River is the third-longest river of the Italian peninsula, flowing 406 km (252 mi) from the Apennine Mountains to the Tyrrhenian Sea.

name: Tibur
desc: A Sabine town, 30 km east-north-east of Rome, Tibur was the seat of the Tiburtine Sibyl.

name: Tomba degli Orazi e Curiazi
desc: A Roman tomb near Albano Laziale connected in tradition with the story of the contest between the Horatii and Curiatii.

name: Tomba di Marco Plauzio Lucano
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Tomba di Marco Plauzio Lucano

name: Tomb of Vibius Marianus
desc: An imperial Roman tomb of Publius Vibius Marianus, erroneously identified as the Tomba di Nerone (Tomb of Nero) by G. B. Piranesi.

name: Il Tondo
desc: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Il Tondo

name: Isola Conversina

name: Libraries' Courtyard at Hadrian's Villa

name: Byrsa
desc: Walled citadel in Carthage built in the early first millennium BCE. The site was destroyed during the Third Punic War in 146 BCE by the forces of Scipio Aemilianus. The hill became the site of the city's forum in the Roman period.

desc: The Capannelle pass is an Apennine pass located in the Abruzzo.

name: Ager Faliscus (region)
desc: The territory of the Faliscans that lay between areas where Etruscan, Latin, and Sabellic languages were spoken. The geographic limits of this territory on the right bank of the Tiber River stretch from Grotta Porciosa in the north to Capena in the south.

name: Via Rovigno d'Istria catacombs
desc: A small catacomb on two levels was discovered excavated in the tuff bedrock in 1953-1954 near the tract of the modern Via Prenestina in the Via Rovigno d'Istria.

name: Via Taranto columbaria
desc: Two early imperial columbaria were discovered in 1932 along the Via Taranto.

name: Le Caldane
desc: Ancient thermal baths in use from the Etrusco-Roman period onward.

name: Villa delle Terme degli Stucchi Dipinti
desc: An imperial villa, perhaps abandoned in the late first century A.D., located near Tor Vergata.

name: Pincian obelisk
desc: The so-called Pincian obelisk is a monument of red granite that Hadrian brought to Rome from Egypt. It bears hieroglyphics that were likely cut at Rome and seem to indicate that the monument in some way commemorated the place where Antinous was buried. name: Archaeological area of Carife
desc: An ancient necropolis at Carife (Campania) with more than 100 Samnite tombs.

name: Temple of Heracles
desc: The Temple of Heracles is one of the oldest temples in the Valley of the Temples in ancient Akragas, Sicily, dating from around the late 6th century BCE.

name: Villa di Grotte di Piastra
desc: The so-called Villa di Grotte di Piastra, ruins of a Roman villa at Castelporziano.

name: Villa della Longarina
desc: The ruins of a Roman villa rustica located near modern Giardino di Roma, just north of Via Cristoforo Colombo southwest of Rome.

name: Domus rustica
desc: The ruins of a Republican-period 'domus rustica' located on the via Alexandre Gustave Eiffel in Rome, Italy, near Ponte Galeria.

desc: A nuragic site located near Tortoli, Sardinia.

name: Li Muri necropolis
desc: A necropolis with four dolmens surrounded by small kerbstone circles.

name: Forum Boarium (at Rome)
desc: Rome's so-called "cattle market", the Forum Boarium is a key area of commercial and ritual activity on the east bank of the river Tiber. It is flanked by the Capitoline, Palatine, and Aventine hills.

name: Ara Maxima Herculis
desc: An early cult center connected with Herakles located in Rome's Forum Boarium.

name: Aedes Herculis Pompeiani
desc: A temple of Hercules located near the Circus Maximus.

name: Vicus Nediensis
desc: A Roman vicus, attested by name in inscriptions discovered in the 19th century. Based on the reported findspots of the inscriptions, the vicus seems to have been located in the vicinity of modern Spechbach, located southeast of Heidelberg, Germany.

name: Roman theater at Salona
desc: The Roman theater of Salona.

name: Villa of Manlius Vopiscus
desc: A villa site near Tivoli that has long been associated Manlius Vopiscus, who Statius mentions. Excavations began in 1825. In 1835 Pope Gregory XVI began construction of his eponymous Villa Gregoriana on the grounds of the Roman villa.

name: Tomb of Cossinia
desc: A Roman tomb on the right bank of the Anio discovered in 1929. The tomb dates to the first century A.D. and is associated with Cossinia, a priestess of the cult of Vesta.

name: Ponte del Viceré de Ribera
desc: The bridge known as the Ponte del Viceré de Ribera crosses the Fosso di Sant'Andrea on the line of the Via Appia. The viceroy of Naples, one Parefàn de Ribera, renovated the bridge in 1568. During the Second World War, the bridge was bombed and was eventually restored in 2005.

name: Nuraghe Bardalazzu
desc: Nuraghe Bardalazzu, a ruined nuragic site located near Dualchi, Sardinia.

name: Via della Fortuna
desc: A major east-west street in Pompeii that is also connected to the Via di Mercurio and the Via del Foro.

name: Unnamed Roman villa (Ladispoli)
desc: The ruins of a well-appointed Roman Imperial villa are now to be seen immured in the esplanade of one of the beachfronts of Ladispoli, Italy. The visible remains include a portion of a peristyle courtyard with an elaborate mosaic pavement.

name: Temple of Divus Augustus (Nola)
desc: According to Cassius Dio, Tiberius dedicated a temple to the deified Augustus at a location marking the site of the princeps' death. Its precise location is not known.

name: Tomba del Peccato
desc: The so-called Tomba del Peccato has been a well-known rock-cut tomb in the hinterland of Falerii Novi since the nineteenth century. The tomb collapsed following heavy rains in 1991 and is in a ruinous condition.

name: Lake Matese
desc: Lake Matese is a glacial lake located in the Matese mountains at the foot of Monte Miletto and Monte Gallinola.

name: Amphitheater of Alba Fucens
desc: A first century A.D. amphitheater at Alba Fucens built during the reign of Tiberius.

name: Domus, M. Tullius Cicero
desc: The house of the Roman statesman and orator M. Tullius Cicero was located on the north-eastern corner of the Palatine Hill in Rome.
